298. *mid-244-e, "doomed to fall by Ghast" at minute 116, two minutes into its Nether (reached at 114).* On a fortress leg along a ledge at y 89, a ghast in sight at seventeen to nineteen blocks shot, and the fireball threw the bot off: twenty-nine blocks down (the damage frames, note 294: "fireball by ghast", then "fall"). It wore full iron with a shield, and nothing answered the ghast: a shooter counted as a threat only within sixteen blocks, the reach of a bow, and neither the shield, the step off the edge from a ghast (note 219) nor the encounter question came. A shooter is now a threat within its own reach (a ghast's forty, a witch's ten, a blaze's sixteen), so a ghast in sight brings the shield, the edge rule and the stance question.
299. *mid-227-e, a loop at minute 53: a cast frame where it could not be cast.* Casting beside its lava (note 283), the frame went down at y 28 in a cave; each pass failed, "nowhere to stand to pour into the frame slot", and after the bot pillared fifteen blocks up to work free, "no route", until the stall watch counted four and ended the trial. A frame was moved only when its ground had been dug away. A cast that fails three passes running at its site with no obsidian in the frame now leaves the site, remembered with why, and another is chosen at least six blocks from it.
300. *mid-235-g, slain by drowned at minute 32, eating that never finished.* Two drowned at arm's length on a tunnel's shore; Jev chose to eat at twelve health and again at nine and at five. The meal began every half second and was never eaten (hunger seventeen throughout, the damage frames a drowned's hit every half second to a second), and the stance was held or chosen again each time. What cut each meal short is not in the record (a swing, the hand swapped, a new consume cancelling the last). However it was cut, a meal not eaten now keeps the eat stance off the list for ten seconds, so the question is answered from the others.
301. *mid-242-f, into the lava sea at minute 49, eight minutes into its Nether (reached at 41).* In the Nether the ladder still wanted iron (armour for the fight, review finding 1), and the iron ore step, finding no ore about, set a staircase toward the ore's depth, y 16, below the lava sea; eleven blocks down it broke into a cave over the lava, fell ten blocks into it, and burned from thirteen in three seconds ("lava", the damage frames said). An ore step for a block found only in another dimension now says so ("no iron ore in the nether: it is only found in the overworld") instead of digging for it, so the stall sets the step aside or takes the way back.
302. *mid-218-b, a loop at minute 106: a portal corner with nothing to place against.* Building its frame from carried obsidian, the bot's temporary corner support at (-384, 66, 692) had no solid block beside it, and "no adjacent solid anchor" came back 126 times over eight minutes of passes until the stall watch ended the trial. Note 299's rule (three failed passes with no obsidian in the frame leave the site) covered only a cast frame; it now covers any frame but a ruin's, whichever way it is being built.
303. *mid-205-g, slain by a zombie at minute 138 under phantoms.* At night at eight health, with a zombie and two phantoms diving, Jev chose between retreat and the pillar, the pillar twice, told that two up is out of reach of all but a list of climbers; phantoms were not on it, and the pillar was no answer to what was hitting it. The climbers' list now carries the fliers: a phantom (only a roof keeps it off), a blaze, a vex, a bee, an allay. Whether note 277's nights underground, which let two nights pass without a question, brought the phantoms on sooner is to be watched.
304. *mid-207-d, a loop at minute 138: every route "partial" (not fixed).* Beside its half-cast frame at (25, 69, 317), phantoms about and its pockets full (Jev dropping coal to make room), the bot's every walk came back "no route (partial)" with no path at all: the log it was mining at (24, 71, 301), the work-free moves Jev chose, the climb to the surface (failing three times, resting three minutes each). No way was found out of wherever it stood; the cast's temporary walls boxing it in is the likeliest, not seen in the record. Next: a stuck bot's surroundings (the blocks round its feet) written to the flight record when every route fails, so the box can be seen.
305. *mid-229-e, slain by zombies at minute 73 in its own shaft.* Mining gold at y -21 with three zombies about, the fight and then the retreat were chosen, and the retreat's shelter was a shaft pocket dug where it stood; two zombies followed it down the open shaft and stood in its cell, a hit a second for ten seconds while the dig went on, eighteen health to five; the seal Jev chose then came too late. Note 295 stopped the shaft for a creeper that would reach it before the cap; a biter at arm's length now stops it too, before the first block and each after.
306. *mid-202-e, three hours and no Nether: nights with no bed, four wool in the pockets.* Nights were the half of it again (37 minutes in a shelter, 28 night-mining, 47 climbing back up), and the bot carried no bed all run with two black wool, a light gray and a gray: three of one colour make a bed, and a sheep of the right colour was searched for. Wool of any colour is dyed with a dye and the game's recipe book has it; a bone makes three bone meal, three white dye. Now wool of mixed colours with the white dye to hand (bone, bone meal, dye or a lily of the valley) counts as a white bed's: the bed steps dye three white first and then craft the bed, and the planner, where no one kind of wool covers every craft, splits the crafts across the wool carried (it had planned a black dye to make a third black). The bed option says that mixed wool is dyed. Whether a bone was carried at the right time in this run is not clear; the rule is for the next.
307. *mid-230-g, into the lava at minute 75, ten minutes after finding a fortress (the Nether at 61, the fortress at 65).* Waiting to heal before the blazes at y 59 by the fortress, it was hit by four ghast fireballs in six seconds and the fourth threw it into the lava ("tried to swim in lava to escape Ghast"). The ghast was never in view: the fireballs came from further out, and nothing answered a shot whose shooter was not a threat seen. A shot on its way (a fireball, an arrow) is now a threat of its own when nothing else is: the survival turn is taken, the shield comes up to it, and a fireball counts as a ghast's push for the step back from a deadly edge. The wait to heal in the open (review lesser finding) is still where it stood.
308. *mid-202-f, froze to death at minute 4 on a mountain at y 121.* Climbing its staircase up to find food it came into powder snow; the way out of the snow was taken once, and then the staircase took it back down into the snow, where it froze a point every two seconds from twenty to nothing while the food question was asked every half second (the damage frames: "freeze", ten times). The escape was never taken again: it is run when the bot's cells are seen to be powder snow, and powder snow has no collision box. The server's freezing damage now sends the bot out as the blocks do; with no way through the snow found, it walks to the nearest firm ground; and firm ground is no longer a cell of powder snow.
309. *mid-211-g, three hours and no Nether: a cast that never cast.* After forty working minutes on the cast, the portal question (asked twice, note 297's clock working) still said ten of ten to cast, and Jev kept the cast at 0.84 and 0.97, told the nearest lava was a pool seven blocks off. The lava fetch was not using that pool: its staircase rested, and every bucket went to staircases toward the deep lava instead, 114 of them set aside for pacing, 38 minutes of fetching for nothing. One bucket was carried and no iron for more. The lava the portal question is told of is now lava the fetch would use (not a pool whose way rests), so the question sees the cast as it is. Why the pool's way rested, seven blocks off, is not in the record.
310. *mid-242-g, into the lava at minute 27, seven minutes into its Nether (reached at 20).* In iron with no gold, a piglin went for it (piglins attack a player wearing no gold on sight): twenty to fourteen to eight in two blows, and the second threw it off the edge into the lava ("tried to swim in lava to escape Piglin"). Golden boots were a rung Jev could set aside for the Nether first, and the crossing kit said nothing of gold. The kit now carries it: a piece of golden armour, what piglins do without one, and a top-up that makes golden boots (worn in the Nether when carried).
311. *mid-243-f, a loop at minute 66: the walk to the lava for casting beside it.* Jev had chosen to cast beside the lava (note 283); the pool was fourteen to eighteen blocks off, below a hillside, and every walk to within six of it ended where it began, the bot going up and down the hill between y 73 and 86 for minutes until the flip watch ended the trial. Three walks there that come no nearer now let the lava go: the frame is cast where the bot is, the pool left with why. (No unit test: nothing in the suite drives the portal step this far; the rule is small and read by hand.)
312. *mid-244-g, "doomed to fall by Spider" at minute 59 in a ravine.* Climbing out, spiders came up after it; it held on its pillar, came down, fought, and Jev chose the fight at 0.39 told no drop was within three blocks, and one second later a spider's hit put it twenty-two blocks down. The no-route frame of note 304, from a moment before, showed open air under the bot's own cell: it stood on the corner of a block over the edge. The drop measure looked at the cells round the feet and never under them; the bot's own cell is now measured first, and the stance options say a drop under the bot as such.
313. *mid-231-h, shot by a skeleton at minute 96, charging at 3.7 health.* At night on the surface with three skeletons, Jev chose the charge at a shooter (0.77), told of the one in sight sixteen blocks off and an estimate of 2.8 damage; two more were three and four blocks off out of sight, and two arrows ended it. The fight option says the mobs out of sight about; the charge did not. It does now.
314. *mid-218-c, a loop at minute 58: a part-cast frame with nowhere to stand.* The frame at (-231, 65, 733) had slots cast, and the next slot had no cell beside it with a floor that the pours could be made from: "nowhere to stand to pour" two hundred and one times. Note 302's rule leaves a site only while no obsidian is in the frame, and obsidian cast is not taken back without a diamond pickaxe, so this frame stayed. With no stand beside a slot, one is now made: a temporary block put under a cell that would do otherwise (placed against solid ground within two blocks, recorded with the cast's other temporary blocks). Not unit-tested: the test world's own temporary walls always gave a floor, so the case did not arise there; what took the floor away in the trial is not in the record.
315. *mid-227-f, slain by zombies at minute 79, a meal begun nine times.* The same as note 300: three zombies at arm's length by its cast frame, Jev chose to eat at nine health, and the beef was begun every half second and never eaten, hunger falling from seventeen to sixteen. Note 300's mark on a meal cut short was cleared whenever the consume came back, and it came back in half a second with nothing eaten. A meal now counts as eaten only if hunger or saturation went up; otherwise it is cut short, and the eat stance stays off the list for ten seconds.
316. *mid-242-h, into the lava at minute 45, twenty-five minutes into its Nether (reached at 20).* Laying a span toward a fortress, a blaze in sight stopped the span (as it should) and its fireballs came: the shield blocked four (note 307), and the bot drifted half a block with each blocked shot, crouch released between, until it went off the one-wide span thirty blocks into the lava. Note 290 walls a span's open sides for a biter within six blocks; shots on their way and a shooter in sight now bring the walls too.
317. *mid-211-h, into the lava at minute 52, two minutes into its Nether (reached at 50).* On a ledge at y 89 over the lava sea at six health, with a magma cube four blocks off, Jev chose retreat and then the pillar, told that walkers cannot reach a player two up; the cube jumped up to it, hit it to three and threw it off, fifty-five blocks into the lava ("to escape Magma Cube"). The climbers' list now carries the jumpers: a magma cube (higher than two blocks, and its hit throws) and a slime.
318. *mid-241-e, a loop at minute 129: a cast frame thirteen blocks below with no walk down.* Its cast frame stood at y -9; the bot came up to y 4 (for food) and every walk back returned "no path", thirty-nine times, a walk not digging down. A cast frame more than eight blocks off is now walked to first, and when the walk fails the staircase is dug to it, as a lit portal's is. (No unit test: the walk here is the real navigation, which the suite's cast fixtures replace.)
319. *mid-244-h, a loop at minute 38: note 318's walk to the frame, undoing the lava fetch.* Note 318 walked the bot back to a cast frame more than eight blocks off at the start of every cast pass; the lava fetch is a cast pass too, so each staircase toward the deep lava was four steps down when the next pass walked it back up, until the flip watch ended the trial. The walk to the frame is now made only with something to cast (a lava bucket or obsidian in hand).
320. *mid-243-g, burned to death at minute 44, four minutes into its Nether (reached at 40), not fixed.* On a fortress leg at y 41 with its route heading east, the bot moved west two blocks a second, went over an edge ten blocks into the lava sea, climbed out at eight health and burned on, a point a second, standing to recover (in the Nether there is no water to put a player out). What moved it against its route is not in the record: no damage before the lava, no controller, the pathfinder running. The flight record's observations now carry the bot's velocity, whether it stands on the ground, and the keys held, so the next one can be read.
321. *mid-235-h, slain by zombies at minute 92 (not fixed).* Walking to a landmark with four zombies about, in full iron with an iron sword at ten health, the options were all bad and said so honestly: the fight at 25.7 damage against 10.3 health, a pocket of thirteen blocks with a zombie at arm's length, and no way to run that passed none of them. Jev chose the fight (0.53) and it went as told. The facts were right; what put the bot among four zombies at ten health on a walk is upstream, and not yet looked at.
322. *mid-211-i, ended as a loop at minute 13 while getting there.* Walking to the lava to cast beside it, the walk failed and the staircase took over, a block nearer a pass (thirty-one blocks to twenty-three), but each pass tried the walk again first, five seconds failing, so the step turned between the walk and the tunnel and the flip watch counted it a loop. Once the walk to the casting lava has failed, the staircase now goes on pass after pass without it; note 311's three passes with no ground made still let the lava go.
323. *mid-244-f, three hours and no Nether, four minutes of it a spin.* With a creeper left be (keep_working) and a skeleton at under three blocks, the skeleton stopped the work each pass while the stance, held for the creeper, did not see it: its line of sight read differently to the threat check and to the stance's list a moment later. The pass spun twenty times a second for four minutes, the skeleton shooting it from seven health to under three. The mob that stopped the work is now always among the stance's mobs, so a newcomer at arm's length ends the held stance and the question is asked. (No unit test: the flicker is of real sight lines.) The run's other hours went on the surface climbs for food (36 minutes) and the walks to the casting lava (15).
324. *mid-227-g, a loop at minute 33: the kit's sword and the staircase's pickaxe.* The combat kit, run before the crossing each pass, put the sword in the hand; the staircase to the lava put the pickaxe back; the next pass the sword again, until the flip watch counted it a loop. The hand holds the tool of the work in hand: a sword carried is ready (the fight takes it up), and the kit no longer puts it in the hand, readiness judged as kitReady judges it.
325. *mid-244-j, "speared by Zombie" at minute 6.* At ten health with spear zombies ten blocks off, Jev chose to retreat; the next pass survival had nothing to answer (the zombies outside its eight), and the loop's loot came next, a minecart just spotted: the bot stopped to open it and the zombies were on it in four seconds, their spears six a hit, ten to none. Loot now waits while a hostile is in sight within sixteen blocks.
326. *mid-242-i, a loop at minute 43: a cast frame in a hillside.* "Nowhere to stand to pour" a hundred and seven times at (12, 73, 63): the frame, part cast, had rock where a stand would be, and note 314 only put a floor under an open cell. With no open cell and no floor to make, a stand is now dug out beside the slot (feet and head, the fewest digs, never a frame cell, the slot's walls or a temporary block).
327. *mid-242-j, a loop at minute 3: a staircase dig refused for the drop it would open.* The staircase toward iron ore chose a step whose dig the digger refuses ("refusing to open a drop beside the feet"), four times a pass, and the mine step and the tunnel turned between themselves until the flip watch ended the trial; the staircase rested only after rounds without ground made. A staircase dig refused for a drop, or for digging beneath the feet, now rests the staircase at once, as a step with no safe way does, so another heading is taken.
328. *mid-243-h, a loop at minute 44: a part-cast frame on a mountain, "nowhere to stand" after a stand was dug.* At (63, 104, -11) the stand was dug out twice (note 326) and still no pour could be made from it; the frame had obsidian cast, so note 302's rule (three failures, nothing cast) never left the site, and it failed ninety-five times. A frame with obsidian cast now leaves its site after ten failures in a row: a cast block is one lava trip, less than the minutes a stuck site costs. What blocked the pours from the dug stand is not in the record.
329. *mid-231-i, blown up at minute 77 at two health.* Searching for food at 2.2 health, the bot had a creeper follow it in from nine blocks to two with no stance asked, and it went off. A mob Jev chose to leave be (keep_working) stayed left be until three blocks, which for a creeper is where its fuse lights. A creeper left be is now a threat again once within its fuse's reach and a second and a half's walk (seven and a half blocks). Whether the creeper here was one left be or one a charge could not reach (still left be to five, trial 73's ledge) is not in the record.
330. *mid-229-f, into the lava at minute 133, three minutes into its Nether (reached at 130).* On a fortress leg after a retreat, walking down a slope with the route running and no hit taken, the bot dropped twenty blocks from y 51 into the lava sea: the same as mid-243-g (note 320), and again not explained by the record (the new velocity fields came only on damage frames). One mechanism fits both: the walk's gap jumps, allowed where the columns jumped over are survivable, but a jump that falls short lands where the body goes, and in the Nether that can be the sea. Gap jumps are now off in the Nether (a physical-safety rule; a gap there is bridged or walked round). If such a fall comes again, this was not it.
331. *mid-218-d, a loop at minute 88: at sea with no shore.* In open water the shore search found no land within sixty-four blocks, and "no reachable dry shore" came back every pass while the bot drifted, until the stall watch ended the trial. Out at sea with no land candidate, none in view and no unloaded ground about, the bot now swims for the land remembered (the sea crossing), and else holds one heading twenty seconds a pass until land is in view, turning when a heading is blocked. (No unit test: the swim runs twenty real seconds.) Also: the flight file's slimmed observation frames now keep the velocity, footing and keys (note 320's fields were being dropped from them).
332. *mid-202-g, into the lava at minute 133, eighteen minutes into its Nether (reached at 115).* On a span a block over the lava sea it held still, crouched, four seconds with a ghast in sight twenty-two blocks off; note 316's walls came only for shots on their way or a shooter within eight, so none went up before the fireball, which threw the bot into the lava. A shooter in sight within its own reach (a ghast's forty) now brings the walls.
333. *mid-205-h, slain by zombies at minute 153 in cave water (not fixed).* Searching for food underground at 13.8 health, the bot walked into three zombies; Jev chose the fight and then the pillar (0.97), the pillar did not go up (the bot ended two blocks lower, in water), and the fight went on in the water to the end, retreat and pillar chosen again at low confidence as health fell. Why the pillar came down instead of up is not in the record; note 289's water stances did not apply until it was in the water, by which time three zombies were at arm's length.
334. *mid-227-h, slain by a magma cube at minute 57 after two falls, fourteen minutes into its Nether (reached at 43).* The first record with velocity and keys (note 331) showed it: at the end of a stretch of span at y 106 the bot slid on with no key held, velocity 0.11 a tick, off the end, ten blocks down, then fifteen more, from twenty to two among magma cubes. The span let go of the walk and the crouch at once, and a crouching player holds at an edge only while crouched; the step's way on carried it over. The crouch is now let go only once the body has stopped (half a second at most).
335. *mid-230-h, "obliterated by a sonically-charged shriek" at minute 151.* Recovering at y -52 in the deep dark, the bot stood still while a warden sixteen blocks off behind the rock boomed it for ten a time; nothing reacted, since the warden was out of sight and past the eight blocks a biter counts at. A warden's boom passes walls and reaches about twenty: a warden within twenty-four is now a threat seen or not, the flee counts it, and the shelter stances (pillar, bunker, pocket, dig down) say it reaches them, so no stance claims to shut it out.
336. *mid-243-i, "impaled by Drowned" at minute 43.* In full iron with a shield, on the way to the portal, the bot met a drowned with a trident ten blocks off; the fight and the retreat were tried and failed, and Jev chose the pillar (every option said more damage than the bot had). Two up, the held pillar returned at once each pass, nothing done and nothing reported: the loop ran twenty passes a second for twelve seconds, the hurt watchdog stopped the work at each hit, and four tridents took twenty health to none. The shield never rose because a thrown trident was not among the projectiles the guard looks for. A trident flying at the bot is now incoming (the shield goes up to it as to an arrow), and the pillar held up top faces the nearest mob and waits a quarter second a pass, reported as pillar_hold, so the swing and the shield do the work.
337. *mid-211-j, a loop at minute 86: a portal that would not light.* The cast frame at (385, 67, -223) was whole, ten obsidian, but a cobblestone stood inside it at (386, 70) that was not among the frame's recorded temporary walls (a stand or a scaffold, the record does not say which); the walls were cleared before lighting, the flint and steel set fire beside the cobblestone, the portal did not fill, and the wait for it timed out a hundred and twenty-five times until the loop watch ended the trial. Before lighting, every block inside the frame now comes out, whatever put it there: the portal takes only air and fire.
338. *mid-218-e, "slain by Spider" at minute 30, sitting in a boat.* A boat crossing had reached its far side when the bots were restarted (for note 336), and the server put Jev back in its boat on joining. Mineflayer runs no physics for a rider, and the work did not know it was seated: the session hung minutes on end (no survival check for two and a half minutes; the stall watch said so and could not act), was restarted again (for note 337) into the same seat, and a spider took it from twenty to none where it sat, the position not moving an inch through the knockback. A crossing always leaves its boat before it returns, so a rider between work passes is one left there: the loop now gets out first, and a seat given within five seconds of joining is left at once.
339. *mid-244-i, a loop at minute 106: on a mineshaft bridge over a cave at y 3, no way up offered that could work.* Down for lava at the bottom of the world, the bot stood on a one-wide plank bridge with open cave on every side. Every staircase heading's first stair had no floor ("no floor 5"), eight headings set aside in twenty seconds; straight up was ruled out by gravel in the column; the staircase was the only way out offered, chosen again at each ask, and the loop watch ended the trial. Two things are fixed. The climb now also offers laying a level span of blocks across the open cave toward the way up (bridging.js, crouched, surveyed first: cells, blocks laid of carried, what it stops at, cells over lava), asked again from the span's end; and the climb is asked again whenever a way not offered before is open, not only the column. And while it stood there with zombies about, the step off the edge (a deadly drop two blocks off) had no ground three from a drop and fell back to ground merely not beside one, which was the cell it stood on: it walked to where it was, twenty passes a second for minutes. A step off the edge now never targets the feet.
340. *mid-229-g, "burned to death" at minute 52, sixteen minutes into its Nether (reached at 36).* On a fortress leg a ghast's fireballs came in one after another; at 13.8 health Jev chose to seal a pocket, and from 22:00 the bot took ten in-fire hurts in seven seconds, from eleven health to none, while the seal was built: the fire the fireball lit was where it stood. The out-of-fire reflex (vitals.js, note on trial 101) runs in the survival layer's turn, and the hurt watchdog, which would have handed it that turn, gives way to a stance Jev holds. Standing in fire is now never a stance carried out: the watchdog stops it, as for no stance. And the server's in-fire hurt counts as being in fire, as its freeze hurt counts as being in powder snow (note 308), whatever the blocks at the feet show.
341. *mid-207-e, three hours and no Nether.* The cast was chosen twenty-two times and the portal never made: twelve frame sites were left, seven of them for "refusing to open a drop beside the feet", which came from the tunnel down to the lava (the fill_bucket step), not from the site. Note 302's count of a site's failures counted every failure of the cast, the lava trips' too, so three refusals far below a good site left it and a new site was picked, the lava walked for again from there. Only a failure within twelve blocks of the frame counts against its site now; one on the way to the lava is the trip's. Where the rest of the run went: filling buckets 29 minutes, the night mine 24, mining 24, smelting 13, surface climbs 12.
342. *mid-242-k, a loop at minute 76, twenty-five minutes into its Nether (reached at 51): the fortress leg and a block of crimson nylium.* At (42, 57, 0) in a crimson forest, the leg south was blocked at head height by crimson nylium, which neither the staircase's list of ground it may dig (tunneling.js natural) nor the crossing's (bridging.js) had: every step south was "crimson nylium in the way", the crossing stopped after two cells, and the tunnel paced the same three cells, the leg turned, until the loop watch ended the trial on the crossing and the leg trading names. The Nether's forest floor and trees (both nyliums, the wart blocks, shroomlight, stems and hyphae, glowstone) are now ground to dig through; magma is still not.
343. *mid-230-i, a loop at minute 39: making obsidian, the same lava dug for thirteen passes.* The staircase toward the lava at (240, 9, 1037) was refused each time for the drop it would open, and rested (note 327); the obsidian step chose the same lava again at the next pass, as the lava-bucket step did before note 286's rule, and the loop watch ended the trial. The obsidian step now skips lava whose staircase is resting, as collectLava does: the pour spots, the pools here, the lake remembered, and the deep lava on the four headings, in that order; with every one resting it says so.
344. *mid-205-i, "slain by Spider" at minute 58.* Mining iron at y 38 in iron armour with a stone sword, the bot met three spiders, one on a ledge a block above its head; Jev chose to fight. The fight and its swing at the mob in reach (defend) traded the survival layer's name four times in two seconds, and the flip watch took that for a stall ("turning between defend and fight") and set the swing aside: from there no swing is in the record, only the fight chosen again every three seconds while the spiders took it from nine health to none. The swing is now one of the fight's own moves, as the raised shield was, and so is the pillar held up top (note 336); the run out of fire is an emergency, never set aside.
345. *mid-235-i, "shot by Skeleton" at minute 137, at y 5 with a skeleton and a zombie.* Jev chose to dig down at 6.7 health; the shaft pocket it runs had failed a moment before ("the saved shelter has no safe approach") and was resting, so its report threw SetAside. That was thrown out through the stance: the stance was not recorded as failed, stayed held, ran again at every tick and was refused again, the survival turn ended with nothing done, and the work step's threat check spun a hundred times a second while an arrow landed every three seconds, from 6.7 to none. A stance whose action is resting is now a stance that failed: set aside for twenty seconds here, and the next tick chooses from what is left.
346. *mid-205-j, a loop at minute 11: every way down toward gold set aside.* With no gold in view, the mine step goes down toward the ore's depth along one of four headings twenty-four blocks off; at (-296, 49, 637) all four staircases were resting, and "every way down toward the gold ore from here is set aside" came back fifteen passes running, the stall's mine-nearby detour between, until the loop watch ended the trial. The ways down are now eight headings at twenty-four and forty-eight blocks, sixteen staircase areas, near first.
347. *mid-207-f, "tried to swim in lava" at minute 32, at y -55.* Tunnelling to a deepslate iron ore, a block beside a lava source was dug a block from the bot's feet ((43, -55, 286), the source at (43, -55, 287)); the lava ran into the gap and onto the bot in a second and a half, and it burned from twenty to none trying to get out through it. The staircase's own digs look for lava behind the rock (safeExcavation), but the dig itself did not, only asking afterwards whether to plug the leak. A block with lava beside it (level or above) is now never dug within the lava's run of the bot (three blocks in the Overworld, seven in the Nether): a hard rule for the body's safety. Refused on a staircase, it rests the staircase, as a refused drop does.
348. *mid-218-f, a loop at minute 49: a ruined portal's corner with nothing to place against.* The frame adopted from a ruin at (-384, 66, 692) needed a cobblestone support at its corner, and the corner had no solid block beside it: "no adjacent solid anchor", 125 failures at the site. Note 302's leaving rule passed over ruins (a ruin cannot be moved), so nothing left it until the loop watch ended the trial. A ruin that fails at its site ten times is now marked as no frame to finish, and the way to a portal is asked again without it on offer. Clearing a ruin's slots and inside now counts as work at the site too.
349. *mid-202-h, "shot by Skeleton" at minute 94, at y 47 by a stream.* A skeleton six blocks off and a creeper at twenty-one; the fight chosen at 20:16 failed and rested, and at 5.8 health Jev chose to charge the skeleton, which failed at once without a step: the option was offered by one water test and refused by the run's other (the body in the stream) or by the feet being in the air, and the charge rested twenty seconds too. What was left was a pillar, bunker, pocket or dig-down each said to cost more than the bot had (the creeper counted as coming), and leaving the mobs be; Jev chose the last three times, at 5.8, 4.9 and 3.2 health, and the arrows ended it. The charge is now offered only where its run takes it (out of the water by either test), and the run waits up to a second for the feet rather than refusing mid-hop.
350. *mid-227-i, "slain by Magma Cube" at minute 85, twenty-five minutes into its Nether (reached at 60).* Magma cubes on a ledge at y 86: Jev chose to fight, and the fight, held only for its estimate's two seconds, was asked again eight times in eighteen seconds; each answer took about two seconds, and nothing swung while it was out: no swing is in the record, and the cubes' hits took it from seventeen to one. At 0.8 health, the fight set aside, it chose to keep working. While Jev is asked the stance, what is in reach is now struck (the swing's own reflex, as the creeper is backed from meanwhile).
351. *mid-243-j, "tried to swim in lava to escape Enderman" at minute 80, thirty-three minutes into its Nether (reached at 47).* Laying a span at y 59 across the lava sea, the bot was hit by an enderman (four a hit through the armour), Jev chose to fight, and the second hit's knockback threw it off the span, thirty blocks into the lava. The span's walls (note 290) were not raised: they went up only when no span was being laid, which kept the wall off the next cell but left every side open while laying. They now go up while a span is being laid too, on every open side but the one the span goes on.
352. *mid-218-g, "shot by Skeleton" at minute 20.* At night a skeleton shot the bot from twenty to seven over half a minute; the retreat got it thirty blocks clear, and then, hungry, Jev chose to walk back to sheep sixty blocks off, on the far side of the skeleton. The option said the walk, the dark and the health, but not the skeleton on the way; two more arrows on the way, and a third in the water it fell into. A herd seen earlier now says the hostiles within ten blocks of the straight way there, in view or not, and how far along it each is.
353. *mid-230-j, "doomed to fall by Ghast" at minute 50, thirty-four minutes into its Nether (fortress reached at 17).* Laying a span of thirty-one toward the portal back at y 68, a drop of sixteen beside it, the bot was shot at by a ghast in sight thirty-nine blocks off; the span went on (the layer stops under fire only for a shooter within twenty-four), Jev chose to dig down, then to retreat, and the second fireball threw it off, sixteen blocks, thirteen of fall from 11.8. A span now counts as under fire for each shooter within its own reach (the ghast's forty), as the threat check and the span's walls already did (notes 298, 332).
354. *mid-241-f, three hours and no Nether (not fixed).* No death and no loop: the time went a little everywhere. Waiting in shelters 25 minutes, searching for food 21 (animals scarce; the searches walked 10,000 blocks in all), climbing to the surface 36 (ascend 19, return 17), mining and smelting 16, lava for the cast 11. The cast frame (at (180, 36, -386), underground) had one failure; three sites were left, one after the walk to its lava came no nearer (note 322). What would have saved the most here is fewer trips up and down between the mine and the surface for food and nights; no one rule stood out to change.
355. *mid-241-g, "slain by Zombie" two minutes in, at y -14.* A skeleton ahead and a zombie behind, out of the list in view: the rule's charge at the shooter (close_on_shooter, not Jev's) reported, broke off at once for the zombie within three blocks, and returned as if it had acted, ten times a second, the swing never reached; the zombie and an arrow took it from four to none. The charge now does not start with a biter within three blocks, in view or not, and one that neither steps nor swings is no answer (the turn goes on, and a chosen one fails as a stance).
356. *mid-211-k, "blown up by Creeper" at minute 100, at y 38 (not fixed).* Four creepers at 3, 4, 9 and 10 blocks, full health in full iron; Jev chose the creeper dance twice in a second (asked again for the second coming within six), told that one blast two blocks off (about 21 through the armour) ends it and that the dance takes one at a time while the others come on. A blast took it from twenty to none a second later. The facts were on the option; retreat, a pocket and a bunker were on offer too. A judgment, not a missing fact or a broken rule.
357. *mid-218-h, "slain by Zombie" at minute 21, sitting in a boat again.* Restarted in its boat (note 338's case), and note 338's fix did not catch it: on joining, the server's seat packet came before the boat itself, mineflayer set bot.vehicle to nothing, and both the join check and the loop's check saw no vehicle. The bot sat thirteen minutes at y 62.11 with no survival check until a zombie killed it where it sat. The seat is now kept as the server says it (the vehicle's id, known or not), and a seat so kept is left with the dismount input whether or not the boat is known yet.
358. *mid-230-k, "slain by Hoglin" at minute 21, three minutes into its Nether (not explained).* Twenty-five seconds after the restart for note 357, at y 84, a hoglin (and a skeleton twenty off) took it from twenty to none in eighteen seconds: pillar, fight, fight, pillar, retreat and dig down were chosen in turn, one swing landed, a step off the edge came between, and the hoglin's tosses kept it in the air. The record does not say why the fights chosen did not swing more; the swing while the answer is out (note 350) was in effect. Watched for.
359. *mid-244-k, three hours and no Nether: forty-six minutes of climbing by hand.* The night mine (343 of its questions answered in the run) wore six pickaxes, 621 uses, to none by 06:39; with one stick, no wood and 128 cobblestone, no other could be made, and the climb from y -22 to the surface went by hand, a stair every forty-five seconds, from 06:41 to 07:27. The night mine's question was told the pickaxes' uses but not what came after them. It is now told how many more stone pickaxes the sticks, wood and stone carried make, and, below open sky, the climb out by hand in minutes, so the dig can be weighed against the way home. (Also: surface climbs took twenty minutes more of the run, waiting in shelters eight.)
360. *mid-231-j, three hours less ten and no Nether; ended on a flip between the cast and the portal step.* The night mine took 37 minutes of the run, the food search 18, surface climbs 20. One stall is fixed: a staircase up a mountain toward (-730, 162, 69) found "no tool for snow block" on four of its steps and rested ten minutes. A block soft enough to dig by hand in a moment (hardness under one: snow, dirt, sand and the like) is now dug on a staircase without its tool, and the staircase's digs no longer ask for the drop; the room is what a stair wants.
361. *mid-205-k, "slain by Zombie" at minute 80, eleven seconds after a restart.* The bots were restarted for note 360 while this one held a pillar at y -8 among zombies; it rejoined in the same crowd with nothing decided, fell to y -10 and was killed in eleven seconds. It is the fifth death of the day to follow a restart by seconds (a boat twice, notes 338 and 357; a span, 353; a hoglin, 358; this). A new build is now taken at a quiet moment: the restart is asked for by touching .bot-state/restart-requested, and each bot quits for it once nothing hostile is within sixteen blocks and it stands on dry ground, off any span or seat, or after five minutes anyway (quiet-restart.js); the supervisor starts the new build as before.
362. *mid-235-j, "fireballed by Ghast" at minute 85, sixteen minutes into its Nether (reached at 69).* A minute after a restart, the fortress search stood at the end of its span at y 41 over the lava sea with no blocks left to build with (sixteen gravel, two planks); a ghast thirty-seven blocks off shot, the walls (note 332) could not go up for want of blocks, and it held still five times until the fireball threw it off, eleven blocks into the lava. With a shot or a biter pressing on a span and no walls to be had, the bot now steps back off the span to firm ground within eight blocks (an emergency, as the step out of lava is).
363. *mid-241-h, "blown up by Creeper" at minute 43, on a ledge at y 74.* At 8.9 health, hunting at night, the bot came onto a one-wide ledge; a creeper walked up, the span's rule held it still and crouched, and the creeper went off beside it. Walls do not stop a blast, and holding still is where a creeper lights. With a creeper coming within twelve blocks on a span, the bot now steps off it first, to firm ground at least two blocks farther from the creeper than it stands (note 362's step off, pointed away).
364. *mid-205-l, "suffocated in a wall" at minute 6.* Twenty seconds after rejoining (a quiet restart), the bot stood at (-368.9, 67, 577.5) in an open two-high cell and took a point of suffocation every half second for eight seconds, twenty to none, nothing dug. The game tests suffocation with a box round the eye four fifths of the body's width, and at x -368.9 that box reached into gravel in the next column (x -370); the bot's test looked at the eye's own cell only, which was open. The test is now the game's: every cell the eye's box touches, and the solid one found is the one dug out.
365. *mid-207-g, "shot by Skeleton" at minute 84 (not explained).* On a pillar of its own two blocks up at (25, 72, 296), a skeleton seven to twelve blocks off shooting every three seconds: the charge was chosen (set aside, no firm ground toward it from the pillar top), then the retreat twice, told a way was found ten blocks off, 1.8 seconds at a run. The retreat's walks stalled three times, three seconds each, forward held, sneak not, and the body hardly moved (velocity 0.02 to 0.07 a tick) from a pillar top with open air on every side; eleven health to none. What held the walk is not in the record: the crouch was off; a raised shield slows a walk to a fifth, and the shield state is not recorded. The flight record's keys now include "shield" while the shield is raised.
366. *mid-227-j, "blown up by Creeper" at minute 67 (not explained).* Thirty-eight seconds after a quiet restart, pillaring up toward its portal at y 103 from (-151, 64, -623), the work stopped for a creeper four blocks off (20:59), and in the three seconds before it went off nothing was reported by the survival layer: no stance asked, no back-off, one navigation that stalled at the pillar's foot (toward (-153, 66, -624), whose it is not in the record). Twenty to none at point blank. Why the survival layer made no answer to a creeper at four blocks is not in the record; watched for.
367. *mid-211-l, "shot by Pillager" at minute 44, by a stream (not fixed).* A pillager patrol, four crossbows six to eight blocks off, arrows about once a second: the rule's charge ran once, Jev chose a pillar and then a retreat (neither went: the bot was in and out of the water, swimming across), and by 5.5 health only the pocket and keeping on were left on offer, every other stance having failed here in the last twenty seconds. Sealed, it was shot through the building. Four shooters at once and water underfoot left no stance that worked; what would have served (out of their sight behind the bank) was the retreat, which found no route in the water.
368. *mid-202-i, "slain by Zombie" at minute 74, at a shelter being built at y 102.* Two zombies; the shelter chosen for the night was walked to with one hitting from behind, and at the site the emergency rule sealed the half-built walls, four seconds of building with a zombie one to two blocks off, from 12.7 to 7.2, because its "no sealing with a mob at arm's length" counted only mobs in sight and the zombie was round the wall. Then the fight, six critical swings in six seconds, too late. A biter within arm's length now rules out sealing whether it is in view or not. (The swings are in the record now as the defend frames' swing kind; the shield's being up is in the keys, note 365.)
369. *mid-242-l, "shot by Piglin" at minute 125, twenty-five minutes into its Nether (fortress reached at 105).* In iron with no gold worn, crossbow piglins went for it at y 42; the retreat found no way, and the rule's "hold defensive position" stood under their arrows forty seconds, from 6.7 to none. At the crossing Jev had chosen to cross without gold every time it was asked, and the gold option it was shown began "undefined Gold: no piece of golden armour carried": its first sentence, the one that says what the option does, was missing from the kit's texts. It now says: make golden boots first and wear them, four gold ingots, smelted from raw gold or gold ore. (Why no stance but holding was left at the end: the retreat and the fight had failed within twenty seconds; not changed.)
370. *mid-244-l, "blown up by Creeper" at minute 42, at y 36.* Stalking a skeleton at 6.7 health with a creeper, a zombie and two skeletons about, the step off an edge (a deadly drop near) chose the cell beside the feet, (49, 36, 120) from 48.8: the walk to it came back at once each time without moving, and the step was taken a hundred times a second until an arrow and the blast. Note 339 ruled out the cell stood on; this was the next cell over, and the walk went nowhere all the same. A step off the edge that does not move the bot now sets itself aside for five seconds, and the rest of the turn (the stance, the swing) answers.
371. *mid-229-h, "burned to death" at minute 143, twenty-one minutes into its Nether (reached at 122).* On a fortress leg the path ran along a one-wide netherrack ridge at y 35, the lava lake at 30 and 31 below on the one side; the bot walked it upright and slid off at z -81.5 with nothing pushing it, into the lava, out of it at 6.8 and burned from there to none. The edge's cost (note 217) still takes a ridge that is the way. While a walk is under way in the Nether, the bot now crouches on any cell beside a drop into lava or one that would take half its health or more, as a player does on a ridge (a crouching body cannot step off an edge), and lets go of the crouch before a step down the path means to take.
372. *mid-202-j, "blown up by Creeper" at minute 17, at full health.* Walling a pocket for the night, the build stopped for a creeper that would go off before it closed (note 292's check), and returned; the next tick began the same pocket and stopped again, a hundred times a second, nothing else answering the creeper, until it went off: twenty to none. The pocket given up for a creeper racing it is now set aside for ten seconds, and the shelter step does not begin a pocket so set aside, so the turn goes to the creeper.
373. *mid-207-h, a loop at minute 28: every way to lava resting.* The lava fetch for the cast had its pool and all four headings to the deep lava resting, and threw "every way to lava from here is resting" three passes running. Note 346 gave the ore descent eight headings at twenty-four and forty-eight blocks; the lava fetch and the obsidian step kept four. They now take the same sixteen, near first (tunneling.js descentTargets).
374. *mid-244-j, three hours and no Nether: thirty-eight minutes carrying lava a bucket at a time.* The cast frame at (48, 71, 129) was at the surface, the walk to the lava beside it given up (three walks came no nearer), and the lava sixty blocks down: with one bucket, ten trips. Making buckets was offered twice, as "twelve more from the 38 iron ingots, about 1 trip against 10", and Jev chose the cast as it was both times; by the later asks the iron had gone elsewhere. The offer now makes no more buckets than the lava still to fetch wants (nine here, not twelve), and says each trip's time to the nearest known lava and the minutes of walking either way. (Also: finding lava pools 15 minutes, food 14.)
375. *mid-244-m, "impaled by Drowned" at minute 38, at a river.* Climbing out to the surface at 8.9 health with a drowned throwing tridents: the shield came up to each one and went straight down, a hundred times a second, and two tridents took it from 8.9 to none. The guard rose for a shot within twenty blocks and held only while one was within twelve, so a trident twelve to twenty off raised and dropped it at once, blocking nothing. It now holds while the shot is still coming at the reach it rose for (to the hold's end).
376. *mid-244-o, "speared by Zombie" two minutes in, at y 14.* Spear zombies at 6.6 health: the pillar went up two, as told "zombies cannot reach a player two up", and a spear's thrust reached the bot on top three times, 6.6 to none. A spear reaches past an arm. The pillar now counts mobs with a spear among those that still reach it two up, in its cost, and says so: "A spear reaches past an arm: the zombie with a spear still reaches the bot two up."
377. *mid-227-k, "blown up by Creeper" at minute 75, at y -15.* Jev chose to leave a creeper be and work on (crafting an iron pickaxe); when it came within its fuse's reach and a threat again (note 329), the work stopped, and the stance, held fifteen seconds, ran again at every tick: "keep working", a hundred times a second, the creeper walking in. The dance was chosen only at three blocks, then a shot, and it went off, 10.4 to none. The same spin was in mid-202-h and mid-227-i. Leaving the mobs be is no longer held once one of them is a threat despite it: the stance is asked again at once.
378. *mid-244-n, "slain by Zombie" at minute 24, eating a golden apple that never went down.* With two zombies at arm's length at 9.6 health Jev chose the golden apple, and the stance "ate" it every half second for four seconds, none eaten, the zombies hitting throughout: the apple's run took the consume's return for a meal, and the consume came back at once. Mineflayer finishes an eat on any change of the held item, and the equip's own change, confirmed by the server a moment after the eat began, ended it. The eat stances now wait for the hand to settle before the bite, and the apple counts as eaten only when one is gone (a stance not done is set aside, as note 345 says). This is likely what cut the meals in notes 300 and 315 short too.
379. *mid-241-i, "shot by Skeleton" at minute 108, at 2.3 health and hunger nineteen.* Clear of the skeleton after a retreat, with health coming back on its own (hunger at eighteen or more), the survival question offered one thing, food (carrying on was off while a food plan was held); Jev chose the sheep fifty blocks off, told "a skeleton 9 blocks from the way, 34 along it" (note 352), and was shot on the way. Staying put while health comes back was not on offer. It is now: when health is under twenty and hunger is eighteen or more, "rest where it is" is offered with the health, the seconds to twenty and the mobs about, held half a minute (catalog updated).
380. *mid-229-i, "shot by Skeleton" at minute 91, twenty-four minutes into its Nether (reached at 67).* Beside lava at y 33 with a skeleton shooting, the run's first move, the step back from the lava edge, went nowhere each time (the walk came back at once) and was taken for done, twenty times a second; then the fight and the charge were chosen and it stood, shot four times more, 7.8 to none. A step back from the lava edge that does not move the bot now tries the next footing, and with none the rest of the run's answer goes on (note 370's rule, for the lava edge). Why the charge chosen did not move is not in the record.
381. *A guard for the spins (no trial of its own).* Notes 339, 370, 377 and 380 were one shape: a survival action that went nowhere (a walk that came back at once, a stance run again) reported itself as the answer twenty to a hundred times a second, the bot standing still, until a mob ended it. Each was fixed where it was found; the shape is now guarded in general: any survival action, an emergency's too, reported twenty times within a second with the bot not moving is refused for five seconds, said in the log, and the rest of the turn answers.
382. *mid-202-k, two deaths at minutes 90 and 91 (not fixed).* First, eight minutes into its Nether (reached at 86): walking a fortress leg along a ledge at y 89 over the lava sea (the route Jev chose), a blaze's fireball was seen eight blocks off and struck 1.3 seconds later, no shield raised in the record between, and threw the bot sixty-five blocks down into the lava. Why the guard did not raise the shield in the second and a third it had is not in the record (the fireball's speed may have carried it past the guard's look). Second, respawned without its armour, zombies at the surface took it from twenty to none in seven seconds, one swing landed. Neither is fixed; the first is watched for.
383. *mid-211-m, "slain by Enderman" at minute 118.* Going home for food at full health (just after resting to heal, note 379's option, chosen and used), an enderman was provoked; Jev chose to retreat three times, told only "a way is found, 2.1 seconds at a run", and each run ended with the enderman beside it again, 16 to none. The retreat now says, with an enderman among the mobs: an enderman after the bot teleports to it, a run from one ends with it beside the bot again (as it says of riders, note on mid-215-a).
384. *mid-235-k, a loop at minute 132, a fortress reached at 127.* With no building blocks left, every leg of the fortress search stopped at the first gap ("0 carried"), the crossing and the search trading names until the loop watch ended the trial. The block top-up was offered three times in the Nether and passed over, described as it is in the Overworld: "seal a pocket for the night or tower out of a hole". In the Nether it now says what the blocks are for there: every crossing over lava or a gap is laid a block a step and one with none stops at the first gap, and netherrack is all around and comes out in a moment with any pickaxe.
385. *mid-227-l, "fireballed by Blaze" at minute 47, at its fortress (reached at 44).* On a fortress bridge at y 77 under two blazes' fire: the span's rule held the bot still and crouched, five times in two seconds; the walls went up once (38:03), too late, and the shield came up only then, twice. The span rule's branch returned before the shield's turn in the survival tick, so with no walls to be had and no firm ground within reach, a shot on its way was simply stood in. The shield now comes up to a shot on its way there, crouched, before the hold.
386. *mid-243-k, three hours and no Nether (not fixed).* The run began underground with no pickaxe and climbed out eighty blocks by hand (the first half hour); then the cast frame went up at the surface at (74, 70, 80) and each lava trip went down and came back up the column: fetching lava 41 minutes, climbing back up 39, most of the day's 43 minutes standing still being the climbs a block at a time. Casting beside the lava was offered three times, with a trip's seconds either way, and Jev kept the frame at the surface; buckets were offered once. Judgment, with the facts given; nothing changed.

The doorway cells (in front of and behind the opening, the three above the floor) are no longer reserved, and once the portal is lit the cast's walls in the doorway come out.
388. *mid-211-n, "shot by Pillager" at minute 17 (not fixed; as note 367).* The same world's pillager patrol by the same stream: retreat, eat, pillar, seal and retreat chosen in turn while swimming, arrows every second or so, eighteen to none in twenty-five seconds. Two of the last three trials of first-days-211 ended at this patrol. Water under the feet undoes every stance that builds or runs; what would serve (out of the water, then out of their sight) is the thing to look at next if it comes a third time.
389. *mid-218-i, three hours and no Nether (not fixed).* No death or loop. The nights went on the night mine (41 minutes) and waiting in shelters (18); the days on gathering wool for a bed (20 minutes, sheep scarce), food (15), lava for the cast (17) and smelting. The cast frame went up late at (-675, 64, 572) after the walk to the known lava was given up 444 blocks off. A day spent on the bed that nights would have been slept through; nothing here stands out as one rule to change.
390. *mid-230-l, three hours and no Nether: an hour and forty minutes in a pocket with a creeper outside.* By day the pocket's question said "stay, though nothing is watching it" and Jev chose to leave sixty-seven times; each time every door was refused for a creeper drifting three to seven blocks off behind the rock, and the pocket waited (67 minutes) or swung at it through the wall (36). The watcher counted an unseen mob only within six blocks, and leaving shuts every door within six of a creeper up to sixteen off. A creeper within sixteen, seen or not, is now the pocket's watcher (so "open on it" and the rest are asked with it named), and leaving says what it does with a creeper by the doors.
391. *mid-242-n, "suffocated in a wall" at minute 17.* Tunnelling toward iron at y 35 under a column of gravel (y 36 to 37 and up), the staircase stepped into (36, 35, 76) and the gravel fell into the head cell as it did; it had already once dug out of gravel there a few seconds before. From 09:02 the bot took a point of suffocation every half second to none, and no dig out is in the record for those eleven seconds (the survival layer's last action was a meal begun at 08:58; what held the turn is not in the record). The staircase now never steps into a cell with sand or gravel standing over the head cell, level and down steps as the climbing ones already did.
392. *mid-227-m, "burned to a crisp while fighting Blaze" at minute 30, three minutes into its Nether (not fixed).* Stalking blazes at 11.9 health on a span at y 86, the bot held still on the span three times, a fireball struck (12 to 9.4), the walls went up and the shield came up (notes 332, 385), and the fire it had caught burned it from 6.4 to none over five seconds. In the Nether there is no water to put the fire out and nothing but waiting burns it off. The hunt at under twelve health with blazes about was the run's own step (the review's open item on the hunt's thresholds); watched.
393. *mid-231-k, three hours and no Nether (not fixed).* No death or loop. With no bed, the nights went on the night mine (65 minutes, 342 coal) and pockets (27); gathering wool for a bed took 17 minutes and ended with none carried; food 15. The cast was chosen only in the last hour, its walk to the lava at (117, 11, 141) under way at the end. Nights without a bed cost about a third of any run; a bed earlier is the lever, and Jev was offered it. 3,362 of the run's 4,050 questions were the night mine's next target.
394. *mid-205-m, three hours, Nether at 113 and no fortress (not fixed).* No death. Of its hour in the Nether, fifty-one minutes went on the fortress search's crossings: legs of ninety-odd blocks at y 96 to 104 straight through solid netherrack, two blocks dug a cell, about six seconds a cell, thirteen legs and nothing seen from inside the rock. A search that tunnels sees nothing and moves slowly; the search's legs keep the height they start at rather than seeking the open caverns where a fortress would be seen from afar. A matter for the search's design (legs through open air where there is any, and down toward the fortress heights), noted here for the next look at it.
395. *mid-227-n, "shot by Skeleton" at minute 17, at y 33 (not fixed).* A skeleton and a spider in a cave: Jev went pillar, charge, pillar, eat, seal, retreat, fight, come down, pillar, and then chose the pillar four times running as the skeleton shot it from 14.4 to none, the pillar told "shooters still can hit" with its cost. The record shows the shield up (note 365's key) at four of the last five hits, which landed all the same: facing matters to a shield, and on the pillar the bot faces the nearest mob each pass (note 336), which need not be the one shooting. Watched: if a hit lands through a raised shield again, the pillar's look should go to the shooter.
396. *mid-244-p, "fell from a high place" at minute 122.* Swimming for shore in a pool at y 49 on a hillside (after an earlier fall into it), the shore search took the nearest dry landing within sixty-four blocks, which was eighteen blocks below the water's surface, and the walk to it went off the pool's edge: 14.7 health to none. A shore landing is now within three blocks below the water's surface; one farther down is reached by a drop.
397. *mid-229-j, a loop at minute 86 at a river (not fixed; with the water problems under study).* Mining oak logs on a riverbank at y 58 to 63, the bot went in and out of the water: the climbs out were staircases refused for "lava or water underfoot", the air ran low, "work free" climbed it out and the mine took it back in, and the loop watch called the mine and the climb trading names. The return to its portal 190 blocks off could not be planned in time ("took too long to decide path"). Handed to the study of fights and work in water.
398. *mid-243-l, "tried to swim in lava to escape Ghast" at minute 75, five minutes into its Nether (reached at 70).* On a one-wide span at y 38 over the lava with a ghast shooting, the span's walls were "put up" eleven times in four seconds (three sides each time) and none ever stood: the placings reported as done without the block there, and each report ended the turn before the shield or the step off (notes 362, 385). A blocked fireball's push then threw it into the lava. A span wall now counts only when the block stands after it is placed; with none standing the turn goes on to the shield and the step off. (Whether the placings failed or the fireballs blew the walls down is not in the record.)
399. *mid-231-l, "slain by Zombie" at minute 41, at y -11 (a slip in note 372).* At 2.5 health with a zombie and a skeleton close, the shelter step "sealed" its pocket a hundred times a second: note 372 set the pocket aside after a creeper race, but its check came after the seal's report, so each tick reported the seal and gave up. The general guard (note 381) set it aside twice, five seconds each, and the rest of the turn did not save it. The check now comes before the report.
400. *mid-207-i, three hours and no Nether (not fixed; as notes 341, 374, 386).* The cast frame at the surface at (33, 70, 319), seventy minutes on the way into the Nether without finishing it: fetching lava 36 minutes, the pockets 26, the night mine 16, smelting 12. The same shape as the other cast runs of the day: a frame far above the lava, fed a bucket or few at a time. Jev was offered casting beside the lava and making buckets with each trip's cost said, and kept this frame each time it was asked (three times).
401. *mid-230-m, "blown up by Creeper" at minute 61.* By a deadly edge with a creeper as the thing pushing, the step off the edge walked for two seconds toward the nearest firm ground, which lay by the creeper; the walk stalled a few blocks on and the blast took it from twenty health to none. With a creeper within sixteen blocks the step now goes to firm ground away from it, and the walk is short (two and a half seconds, giving up after most of one without progress) so the turn comes back to the fight.
402. *Jev and time (the user: "Jev doesn't care about time").* Every choice was told that real minutes are what the player counts, and each option said its own minutes, but no question said the run's: mid-207-i was offered casting by the lava three times over seventy minutes on its surface frame and kept the frame each time, told only of the twenty minutes just gone (note 400). Every question about playing the game now carries `runClock`: minutes played toward the goal, when each milestone was reached, what the bot is on now, and where the minutes went, all told and in the last half hour (a survival action by name, work by its rung and step), with a sense of pace said as a fact: a practiced player from a settled start with iron reaches the Nether within the first hour and has the rods and pearls within the next two. Played time is counted from the trail's fifteen-second samples, a restart's gap at most half a minute.
403. *Testing the run clock (note 402) on mid-207-i's own question.* The portal-way question at 61 minutes on the surface frame, asked of Jev again as recorded: the frame five times in five (0.90 against 0.08 for casting beside the lava). Three things were wrong with what it was told. The portal-way question is a work question and work questions were given none of the time facts, the clock included; they are now. The frame said "10 of the ten to cast" with 3 standing; the blocks standing are now counted. Its trips to lava were said as a walk on the level, 66 seconds, to lava 136 blocks down; a lava far below is now said to be so, with each trip down and back up that far. And the way held said its minutes and its blocks but not the two together: it now says the pace, "3 obsidian in 61 minutes (about 20 a block), the 7 still to come would take about 142 minutes more." Asked again with all of it the frame fell to 0.55 against 0.32; given also a minutes figure for casting beside the lava (from the casting time measured here), it was even (0.46 against 0.45). Casting beside the lava does not yet say its minutes from a measure; that is next.
404. *The fortress search's legs, after note 394 (mid-205-m: fifty-one minutes tunnelling at y 96 to 104, nothing seen).* The leg kept the height it started at because the level crossing (nether-travel.js crossToward, surveyed at the feet's height) ran before the staircase and always made a little ground through the netherrack, so the sweep never turned or descended, and the heading was the compass's own. Each heading is now surveyed before a leg begins (surveyLeg: cells of open air, how many over a drop of four or more where a fortress is seen from afar, cells of rock at the six seconds a cell mid-205-m measured, what stops it), and the leg is Jev's (fortress_leg, src/decisions/travel.js): one option a heading, and from more than eight blocks off y 64 a staircase toward the fortress heights (corridors and bridges mostly between y 48 and 75 over the sea at 31), which runs the staircase alone until the bot is within the band. Without Jev the heading with the most open air, the compass's own at a tie. Test: mob-hunt.test.js, the next leg of the fortress search is Jev's.
405. *A held pillar's facing, after note 395 (mid-227-n, hits through a raised shield).* On its pillar the bot looked at the nearest mob each pass; a shield covers only the way the bot faces. The pillar hold now faces a shot on its way first, then the nearest shooter in sight, then the nearest mob (survival.js shieldFacing), and the record says which. For note 382 (mid-202-k's fireball seen eight blocks off, no shield in 1.3 seconds): the guard counted a shot whose velocity had not arrived only within six blocks; it now judges such a shot by where it has moved since the last look (projectile-guard.js incoming). Tests: survival.test.js, a held pillar faces the shooter; a shot whose velocity has not arrived.
406. *The hunt's start conditions, after note 392 (mid-227-m, blazes at 11.9 health).* canBegin refused a fight under fourteen health or hunger, without the kit, alight under ten, or hungry with nothing to eat, and said nothing: a hidden rule. Those are facts now (mob-hunt.js fitness, fitnessSays) on every option of the hunt_target question and in its state, with what the code once required and why it mattered (health comes back only at eighteen hunger; fire in the Nether burns off only by waiting); the footing (dry ground, not a span, air) stays the rule. Left open: with no blaze in view, prepareMobHunt still recovers on the same fitness (cover, food, health) without asking; a fight is only chosen where one is in view, so the judgment Jev makes is the one that mattered here. Test: mob-hunt.test.js, the hunt's health, hunger, food, fire and kit are facts.
407. *A creeper beside a pocket, after note 390 (mid-230-l, a hundred minutes in a pocket).* The door rule (no door within six blocks of a creeper) stays: it is physical. What was missing was any other way out. The pocket's question now offers tunnel_out (survival.js passageOut, tunnelOut): a passage one wide and two high dug through the far wall away from the creeper, level, each cell checked for lava or water behind it and a solid floor, until its end is ten or more blocks from the creeper and at least four cells long; said with the direction, the cells, the time, the clearance at its end, and that it stops, the bot still enclosed, if the creeper comes round toward its head. The pocket is forgotten as one left by a door. Test: survival.test.js, a creeper that keeps every door shut.
408. *Fights in water, after notes 367 and 388 (mid-211-l, mid-211-n: shot swimming a stream).* The stance to get out of the water (reachShore) ran the threat check at each step and threw at the first pillager in sight, so it ended at once every time it was chosen; and its landings had to be twenty blocks from every shooter (safeFromHostiles), which a stream with four pillagers on it never has. Chosen as a stance it now runs without the threat check (the stance is the answer to the threats) and swims first for the bank the shooters cannot see (a ray from each one's eyes to a player standing there), the option saying how far that bank is and whether the nearest bank of all is in their sight. Tests: shore.test.js, out of the water in a fight; survival.test.js, in water with a drowned (the pillager).
409. *Silences in the survival layer, after notes 358, 366 and 391.* Nothing found by reading that would hold the turn for seconds while hurt: the meal has a three-second bound, the dig out of a block runs first in maintainVitals, and the stances report as they run. So the record now says who has the turn: every layer marks it as it takes it (src/turn.js takeTurn: the survival step, a stance and the mobs it was chosen against, a question out to Jev by id, a meal, the dig out of a block, the hunt, the work's step), and every flight frame carries the holder, the phase and how long it has been held (recorder/observer.js turn). The next such stretch names what held it. Test: recorder.test.js, every frame says who has the turn.
410. *mid-218-j, "killed by Witch using magic" at minute 90, back in the Overworld on the way to its portal at night.* A witch four blocks off: Jev chose to fight (6.5 seconds, about 13 health, estimated), then ate, then chose the retreat, which found no way. The survival layer went on to the night's shelter, whose held answer was a shaft pocket, and dug straight down beside the witch for twelve seconds with the shaft open over it; its potions came in (harming through the armour, poison), twenty health to none. The shaft as the night's shelter already waited for a creeper that would reach it and a biter at arm's length; it now waits too for a shooter in sight and in its range (a witch ten blocks), and the encounter goes back to Jev's stance question. Jev's own dig_down, chosen with the shots of the dig counted, is not refused.
411. *mid-244-q, "fell from a high place" at minute 158.* Staircasing down from y 41 toward lava at y -56, the step chosen went two down onto a one-block stone lip at the edge of a ravine, the next cell over open for forty blocks to a mineshaft's rails. A skeleton sixteen blocks off stopped the step mid-drop, the body carried on past the lip, and the survival layer's step back came too late: forty-three blocks, twenty health to none. The staircase checked the landing's floor and not what lay beside it. A step now does not land beside a deadly drop (lava, or a fall costing half the health or more, as the Nether crouch counts it, note 371); the staircase takes another cell, or says the drop is what blocks the way.
412. *mid-230-n, "obliterated by a sonically-charged shriek" at minute 28, in a pocket at y -25.* Sealed in for the night beside its obsidian work, the bot was asked five times over two minutes what next, with a warden seven to eleven blocks off, told only that it was outside (heard, not seen), as a wall keeps a zombie out; it stayed each time. The warden's anger grew and its sonic boom came through the wall three times in eleven seconds, twenty health to none; asked between the second and third, it stayed again (0.74). Nothing it was told said a wall does not stop a warden, and the only other way was the door past it, priced as fighting it. The pocket's choices now say what a warden does (finds a player by vibration and by smell, angrier at each sniff; angry at one it cannot reach, a boom through blocks and armour, about ten a time, within fifteen blocks across and twenty up or down), whether it is within that reach, and the booms taken in the last minute (counted from the server's damage events); and a way away from it: a passage dug through the far wall to seventeen or more blocks across from it (the creeper's passage of note 407, generalized). Asked again as recorded: before any boom, stay 0.45 against the passage 0.40 (it was stay 0.75 against the door); after two booms, the passage six times in six (it was stay six in six).
413. *mid-207-j, "slain by Zombie" at minute 42, at y 17 beside a dungeon (partly fixed).* Fetching lava, the bot fought zombies for a minute six blocks from a zombie spawner it was never told of: each stance question said "a zombie, about 2.5 seconds", and eight zombies came in the minute, three at arm's length at the end. It swung about once a second (near the iron sword's own pace) and killed three, but the spawner made them faster; a bunker chosen at fifteen health was dug with three zombies at 0.6 blocks and never closed, and it ate and fought on to none. Every stance now says a spawner within sixteen blocks, how far, that it keeps making its mob while the bot stays within sixteen blocks, and that beyond them or with it broken no more come; the state carries `spawner`. Asked again as recorded with the sentence, the choices stood (fight at full health against one, 0.84; the bunker at fifteen, 0.77): both fair answers told the truth. Open: the bunker's dig against biters already at arm's length, which is what failed.

No question had ever said sculk was there. It mined a deepslate diamond ore in sight and set about its obsidian at the lava there, digging and placing within a sensor's hearing, and the warden came up eight blocks off within a minute. Now every question about playing the game carries `sculk` when sensors or summoning shriekers are within sixteen blocks: how many and how far, whether the bot is within a sensor's hearing, what it hears (walking, landing, digging, placing, eating, a chest; crouched walking none), that a shriek is a warning and the fourth in about ten minutes calls a warden, and the warnings so far (each shriek's darkness, counted in session.js). The retreat's footings leave out those within a sensor's hearing when any others are left. Open: nothing yet offers to move the work at hand away from sculk, or to do it crouched.
415. *Work by sculk is Jev's (after note 414).* Told of sculk, the bot still had only the work at hand to do beside it. Between work steps in the Overworld, within a sensor's hearing or sixteen blocks of a shrieker that can call a warden, Jev is now asked `sculk_work` once per patch (held five minutes): carry on as now; carry on walking crouched (five minutes of the crouch held on every walk, the note 371 crouch now in the Overworld too, let go when the time is up; digging and placing still heard, said so); or take the work out of the sculk's reach, to the nearest standing place out of every sensor's hearing within thirty-two blocks, with the lava and remembered places within sixteen blocks of the patch passed over for thirty minutes (`goal.quietZones`, filtered in the lava surface search and the landmarks). Asked in mid-230-n's place (four sensors, the nearest three blocks off, a shrieker six): crouched four times in four (0.57), moving away 0.35, carrying on as it was 0.08.
416. *mid-244-s, "shot by Pillager" at minute 25.* On a two-block pillar eight blocks from a pillager, a skeleton and another pillager about, the bot was asked what to do eight times in a minute: each time the fight and the charge were offered as "about 6.2 seconds and 2.9 damage", though the same texts said the ground toward the pillager "stops after 0 blocks". It chose the fight, which ended at once with nothing to swing at, then the charge, which ended at once, then the pillar; twice. Arrows came every three seconds, 19.8 health to none. A charge whose ground carries no step toward the shooter is no longer offered; with only shooters about, none at reach and no step toward the nearest, the fight is priced as the shots taken standing (about fifteen seconds' worth) with no end, and the held pillar says the same. Asked again as recorded: seal six times in six (0.35; the pillar 0.2, the fight 0.13), where it had been the fight three in three.
417. *mid-218-k, "slain by Wolf" at minute 33.* Out for beef among four cows, with a wolf pack near them, the bot was bitten five times in eleven seconds (4 each), twenty health to 1.7 and then none, and was asked only which cow to hunt next: no wolf was ever a threat, so no stance was asked and no fight fought. danger.js said a neutral mob "the bot struck" had turned, but only endermen and piglins were ever counted. Now any mob that hurt the bot is a threat for thirty seconds, and wolves, bees and llamas turn as a pack (as piglins did) when one of them has; the fight estimate knows wolves, bees, llamas, iron golems, pandas and dolphins. Whether a swing at a cow struck a wolf first is not in the record.
418. *mid-227-o, "slain by Wither Skeleton" at minute 94, at its fortress (reached at 75).* Ten blocks over the fortress's bricks, the bot was asked the way in with "threatsInView: none"; six wither skeletons, a blaze and a magma cube were at the bricks, out of sight. It dug straight down, landed ten blocks lower beside the blaze with the skeletons coming, every stance priced at two hundred damage or more and no route out, and was dead in five seconds from twenty. Every way to a fortress now says the mobs within sixteen blocks of its bricks, seen or not (the bot knows them through a wall), and that a way arriving among them arrives in their fight; the state carries `atTheBricks`. Asked again as recorded with it: the staircase six times in six (0.49; the drop 0.27), where it had been the drop five in six.
