549. *The reflexes, asked of Jev (the user, 2026-09-28: "Which reflexes do we have? Can we get rid of them and just ask Jev").* No death behind it: a list of what the code did by rule before Jev was asked. The body's own dangers: in lava, the walk to the nearest cell out (water first), a pillar when that cell was two up, else back toward the last dry footing, else up; alight, the bucket poured, else the water run into, else nothing; in fire, the run out; a head in a block, the step aside, then the dig; out of breath, the swim to air. And the encounter's first moves, all before encounter_stance: on a one-wide span the hold (still, crouched, walls, off away from a creeper), off an edge with a mob close, the swing at arm's length, the shield at every shot, a mob in reach in a sealed pocket fought, and the hunt's step off a deep drop when hurt while it healed. Now the body's dangers are one question, body_way (src/body.js), asked the moment the step meets one, with the ways the code can carry out from here, each with where it goes and its seconds, and how long the body lasts at its rate (lava about eight a second before armour, burning one, a head in a block two, the breath's seconds then two); Jev answers in about 0.2 seconds (note 530), and the old order is the fallback when it has not answered in a second. The ways are the old mechanics (survival.js lavaWays, vitals.js fireWays, headWays, airWays), with an enchanted golden apple offered in lava or alight, and in the Nether the bucket and the pond are not offered and burn_out says nothing else puts it out there. Note 548's gate stands under it: the fire takes the turn from the other claims only while the body can act on it (in flames, or alight with water at hand, and now an enchanted golden apple carried, in any dimension, vitals.js fireToAnswer); and 548's price of the burning (combat-estimate burnLeft) is body_way's too, the seconds of fire left and the health they take, said as all the health the bot has where they are. Burning left to burn out by Jev's choice is held until it could have ended or health falls four more: the survival step does not ask again meanwhile, and the arbiter's fire reflex does not take the turn for it (observeReflexes), where standing in fire still does. The vitals ask with the client they are handed, which every caller now hands them (the survival step, the work's turn, the idle loop, the End fight): before this the survival step called them with none, and its head in a block went to the fallback unasked. The encounter: with Jev reachable and no stance holding, flee asks the stance before anything is done; the span's hold is a stance, hold_on_span, said with its open sides, the blocks for them and what can push; the edge is the fight_from_footing stance and the drop said on every stance; the swing is every stance's own and the question's wait (it swings meanwhile, as before); a mob in reach in a sealed pocket goes to the stance; the hunt's step off a deep drop hands a mob it can see to the survival step's stance. The shield is shield_policy: a shot is in the air a fraction of a second, less than an answer, so what to do about shots is asked for the shooters about, beside the stance and not waited for, with each shooter's shot's flight (rough speeds, not measured) and what a shot does through what is worn; take_shots keeps the shield down (projectile-guard.js deflect) until a shooter not counted comes, health falls four, or a minute. Without Jev every one of these is the code's first as it was. A lastDry kept before the dimension was recorded counts again (the lava's way back had refused it). Replay, five new cases built from the questions as the code asks them now: in lava at 14 with no armour, the cell out 3.2 seconds off and an apple carried, eat_golden_apple 5 of 5 (the old rule walked, about 25 health of lava); alight in the Nether at 6 with twelve seconds of fire left, eat_golden_apple 5 of 5; alight at 7 with a bucket, douse_bucket 5 of 5; a skeleton at twelve at 5 health, shield_at_shots 5 of 5; a zombie on a span over the lava sea, pillar 5 of 5 (two up out of its reach, the drop said with it; hold_on_span offered and not taken). Suite 32 of 33 with the known gap (warden-booming-no-way-away passed on its second run, 3 stay in 5 on its first). Still open: a held stance still swings by rule between its questions, as its text says, and raises the shield as shield_policy stands; the hunt's step off an edge with nothing seen to ask about is still the code's; and none of this has run live yet.
555. *Note 550's open point: the charge that routed to where the mob stood.* In both wither skeleton deaths of note 550 (mid-235-p-nether-4 on 25590 at 01:17, mid-235-p-nether-4-fortress-2 on 25585 at 01:30) the fight's charge (survival.js charge) walked a route to the spot the skeleton started from, GoalNear with nothing to end it but arriving or a stall, for about four seconds with the skeleton 0.9 to 1.8 blocks off, and swung nothing until it ended: three hits, 20 to 15.5 to 11 to 6.6, before the first swing. Now the charge follows the mob where it is (GoalFollow, re-routed as it moves) and ends the moment the sword reaches it (stopWhen canStrike, or the mob gone); the swing (defendNearby) comes next. The same for every close-in that approaches a mob to strike it: the creeper dance's close-in aims at the creeper where it is when the step begins and, at reach and not lit, strikes at once rather than on the next look; the food hunt's walk to an animal (foraging.js) ends at its own swing distance, 2.8, not the follow's two blocks; the End fight's approach to a perched dragon head ends as the sword reaches it, for strike_head to be offered. charge_shooter (closeOnShooter), the step onto a hovering blaze, the night hunt and the mob hunt's approach (mob-hunt.js, stopWhen canStrike, re-routed to the mob each four seconds) already stopped at reach. Re-measured on a synthetic field (test/close-in.test.js: open stone, the bot walking at 4.3 blocks a second, the mob standing or walking in at 2.3 or 2.7 to a block off; no route search time, no server lag): from the charge's start to its first swing, a standing mob at 4, 5.5, 6.5 and 8 blocks is struck at 0.3, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.2 seconds, from 2.9 to 3.3 blocks; one walking in at 2.7, at 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 seconds; in every run within 0.1 seconds of the sword first reaching it. The old charge on the same field swung 0.5 to 0.9 seconds after reach (0.66 to 1.64 seconds in all), from 0.2 to 1.4 blocks, having walked on into the mob; in the trials, with a real route and the mob on its spot, it was four seconds. So note 550's measured closing (1.6 seconds a block past three and a half, 13 seconds from seven to eight) is largely this charge, and a walk is about a quarter second a block: PACE.closePerBlock and leadFor (combat-estimate.js) should be fitted again from the trials' fights once this is live; they are not changed here. The charge's refusals (a creeper, more than two up or down, from an edge, lava beside the mob) are still read where the charge begins; the follow walks with no digging, towering or drop past two, as before. Tests: the charge's first swing within a quarter second of reach at a skeleton walking in from seven, one standing still struck from its reach, and one walking away followed and struck (all three fail on the old charge). npm test and JEV_ARBITER=shadow npm test 1733 of 1733.
551. *Three deaths to a ghast: mid-235-p-nether-4-fortress-2 at 01:27:49 under its fireballs, mid-242-aa-nether-2 "burned to death" at 01:58:04, mid-208-k-nether-3-fortress-1 "tried to swim in lava" at 02:01:18.* The first hid. At 15.3 health (01:26:52) Jev chose out_of_sight from a ghast twenty-five to forty blocks off, told it "has none within the fifteen seconds": that is a walker's way to a line (bunker.js lineRegained), and a ghast flies and drifts at random. Past twenty-four blocks the held stance kept nothing (danger.js stanceMobs counted within twenty-four), so the work had the turn and stood still, twenty-one loop passes a second, while the ghast drifted to new lines and fired at 01:27:04, :07 and :25. A hit inside the hold's slack (its estimate and one blow) asked nothing again; the stance was asked again only when the bot was off its spot (01:27:27.9 at 7.0 health, out_of_sight again at 0.75), and three more fireballs ended it. Its shots were said "2 arrows from the ghast (about 5.2 each)": 9 is Hard's fireball, Normal's is 6, 3.1 through iron, what each cost. Nothing offered sent a fireball back, and no bow was carried. The second chose take_cover (0.78, 01:57:42) behind a cobblestone already in the line of a ghast sixty blocks off; the cobblestone held and the option said the five-block drop into lava beside the bot. But behind it the ghast was out of sight, the stance kept nothing past twenty-four, and the work's cross_toward walked the bot out onto a span in the ghast's line. There the span's hold looked for shooters within forty-eight blocks only, raised no wall with 102 blocks carried, and held still four seconds with the ghast in sight fifty-eight to sixty-two off; its fireball (18 to 12.8) threw the bot five blocks down into the lava, and the burning after it took the rest. The third chose pillar_up (0.65, 02:01:06) from a ledge of the lava sea, told "on top a push is a fall of up to 9 blocks": the pillar's height, not the drop beside its foot. On top at y 64 a ghast came into view at fifty-four to sixty-three, the span's hold held still three seconds at full health by the same forty-eight, and the fireball (20 to 16.4) put the bot thirty-seven blocks down into the lava; the wall came after the hit. Checked in the 26.1.2 jar: a ghast fires only at a target it can see within sixty-four blocks, about a second after it has a line (a shriek at half), then every three seconds while it keeps it (Ghast$GhastShootFireballGoal); its fireball starts four blocks in front of it at 0.1 a tick, gains 0.1 and keeps 0.95 of its motion each tick (about 1.0 seconds over twenty blocks, 1.7 over forty); the fireball damage type scales with difficulty (6 on Normal); a player's strike at a fireball, with anything in hand or none, turns it along the player's look at a block a tick, owned by the player, before any damage (Player.attack, deflectProjectile, ProjectileDeflection.AIM_DEFLECT), and a large fireball owned by a player hits a ghast for 1000; the server takes a strike at an entity whose box is within six blocks of the eyes; an arrow does not return it (AbstractHurtingProjectile.hurtServer takes nothing); its blast has a power of 1, at most 1.3 at a block, each block taking (resistance + 0.3) x 0.3 off, so a block of blast resistance about 4 or more never breaks (cobblestone, stone, deepslate, blackstone, basalt, obsidian) and netherrack, dirt and planks can; an arrow lands for its speed times 2 rounded up, at least 6 to forty blocks and 5 from fifty. Now a held stance keeps a shooter it was chosen against as far as it fires from (a ghast sixty-four, a blaze forty-eight; danger.js stanceReach), so survival keeps the turn behind the cover and in the hiding place. out_of_sight, nook and take_cover are asked again once a shooter they were chosen against lands a hit, said in previousStance. The hiding place says the ghast drifts and when it next has a line cannot be worked out, its fireballs left out of the figures and priced a hit. Every stance with a ghast within sixty-four says when it fires and that it drifts. A new stance, return_fireball: stand in its line, look at it, and strike the fireball when it comes within five blocks, said with the flight each way, that a struck fireball kills the ghast it hits, the price of one missed, and that no trial has yet measured how often it is struck (src/ghast.js); the shield at a shot gives way to it. A ghast in sight twenty to sixty-four blocks off is offered to the bow, with the arrow's flight and the arrows that bring down its ten health. Cover, the rail and rail_and_fight against a ghast are put from a carried block its blast does not break, and the cover and the rail say which carried blocks hold. A shooter's shot is called by its name (fireballs, a potion, wind charges). The ghast's hit is 6. The span's hold looks for shooters within sixty-four, so the walls go up for a ghast at sixty. pillar_up says the fall from its top as the pillar and the drop beside its foot, into lava where that is lava, and names the shooters in view that can push the bot off it. Tests for each; a replay case (ghast-hidden-from-drifts-to-a-line) from the second question at 7 health, its text as the fixes leave it, where Jev still chose out_of_sight five times of five (now asked again at the next fireball that lands); replay suite 29 of 30, the known gap unchanged. Seen and left open: the fight's estimate still prices a ghast out of reach as "2 swings, 9.8 seconds" (combat-estimate.js fightEstimate); how often the strike lands, with the server a tick or two behind, is for a trial to measure; on a span or a pillar top the stance is not asked, so return_fireball is not offered there, only the walls.
556. *mid-208-k-nether-3, "3× The staircase toward (10, 73, -13) is set aside (no safe step toward it from (-15, 35, 14) (no floor 6)); trying another way", and mid-235-p-nether-3-fortress-3, every patrol pass reaching 0 stretches for an hour.* One cause: the staircase steps on ground and digs rock, and both bots stood where the way on was a gap of open air. mid-208-k-nether-3 chose go_back for food at 8.6 health (leave_nether, 01:56:37); the staircase was for the portal back, 37 blocks across and 38 up from the end of its own span over the lava sea at y 34. At the fortress, the patrol's walk to the next stretch, 12 blocks off across a gap of two at the same height, was refused at the edge, and the staircase after it found "no floor 2" and rested; each pass after met the rest, and lastPass said "reached 0" while every fortress_leg question after that chose leg_south. The span over the gap was fortress_approach's (cross_level), asked only from off the fortress's floors. The way to a portal in view is the one to a portal remembered (stairsOrWay): the crossing at this height, then the staircase, and once that rests (by the target's area or from this landing, tunneling.js restingWay) or stalls, portal_way, asked once for each rest from each place, its place now its height too (a pillar up is somewhere else). portal_way offers climb_here: pillar straight up to the portal's height from a column within five blocks with no lava or water in or beside it, said with the rise, the blocks against those carried, how far across the portal is from the top, and the push's fall ("a fall of 41 blocks into lava"); state.portalAbove says the height. On the fortress's floors, a stretch the walk did not reach is Jev's way to choose (fortress_approach toward it, state.stretch saying the walk's failure, the failed walk among what failed, the record kept per stretch): the span over the gap priced by its cells and blocks, a pillar or a drop where one fits, the staircase with its rest said, or leaving; the staircase is no longer run unasked after the walk. Tests: a stretch 13 blocks off across a two-block gap at the same height is asked and the span chosen reaches it (2 blocks laid); the portal back in view with the walk failed and the staircase resting asks portal_way with climb_here ("Pillar straight up 38 blocks ... 26 left after ... 37 blocks across"), once from a place, WaysResting met again; both fail without the fix (the staircase's rest thrown). npm test 1732 of 1732; replay suite 28 of 29 and the known gap. 558. *A tool: busy but going nowhere, caught by us, not by watching.* The watcher (scripts/trials/watch.sh) stops for a death or a loop, and mid-242-aa-nether-1-fortress-1 was neither: for over seventy minutes it walked back and forth at a fortress and dug here and there, 81 patrol passes, no stretch reached, no blaze seen, and only the user watching caught it. `node scripts/trials/progress-audit.js [auto | port ...] [--minutes 15] [--history 60] [--json]` reads the last minutes of each running midgame trial's flight record (the window's files in full, the history's observation lines alone) and the tail of its bot log (placed in time by the stamps inside its lines), and says per trial: the dimension, the last milestone (the bot's own and the midgame verdict's) and how long ago; the run clock's minutes by step or rung in the window; the 4×4 columns stood in and how many are new against the history, walked against net, ground blocks gained and laid; for a fortress the last fortress_leg's fortressInView (passes, minutes there, blazes seen near it, the last pass's stretches reached); the questions asked most with their commonest answer, the none-good share, and the bot log's none-good, [stall] and [still] lines. Each flag says its threshold (under 10% new ground; 150+ walked and under 16 net; 48+ ground blocks dug with under 25% new ground; one step 80%+ of the clocked minutes; no milestone for 45 min; one answer to one question 15+ times and two thirds of its answers; none good in 20%+ of Jev's answers; at a fortress 10+ min with under 25% new ground or a last pass reaching under half its stretches; no frame for 3 min). Its first run on the thirteen live trials (2.5 seconds) flagged mid-242-ac-nether-1 at its fortress 16 min, 0 of 18 columns new, 697 blocks walked for 21 net, 2 of 5 stretches reached, fortress_leg answered 206 times; mid-242-ad-nether-1 answering stay_in_fortress 68 times in six minutes; mid-243-ab pacing 693 blocks within three of one spot on search food; mid-242-ab's portal_method 405 times cast_frame. Test: a fixture fortress trial pacing ground it walked before, digging, asked the same leg twenty times, is flagged on each count with the verdict's words; one covering new ground past a milestone is not.

557. *mid-242-ac-nether-1, "flipping find_fortress" on its fortress's floor, and mid-242-ad-nether-1, "flipping cross_toward <-> find_fortress" below it (the user: "keeps coming back to a fortress wall in the middle of the lava, looking at it, walking away, coming back").* mid-242-ac-nether-1 stood on a floor at (-122.5, 72, 106.5) walled by a lava fall, its fortress set aside eight minutes before (Jev's keep_searching on the way to one stretch set aside the whole fortress), blazes seen near it forty times, no pickaxe. fortress_leg was asked every three seconds for fifteen minutes, leg_east 49 times and leg_north 44 in the last five: each leg made a block or two to the lava's edge, every way on failed (no route, "lava in the way", the staircase resting "no tool for nether bricks"), the leg's tick was tried again a thousand times from the same spot until the stall's loose ends dropped its target, and the next ask chose it again. The hunt was not running because a blaze claims it only in view; the hunt walks back to a sighting four times (rememberedSpot) and after that only the search ran, the forty sightings one field among the fortress's facts. mid-242-ad-nether-1's legs at (-105, 43, 106) were the same shape. Now a leg whose every way fails within eight blocks of where it began ends there and its heading rests from that spot for five minutes (legRests): not offered from there, said in the state (legsResting: how far it got, why), offered again from elsewhere or after; with every way from a spot resting, the step throws and the stall's own question answers it. Each leg says its first sixteen cells in order (rock, a floor, no floor, lava a block down, then what stops it). The blazes lead the question: blazesSeen is the first fact (how many times, where, how lately, how many were in sight and how many heard through the walls, the hunt's walks back and how the last ended), and go_to_blazes is a fortress_leg option: walked on foot (skills.navigate onFoot: no digging, no laying) and, where that finds no way, the way there asked (fortress_approach, state.stretch "where blazes were seen"). The pickaxe carried is a fact. On a fortress's floors a way that is left is left, not the fortress: fortress_approach for a stretch or a place offers other_way instead of keep_searching; and a fortress Jev left over its ways in is offered back (back_to_fortress) from its own floors, where going back walks them rather than asking those ways again. A floor under lava is no floor (fortressFloors). Test: the ac state (a floor ringed by lava at the feet, the fortress set aside from that spot, forty sightings, no pickaxe): blazesSeen leads, back_to_fortress and go_to_blazes are offered, leg_east ends two blocks along and rests (asked once more, not every tick, and not offered), go_to_blazes walks on foot and asks the way with other_way, and the fortress is not set aside again; fails without the change. npm test 1758 of 1758 (shadow arbiter the same); replay suite 34 of 35 and the known gap.
561. *mid-244-ad-nether-2, "was building a bridge and then just stopped, and is now walking back and forth".* At 02:34:01 its leg north ended on its own cobblestone span over the lava sea at (6.5, 73, -74), 61 blocks carried and every leg needing 87 to 96 laid ("the blocks run out at cell 61", as each leg said). Jev chose restock_blocks, told "Mine 64 netherrack ... the nearest 10 blocks off, about 21 seconds ... 288 netherrack, 23 cobblestone" within sixteen. The nearest netherrack was across the drop. Nothing on foot from the span was counted apart, and each restock tick was one acquireStep: a mine step for the nearest netherrack within 48, which walked back along the span toward it, found no dry place to stand and dig from, and went exploring. Three things kept it there. The restock was looked at only within eight blocks of the leg's end, so the tick after a mine step that had carried the bot ten blocks off went to the leg, which walked it back to the span's end: mine netherrack, tunnel, mine netherrack, tunnel, ten seconds each, and no netherrack gained (still 61 carried). It began digging the blocks at y 72 under its own walk (5, 72, -74) and (1, 72, -70). Now the restock offers only what can be dug from ground walked to from where the bot stands (bridging.js spanBlockSources): a walk of up to 32 steps from its cell, up, level or down, no digging, placing or jumping a gap, within 16 blocks. A block counts when a cell of that walk has it within reach of the eye, it has an open face, no lava is beside it, and there is something under it for its drop to land on. A floor with open air under it (a span, its own among them) is never counted. The option is priced with how many to dig (what the longest leg short of blocks needs past those carried, as far as can be had here), the kinds, the nearest and the walk to it, and the seconds (the walk, then a dig and a step a block). It also says what lies within sixteen out of reach and why, and what the last restock gained. Chosen, the restock is gathered in one go (bridging.js gatherSpanBlocks, one block after another through work.js mine with the block chosen, walked to first) until the count is carried, nothing more is to be had here, three blocks in a row give nothing, or twice the time said runs out. A restock held when a threat breaks it off is taken up again wherever the bot stands, before the leg. The leg is then chosen again from the span's end. Tests: at the end of a 21-block cobblestone span, with an outcrop beside it and an island across the drop, 61 carried, the option says "Dig 35 blocks ... from the 53 that can be dug from ground walked to from here (53 netherrack) ... 35 short ... not to be dug ...: 514 netherrack, 17 cobblestone". Chosen, it digs all 35 from the outcrop in one tick, each from where the bot stands, with no walk toward the leg's end, and a held restock ten blocks from the leg's end goes on. The basalt ledge test now digs its basalt from the ledge. Both fail without the fix (the first on the option, the second on the leg taking the tick). npm test 1760 of 1760, and the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Still open: when nothing within 16 can be had on foot, a short span to a face in reach (the blocks carried spent to reach more) is not offered; only return_for_blocks is.
562. *A tool: the trials drawn, so what a person sees at a glance is seen by us too.* The audit (note 558) counts; it cannot show the bot walking back and forth on a bridge, pillared up out of a piglin's reach, or circling a fortress wall, which the user spots in a second of watching. `node scripts/trials/trail-map.js [auto | port ...] [--minutes 15] [--history 60] [--out dir]` writes one PNG a trial (default artifacts/trails/<world>-<time>Z.png): a top-down map of the ground the window's walk covered, read-only from the server's own saved region files (a small NBT and palette reader, no new dependency), cut at the walk's usual feet height, each column the first block below head height (walls bright, the floor plain, ground farther down dimmer and hatched as a drop, lava and water keeping their hue at depth, open air black, chunks not in the files checkered); a side view below it along the walk's long axis, down to the ground under the walk (the lava under a bridge, the grass under a pillar); the path colored by what the run clock says it was on (the step without its rung, or the survival stance), a dot a minute labeled with the minutes before the end (minutes on one spot share one label, "-1,5,13"), start, end and deaths marked, and the mobs known at their last positions, lettered by kind, filled when in sight; and a header of the audit's own measures and flags (progress-audit.js now exports its window reader, trialWindow). A pure-JS PNG writer and a 5×8 bitmap font; thirteen live trials drew in 1.5 to 2.5 seconds. The region files are what the server last saved, so a span or pillar laid in the last minutes may be missing under the path. `--view` (a first-person render) is not built: prismarine-viewer and its headless renderer are not installed and are large native dependencies. The first run showed at a glance what the text needed paragraphs for: mid-243-ab (25598) standing on a pillar stub at y 121, twenty blocks over the treetops, 408 blocks walked within three of one spot on descend pillar and search food; mid-244-ad-nether-2 (25590) going back and forth along a bridge at y 74 over a lava cavern, minutes 7 to 11 on one stretch of it, answering fortress_leg return_for_blocks 28 times; mid-242-aa-fortress-2 (25585) out of a fortress corridor onto a span over a forty-block drop and stopped at its end on errand persist for four minutes. Test: a section's packed indices decode; a region file written by hand reads back lava, air, and unknown for a chunk or region not saved; the PNG inflates back to its pixels; positions take the run clock's label, else the step; a trial with no saved world still draws its walk, mob and death.

559. *Three wither skeleton deaths at fortresses in forty minutes: mid-242-aa (25581, 02:14:17), mid-242-ac-nether-1-fortress-1 (25590, 02:31:28) and mid-208-k-nether-3-fortress-2 (25584, 02:44:30).* mid-242-aa had died to piglins at 01:27 in an iron helmet and chestplate, thirteen blocks from its Nether portal at (-5, 48, 38); it came back through that portal at about 01:55 in no armor with a stone sword, and at 02:14, at 20 health in a tunnel at y 73 beside a fortress floor at 74, three wither skeletons about, chose the pillar at 0.65. The pillar did go up (73 to 75, 02:14:14.0 to 14.8), and its option said three times that a wither skeleton reaches a player two up; it was priced at 16.3 against the fight's 23.8, and it was the fight: the top was one above the floor round the column, the skeleton walked in and struck twice in 0.85 seconds, 20 to 12 to 5 (8 a blow, nothing worn), the first blow moving the bot 0.8 of a block and the second putting it off the top, and the skeleton stepped up onto it. Read from the 26.1.2 jar: a mob's melee range is its own box widened sqrt(2.04) - 0.6 (about 0.83) to the sides and not at all upward (Mob.isWithinMeleeAttackRange, getAttackBoundingBox), so a blow reaches as high as the mob stands (EntityType sized: a wither skeleton 0.7 by 2.4, a zombie or a piglin 1.95, a skeleton 1.99, a hoglin 1.4, an enderman 2.9); a blow knocks a player back 0.4 a tick with a hop (LivingEntity.knockback); and a skeleton kind with a blade chases at 1.2 times its speed (AbstractSkeleton's meleeGoal, MeleeAttackGoal(this, 1.2, false)), 3.9 blocks a second, not 2.7. Three rules had it wrong. The pillar measured "two up" from the bot's floor: a mob on higher ground counted only within five blocks (the ledge rule), so a floor one up seven blocks off was none. Its fight from the top was priced with no approach, where the fight here has its closing (note 550), so the same blade read seven cheaper. And the way back for the drops (corpse-run.js) waited for the kit before it asked: no kit, no question, so the kit's own way back was shut until the kit was made again, and the list of what to fetch was the pockets only, the armor worn never on it. mid-242-ac-nether-1-fortress-1, in iron helmet and chestplate with an iron sword: a wither skeleton came round a fortress corner, unseen at 3.6 blocks; nothing counted it a threat (an unseen biter was one only by a deadly edge), the stance's back_to_wall read "about 0 damage ... none of them reaches it" (the blaze stands were priced with the mobs in sight only), the survival claim lapsed, turn_priority offered the meal and work, Jev answered "none of these" at 0.45, the meal was taken, and the first blow took 6.7. It then ran three times at 6.4 health, told the skeleton would be about 10 blocks behind; at 3.9 a second it was at the bot again each time while the wither ticked, 6.4 to 2.4, and a blow finished it. mid-208-k-nether-3-fortress-2, in iron with golden boots and a shield: the pillar at 0.42 (priced 35.6 against the fight's 66.2 with two skeletons), up two, and held facing a blaze twenty blocks off (the held pillar faces the shooter, note 395) while the skeleton three blocks behind on the floor below struck it, 20 to 15.2, and knocked it off; then eat at 0.29 (priced at 13.1 while it eats, and hit for about 10), back_to_wall, and a fireball at 0.8. Now: the heights are the jar's (combat-estimate BODY_HEIGHT); the pillar reads the ground round its column (survival.js groundBeside, the eight cells from the base to the top) and counts every walker whose ground and height are over the top as reaching it, wherever it stands now, and says so ("The ground beside the pillar's column is 1 up ... two up is one above it ... one there steps up onto the top once the bot is off its middle"); a mob on a ledge within five reaches by its height, not by standing within 1.2 of the top; the walkers that reach are fought from the top as the climbers are, and that fight is priced as the fight here meets it, its closing counted, begun once the blocks are down (stanceCost fight.lead): the first death's pillar reads 23 against the fight's 23.8; where every biter about reaches the top the option opens with it ("Here two up is no cover from any of the mobs that bite ... the fight up there is the fight here, begun once the blocks are down, on a top one block wide") in place of the rule that walkers of a player's height cannot reach two up, and a blow that knocks the bot off a top one block wide is said. A held stance faces a biter at arm's length whose blow reaches where the bot stands before a shot or a shooter (survival.js shieldFacing, the guard's own meleeClose rule); a spider at a pillar's foot still does not turn it from the shooter. The chase is the jar's: a wither skeleton 3.9 a second (combat-estimate CHASE), which note 550's runs measured (8.6 to 9.2 behind, told 12 to 15), and a run says the health the wither leaves when the first chaser is at the bot again. A walker out of sight within five with a way to the bot (walk-reach, which now judges the wither skeleton and reads how far below a tall mob touches from its height) is a threat and keeps the meal off (danger.js unseenClose, vitals.js closeHostile); the blaze stands are priced with the unseen biters that have a way, as every other stance is (note 542). The death records what was worn and in the off hand (recovery.js), the way back lists it, the question is asked in the drops' dimension whatever is worn, the drops' clock runs from when the bot comes near whether it goes or not, and the kit or daylight is only the fallback's rule. Replay case wither-skeleton-pillar-ground-one-up (mid-242-aa's question re-rendered, the ground beside's cell inferred from the skeleton's step onto the top): pillar 5 of 5 with the ground and the knock said and the price at 20.9 (the closing less the building's seconds), pillar 4 and retreat 1 with it at 23, fight 4 and retreat 1 with the opening. Tests: the ground one up beside the column (the zombie seven off reaches, said and priced); a wither skeleton's pillar priced as the fight; the held pillar facing the wither skeleton, not the blaze; the stands priced with an unseen biter; an unseen wither skeleton round a corner a threat and no meal, walled apart neither; the chase at 3.9 and the wither at the next meeting; the worn armor on the way back and the question asked unarmored in the Nether; each fails without its change. npm test and JEV_ARBITER=shadow npm test 1764 of 1764; replay suite 35 of 36 and the known gap. Still open: the fight's closing (PACE.closePerBlock, leadFor) is still the old charge's, not refitted after note 555, and the pillar now shares it; a block in a walker's path (a wall two high between, as block_creeper does for a creeper) is not offered against a wither skeleton; partial iron armor (a chestplate first) is not a rung of its own, only the full set; which way the bot faces while it walks to a stand or eats is unchanged.
560. *The same question, the same answer, and nothing came of it (the progress audit of note 558, and the user's 25590).* The audit's worst: mid-242-ab answered portal_method cast_frame 532 times in fifteen minutes with no milestone in 98; mid-243-ab answered survival_priority 222 times for the same walk to a sheep, 693 blocks walked, never three from where it began; mid-242-aa-nether-1-fortress-1 "asked" body_way forty times with one option, burn_out; mid-244-ab answered night_mine_target ore_0 65 times, a walk toward it every two seconds; mid-244-ad-nether-2 chose the pillar every fifteen seconds for minutes on its own bridge while a sword piglin stood on the slope below; mid-208-k-nether-3-fortress-2 was asked shield_policy five times in eight seconds under a wither skeleton's blows. Each answer returned at once or did nothing, and the step asked again, told nothing of the answer before. The causes, one by one. mid-242-ab: nine of ten cast, a cobblestone stood on top of the last slot (18, 75, 58), the one way in for the lava; no stand could see into the slot, "Nowhere to stand to pour" 3,463 times (the saved world, read). The cast now digs out whatever stands over the slot before it looks for a stand (clear_top), and no stand's anchor is put there. mid-242-aa: burn_out was held only as Jev's choice (note 549), so as the only way it was not held, and every step took it again; the one way is held as a choice is. mid-208-k: the shield policy counted the shooters in sight when chosen, so a blaze coming out from behind cover was "new", and every blow's four health ended it though it was the shield at the shots; now every shooter about is counted, seen or not, a new one is a kind not counted or more of a kind than were about, and the health falling asks again only where the choice was to take the shots. mid-244-ad-nether-2: the bridge ran thirty blocks back, the walk-reach search (note 525) left its twelve-block bounds along it and so said nothing, and every stance priced the piglin at the bot; the search now stops at its bounds and says what it did not reach there as having no way within twelve blocks, any way round being at least so many blocks of walking (17 here), a piglin said with what it holds (a sword hits at arm's length only; a crossbow piglin shoots and is no walker); the fact leads the option to carry on, which names the work, and every other stance says the work waits and how long it has waited for these mobs. mid-243-ab stood on a tower of its own blocks twenty over the canopy and every survival walk found no route (the tower itself is not settled here); mid-244-ab's night mine walked a block or two toward its ore and asked again. mid-244-ae's turn_priority 24 of 24 was the minute's ruling asked again in a shelter at night, survival each time: not a loop. And the general rule, in decide (decisions/index.js, repeats.js). A question with one option is not asked: the one way is taken, said once in the log ("[one way]"), and not recorded as a decision, nor does it take the turn. Every question about the game is remembered by a fingerprint of its facts (its state and options, clocks left out and the numbers in words set aside, so "failed 3,466 times" is the fact "failed 3,467 times" was) and its answer; asked again with the same facts after the same answer, with nothing measurable between (moved over three blocks, what is carried changed, a block dug or placed, the stall watch's progress), the next asking says so in its facts (sameAnswerAgain: "cast frame was chosen 2 times in the last 1 second with these same facts, and nothing measurable came of any of them ...; each came back within a second: Nowhere to stand to pour into the frame slot at (18, 75, 58)", the failure from the work's own record, lastFailure, or a survival walk's). When it came back within five seconds twice running, it is not asked a third time: it is held as failed, said to every question for two minutes after (answersThatCameToNothing, the detour's too), and a stall is raised for the step in hand, which the loop answers as any stall (another way, a detour, the rung left for later). A wait chosen (stillness.js HOLDS: a shelter held, a pillar up top) and an emergency (EMERGENCIES) are said, never held, and so are turn_priority and stillness_detour, the routing and the stall path themselves. Tests: ruined-portal.test.js, a cobblestone over the last slot is dug and the tenth block cast; body.test.js, burn_out as the one way is not asked and is held, and the shield chosen holds through ten health of blows and asks again at a third blaze; decisions.test.js, a one-option question is not asked or recorded, the same answer to the same facts is said at the second asking and held at the third with the stall on the step, and moving on, new facts or a wait start afresh or are only said; survival.test.js, a sword piglin on the slope with no way onto a short bridge (sure) and a long one (a way round of 17 or more) leads the option to carry on, every stance says the crossing waits, and a crossbow piglin is said as no walker. Replay case bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, from the recorded 02:38:19 question: the recorded text chose the pillar 5 of 5; told as now, fight_from_footing 4 of 5 and the pillar once, then 5 of 5 in the suite (expected: carry on or the firm ground; forbidden: the pillar, the hold, the pocket). Jev still does not take the crossing while the piglin stands there, told it has no way within twelve blocks: open. Suite 35 of 36 with the known gap.

557. *mid-242-ac-nether-1, "flipping find_fortress" on its fortress's floor, and mid-242-ad-nether-1, "flipping cross_toward <-> find_fortress" below it (the user: "keeps coming back to a fortress wall in the middle of the lava, looking at it, walking away, coming back").* mid-242-ac-nether-1 stood on a floor at (-122.5, 72, 106.5) walled by a lava fall, its fortress set aside eight minutes before (Jev's keep_searching on the way to one stretch set aside the whole fortress), blazes seen near it forty times, no pickaxe. fortress_leg was asked every three seconds for fifteen minutes, leg_east 49 times and leg_north 44 in the last five: each leg made a block or two to the lava's edge, every way on failed (no route, "lava in the way", the staircase resting "no tool for nether bricks"), the leg's tick was tried again a thousand times from the same spot until the stall's loose ends dropped its target, and the next ask chose it again. The hunt was not running because a blaze claims it only in view; the hunt walks back to a sighting four times (rememberedSpot) and after that only the search ran, the forty sightings one field among the fortress's facts. mid-242-ad-nether-1's legs at (-105, 43, 106) were the same shape. Now a leg whose every way fails within eight blocks of where it began ends there and its heading rests from that spot for five minutes (legRests): not offered from there, said in the state (legsResting: how far it got, why), offered again from elsewhere or after; with every way from a spot resting, the step throws and the stall's own question answers it. Each leg says its first sixteen cells in order (rock, a floor, no floor, lava a block down, then what stops it). The blazes lead the question: blazesSeen is the first fact (how many times, where, how lately, how many were in sight and how many heard through the walls, the hunt's walks back and how the last ended), and go_to_blazes is a fortress_leg option: walked on foot (skills.navigate onFoot: no digging, no laying) and, where that finds no way, the way there asked (fortress_approach, state.stretch "where blazes were seen"). The pickaxe carried is a fact. On a fortress's floors a way that is left is left, not the fortress: fortress_approach for a stretch or a place offers other_way instead of keep_searching; and a fortress Jev left over its ways in is offered back (back_to_fortress) from its own floors, where going back walks them rather than asking those ways again. A floor under lava is no floor (fortressFloors). Test: the ac state (a floor ringed by lava at the feet, the fortress set aside from that spot, forty sightings, no pickaxe): blazesSeen leads, back_to_fortress and go_to_blazes are offered, leg_east ends two blocks along and rests (asked once more, not every tick, and not offered), go_to_blazes walks on foot and asks the way with other_way, and the fortress is not set aside again; fails without the change. npm test 1758 of 1758 (shadow arbiter the same); replay suite 34 of 35 and the known gap. Second, mid-242-aa-fortress-1 (the user: "walking back and forth and randomly digging instead of actually trying to map out the fortress", "where are the blazes", "now it left the fortress"): eleven minutes and ten passes on its fortress's floor at (-122, 66, 104), each pass setting out for five or six "stretches" picked from every nether brick within 128 blocks with two air over it, seen or not; two reached, the rest "No path to the goal!" and, the way asked, staircases dug straight through the walls (phase tunnel); no blaze seen, stay_in_fortress every ten to fifteen seconds, then combat_kit and return_for_kit, and it left. Now the bot keeps a map of the fortress as a player sees it (src/fortress-map.js, goal.fortressSearch.map): a floor is a nether brick, stair or slab with two blocks of air over it (lava is not air), added only when a line from the eyes reaches its top through open air; each keeps when it was walked (within two blocks of where the bot stood) and which of its sides are still unseen. A side is settled by a floor seen there (a step up or down included), a wall at the feet's height, or ground looked at; lava on the floor or the floor's edge over open air stays a way on until the edge is walked, since what lies past it is seen from there. A way on (the frontier) is a seen floor not walked with a side unseen. On its floors the bot walks, on foot (no digging, no laying), to the nearest way on joined to it by seen floors; a walk that fails is passed over five minutes with its why. With none left the choice is Jev's (fortress_leg) with the map said (fortressInView.map: floors seen and walked, how many joined to where it stands, ways on foot, spawners seen and whether floors join them, stairs seen, the nether wart room, chests, ways that failed): stay_in_fortress (walk its corridors again for three minutes, the least lately walked first, offered only when there are some twelve steps off), unwalked_1 to 3 (floors seen that no seen floor joins to here, each with the nearest crossing and what lies between: lava, open air with no floor, wall or rock; walked on foot first, then fortress_approach with other_way), wait_at_spawner (only a spawner seen through open air, never one behind a wall; the walk there on foot, the way asked once where it finds none), go_to_blazes, and the legs. Checked against the saved world (.trial-checkpoints/stages/fortress/mid-242-aa-020157, the region read and walked in simulation with fortress-map.js): the bot's stretch of corridor (x -128 to -98, z 100 to 108, about 120 floors) is cut off from the rest of the fortress (3,458 floors, both spawners) by a lava fall down a stair onto the corridor's floor at x -137 to -129 and by netherrack filling the parallel corridor's mouth at x -113 to -104; with the lava crossed, the spawner at (-108, 77, 155) is 184 steps of corridor away. The map walks the stretch, sees pieces of the corridor on past the lava (over the stair the lava falls down) and the nether wart room, and offers the crossings with what lies between; the old patrol's targets were floors behind those walls. Tests: a corridor walked on foot to its open end and the question asked once with the map (stay, then a patrol back to the least lately walked, then a leg; what was walked kept); a spawner behind a wall not known, and through a window offered as a wait walked on foot; floors across a gap of two offered as unwalked_1 with "2 of open air with no floor", the walk failing and the span chosen reaching them; each fails without the change. npm test 1757 of 1757, shadow arbiter the same; replay suite 34 of 35 and the known gap (one run 33, a live-model case). Still open: crossing lava that lies on a floor (a causeway of blocks laid into it) is no way of its own yet, and in the saved world the stretch reaches the spawners only across that lava fall or through the netherrack. Third, mid-208-k-nether-3-fortress-2 (the user: "saw the blazes, ran around a lot"): two blazes sixteen to twenty-four blocks off, both out of sight, and hunt_target asked four times; Jev chose defer each time (0.82 to 0.84). Each blaze was offered as a JSON record ("action": "Fight this observed isolated mob ...", "fight": {"hitsBot": 2.7, ...}) beside a worded defer. The stands (dig_in_and_fight, fight_at_spawner, back_to_wall) were offered only with a blaze in sight, so the only way to fight was the open one, priced at 13.4 damage to 6.6 health after, with riskNow's fight with both at 30.4. 566. *A mob that cannot get to the bot is no encounter (note 560's open end, mid-244-ad-nether-2 on port 25590).* On its own one-wide bridge, a golden-sword piglin on the slope below with no way onto it, the stance was asked every fifteen seconds for minutes; told as note 560 left it, the recorded question took "step to firm ground and fight there" 4 or 5 of 5 and never carry on. Why, by swapping the old and new text a part at a time (5 asks each): all of it as recorded, fight_from_footing 5 of 5; carry-on's text alone as now, keep_working 5 of 5; the state alone as now, keep_working 5 of 5; the other stances alone as now, keep_working 4 of 5 and the pillar once. Carry-on was priced by the piglin ("nearest 8 blocks"), said the drop's knock, and said nothing of the crossing; the state listed the piglin among the threats and riskNow said "fighting all here: 8.2 damage"; the firm ground said nothing of whether the piglin could get there, "the mobs hitting freely meanwhile" with none that could; and the fight, the pocket and the bow priced it walking up ("at the bot in about 1 seconds", "58.1 damage"), because a walker whose search left the twelve-block bounds (the "any way round, 17 or more" of note 560) was said apart but left in the figures. Now: a walker with no way to the bot, by walk-reach, sure or only round past the bounds, is not a threat while it stays so (danger.js immediateThreat, cannotGetToTheBot; the search kept half a second, noWayIds), unless it hit the bot in the last five seconds; a shooter is never judged (a crossbow piglin is one). So the stance is not asked for it, and the work goes on. Asked for another mob, the stance lists such walkers apart: in the state as cannotGetToTheBot (not among the threats), and left out of every figure, the round ones as the sure ones (walk-reach ids), riskNow too ("low: none of the mobs about has a way to the bot, and none shoots", cannotGetToTheBot, a fight of 0). A walker outside the search's bounds is no longer said to have no way: it was, a zombie fourteen blocks off on open ground told "any way it has goes round, 10 blocks or more". Carry-on is priced by the others' real reach: the nearest that can get to the bot and how soon it is at it at its own speed, or "none of the mobs here can get to the bot, and none of them shoots: nothing here stops the work while that holds"; and it says where the work stands (survival.js workProgress: the target and how far, the stretch's blocks to lay and those carried, and by the stall watch's record whether it was making headway when the mobs stopped it). The firm ground judges the walkers apart again from the ground it steps to (walkersApart's at): "has no way to that ground either: nothing here comes to be fought there", or "is not kept from that ground (a way there, or none the search can rule out): stepping there can put the bot where it can get to it". The bow says one with no way "does not come on meanwhile". Tests: danger.test.js, the sword piglin on the slope below a short bridge (sure) and a long one (round) is no threat, is one once it has hit the bot, as a crossbow piglin, or with a ledge up beside the bridge, and riskNow leaves it out; a zombie fourteen blocks off on open ground is not said round; survival.test.js, carry-on says where the crossing stands and that nothing can get to the bot, not "nearest 8", the state lists the piglin apart with a fight of 0, and the firm ground says whether the piglin can get there, across the valley or on a slope level with the bridge. All fail without the change. npm test 1783 of 1783, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Replay case bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up told as now (the firm ground's reach is not in the record, said as the search's unsure answer): keep_working 5 of 5, now its only expected answer (forbidden: the pillar, the hold, the pocket, the rail, the retreat). Suite 36 of 37 with the known gap. Still open: what can push the bot (danger.js pushersAbout: the span's hold and the Nether pathfinder's edge refusal) still counts a walker with no way within eight blocks; the fight chosen with none that can get to the bot still charges the nearest; none of this has run live.

567. *mid-242-ab (25594), "walked 982 blocks, net 0" for ten minutes in a one-wide water pit at (18, 71, 59), unstuck_move 51 times (26 climb_west), body_way 12 (11 straight_up), no milestone in 136 minutes.* The pit was no trap: every climb out worked (climb_west put the bot on the cobblestone at (16, 72, 59) each time, reach_shore on the grass at (16, 71, 61)), and the work walked it straight back in, every two seconds from 02:45 to 03:09. The portal was lit (note 560's fix cast the last slot at 02:35), and its south face stood over water. The saved world: one water source, (19, 76, 58), on the dirt at the frame's top corner, the water poured on the last slot's lava; running down past the portal's face it filled the one-deep hole before the portal at (17, 70, 59) (dug before 02:16, dry then) and the cells over it, so the doorway cell (17, 72, 59) had water under it and no floor. The saved goal: castWater (19, 76, 58), castWaterError "Water source is outside visible interaction reach", two empty buckets carried. The cast takes its water back at the start of each slot and after each pour; the last scoop failed, and at the next pass the frame was whole, the loop over the slots skipped all ten, and nothing ever came to the scoop again. Then the crossing: enterPortal's walk to the sheet (GoalNear, one block) ended afloat at (17, 72.2, 59.7), its step in was crouched, and a crouched swimmer sinks: to the bottom of the hole, "Could not step into the portal", the staircase thrown to at once and resting ("paced the same few cells"), reach_shore out onto the bank, and the crossing again. The water column itself was never the problem: it reaches the air (water at 70 and 71, air at 72), and swim_up and the climbs out were offered and did what they said; a place into the water and a dig beside were offered too. A bucket on the source was not, and could not have been from the pit (5.3 blocks up and over, past reach), and the water in the pit was running, not a source. Now the cast leaves no water: once the frame is whole its sources are taken back (leaveNoWater, portal-cast.js), each scooped, or where the scoop cannot be made, filled with one of the cast's temporary blocks as a slot's feeder is; tried on three passes, then kept with why (castWaterStanding). An earlier pour's source not taken back is kept under the next (castWaterLeft), not forgotten. A lit cast frame with its water still standing (a restart between the pour and the scoop, or this trial's saved state) has it taken back before the crossing steps in. And the step into a portal from water is a swimmer's climb out, forward and jump, upright (enterPortal): in the water, bobbing above it or in a bubble column. No question changed. Tests: ruined-portal.test.js, a whole frame with the last slot's water recorded takes it back, scooped with a bucket and filled with cobblestone without one, and an earlier source kept under the next is taken back with it; expedition.test.js, afloat before a portal whose floor is a block up, the step in climbs out of the water into the sheet (fails without the change: "Could not step into the portal"). npm test 1783 of 1783, shadow arbiter the same. Not done: the pathfinder's GoalNear still takes a node over water as the sheet's face (the climb now carries it the rest of the way), and the cast's recorded walls (castTemp) still list cells since dug away, (17, 71, 59) and (18, 71, 59) among them.
563. *mid-243-ad, "tried to swim in lava" at 03:00:48 (port 25586, the Nether): off its own span by a ghast's fireball, twenty-two blocks into the lava sea.* The bot stood on its own one-wide netherrack span at (190.5, 54, 118.3), crossing toward a fortress leg with the lava sea at y 31 under it, a ghast thirty-seven to fifty-eight blocks off; it carried three oak planks, five oak logs, sixteen gravel and two crafting tables. At 03:00:20 the turn went to survival (0.69) and the stance to return_fireball (0.61); hold_on_span was offered as "too few blocks carried (3) to wall the 2 open sides (4)", the logs not counted. Between return_fireball's watches the flee step's span branch ran the code's own hold in its place (a stance held skipped the question, and the span branch came next), four turns in twelve seconds, the stall watch's "turning between return fireball and hold on span"; that hold found no wall to put (railSpan also wanted one stack of two a side) and no firm ground within eight, and stood. return_fireball again at 03:00:32 (0.70); take_cover at 03:00:35 (0.48), told none of the blocks carried holds, put the last three planks in the ghast's line. At 03:00:36 the stance was asked again with the ghast out of sight behind them: fight, keep_working and a retreat with no way out; no hold_on_span (with the planks beside it the span was not one-wide at the feet), no rail (0 blocks counted). keep_working (0.56) said "a hit's knockback or a step back over it is into lava", the state a drop of 22 "damage 19" from 20 health (lava breaks a fall; the fall does nothing and the lava is the cost), and the hidden ghast's fireballs were priced at nothing: only shooters in sight were counted, and nothing said that one fireball landing was the fall, or what the fall was. The work walked the bot 0.8 of a block, out from behind the planks; four fortress_leg answers, a portal_way and a stillness_detour came in the next four seconds (none of these on top in three), and at 03:00:42 the ghast had a line and its fireball (20 to 16.6) threw the bot four blocks east and twenty-one down. In the lava each hurt was 4 through the iron to 2.1, twice a second: 16.6 to none in four seconds. body_way offered one way, back_the_way_came, twenty-seven blocks: nothing out of the lava within six (lavaExit), and nothing else was carried that could have saved it (no fire resistance, no enchanted golden apple, no ender pearl; a water bucket, which the Nether boils away; logs, gravel and tables, with no block to place against in the open lava). The death was settled on the span. Now: a drop into lava is priced by the lava, not the fall (terrain.js lavaFate): the nearest ground from where the body comes up, at the lava's surface or a block under it within twelve blocks, at roughly a block a second swimming, and the lava's 4 a half second through the armour worn; none, or more health than the bot has, is death, and the stance's dropWithinThreeBlocks says so (damage "death", its figures, dropFacts), as does the drop's sentence on every stance (dropNote). With a shooter that can push the bot over a drop of half its health or more, one in sight within its reach, or a ghast or a blaze out of it within its reach (it flies, and has a line again at any moment), every stance that leaves the bot open says one shot that lands is that fall, priced by it and not by the shot's own damage ("the bot's death, and everything carried lost with it"), keep_working adding that the hit that would stop the work is the one that throws the bot over; the walled stances (rail_and_fight, the span's hold with its walls) say that walled, a shot that lands costs its damage and a push into the wall (survival.js shotOverEdge). The span's hold walls for such a flyer out of sight too, in the option and in holdOnSpan, and says the walls stay up while it holds. The planks the logs and stems carried make count for the span's walls and the rail, said as made first (about a second), and railSpan makes them (shelter.js plankCraft) and asks only the blocks the open sides need. And on a span a stance Jev chose and that holds is carried out, not the span's hold in its place (flee). Tests (test/span-fall.test.js, each failing on the old code): the lava sea under the span priced as death with no shore, 12.6 health with ground three blocks from where the body comes up; with the ghast out of sight, keep_working and the fight say the fall and death, the hold and the rail do not and say the walled price, the hold walls for it; three planks and five logs wall the span and the rail, and railSpan makes one log's planks and places four; a held take_cover on a span runs, not the code's hold. Replay case span-ghast-hidden-keep-working, the 03:00:36 question with its texts as the fixes give them (the rail offered from the logs): the recorded text chose keep_working 5 of 5; the fall said on the open stances alone left it split among the work, the fight and none of these; with the walled price beside it, rail_and_fight 10 of 10, and 5 of 5 in the suite (expected: the rail; forbidden: the work, the fight). 568. *mid-244-ad-nether-2 (25590), a one-wide span ninety blocks long at y 74 over a netherrack cavern whose floor was walkable fifteen to twenty below, piglins on it, return_for_blocks chosen 28 times; and mid-244-ad-nether-1 (25587), a diagonal cobblestone span at y 63 over a crimson forest walkable at y 32 to 45, then portal_way asked 95 times in ten minutes (47 around_right), none good 57 of 179, no new ground (the trail maps of note 562).* Every way on the Nether offered was a straight level line at the height the bot stood. A leg is its cells ahead at y N (surveyLeg) and its target at that height (fortressLegTarget); the crossing is at the feet's height (surveyCrossing, crossToward, run unasked after a walk fails); and the pathfinder, which the legs, portalLeg and portal_way's legs round all walk by, drops three at most (maxDropDown), digs no netherrack (blocksCantBreak), and in the Nether refuses the cells of a one-wide span while anything that can push is about, so from a span nothing it found went down. Going down to the floor was no option anywhere. The 95 portal_way askings: each around leg came back within a third of a second having moved nothing (sideLeg swallowed the walk's error, portalWay returned as if it went), "chosen from here before" was put on the last pick only, so the other looked fresh, and Jev answered right, left, right, left; with the answer and the facts changing at every asking, note 560's same-answer rule never saw a run of one answer to one set of facts. Now the floor below is a way of its own (nether-travel.js): floorBelow reads the ground under the sixty-four columns out to sixteen each way and, where eight or more show it four or more below the feet, takes its middle height; wayDown finds the way down to it within sixty-four across (a walk, a step up or level, a drop a body takes with its damage under half the health and no lip beside lava or a deadly drop at the landing, as the pathfinder lands, and with a pickaxe a step dug down into natural rock with nothing flowing behind it), the cheapest by seconds and a fall's damage weighed at four seconds a point, on a cached view of the world, capped at 8,000 cells (71 ms in a stubbed worst case); walkFloor follows the ground from the foot of it along a heading or the straight line to a target (a step up one or down three walked, soul sand at under half the pace, magma, rises of two to six climbed, walls dug, drops taken, lava on the floor and open air needing a block against those carried) with the mobs within eight of the ground walked. fortress_leg offers floor_<heading> where eight or more cells of floor lie that way, said with the way down, the floor and its first cells, the mobs, how the last such leg this way ended, and the fortress heights from down there; chosen, the pathfinder goes down the way found (its drops allowed as deep as the way's deepest, the rock of the steps down let dug, the way's own cells walked though an edge is beside them), the leg then goes on at the floor's height; a way down that does not get there ends the leg and that heading's floor rests from there (floor_ keys, kept apart from the level leg's history and rests). 573. *The design review's measures in the audit (notes 558, 562).* `progress-audit.js` (and `--json`, as `review` and `targets`) and the trail map's header now say per trial over the window, each against its target: answers that came back at once to nothing (the same question asked again under 2 s after, no move over 3 blocks, nothing carried changed), per question a 15 min, under 5; askings of a question within 2 min of its hold ([repeat] in the bot log, the asking placed by its decision line's stamp), 0; the clocked minutes on persist, detour (its choices by name, "differently" among them) and shake loose, under 10%; new 4×4 columns a 15 min of Nether time, given 5 min of it (20+, ours: the review set none); the rates are of the minutes asked for, not of a younger trial's; minutes from the Nether to the first fortress seen (the bot's world file's landmark firstAt, else the trial record) and to the first blaze rod (the flight record, read from the Nether on only for a trial that has carried one), 30 and 60 (ours, from the pace told to Jev); and the rung's target (the portal, the fortress, blazes, endermen, else the step's own), its distance at the window's start and end and the best, 8+ closer or reached. First run on the thirteen live trials: fortress_approach answered other_way 1,272 times in 30 min on mid-242-ac-nether-2-fortress-1, 1,266 of them within two minutes of one of its 589 holds (the hold stops nothing: the next asking starts a fresh run); persist and detour 87% of mid-242-aa-fortress-3's clock, 67% of mid-242-ac-nether-2-fortress-1's; unstuck_move back at once to nothing 16 times on mid-243-ad-nether-1; no first rod in any trial, 42 to 398 min after the Nether. Test: a Nether window with eight quick answers, a hold and one asking after it, persist a quarter of the clock, a walk over new ground toward a fortress and a blaze, a fortress seen 35 min and a rod 50 min after the Nether, each measured and flagged or not against its target.
575. *mid-243-ad-nether-1 (25586) and mid-242-ac-nether-1-fortress-3 (25584), each "went up in flames" standing still in fire.* mid-243-ad-nether-1 stood at the west end of a one-wide basalt span at y 33 over the lava sea (its top at y 31), its own oak planks at the end, with four magma cubes two to four blocks about, on rail_and_fight then fight; a fire lit on the planks at 03:53:02 and it stood in it at (31.8, 34, 15.5) from 7.5 to none in seven seconds, never moving a block. mid-242-ac-nether-1-fortress-3 stood in fire by a fortress at (-115.3, 74, 153.6) with four blazes five to eight blocks off, 9.2 to 5.4 in four seconds, and moved two blocks only as it died. Two causes. The first, in both: the work's turn hands the vitals its task with the threat check on (work.js), and maintainVitals checked it before anything else, so "Threat nearby" was thrown before the fire was looked at, twenty-one passes a second (the loop's "spinning" lines); mid-242-ac's way out, two steps, was reported once at 04:03:42.6 and never walked, the move's own check throwing on its first tick, and mid-243-ad's was looked for once. The second, mid-243-ad's: note 548's rule refuses every cell beside a fall that kills on the run out of fire, and on a span over the lava sea every cell is beside one, so no way was found ("steps": null) though the span's cells three east were clear of any flame. Now the body's own dangers in maintainVitals (a head in a block, powder snow, fire, burning, air) are answered under a task only a cancellation stops, as body_way's question already was (vitals.js bodyTask); the threat stops the meal and what comes after, as before. The run out of fire looks for a way along cells beside a fall when none clear of one is found, and walks each step to or from such a cell crouched (sneak, no sprint, each cell stood on; a crouched body does not walk off an edge, which prismarine-physics models as the game does), a step down beside a fall not taken. A mob in a cell is no wall to the route and the keys stay held until the cell is reached. body_way's fire question offers every way there is: out_of_fire (the run clear of any edge), crouch_out_of_fire (the crouched walk, where it is the only way or the quicker, said with the steps beside the drop, what the drop falls into and the seconds at about 1.3 blocks a second), and rise_on_block (a block of anything that holds on the floor, gravel included, put in the fire's cell on a jump, which puts that flame out, the body a block up; said with the flames beside where it stands, those a level down that do not touch it, and a drop beside it), with the golden apple as before. Asked live with the span's scene, rise_on_block 5 of 5 with sixteen gravel carried (mid-243-ad had them), crouch_out_of_fire 5 of 5 (the only way) with none. Tests: vitals.test.js, on mid-243-ad's span as the region file has it the way out runs east along the span and is offered as crouch_out_of_fire then rise_on_block, walked sneaking every step, and without blocks the crouch alone; in fire with the threat check throwing, maintainVitals walks out first and throws for the threat after. Both fail without the change. npm test 1814 of 1814, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 38 of 39 with the known gap. Still open: inFire counts flames beside the block under a body that has risen on it (fireNear reaches a level down), so the question may come once more from the top, offering another block; the fight stance was held by rule between its questions while the body burned, and whether its close-in walks back into flames is not looked at here; none of this has run live.
574. *return_fireball chosen in two deaths and failing both: mid-235-q-nether-3-fortress-3 (25585) at 8.3 health, 03:45:27 and :35, two fireballs landing (8.3 to 4 to none by 03:45:40); mid-242-ab-nether-2 (25585) at 19.3 health (0.59), 03:53:44, two blocks from a drop into lava, the first fireball at 03:53:46 throwing it from y 40 into the lava at y 28, dead in four seconds.* Every return_fireball in the day's logs and flight records (read only): chosen eleven times in seven runs (mid-242-aa-nether-1 at 02:40, mid-242-ad-nether-2 at 02:39, mid-243-ad at 03:00 twice, mid-243-ad-nether-1 at 03:16 and 03:22, mid-242-aa-nether-1-fortress-1 at 03:40, mid-235-q twice, mid-242-ab-nether-2 at 03:52 and 03:53); a strike was sent in four watches (02:40:31, 03:16:56, 03:45:31, 03:45:35, one fireball each); none was seen to go back and no ghast was killed (no ghastGone, no ghast tear); six fireballs landed during the watches (03:45:36.9, 03:45:40.1, 03:53:46.5, 03:22:33.9, 03:22:37.1, 02:40:31.9), and three of the runs died of them, two thrown into lava (mid-242-aa-nether-1 at 02:40:33 from 1.9 health, mid-242-ab-nether-2). Why no strike connected, checked in the 26.1.2 jar and mineflayer 4.39: the strike is its own packet in 26.1 (ServerboundAttackPacket), and mineflayer's bot.attack sends it (attackUsesOwnPacket), so it goes; handleAttack takes it while the struck box is within the attack range of the eyes, which with no attack_range on the item is the entity interaction range (3) and a slack of 3 (Player.isWithinAttackRange, AttackRange.defaultFor): six blocks, as note 551 said; no charge is asked of a plain item (cannotAttackWithItem looks only at a minimum_attack_charge) and the deflection comes before any damage, so a strike every tick is taken every tick; the fireball struck flies along the player's look (AIM_DEFLECT, getLookAngle) and is sent to the clients at once (needsSync). What failed was where the fireball was: the server sends a fireball's place only every ten ticks (EntityType FIREBALL updateInterval 10) and a client flies it between; mineflayer does not, so bot.entities had it where it was up to half a second before (its motion is right, compatibility.js undoing mineflayer's 1/8000ths on the lpVec3). The strike struck a fireball within five blocks as last sent; the server takes a strike in the last three or four ticks before the fireball lands, and an update every ten ticks falls in them at nine distances in fifty from fifteen to sixty-four (worked through the jar's flight), and then a tick late. The look was on the ghast (lookAt every 50 ms with force, sent at the next physics tick), so it was not the look. Now (src/ghast.js): each fireball is flown between its updates as AbstractHurtingProjectile.tick flies it (flyTicks: gain 0.1 along itself, drag 0.95, then the move) from its last place and its motion read from the packet (spawn_entity, entity_velocity; a vector over 4 is taken as the older 1/8000ths), or from two places; the watch looks at the ghast, waits for that look to go out with the physics tick, and strikes on every tick the fireball's box is within six blocks of the eyes now or a tick on; it counts what came of each (came, struck, sent back when the next update goes away from the bot, landed when it is gone within reach and not sent back, the ghast killed) and watches a fireball sent back home for up to three seconds more. The count is kept with the goal (goal.fireballReturns) and on survivalAction. The option says the server's six blocks and three or four ticks, the record before this change and this bot's own since ("Since then it has not been tried"), and is priced by it: the next two fireballs landing but for the share measured sent back (0 of 6: both, 12 on Normal with no armour where it said 6 for one missed); over a drop a shot can push the bot off (survival.js shotOverEdge, note 563), "the first that lands is the push over the drop below: the price is that fall, the bot's death, ... not its 4.8 damage", where it said "Priced with one fireball missed: about 4.8 damage" beside note 563's sentence. Tests (test/ghast.test.js): a server and a mineflayer client as they are for a ghast's fireball (ten-tick updates, the strike taken within six blocks, the look last sent, the client tick between the server's, the world's own clock): at 22, 30, 44 and 60 blocks the fireball is struck while the server takes it, goes back and kills the ghast, counted came 1, struck 1, sent back 1, killed 1 (each fails on the old strike, which never struck in time, and they pass in real time too); a fireball not struck is counted landed; flyTicks against the jar's two ticks. survival.test.js: the record and the price said, and this bot's count since changing both (2 of 8 sent back: 1.5 of 2 landing, 9); span-fall.test.js: on the span over the lava sea with a ghast in sight, return_fireball priced by the fall, death. Replay case ghast-strike-over-lava-drop, the 03:53:44 question with return_fireball's text as this change gives it: the recorded text chose return_fireball 10 of 10, the new take_cover 10 of 10 (the cover from the cobblestone carried), 5 of 5 in the suite (expected: the cover or the pocket; forbidden: return_fireball, the work). npm test 1818 of 1818, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 39 of 40 with the known gap. Open: the strike is not yet measured live; the look is at the ghast's middle as it is, not where it drifts to while the fireball flies back; a busy bot's event loop (2 to 4 s stalls at twenty trials) misses the three or four ticks whatever the timing; whether the other projectiles read from bot.entities (projectile-guard.js, risk.js) are as stale between their updates is not looked at here.
576. *mid-242-ae-nether-1 (25586), "slain by Piglin Brute" at 04:06:32 in a bastion, at 20 health in an iron helmet and chestplate with an iron sword and a shield: dead in two blows a second apart.* The stance was asked five times in twenty-one seconds at 20 health (04:06:09 rail_and_fight 0.77, 04:06:12 fight_from_footing 0.32, 04:06:21 pillar 0.53, 04:06:30 rail_and_fight 0.66, with retreats at 04:05:40 and 04:05:54), eighteen piglins within twenty-four, the brute (golden axe) 6.9 blocks off at the last, two crossbow piglins in sight, a drop of 34 into lava two blocks off. And the retreat said "No way out: none of the 12 spots further from every mob has a route that passes none of them": with eighteen piglins about, footing further from every one and a route passing none is nowhere in a bastion, and a bastion's own floors (polished blackstone bricks and the rest) were not footing at all (ESCAPE_FOOTING); the way off the brute's ground, past its reach with the crossbows' bolts taken on the way, was never offered, and retreat got 0.02. Read from the 26.1.2 jar: a piglin brute has 50 health, 0.35 speed (5.3 a second on the ground, a sprint's 5.6 barely ahead) and a follow range of 12 (PiglinBrute.createAttributes); it goes after the nearest player it sees within that 12 (the player sensor's range is the follow range), or one it is angry at (struck by it; ANGRY_AT, 600 ticks) within 12 seen or not, and drops the target otherwise (StopAttackingIfTargetInvalid); it strikes once a second (MeleeAttack 20 ticks); idle, it walks back to its HOME, the spot it was made at (initMemories), from within a hundred blocks (StrollToPoi), and strolls within five of it; no biome spawns one (none in the biome data): brutes come only with a bastion. So "brutes do not leave their bastion" is not the rule: one follows a player it sees anywhere within 12, and gives up past 12 or out of its sight (unless struck), then goes home. Now: every stance opens with the hardest blow of those that can get to the bot (survival.js blowsSay): "The piglin brute 7 blocks off hits for about 12.2 a blow through the armour worn (13 before it), a blow a second at arm's length: 2 blows end the bot from 20 health, and at its own speed (about 5.3 blocks a second) it can be at arm's length in about 1 second." The rail is priced as every stance is, where something can be fought too: its walling with what gets to the bot hitting, then the fight here begun once the blocks are down (stanceCost fight.lead, as the pillar's, note 559), with expects; the step to firm ground the same, its seconds of stepping then the fight there. Every stance's price brings a biter in at its own chase speed (combat-estimate arrives: blocksPerSecond; a creeper keeps the walk its fuse is reckoned with). A new stance, leave_reach: where no run passes every mob, the scout before the question (scoutRetreat, reachFootings) looks for footing further from each biter that can follow the bot than the range it follows a player to (plus two) and nearer the bot than any of them, by a route passing none of those that bite, the shooters not kept clear of; offered only where one is found, said with the blocks, the seconds at a run, the shooters' damage over them, how each biter follows (the chase, and whether it gives up), and run to the way found (leaveReach). Every chase said (chaseSays) adds, for a piglin brute, how it gives up by the game's rule: within 12 and in its sight (seen or not for 30 seconds once struck), then home to the spot in its bastion it was made at, found nowhere else (combat-estimate GIVES_UP). A bastion's floors are footing (polished blackstone bricks, cracked, polished blackstone, chiseled, gilded blackstone, polished basalt). Probes (5 asks each through decide, not in the suite): the 04:06:30 question as recorded, rail_and_fight 5 of 5; its texts as the fixes give them (the blows first, the rail 103.6 and the step 87.2 with the two crossbows over fifteen seconds, the brute's rule on the retreat), out_of_sight 5 of 5 (55.9 as recorded; the brute a second off, no stance there survives two blows at reach); 04:06:09 (brute 11.2 blocks off) as recorded and as fixed, rail 5 of 5 (63.9 now), and with a leave_reach beside it (a hypothetical way 18 blocks off, 29 from the brute, 3.2 seconds, the bolts over them), leave_reach 5 of 5. Whether such a way stood there is not known: the earlier retreats from 17, 64, -163 found 19 blocks south to footing, so it is likely, not shown. No replay case: with the brute a second off every stance recorded is death, and which way is out is not in the record. Tests (test/brute-reach.test.js, each failing on the old code): a brute 6.9 off is at the bot inside a rail's 2.4 seconds and priced over one blow; on mid-211-s's ledge with a brute seven off every stance opens with the two blows, and the rail and the step to ground carry figures and expects of 20 or more; the scouted way past the brute offered with the 24 blocks from it, the bolts, the chase and the brute's rule, run to the spot, and not offered without one; reachFootings keeps footing past 14 from the brute and nearer the bot, and a bastion's floor counts.
