Open: the fight's closing (PACE.leadBites, 0.18 hits a second, fitted to slower mobs) prices the brute's walk-in at a sixth of a blow a second where it is at reach in one second and strikes once a second, so the fight here (41 with a lone brute) reads below the rail (58) it contains; out_of_sight and the nook still say a biter "still reaches it" where a brute not struck gives up once out of its sight; the brute's anger at a struck bot is not known to the bot (the 30 seconds are said as a condition); leave_reach is searched only when no ordinary way is found, a further 0.3 seconds of route searches at most (standing still); none of this has run live.

578. *mid-242-ac-nether-3 (25591), "slain by Enderman" at 04:10:16 on a span at y 54, 22 blocks over the lava sea, eight seconds after one came within four blocks at full health.* Why it turned: the span was being laid crouched, each step looking at eye height over the next cell (bridging.js creepTo, the cell's middle 1.6 up), which from a crouch's 1.27 is about fourteen degrees up (the recorded pitch 0.25), and an enderman stood still on the span's own line at 41.5, 114.5. Its eyes (2.55 up its 2.9) were in that look: the game's stare test (26.1.2 EnderMan isBeingStaredBy, LivingEntity.isLookingAtMe: the look against the line from the player's eyes to the enderman's closer than 1 - 0.025 / distance, a line of sight, no carved pumpkin) passed from about five blocks, the recorded look 0.015 radians off its eyes at 3.9, where the cone is 0.11. It was not hit first. gaze.js lowered only a level gaze while walking; a look up was left alone as deliberate. It came 2.2 blocks in a quarter second (8.8 a second: an angry enderman goes 0.15 faster than its 0.3, EnderMan SPEED_MODIFIER_ATTACKING) and hit at 04:10:09.7. Did the fight strike: yes, in the 1.8 seconds it held, one swing at 1.02 blocks 1.3 seconds after the answer (the first hit's knock had the bot in the air) and one more as the rail was asked; one more during the rail at 2.93; three in all, about 18 of the enderman's 40 at most. The retreat says the enderman's 8.7 against the bot's 5.6. None of this has run live yet.
571. *Busy but going nowhere, as one cause (a design review's advice, and note 573's audit): every place that offered ways kept its own memory of what had failed, and none saw the others.* On 25592 (mid-242-ac-nether-2-fortress-1) fortress_approach was answered other_way 4,423 times; note 560's hold fired 589 times, and each hold went to the stall's detour, "differently", an eight-block walk that reset every counter, after which the search derived the same failing way again. Note 573's audit: 1,266 of 1,272 other_way answers in thirty minutes came within two minutes of a hold, because the hold was forgotten as it fired (repeats.held drops the run) and the next asking began a new one; 25583 asked again 25 times after holds, 25584 11 times. Measured on the recorded logs before the change: of the 1,580 decisions in 25592's status lines, 1,361 were the same question and answer a third time or more from within four blocks in six minutes (other_way 1,279), with 589 [repeat] holds, 640 [stall] lines and 48 "differently"; over the 30 latest midgame logs, 12,500 of 17,329 (portal_method cast_frame 4,108 in mid-242-ab, encounter_stance fight 1,689 in mid-244-ad-nether-2, survival_priority in mid-243-ab and mid-244-ad). And the memories: approach.failed, the legs' history and rests, the fortress shunned, the ways left, the detour log, goal.lastFailure, lastStruggleStep, the answers that came to nothing, each with its own radius and clock. Now one ledger (src/tried.js, goal.tried): every answer given, asked or taken as the one way, is an entry (question, answer, where it was going when the option says so or else where the bot stood, the work it was for, and its outcome: progressed, blocked with why, waited, pending), settled when its question is asked again, at the loop pass's end when something came of it or the pass failed, or when a question below it escalates. decide reads it for every question about playing the game: an option tried from within four blocks of here (toward the same target from within sixteen, for one that names a target: go_to_blazes, the unwalked floors, fortress_approach's place, portal_way's portal, the Nether crossings) in the last ten minutes and come to nothing is said on the option ("Tried 2 times toward the same place from about here in the last 1 second, and it came to nothing: No path to the goal!"); come to nothing twice, it rests five minutes from the last, left out and said in the state (waysResting). The stance, the body's way out and the shield are recorded and not read back (their own options say their failures, note 521); turn_priority is not recorded. Escalate, never re-ask: every question about playing the game names its parent in define (step, way, plan, rung: fortress_approach under fortress_leg, fortress_leg and portal_way and the stall's question under the new rung_progress; the survival questions under survival_priority; null where none is above, the stall's question taking it as before). With every option resting, or its same answer held by note 560/570's rule, a question is not asked: the answer above that led there is marked come to nothing with this failure, and the parent is asked next with it said (whatFailedBelow); an escalation to a parent not asked since the last one climbs to that parent's own, so a held way or a plan derived without a question cannot keep a child going round. A hold rests the answers held in the ledger for five minutes (the audit's point). The rung's own budget (watchRung): ten working minutes, waits not counted, without more of what the rung is for, a milestone, a new best distance to its target (the blazes seen, the fortress, the portal frame, the step's target) or sixteen blocks of new country, and the rung's question is asked: keep_at_it (what has been tried said from the ledger, the budget starting again), the stall's answers, and the rung set aside for any rung (one the game needs says so). goal.struggles is reset on the rung's new best, not on any movement, and the stall's answers are judged by the rung (a detour's eight blocks are no longer something coming of it). The stall's "differently" is offered only while a way tried for the work rests by place alone, which a step off leaves behind; when every way tried was toward its own target it is not offered and that is said. persist writes the failed step in the ledger, does not put it back in hand unless Jev chose "again" (offered only while the step does not rest from here), and asks up the chain: the question whose answer the step was carrying out, told of the failure; with none, the stall's question with the failure. One mechanism answers a failure: the recovery adviser's moves (gather footing, the surface, another standing spot, another source, down off a pillar) are recover_ options of that question, carried out by the adviser (adopt); recovery_action is no longer asked by the loop, and three failures go to persist, not five after a separate question at three. Measured again by replaying each recorded decision of the logs through decide, at its time and place with its options and a Jev that gives the recorded answer while it is offered (it counts what would not have been asked, not what the bot would then have done): 25592's fortress_approach, 1,348 recorded, before 934 asked and 414 held, after 78 asked, 4 taken as the one way and 1,266 not asked; the whole log 1,155 askings to 285; mid-242-ab 3,597 to 731; mid-244-ad-nether-1 684 to 474; mid-242-aa-nether-1-fortress-1 439 to 360; mid-244-ab 650 to 544; mid-235-q-nether-1-fortress-3 395 to 358. Probed against the live model from the 25592 state as the rung's question now asks it (ten minutes with no new best, what was tried, "differently" not offered): floor_toward 5 of 5 (0.64 to 0.69), set_aside_rung 0.21 to 0.26, keep_at_it 0.04 to 0.06; added to the replay suite as rung-no-best-every-way-spent-25592. Tests (tried.test.js): the way to the blazes whose way there fails at once, ten passes: fortress_approach asked twice, then fortress_leg asked with the failure said on go_to_blazes and in whatFailedBelow, and a leg taken; the same failing question ten times, two askings, the one way left twice, then escalation to fortress_leg, then rung_progress, never asked again; a repeat hold rests its answer at the next asking; a rung busy walking back and forth eight blocks for ten simulated minutes is asked the rung's question with its best said, the struggle count not reset; persist asks the answer it carried out again and does not put the step back, and puts it back only on "again", not offered once it rests; every parent named is a question. decisions.test.js's repeat tests now show the ledger resting first and the escalation after; recovery-adviser.test.js's loop test, the recovery move chosen among the stall question's answers. Each fails without the change. npm test 1819 of 1819, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 39 of 40 with the known gap. Still open: the other memories (legRests, waysLeft, approach.failed, the detour log, portal_way's tried) stay as they were beside the ledger, special cases it now also sees, not yet folded into it; the replay counts askings, not outcomes, and none of this has run live.

572. *The design review of 2026-09-27 (Fable, recommendation D: "Search has no coverage model"), and mid-244-ab-nether-2 (25586, 04:07 to 04:21, "Every leg from here ended at once and rests" seven times, "flipping find_fortress <-> persist").* The search's legs were ninety-six blocks at the feet's height from a compass, and nothing kept what had been seen: a leg into air already looked across was offered on the same terms as one into space never seen, and the outage default was the most open air ahead, the compass's own heading at a tie, which in a simulation walked a leg out and straight back along its own open line and back again, thirty legs, in 45 of 68 starts. Now the search keeps what it has seen of the Nether as a player would (src/nether-coverage.js, goal.fortressSearch.coverage, saved with the goal, per dimension): columns of 4 by 4 blocks, sixteen to a chunk, each chunk a sixteen-bit mask; a column is seen when a line from the eyes reaches into it through open air between y 48 and 79 (never through rock or lava), and stood on when the feet were in it. The lines are sampled, not every block: 192 from where a leg is chosen, turned a little each look so looks from one place fill in between, and six a tick while the search runs (a leg walked in one go is looked along its length), read from the world's state ids; about 0.3 ms a look in the simulation, and 3 to 8 KB saved after two thousand blocks walked. Each leg (and each floor leg) now says the ground within 128 blocks of its line, ahead and on past its end, that is unseen at fortress heights, how much of that lies within 128 of the stretches of its line in open air at this height past its first eight blocks (from inside the rock nothing is seen), "Mostly seen ... so this leg goes mostly over ground already looked over" where four fifths or more is seen, and how many of its 96 blocks the bot has stood on ("it walks again ground already walked and looked at from, and what is unseen that way lies off to its sides and past its end" at half or more); and what seen before lies that way within 256 blocks: where blazes were seen, a spawner seen, the fortress bricks last found, a fortress remembered. seenSoFar in the state says what has been looked over in all and within 96 of here. go_to_blazes says which way the place lies and whether the bot has stood within 32 blocks of it ("the bot has not stood within 32 blocks of it, so whether it can be walked to is not known"). What a player does against a ghast on a span, checked: off the span to ground (none within twenty); a bow (none carried); the shield (checked in the 26.1.2 jar, ServerExplosion.hurtEntities: the blast pushes by (1 - distance / 2) x the share of the body it sees x (1 - explosion knockback resistance) after the hurt, with no look at a raised shield, so a shield takes the fireball's own hit and not its blast's push, as the hold already says); a block in its line (a ghast fires only with a line); a wall on the side the push goes (a push goes away from the shooter). The server's in-fire word counts only until a way out of the fire has moved the body off the cell (vitals.js leftFire, set by the rise and the walk out), and flames a level below the feet are not fire the body is in, as the rise onto a block already said; so one block is put, not four. The work that holds an answer of a question ends it and asks the question when an escalation is owed to it (tried.owed): in the fortress search, the walk of the floors, a leg, a way to a place, a wait by a spawner, a patrol and a restock end, and the leg's question is asked with what failed. An answer cut short by the survival layer or a cancellation is settled "cut", said, and not counted. A saved ledger is moved on by the time the save lay unplayed when a goal is taken up again (tried.resumed, session.js), so a trial begun from a stage's save reads its tries, rests, escalations and the rung's budget by its own clock. 593. *mid-242-ag (25594), "shot by Skeleton" at 05:50:46 on a fresh world, standing at (29.3, 70, 61.3) for thirty-three seconds while a skeleton 4.5 to 7 blocks off shot it every three or four seconds, 20 to 17 to 14.9 to 11.1 to 8.6 to 6.5 to 4.3 to 5.3 to 2.3 to none; turn_priority chose survival six times (0.84 to 0.98), and no stance was asked, nothing moved, swung or raised the shield.* From 05:50:13 the survival layer had the turn and its step returned at once, twenty-one passes a second ("[loop] spinning"), the last action reported still the leave_shelter of 05:49:52 until the two meals its vitals ate. 594. *mid-243-ae (25590, 74 minutes, no milestone, one death) and mid-244-ah (25581, 54 minutes, no milestone): fresh worlds past their first three days, where a player is through a portal within the hour. Each spent more than half its time on one thing the Nether needed, gotten the slow way: a water bucket, then food.* mid-243-ae, minute by minute from its status lines and flight records, began at 04:53 with iron armor, an iron pickaxe, 139 coal and a water bucket. 04:53 to 05:08: upkeep wood_reserve at y 19 (0.45), then the stone pickaxe rung's log, climbed straight up from y 25 to 92 (10 minutes, two restarts in it); the iron pickaxe was made at 05:08:46. 05:09 to 05:17: reach nether. It made buckets and chose cast_at_lava (0.24): stairs down to lava, five lava buckets, and a frame cast on the mountain at (51, 109, -33), 7 of 10 in by 05:17. At 05:17:56 it stood on the mold's top at (51, 113, -34), walking four blocks over to (55, 112, -33), and way_down offered dig_down ("1 block to dig (1 cobblestone), about 1 seconds ... where a walk goes on", 0.40) and ride_water ("the bucket comes back empty and the water stays up here (any water refills it)", 0.54). Its only water bucket went into the ride. No other water was in reach: a copy of the region file holds one water source between x 30 and 110, z -90 and -20, y 95 and 118, the one poured, on the pillar's top, with 170 cells of its runoff below. 05:18 to 05:54 (36 minutes): the cast asked for a water bucket. collectWater found no source with a dry cell to stand on that a quarter-second survey could reach, and explore('water') took over. It asked search_heading about 30 times and swam its own runoff 181 status lines ("water from 18 to 18"). A skeleton (05:27, a pocket at 13.7), two food hunts (05:29, and 05:42 to 05:45 up to 200 blocks east) and a creeper (05:41) came between. portal_method was asked again at 05:51 ("Needs: a water bucket (none carried)", nothing of where water is or how long it had been looked for), cast_frame 0.52. At 05:54:18 a skeleton killed it, and the 3 lava buckets, 28 iron ingots and the kit dropped. 05:54 to 06:01: a shaft pocket at the respawn at night, stay five times: the audit's "wait in shelter". 06:01 to 06:12: from nothing, wood, a stone pickaxe, a stone sword, wool for a bed, the iron pickaxe rung. The clock: 36 of 74 minutes on the water, 15 on a climb for a log, 9 on the lava and the cast, 7 in the pocket after the death. A player does not pour away the water a cast needs to get down four blocks; it digs the one block. mid-244-ah: 04:46 to 04:54, the bed's wool underground (a fight to 3.9 health, a pocket, food), the bed made at 04:54. 04:55 to 05:35 (40 minutes): reach nether, the crossing kit short 40 food points of 40. top_up_food was chosen at 05:01:40 (0.65; cows 114 east, sheep 116 south), at 05:08:49 (0.53; "a cow in view, 10 blocks off", 1 cow 35 southeast, 4 sheep 77 south) and at 05:21:06 (0.58; "22 working minutes have gone to it at this crossing, from 2 to 0"). Each time the option said "The food known (the search does not go to it first)"; the known-food way (top_up_food_near) was offered only with a frame begun. The step, hunt_food_for_nether, was explore('animals'), and no block is named animals: the search had nothing to walk to and walked its legs by heading, x 70 to 618, z -493 to 95, and twice "Could not find reachable animals after 128 exploration steps". The kills were the survival layer's stock hunt (11, in four bursts). It ate each raw, at hunger 15 to 19 from the walking and swimming, while turn_priority gave the turn to the work, "hunt food for nether", 30-odd times (0.89 at 05:13). Food carried stayed 0 to 3 for 35 minutes and was 27 (9 raw beef) at 05:33, with 126 coal and two furnaces carried all along. A player kills the cow ten blocks off and the sheep, and cooks them: that is over forty. 05:35 to 05:39: buckets, a frame at (332, 67, -271), cross_now (0.59), the lava; then skeletons, water, and the drowned at 3.1 health (not looked at here). The rule behind each: the option that spent the time said something untrue or left the route out. The ride said any water refills the bucket where none was in reach, and said nothing of the cast. The food top-up promised a hunt that only walked, counted a cow as 16 points where its kill counts 6, and offered the food in view only once a frame was begun. Now: way_down's ride_water says the water stays on the top, so many blocks over where the ride lands, and only a climb back takes it again. It says the nearest other water source within 48 blocks and where (or that none is in view there, so water must be found first), and what the work in hand needs the bucket for: a portal being cast from lava and water, its frame and how many of 10 are in (waterBucketUse), or a planned step that uses one. The crossing kit offers the known food as its own way (top_up_food_near) with no frame begun too: the nearest by the trip there and back here. Chosen, it walks to a herd, a village, the plot or the chest as before, and hunts an animal in view itself (foraging.hunt; it used to leave that to the survival layer). The open search hunts a grown cow, sheep, rabbit or mooshroom in view within 32 blocks before it walks on, and says so. A kill that fails (behind cover, no way to it) is kept two minutes as the survival layer keeps it (failedPrey) and is not said as food in view meanwhile. Meat on a trip is said as the kill leaves it, raw (healing RAW_MEAT_POINTS: a cow about 6, a sheep 3, a hoglin 9), with what cooking makes of it beside. top_up_cook is offered where raw food is carried with fuel and a furnace (or 8 cobblestone for one): the points as carried and once cooked, and the seconds at a furnace put down here (the code's fallback takes it before the other food ways). The open search it keeps now hunts what it meets. A source on a pillar's top with only its own runoff around it, no dry cell to stand on that the survey reaches, is never scooped, and the search swims the runoff with no bound. portal_method says "a water bucket (none carried)" with nothing of where water is or how long it has been searched for. By 05:51 the cast was asked about a new frame at (76, 109, -55), 0 of 10, the frame with 7 in left behind (not looked into). 577. *No blaze rod taken in any trial: the fortress stage's blaze deaths (mid-208-k-fortress-4 on 25584, 04:08:29, take_cover twice and burned from 10.6 by blazes twenty to twenty-five off; mid-235-p-nether-4-fortress-4, a wither skeleton at 1.8 and blazes eight to twenty-five off; mid-242-ac-nether-3-fortress-1, a blaze 3.6 off never struck from a bunker; mid-242-ab-nether-3-fortress-2; notes 548, 557), taken to the arena.* The arena's server folder was gone: `scripts/trials/arena-start.sh` makes `.test-combat` in the main checkout (the trials' 26.1.2 jar and Java 25, a flat world, port 25574, the console pipe and `logs/arena-console.log`; `ARENA_DIR`/`ARENA_PORT` for a second one), and `arena.js` finds it from any worktree. The bot is no longer opped (only a watcher is). The arena's gamerules had been refused since 26.1 renamed them ("Incorrect argument", `doMobSpawning` and the rest), so drills ran with natural spawns; they are `minecraft:spawn_mobs` and so on now, fire keeps its own ticking (at `fire_spread_radius_around_player 0` no fire ever burns out and the floor stays walled with it), and the new drills have `mob_griefing` on, so a fireball that misses lights the ground as in every trial. New drills, with the trials' kit (iron sword, shield, iron armour, iron pickaxe, cobblestone and netherrack; `FORTRESS_KIT`), no nudge (a blaze that sees the bot keeps off and shoots): `blaze_fortress_spawner` (a seven-wide brick floor along a netherrack cliff over a lava sea, a live blaze spawner at its end, three blazes by it twenty-one to twenty-five off), `blaze_wither_fortress` (the same, a wither skeleton at two blocks, blazes ten and twenty-one off), `blaze_pit_above` (the bot two deep in a pit, three blazes five to eight over it), `blaze_open_eight` (one blaze eight off on open ground). `ARENA_PREFER` answers named options wherever offered (one stand measured at a time), every answer is logged with what was offered, and beats say each mob's height. Measured first (`scripts/blaze-probe.js`, a probe player in iron on the arena server): a blaze glows (metadata 16, bit 0) three seconds, throws three fireballs at about 2.9, 3.2 and 3.5 seconds, stops, and rests five; at five blocks with the shield down, 15.5 damage in 31 seconds, 8 of it the fire (a fireball is 2.5 through iron and five seconds alight at one a second); with the shield timed to the glow, 1 in 36; held up, 0 in 36 facing it, and from three or five blazes spread thirty degrees apart about one fireball in thirty still lands. In the drills the hurts said why the bot died where it stood behind a raised shield: the fire at its feet, lit by its own blocked and missed volleys (in-fire 0.4 a half second and relit every moment), and walks to the blazes and the cage refused outright: `safeFromHostiles` refuses every cell nearer a shooter in sight, so with blazes about every route toward them was "no path" (a scratch run: the same floor walked in 3.7 seconds with no blaze about, no path with one). Now (blaze-stand.js): `shieldVolley`, a reflex, stops and holds the shield facing the middle of the blazes whose volley is due (2.4 seconds into a glow to a second after it ends), held through the whole of it (lowered and raised again it takes a quarter second to block), walking on crouched behind it when the way on is where it faces; `putOutFlames` punches out the fire the body stands in; `closeIn` walks in (onFoot, sprinting, the blazes claimed as the fight's so the walk may near them) to ground within a sword's reach of the nearest blaze over ground with a block to spare from any drop or lava, strikes a biter at arm's length first, then the blaze struck last while it is in reach, picks up rods near between volleys, and is asked again after 45 seconds, a rod, or six health gone; `sortie` steps two blocks out of a hole or off a wall to a blaze just past the sword and back (the bunker's hold, holdBeat); `breakSpawner` walks to the cage behind the shield, breaks it with the pickaxe and then closes in; a hole beside the cage with its mouth toward it (`spawnerHoleSite`); the spawner's cell takes rock at its back where there is no ceiling; the bunker's hold and its rod pickup go between volleys, not waiting for no blaze in sight (at a spawner there always is one). 598. *The audit's measures for the deploy of 2026-09-28T06:45Z: waiting, the stance asked while nothing changes, none-good runs, and before against after (notes 558, 573).* `progress-audit.js` now says per trial over the window, in the text and in `--json` (`review.waits`, `review.stance`, `review.noneGoodStreak`, and their `targets` lines `waitShare`, `stanceRate`, `noneGoodStreak`), each flagged when its target is missed: the clocked minutes spent waiting, as a share (under 20%): hold_bunker (the step), wait_in_shelter (the pocket_next stay and every wait in a shelter), pillar_hold (a pillar top), back_to_wall, wait_for_day(_sealed), and a stay_in_fortress walk (a fortress_leg answer) for its three minutes or until the legs are asked again, the find_fortress minutes inside it; encounter_stance and turn_priority askings a minute over the stretches of a minute or more in which health stayed within 1 and the nearest mob's distance within 2 blocks of the stretch's start (a mob coming or going, or a change of dimension, starts a new stretch; health is in every frame, the mobs only in an event's full frame, so the nearest mob is what the last one said), under 1; and the longest run of none_good answers in a row to one question, other questions between not breaking it (no target: said, not flagged). The run clock is now read from every frame that carries it, joined, not the last frame's half hour alone, so a window or a trial longer than thirty minutes is clocked in full; with no clock the observations' current survival action counts before their step. `--since <iso>` keeps the trials begun after it. `--cohort <iso> [--since <iso>] [--json]` reads every trial record (artifacts/midgame) over its whole span (to a done verdict's end; a verdict not done says only the minutes at its last update, so the last write to its port's flight files before the next trial there ends it) and sums before and after the time: reaskAfterHold (the bot log read forward in chunks, half a gigabyte for mid-243-ab, each line on the side of its newest stamp), quickNothing (and its busiest question a 15 min against the target of 5), stallShare, waitShare, the stance rate, the none-good share and longest run, deaths per trial hour by cause from the servers' own logs (death-index.js's pattern; the day from the archive's name carried past midnight, or latest.log's last change counted back, and a day wrong by one moved into its world's trial), and by the side a trial began on the minutes to the Nether (trials not begun at a checkpoint), Nether to the fortress (not begun at a fortress checkpoint) and to the first rod, and from a fortress checkpoint to the first rod. A trial running across the time counts on both sides by time. 458 trials in 25 seconds. First run, the thirteen live trials at 07:03 (window 15 min): waiting over on mid-242-ab-nether-3-fortress-1 (100%, 13.9 min in a shelter, pocket_next stay 29 of 29), mid-242-af-nether-3 (74%) and mid-242-af-nether-2 (42%); the stance over on mid-208-k-nether-4-fortress-1 at 7.68 a minute (115 askings in 15 unchanged minutes, encounter_stance fight 98 times), and on four more at 1.15 to 1.56; the longest none-good run 8 stillness_detour on mid-243-af-nether-3. `--cohort 2026-09-28T06:45Z` at about 07:12, before (458 trials, 520.8 trial hours, 334.9 clocked in the 355 with a flight record) and after (the 13 running across it, 4.5 hours, the first 27 minutes): reaskAfterHold 1,927 (3.7 an hour) and 72 (16.1 an hour); quickNothing 45.6 and 24.5 a 15 min, the busiest question survival_priority 16.8 and encounter_stance 11.7; stallShare 4.2% and 11.1%; waitShare 9.1% (wait in shelter 1,421 min, pillar hold 227, stay_in_fortress 115, hold_bunker 50, back_to_wall 16) and 15%; the stance while unchanged 0.64 and 1.6 a minute; none good 5.3% and 11.7%, longest runs 1,393 encounter_stance in a row (mid-244-ad-nether-2) and 12 stillness_detour; deaths 0.349 and 0.224 an hour (182 and 1; before, zombie 26, creeper 21, lava 19; after, one lava); to the Nether 75 of 339 (median 56 min), Nether to fortress 30 of 134 (median 12), Nether to first rod 1 of 134, fortress checkpoint to first rod 1 of 57, and none of the four after: no trial has begun since. What the records cannot give: the minutes-to measures after the deploy until trials begin after it; the fortress sighting across trials is the midgame verdict's fortress milestone, not the sighting (the landmark's firstAt lives in the port's world file, which the next trial overwrites); the first rod only from a flight record, since the trial record holds the count and not the time; the flight record runs from 2026-09-27T01:28Z on most ports, so 103 earlier trials have no flight measures (their hours and deaths still count); the nearest mob between events is carried from the last full frame. Tests (progress-audit.test.js): a Nether window with a bunker held, a shelter, a pillar top and a stay_in_fortress walk cut short (9 of 20 min, flagged), the stance asked 18 times in six still minutes (health at 19.5 within 1) and twice after the zombie moved off (1 a minute, flagged), and unstuck_move none_good seven times running between other questions; a mob closing two blocks every 40 s counts no still stretch, a health drop splits two; deaths across midnight, latest.log counted back, a wrong day moved into its trial; a bot log scanned in 64-byte chunks split at the deploy; and the cohort over two trial records either side of a deploy, their deaths from a server log, the first's Nether and fortress minutes, and `--since`. npm test 1942 of 1942.

From (-39, 46, 66) the eye clears the edge, the hoglin's box is 2.3 blocks off, and its top (45.4) is 0.6 under the feet: a mob's blow lands where its box widened sideways, not up, touches the target (26.1.2 Mob.isWithinMeleeAttackRange, note 586), so it cannot strike back; seven swings of the iron sword kill it, and it drops two to four raw porkchops, the food the bot lacked. Now: walk-reach searches for a creeper's reach only for creepers, and with creepers and other walkers together searches each by its own (walk-reach.js). A new stance, strike_from_above (src/strike-below.js, survival.js strikeBelowOption): offered for the nearest walker within six, not a creeper, whose top is at or below the feet of a stand on the bot's own level within two steps from which the swing's own test (canStrike, now with `from`) reaches it; said with the step, the rule, the swings, its way up (walk-reach's: none, round, or one it can walk and then it is the fight), the knockback (a hoglin barely moves), what it drops and where (its floor below, fetched by going down) and that nothing to eat is carried, and the price with every other mob still reaching; run: the step (no towers, digs or drops), crouched, swings while it is below and in reach, failed with why when none could be made. The fight's run swings only when something can be struck; otherwise the charge and the stand as before, each failure now saying why ("nothing was struck: the hoglin 2.98 blocks off is 2 blocks below the feet and out of the sword's reach from where the bot stands (no clear swing at it), and the run at it found no way to it", or "held 8 seconds facing ..."). And the general rule in the stance loop (stanceStep): whether a stance acted is measured from when it was chosen (a swing, a block placed or dug, a step of a block, what is carried changed; stanceMark, stanceActed). A stance that failed without acting, or a striking stance (fight, fight_from_footing, rail_and_fight, strike_from_above) held to its end without acting, is kept with the scene it ended in (the bot's place, health, each mob about); while the scene is the same (the bot within a block, each mob within a block of where it stood and none come, health within a point) it is left out of the question and said in the state (notOfferedNow: "ended here without acting, the last 1 second ago: ...; nothing has changed here since ..., so it would end the same; offered again when something changes"), only while two or more other ways stay on offer: with fewer, leaving it out would be the code's choice taken unasked, and it stays on offer with that said. A meal cut short is not counted (note 475). Asked faster than anything changed, each answer ending at once, is the loop; the question is now asked again with the same way on offer only when something has changed. Tests (test/strike-below.test.js, on the saved ground, test/fixtures/ledge-hoglin-25589.json): the hoglin two below has no way to the bot, and a creeper there still lights; from the ledge's end a block on the sword reaches it (not from where the bot stood) and it cannot reach up; the recorded 06:47:06 question offers strike_from_above with its words, the fight says none of them can get to the bot, and the run steps to (-39, 46, 66) and strikes the hoglin; the 06:27:21 fight whose run finds no way fails at once with its why, is left out at the next asking and said in notOfferedNow, and is offered again once the hoglin walks a block and a half; a minute of askings at the ledge's end chooses the fight once, not eight times, and strike_from_above is on offer. 599. *Busy but not progressing, in the layer note 571's ledger left out (a design review's advice, and note 598's audit at 07:12: reaskAfterHold 16 an hour against 0, the stance asked 1.6 a minute while nothing changed against under 1, 7.7 on mid-208-k-nether-4-fortress-1, and a none-good run of 1,393).* Note 571 built one ledger with rests, escalation to a parent and the rung's ten-minute budget, and exempted the layer where the day's loops live: SAY_ONLY and NEVER_HELD kept encounter_stance, body_way, shield_policy, turn_priority and stillness_detour out of resting and escalation, every wait was recorded as `waited` and never came to nothing, and watchRung counted no minute a wait held (permittedWait), so a pocket (notes 584, 589, 597), a pillar (590) or a stance loop (596) could run half an hour with nothing above it asking. Each hold then grew a ledger of its own (pocket-wait, pillar-wait, the stand's results). Now, in five parts. (1) A wait is a ledger entry with an outcome (tried.js). A wait begun (an answer given while a hold or an emergency holds the turn, as before, and now also any answer that is a wait by what it is: stay, back_to_wall, the dug-in and spawner stands, stay_in_fortress, wait_at_spawner, wait_for_day_sealed, rest_to_heal, pillar, seal, dig_down, hold_on_span, take_cover, out_of_sight, nook) keeps the scene it began in: health, hunger, the bot's place, the nearest mob within sixteen (which, how far, in sight), how many are in sight, the last swing. Settled, a wait of ten seconds or more whose scene did not change (health and hunger within a point, moved under two blocks, the nearest no nearer or farther by four and not come or gone, the same number in sight, no swing) came to nothing: blocked, said as a wait ("Held from about here 2 times in the last 3 minutes, 3 minutes in all, and nothing changed in any of them: health 12.8, nothing within 16 blocks, no swing throughout"), resting and escalating as a way does; one whose world changed is `waited`, with what changed; a wait that failed is blocked with its error. The ledger reads these back on every question, a stance's too (a say-only question reads only its waits, never its failures, which its own options say, note 521). A resting wait is left out only while two or more other ways stay on offer (note 596's rule); with fewer it stays on offer with its rest said; a say-only question is never escalated from it. The three hold records keep their texts: pocket-wait's and pillar-wait's mob records now also feed part 5; the stand results are unchanged, the stand's answer itself being the ledger's wait. (2) The rung's budget runs on the wall clock whoever holds the turn (arbiter.js rungWatch, called at the head of every pass in place of the work's own call): only a wait something is bringing to an end is not counted (stillness.js waitEnds: asleep, with the player, a batch cooking, health coming back on a recover step or rest_to_heal, and the Overworld night in a shelter); a pocket, a pillar's top, a stand or a fight is ten minutes like any other. Due, the rung's question is raised for the work as before and says which layer has had the turn and for how long. (3) None good as escalation (decisions/index.js; repeats.js noneGoodAfter and noneGoodSpent): two answers in a row to one question with none good the top at 0.4 or more, to the same situation from within four blocks, mark the question spent there for five minutes. The situation is the fingerprint of the facts less the record of the answers themselves (failedHereJustNow, notOfferedNow, previousStance, the ledger's and the repeat rule's words, the trail, the clock): on mid-244-ad-nether-2 those were all that changed between 1,708 of its 1,772 sure none-good stance askings. At the second, the question's parent is told through the path a resting way takes (tried.escalate, whatFailedBelow), the answer above that led there is marked blocked, and the stall is raised, not thrown: the best listed is carried out meanwhile. While spent, the question is not asked: the best of the options now offered by that answer's weights is taken, said once ("[spent]"). (4) A hold ends on divergence, not on the clock (src/holds.js). A stance now carries what it was chosen on: its estimate (`expects`), each mob it was chosen against (id, distance, in sight), and the options on offer (those left out by note 596 included). At the end of its estimate's time, a stance with nothing new is held on without a question, 15, 30, then 60 seconds at a time, and every look while it is held on checks what it was chosen on: more damage than priced at its own rate plus one blow, a mob it was chosen against nearer by four, into or out of sight, gone or hurting the bot, a shot on its way, the bot off the spot it held (1.5 blocks, taken at the first holding-on), or a way not on offer when it was chosen (body.js's held way out of the fire, note 595, made general); any of these asks again, said in previousStance.askedAgainFor. At five minutes it is asked again ("held 5 minutes and nothing it was chosen on changed") and the rung's question is due at once (tried.rungDue). The physical triggers are as they were (six health, a newcomer within six, a shooter's line where it hid, a creeper's line, a hit while leaving them be), and within the estimate's own time only they and the estimate apply; keep_working, a meal and a striking stance that has not acted (note 596) are not held on; the reflexes give way to a stance held on for its hold's time (danger.js stanceHeld, stanceMobs). (5) The ways off priced as the hold is (src/held-off.js): every look the stance and the pocket take records each mob about, and one about three minutes or more that in the last three has not come nearer by two, come into sight or hurt the bot (or, from a pocket's or a pillar's own record, never nearer and never seen) is priced at what it has done, nothing, on every option that does not go at it, the hold and each way off alike (stanceCost, the fight's shots while it stands with nothing to swing at, the work's shots, the pocket's leave); a fight that goes at it is priced as that fight; each option says so ("Held off: the piglin 13 blocks off (5 minutes, out of sight; about 8 a hit should it come). It has been about that long without coming nearer, coming into sight or hurting the bot, so it is priced at what it has done, nothing, on every option here that does not go at it, the hold and the ways off alike; a fight that goes at it is priced as that fight."). This replaces note 584's "should they all come at the bot at once" where it applies. Measured by replaying each trial's recorded decisions from the flight record, in time order, through the new code's own functions (holds.diverged and extend, repeats.situation, noneGoodAfter and noneGoodSpent, tried.sceneChanges), the recorded mobs matched by kind and nearest distance; it counts the askings that would no longer happen, not what the bot would then have done. 25589 mid-208-k-nether-4-fortress-1: 1,305 askings to 492, encounter_stance 1,053 to 240 (567 held on, 246 spent by none good); its pillar 05:24 to 05:53 125 to 7, its pillar 06:12 to 06:26 59 to 3, the burst 06:27:20 to 06:29:42 340 to 102, the ledge 06:29:42 to 06:50 188 to 39, and 06:52 to 07:12 (the audit's 7.7 a minute) 87 to 25; four stretches of 21 to 37 minutes with the survival layer asking and no rod, each now asked the rung's question two or three times. 25598 mid-242-af: encounter_stance 111 to 68, its pillar 05:14:51 to 05:26:58 46 to 8, and the rung's question once. 25592 mid-242-ab-nether-3-fortress-1: 111 of its 129 pocket_next askings were two pockets (05:09, 33 minutes, 39 askings; 06:28, 47 minutes, 72); the stay would rest 4.2 and 3.1 minutes in, left out with two or more other ways, after which 91 askings of the stay would not have come, and the rung's question comes at ten minutes in each; encounter_stance 81 to 66. mid-244-ad-nether-2 (25590): 1,925 askings to 245, encounter_stance 1,800 to 120, the none-good runs of 1,392 and 380 each ended at their second. Probed against the live model, 5 runs each: 25598 at 05:19:42, the pillar's first cap, as recorded pillar 5 of 5 (0.61 to 0.71); as now asked (askedAgainFor the cap, the pillar's wait said from the ledger, the piglin 8 off in sight, the hoglin and the four unseen priced at what they had done, the prices re-worked with the code's estimate: the pillar 48.4 to 23.3, the fight's shots 100.5 to 50.3, the work's 101 to 50) pillar 5 of 5 (0.56 to 0.69); at the second cap, 05:24:31, the pillar resting and left out, retreat 4 and fight 1 (retreat 0.20 to 0.30, fight 0.22 to 0.27, none good 0.21 to 0.25), and that recorded retreat says a run fails at once (the recorded texts are from before note 590, with no way down on offer). 25592 at 05:12:13, the pocket as recorded stay 5 of 5 (0.52 to 0.58); with the first stay that came to nothing said on it, stay 5 of 5 (0.50 to 0.54); at 05:13:05, the stay resting and left out, leave 5 of 5. So the facts alone did not move Jev off a quiet hold in either; the rest, the cap and the rung's question are what end it. Not added to the replay suite: the pillar's answer once rested is a way that fails at once, not one to hold Jev to. Tests (test/waits.test.js): two pocket stays with nothing changed rest the stay, left out with three ways on offer, and kept with its rest said with one; the scene's changes; a stance held to nothing twice rests (the pillar left out, no escalation); a hunt's stand held twice with nothing changed rests; the rung's question after ten minutes sealed in a pocket with the survival layer holding the turn every pass; waitEnds; none good sure twice to the same situation (the failures just now changing) asks twice in six and takes the fight, escalates to survival_priority raised and not thrown, a new situation is asked, an unsure none good starts no run; fortress_leg spent escalates to the rung; holds.diverged and extend; held-off's quiet and the prices with and without it; and, as a guard, a resting wait left out only for two open ways, every way resting still escalating. test/pillar-wait.test.js: the recorded hold of note 590 is asked at 15, 315, 330 and 630 seconds (was 45 times), the zombie's blow asks again at 60 seconds, coming down the pillar asks again, and a hoglin gone out of sight and back asks at once each time. test/pocket-wait.test.js: the piglin held off five minutes is priced at nothing on the leave and the stay. Each but the guard fails on the code before the change. npm test 1961 of 1961, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 59 of 61 with the two known gaps. Still open: the way down from a pillar prices walkers at what they did while the bot was out of their reach, which is not what they do once it is within it (each one's hit is said beside it); turn_priority is still asked each minute while a hold stands; a spent stance escalates to survival_priority, which is asked only at night or for food, so there the escalation is said, not asked sooner; the replays do not measure reaskAfterHold, which counts note 560's repeat holds, unchanged here; within a stance's first estimate only the old triggers apply, and sight flickering at an edge can end a hold held on; none of this has run live.

The gravel fell at once. climb_east was offered 0.8 seconds later onto the gravel read before it went (0.57), the body jumped into the empty cell and fell, the next question was again asked mid-fall at y 39.7, and the body was in the lava at 32.4. mid-243-af-fortress-2 (25600, 11:55:21): the stall's blind step (skills.js shakeLoose, stage 1) stepped a block south onto a ledge thirty-eight blocks over the sea and, released once it had moved a block, ran on off it (mine_nearby was answered mid-fall). mid-242-ae-nether-2-fortress-3 (25600, 11:58:02) and mid-243-ag-fortress-2 (25592, 12:06:07), the same both times: the mine's and the restock's crouched walk to a drop stopped with the body's middle over the sea, held up by the edge of the block beside by a hundredth of a block, and when the walk let the crouch go, what was left of its speed took it off (x -102.713 to -102.700, straight down 25 blocks; x -144.71 to -144.70, 24 blocks). Not the tunnel and not lava flowing in: in neither was a block dug under or beside the body. Now, one check for every dig and one for every upright step. terrain.js fallFrom reads a fall to its end, at any depth, and a landing where the body stands in lava is lava (note 580). terrain.js digExposes is the dig's: a block the body stands on or beside (its columns and the ring round them, from the floor to over the head) is not dug with lava in any of its six neighbors, source or flowing (lava beside or over it flows in, lava under it opens a hole onto the lava beside the feet); the floor under the body is not dug out, nothing else holding the body, where the fall under it ends in lava; and no block is dug beside the lowest of a column of gravel or sand the body stands on where it drops into lava or for the body's health (note 592). It is checked on bot.dig itself (skills.js digGuardPlugin, loaded with the other plugins in session.js), so every dig, the mine's, the restock's, the tunnel's, the bunker's, the bridge's, the unstuck move's and the pathfinder's own, meets it and is refused with why ("Not dug: the netherrack at (-104, 37, 104): the floor under the body at (-104, 37, 104) dug out, it falls 6 blocks into lava"). The step's is motion.js move, the one way the bot holds keys: an upright move reads the whole fall ahead into lava, not four blocks (burningAhead deep), and refuses it; a crouched move keeps the four-block look (the edge holds the body, so a span over the sea is still walked crouched to its end), and does not end with the body's middle over a fall into lava: it walks back onto the block it hangs from, still crouched, before the crouch lets go (backOnFooting). motion.within keeps a move to its own cells, stopped where the body's middle leaves them. The blind step goes through move (it held its keys by hand), keeps to its two cells, and is not taken toward a ledge where a step that runs on past it falls into lava. The unstuck moves (unstuck.js): read once the body has landed (landed, up to two seconds); a move read from another cell is not run; no move ends with the body in lava (standsInLava), no dig down whose fall ends in lava, no dig that digExposes refuses, no move that drops the floor stood on (floorDrops), no move onto gravel or sand resting on nothing over lava, and no gravel or sand put where nothing under it holds it (another carried block is used there if there is one); each said in here.notOffered. A drop past a step that ends in lava is said as that, with what one touch costs this body (lavaTouchSays); a level step with lava past it is crouched; the run keeps to the step's two cells. The recovery adviser's relocations are not offered onto footing where the body stands in lava. Which move the five none_good answers on 25592 missed is not settled here: the bot carried no pickaxe, so no netherrack was offered to dig, and its moves were a block at a time on its own span; a way back along the span to ground it had stood on, several cells long, is the likeliest, and nothing offers a walk of more than one cell. The rung's question. At 11:37:26 on 25583 it was not the ten-minute budget. The stage save mid-242-af-053454 held the rung's budget at 22 seconds of idle; note 583's shift by the gap was applied; note 599's none-good escalation fired nowhere in either log. From 11:33:56, 58 seconds into the trial, to 11:37:26 the rung's question was asked 22 times, every one an escalation: the legs, restock_blocks and return_for_blocks each came back at once (0 blocks carried, the portal unreachable), note 570's streak held them, fortress_leg's every way rested five minutes, and each pass asked fortress_leg again, escalated, and asked the rung's question again, the rung's own answers, each met at once by the same escalation, coming back at once in their turn (keep_at_it "10 times, 10 coming to nothing" by 11:34:43), until setting the rods aside was the answer taken. Its first asking told Jev "worked on this rung in 31 minutes on it: 48 answers given": thirty of those minutes and all but a few of the answers were from before the save (the rung's `since`, moved by the gap, counted from 05:04). The rods were set aside 8 times in those 3.5 minutes and taken back 6 times, each within a second: twice by the stall's take_up_obtain_blaze_rods ("set aside 1 minutes ago", the minutes floored up to one) and four times by leave_nether's search_on, the rods' own question, which offered them straight back. After 11:35:09 the rods waited (rods_waiting) and the rung in hand by its clock was still the rods: the stall's escalations brought the rung's question for a rung already set aside ("keep at the none"), and at 11:37:26 it set them aside again, restarting their half hour. mid-242-af-nether-2-fortress-1 (25584) was the same: fortress_leg's quick streak held at 11:35:45, the rung's question 11 times in the next 75 seconds, the rods set aside and taken back by search_on four times, each within three seconds, then brought to the rung's question and set aside again at 11:40:00 and 11:42:33 while they waited (the watcher's loop of "The blaze rods step waits"). Now: a save that lay unplayed longer than the rung's own budget is a new session on the rung (tried.resumed): its budget and its count start at the resume, and the minutes before the save are said beside them ("in 0.9 minutes on it in this session (and 30 minutes before the save it was taken up from)"). A rung set aside is not the rung in hand while it rests (tried.rungOf): its budget does not run, its question is not asked (the stall's is), and set_aside_rung is not offered for it. An escalation for every way resting says when the first comes off rest (escalateFrom's until, from tried.read); the rung's question then offers until_rest_ends, other work until then with the rung kept in hand and not set aside, and keeping at it says that from here the next pass meets the same rests and the question comes again. Setting a rung aside keeps what it was for, from where and until when (goal.rungAside: the rests below, or five minutes); while that stands from within four blocks of there, taking it up again is not offered, neither the stall's take_up nor leave_nether's search_on, and is said why (takeUpNotOffered, searchOnNotOffered); offered, take_up says how long ago in seconds or minutes, from where and for what. Now: close_in is priced by the sum of the fight at hand (blaze-stand.js closeInCost, closeInSays), the game's numbers blaze by blaze: each that sees the bot throws three about every nine seconds, each landing by its distance (fireballHit), a blaze within two swinging once a second instead; a landing is its hit through the armour worn and five seconds alight, the chance of being alight 1 - e^(-5λ); the shield faced at their middle covers those within sixty degrees of it at the probe's one in thirty, the rest land as if it were down; the walk goes only in the lulls, (1 - 2.2/8.9)^k of the time with k in sight; each blaze in reach takes the sword's swings at the fights' pace (four at 0.9) with the shield down while the rest shoot; the fire on the body burns on; a live spawner within sixteen puts in about one every six seconds up to six. The option says each part and what it comes to, and when the health runs out if it does ("the health runs out at about 9.9 seconds in, after about 1 of them killed" for mid-243-ag at 11:45:02; "about 1.9 seconds in, after about 0" for the eight at 11:58:35; one blaze at eight in the open, about 2.7 over 5.1 seconds and the blaze killed), its expects is that sum, and the arena's rows follow it, each said with its own fight. break_spawner is priced the same way, the walk to the cage and the digging first and no newcomers after (taken twice to death in the drill once close_in said its sum, on its own row's 34.1). dig_in_at_spawner is priced by its own cost, not the row. (3) The way back (25589, 25592). leave_nether's go_back (11:39:13; 12:25:33) led to the staircase toward the portal 329 blocks off, which paced three cells ((-230, 53, -226) to (-231, 53, -225); (-145, 60, 337) to (-145, 60, 339)), began a new round where it paced ("not gaining on it; starting round 2"), tried the crossing between rounds (0 blocks carried) and paced again: "turning between tunnel and cross toward". Then portal_way (none good 0.36), the rest held with no detours, and working free, where place_north put a gravel at the feet north and dig_north_feet dug it out, six times each at 11:43:40 to 11:43:50, every answer "a block was dug or placed" and so getting somewhere in the ledger (the archived goal's entries), so neither rested. (4) 25584 at 12:04:35: the legs each ended at once and their crossings with them, struck as survival:keep_working, the stance answered three seconds before (actionOf's recent survival action), and that stance set aside; at 12:07:08 rung_progress set the rods aside, leave_nether's search_on took them up again a second later, the fortress legs every way resting escalated to the rung, round again four times in a second, and search_on was offered each time as untried. (5) mid-244-bd's staircase to its frame (11:54:04 to 11:54:19, 12:13:34 to 12:15:05) dug a new step every few seconds under the ladder's enter_nether and was raised three times as "turning between enter nether and tunnel"; the answers ("differently") dropped the shaft. Now, in general. A stand the cast made for a slot is remembered on the frame (standsMade) and walked to, the whole walk with the tower allowed, not a half-second survey; not reached, the cast throws "Nowhere to stand to pour into the frame slot at (x, y, z): the stand made for it at (...) could not be walked to from (...) (why)", a site failure (with obsidian cast, portal_method is asked with it said), and no second stand is made for that slot; gone, the record is dropped and that is thrown. The planner prices one more of an ingredient whose carried stack is already spoken for at its cost without that stack (estimateWithout), so the Nether's second plank is crimson; the one oak log is still used. An errand set aside waits its rest like any rung (errandStage reads the set-aside). A block dug or placed counts as something done (stillness.js marked, repeats.js cameOf, the ledger) only in a cell not dug or placed in the last ten minutes, the stall watch's own rule, so a gravel put down and dug back is nothing done. Two steps trading the turn: a step and its own retry (persist) are one step; a block dug or placed in a new cell is getting somewhere, as the stall watch counts it; the work's flip is keyed to the work, not a stance a few seconds old; and the flip is the work's failure in the ledger, the step's entry written blocked and the answer the work was carrying out (tried.owner) marked come to nothing with the flip said and owed to its question (tried.escalate), so it rests at the second, while the stall's question is raised as before. 605. *mid-242-aa-nether-1-fortress-4 (25590), begun 12:31:57 from the fortress save mid-242-aa-nether-1-014452 with main at 0ae699f (note 600 live, 603 not): the rods set aside at the rung's question 3.2 minutes in, and within sixteen minutes the watcher's "loop: 3x The blaze rods step waits (Jev set it aside at the rung's question, worked on in 3.2 minutes on it: 17 answers given, 1 ...", with unstuck_move asked 41 times.* Read from the log, the flight records, the save's goal and the archived one. How the rung's question came at 3.2 minutes: by escalation, not by its ten minutes, and not by working free (all 41 unstuck_move askings came after, from 12:36:52). The repeat rule held keep_searching, tunnel came to nothing twice, and cross_level was the one way; at about 12:35:04.5 fortress_approach's every way rested and it escalated to fortress_leg. fortress_leg was then owed, and the fortress search's hook for that (note 583) dropped the search's target and its rememberedTarget mark. The step then threw WaysResting, "The blaze rods step waits (...). Jev chose other work in the Nether until then." (game-progress.js). persist wrote it as the step failing and asked the stall's question, which offered until_rest_ends, the same answer again (0.48). That answer's hold was keyed step:rods_waiting. But gameStep's timeRung put obtain_blaze_rods back in goal.rungTime at every pass, and stillness.actionOf keyed the work by that phase with no look at the set-aside. So the stall watch struck "45 seconds on rung:obtain blaze rods" (strikes 2, 3 and 4 at 12:36:52, 12:37:47 and 12:38:33), a key the hold did not cover, and each stall's question offered work_free and "keep at the obtain blaze rods another way". Then the ladder ran rods_waiting again and threw again: 22 times in the flight, from 12:35:13.9 to 12:47:29.6. Note 600's rungOf had taken the set-aside rung out of the rung's budget and question only; the ladder, the stall key and the stall's question's rung still named it. Would note 603 have prevented it: no. Each test below fails on fa65438 (603 live). 603's set-aside read is errandStage's, and the rods are not an errand. Its flip rule charges a flip to tried.owner and escalates it, which adds escalations owed to the same question, so the pass-over comes no later. Now, in general. (1) The fortress search: with the leg's question owed, the fortress remembered is not taken as the target unasked (mob-hunt.js findFortressStep). The leg's question is asked with what failed, and the fortress remembered is said on the legs that lie its way (sightingsThatWay, as before). (2) The work's own questions (those under the rung's question and not the stall's: tried.workBelowRung) are not waits because of the survival layer's action of a few seconds before, since the work asks them only while it holds the turn. What an answer is (WAIT_ANSWERS) and a hold step still make a wait, and the stance's answers are waits as before. (3) The rung's question says how little (tried.workedOn): the answers given to how many different ways of those its questions offered, the waits, and, when a failure below brought it, how far into its ten minutes ("in 3.2 minutes on it: 9 answers given to 5 different ways of the 16 its questions offered, ...; brought to this question by a failure below 3.2 minutes into the rung's ten, not by its ten minutes running out"). (4) Escalate, never re-ask, at the top: brought to its question by a failure below while a question of its own work below still has ways not yet tried from here (workedOn.openBelow: fortress_leg's legs, floors, heights and blocks, fortress_approach's ways in), the rung is not set aside. That is said in setAsideNotOffered and the situation, and keep_at_it sends the work back to that question, owed (tried.sendBack), which the fortress search asks with its ways. Its ten minutes running out still offers it, as does a rung question reached once the ways below are spent. (5) The rods waiting: Jev's wait_here, asked now or held for this rest, is the waiting stage's own work (leaveNetherStep calls the game's hold_for_rest, work.js holdForRest, keyed step:rods_waiting), not the rods step thrown as a failure at each pass. It is not persist's and it is not asked again as until_rest_ends. A caller with no hold gets the old throw. 609. *Two trials sat idle on main at 4f147ba (notes 571 to 604, after quiet restarts): mid-242-ah-nether-1-fortress-1 (25586), "obtain blaze rods: detour" 17 of the last 19 minutes before 13:12Z, 13 blocks walked, net 0, nothing dug or laid, turn_priority asked 9 times; mid-243-af-nether-3-fortress-2 (25587), "errand: detour" 16 of 21 minutes, 0 walked, "between steps" before that.* Neither was playing the game. What spun first: on 25587 (about 12:22:42) the errand was set aside (the oak log in the Nether, note 603), the stall's question (stillness_detour) had every way resting from here (differently, work free, until rest ends, hoglin food, each tried twice and come to nothing), and escalated to the rung's question, which answerStall does not ask for a rung set aside (note 600); the next pass took that stall, asked the stall's question again with the same ways resting, and escalated again, 24 times in about a second, enough to trip the spin line. On 25586 (about 12:29:37) the return-for-food step failed "No loaded return portal observed in the Nether" and was sent to leave_nether 21 times in a second without it being asked (persist's escalation to a question the stage does not ask; left to note 607's work). Then the idle loop: a stall on the idle work (the torch, then the detour itself, "step:detour:until_rest_ends") answered with the stall's question, every way resting, escalated to rung_progress, which is never asked between requests (answerStall's idle), and the idle loop went straight round with no pause after a stall's answer or a caught Stalled: 52,132 "[escalate] stillness detour -> rung progress" lines on 25586, 110,608 on 25587, none asked. Between the spins, until_rest_ends taken as the one way held the rest with nothing on offer, "[still] holding step:torch until its rest ends; detours: none" every five seconds (55 and 91 times), the step saying only "detour", until the stall watch raised the hold itself as a stall 45 seconds in; hoglin_food was run as the one way (Jev, asked once at 13:02:15, answered none good at 0.88) and its walk found no route. Now, in general. The spin line cannot throw (work.js spinGuard, shown), and the idle loop is paced by the same guard. The stall's question escalates to the rung's only where the rung's is asked (stallAbove): between requests, or with the rung in hand set aside, nothing above it is asked, and with every way resting the question is asked itself, each option with its rest said on it (tried.read, for any question with nothing above) and why nothing above is asked in its state (nothingAbove: "The errand is set aside, and a rung set aside is not brought to its own question while it waits: nothing above this question is asked; every way here stays on offer with its rest said."); decide takes the question above from its caller where the caller knows it is not asked (`above`), for the resting ways and for none good alike. A hold for a rest with nothing on offer says what it waits for, once, and keeps it on the step (restWaitSays: "[wait] waiting for the torch's rest to end, 240 seconds more (at 13:06:27Z), set for: ...; nothing else is on offer from here meanwhile", goal.step.waitingFor); it is still counted by the rung's wall-clock budget (note 599), which is what escalates it in a game. Not the crouch route and not a crouch let go: none was pressed. mid-243-ag-nether-2 held the fight on its span of dirt, diorite and basalt at y 36 over the lava sea (fight 0.45, none_good 0.29; the push claim of note 586 did fire, "Preempted by push", and every stance said the fireball was the fall); the first fireball at 14:18:15 threw it 4.2 blocks along the span to its south lip, and the stance was held, not asked again; the second at 14:18:18 threw it off the south side. It carried one plank and sixteen gravel, told "too few blocks carried (1) to wall the 2 open sides (4)". mid-242-ba-fortress-4, reported as the fight's charge stepping into the lava with no hit first: the frames have a ghast fireball at 14:25:55.749 (16.8 to 12.0), only the shield key held, x held at -24.7 by its own netherrack wall to the west, and the body going straight down through the cell under it; the save has that netherrack gone. The fireball broke the floor. Every stance had said "Walled here toward the push ... a push into the wall, not the fall": the wall held, the floor did not. The charge and the closing walk go through motion.js (note 600) and the pathfinder, and did not move the body here. mid-243-af-nether-3-fortress-4, nothing about: in fire on a netherrack slope at y 71, out_of_fire (0.65) "5 steps ... about 0.9 seconds at a sprint"; the route, rebuilt on the save, is five cells none of them beside a fall; by 14:45:21.5 the body was at (-130.7, 69, -197.3), a block west of the route's fourth cell, and it ran on west off a ledge thirty over the floor (14.8 to none at y 41). The run's moves held their keys until each cell was reached, with nothing keeping the body to the route; the frames do not show what turned it west. What a player does: on the ridge, a block of gravel west and north on the basalt, the sides the ghast's push goes toward; on the span, the plank as a floor south and gravel on it; standing on netherrack over a drop, not walled but off it; out of a fire, on the cells it means to. Now: the rail walls, besides the sides open over the drop, each side a blast's push (a ghast, a breeze) goes toward that is floored but has the drop within three beyond it (survival.js wallCells); gravel and sand count for a wall on a floor, the floors from a block that holds (wallStock); short of blocks for every side, only the sides a shooter's push goes toward, said with what stays open (wallPlan); railSpan lays the same cells, never gravel over air. An escape's way is counted against the push (routeEdge): out_of_sight's walk (coverWithin now keeps the way) and fight_from_footing's (bunker.js wayTo) say how many of their cells lie beside a drop that kills, the seconds along them crouched in the Nether, and the chance a shot lands meanwhile by the shooter's rate; the walk takes those cells as offered (navigate edgeTaken, movement.js: the edge rule's opt-out for the escape's own cells, lava beside the feet still refused); crouch_out_of_fire says the same. A floor a ghast's fireball can break (blast resistance under about 4, ghast.js HOLDS_AT) over a fall that kills is said on every stance (blastFloor), and a bot walled toward the push on it is not told "not the fall". A stance held while a shooter it was chosen against lands a shot, the bot still open over the drop, is asked again ("landed a shot ... still open over the drop a push puts it over"). motion.js refuses an upright step toward a fall onto ground of half the health, as toward lava; the run out of fire is kept off every cell beside or over a fall that kills, the route's or any it is carried to, and stops there to be asked again. Tests (test/push-escape.test.js on the four saved regions, test/fire-run-edge.test.js on the fifth under prismarine-physics, the heading turned west halfway as the recorded run went; each fails before the change): the ridge's rail walls west then north with gravel; out_of_sight on the ridge says 4 of its 4 cells beside the lava 20 down and the fireball all but sure on the way, and its walk finds the route the pathfinder refused; on the span, the plank then gravel south; a held fight asked again after a fireball lands; walled on the netherrack of 25584, every stance but the pocket and the bunker says the floor; on 25587's span the floor and the crouched walk's push; upright toward the slope's ledge refused; the run out of fire stays above y 60 (without the change, down to 41).
