611. *The repeat hold did not hold (note 560's hold, the audit of notes 573 and 598): the cohort from 13:55Z with notes 571 to 609 live counted reaskAfterHold 880, 102.7 an hour, against 430 holds (7.3 an hour before).* Read from the bot logs of the 42 trials after 13:55Z, each asking within two minutes of a [repeat] hold of its question sorted by whether the held answer was on offer again and how far the bot stood from where it was held. Of 973 such askings at 17:50Z, 769 were mid-243-af-fortress-4's survival_priority (362 holds, obtain food/return for food held and then offered and chosen again 769 times, each within two seconds, the portal "293 blocks off and cannot be reached from here"); 91 were mid-242-bb's rung_progress (31 holds, keep at it offered and chosen again 90 times, the bot not moving); 26 each of fortress_approach on mid-242-bb and mid-243-ah-fortress-5, 21 of them with a held answer on offer again; the rest fortress_leg and unstuck_move, one to seven a trial. None came from note 599's wait outcomes or note 605's "not counted as waits"; the rung's case is the keep-everything-on-offer of a question with nothing above, which note 609 only gave words (it stood before). What set off the jump is note 607 (81e3424, deployed at 13:55Z): return for food, nested under obtain food, had been left out by survival's own set-aside once it failed (nether_return), and is now always offered, which left its holding to the ledger, and the ledger could not hold a nested answer. Four leaks in the rule itself, and one miscount in the audit. (1) A nested answer was never held: tried.read read the top level of a tree only (a branch was passed through whole), while the ledger records an answer by its path, obtain_food/return_for_food, so the hold rested nothing, and decide looked the held answer up as a top-level key, missed it, and asked again with it on offer. (2) At a question with nothing above (rung_progress, survival_priority, or `above` of note 609) with every way resting, all stay on offer with their rests said, the held answer too, and Jev chose it again at once: keep at it, chosen 0.68, came back within a second (fortress_leg's escalation, every pass), was held, escalated to the stall's question, which escalated back to the rung's, and was asked again. (3) A hold was kept only among the ledger's last 160 entries: in the replay of mid-243-af it was dropped within a minute and a half by the one way taken at every pass after it. (4) A hold on answers that came back at once whatever the facts (note 570's run) rested each answer toward its own target only: on mid-242-bb fortress_approach was held on tunnel, keep searching and cross level with the fortress place found moving 15 to 40 blocks at each asking, (-67, 69, 143), (-106, 76, 153), (-121, 73, 143), (-100, 46, 105), the bot within a block and a half, and each place found anew offered the held ways again. And the audit counted every asking of the question within two minutes of a hold: an asking with the held answers left out is the question asked with its other ways (note 583), and one from new ground is asked afresh (note 560); 80 of the 973 were those. Now, in general. The ledger reads, rests and holds every answer by its path (tried.js leavesOf, rebuilt, leafAt; a branch with nothing left goes with its last leaf), decide finds a held answer by its path, and the options kept with each asking (offeredOf, for spent and the rung's question) are the leaves by path. Every way resting with nothing above: an answer held by the repeat rule is left out while one not held stays on offer, said in waysResting (read's heldOut); with every one held, all stay on offer with their rests said, as note 609 has it. A hold still in force is kept whatever came after it (prune). A hold on answers that came back at once whatever the facts is held from within four blocks whatever the target (anyTarget), for its five minutes. The audit (`progress-audit.js`, `botLogCounter`): a re-ask is an asking after a hold, within its two minutes, that offered a held answer again (the answers parsed from the [repeat] line, the options from the decision line, nested by path) from within four blocks of where it was held (the status line's position before the hold); every asking within the two minutes is still counted, as askedAfterHold, and said beside it in the text, `--json` and the cohort table. The cohort at about 18:00Z, as now counted: before 3,159 of 4,452 askings (5.2 an hour, 2,016 holds), after 893 of 1,001 (75.5 an hour, 476 holds). Replayed, each recorded decision from 13:55Z to 17:50Z through decide at its time and place with its options and state and a Jev that gives the recorded answer at each branch while it is offered (else the likeliest offered by its recorded weights), on 81e3424 and on this change, counting re-asks as the audit now does (it counts what would not have been asked, not what the bot would then have done): mid-243-af-fortress-4, 886 recorded, before 886 asked, 366 holds, 776 re-asks after a hold; after 113 asked, 770 taken as the one way (continue request, with return for food held), 3 escalated, 6 holds, 0 re-asks; mid-242-bb, 502 recorded, before 465 asked, 35 holds, 80 re-asks (rung_progress 66, fortress_approach 14); after 394 asked, 96 one way (work free at the rung's question 85, keep at it and differently held), 12 escalated, 15 holds, 0 re-asks; mid-243-ah-fortress-5, 122 recorded, before 118 asked, 4 holds, 3 re-asks; after 110 asked, 2 holds, 0. Tests (test/held-answers.test.js): mid-243-af's survival_priority answered obtain food/return for food eight times, each ending at once, offers it at most twice and rests it from here; mid-242-bb's rung_progress with work free and until rest ends resting and keep at it held asks with the two, keep at it said in waysResting, and with all three held asks with all three; a hold followed by two hundred entries still rests its answer; fortress_approach answered tunnel, keep searching and cross level at six places found 15 to 40 blocks apart is asked three times and held, escalating at each place after, and asked afresh seven blocks on. test/progress-audit.test.js: after a hold, the question asked with the held answer left out, from six blocks on with it offered, and from where it was held with it offered: three askings, one re-ask. Each fails on 81e3424. Changed: the review measure's test now carries `asked`. npm test 2045 of 2045, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 64 of 66 with the two known gaps. Still open: with its held answer left out mid-243-af takes continue request as the one way at every pass, at 2.8 health with nothing to eat and the portal out of reach, where hoglin food was not on offer; the rung's question at mid-242-bb takes work free as the one way for five minutes while fortress_leg escalates every pass (why that escalation comes at every pass, not once, is not looked into here); the audit's four blocks do not see a target, so an answer held toward one place and offered toward another from where it was held counts as a re-ask; none of this has run live.
613. *mid-242-bb (25581), a fresh world at its fortress with main at d3039af (notes 571 to 610 live), 15:02 to 15:08 (the user: "seems really confused trying to get into a fortress"): fortress_approach, fortress_leg, stillness_detour and rung_progress asked in turn every few seconds, walk_route "a whole route of 3 cells" to a floor "7 blocks off and 2 up" chosen at 0.66 and never arriving, pillar_up and cross_level offered beside it, and "shield_guard ran twenty times in a second without the bot moving".* Read from the flight records, the log's step lines and the region files as flushed when the trial was stopped (a copy, read-only). The floor at (-79, 46, 127) was two nether bricks the bot had stacked itself at 14:54:22 (its bricks went 11 to 9 standing at (-78.6, 44, 126.5)), in the open over netherrack at y 43. The fortress's own floors were a bridge deck at y 73 over x -150 to -66, z 140 to 144, on a pier at x -72 to -70 rising from the lava, and a structure at y 65 at x -106 to -98, z 102 to 106: twenty-two to thirty blocks up. The bot carried no pickaxe (its wooden one made at 14:38 was gone), 9 nether bricks and 16 gravel. Why the three-cell walk never got there: walk_route's run walked to a point level with the bot within four of the floor, and ended there whenever that came nearer ("then to the bricks' own height if that comes no nearer"), so the walk that ended at (-81.5, 44, 125.5), three off and two below, was the approach "getting somewhere" (its failures cleared, the answer held), while the ledger read no new ground and rested it; being two below, the bot was never on the fortress's floors (onFortressFloor), and the next pass aimed somewhere else. Why the place moved fifteen to forty blocks at each asking (the coordinator's open point): the approach's place was the nearest "floor" (any fortress brick with two clear over it) picked afresh at every pass, and near the bot those were its own bricks ((-79, 45, 127), (-74, 43, 139), (-61, 43, 143)) and the foot of a shaft it had dug up the pier at 14:38 ((-71, 43, 141), (-72 and -71, 44, 140)); a few steps changed which was nearest, and keep_searching's set-aside (a circle the fortress's extent round the nearest) left the next nearest just outside it: (-79, 45, 127), (-71, 43, 141), (-111, 63, 96), (-112, 67, 96), (-118, 66, 103), (-79, 45, 127), (-71, 43, 141), (-111, 63, 96), (-140, 41, 153) between 15:06:50 and 15:07:34. The ledger rests a way toward "the same place from about here" (within four blocks of the target), so no way toward a new place rested and each asking offered them all again; held answers (the approach holds its choice five minutes within 32 blocks) were carried to the new place unasked: at 15:07:25 walk_route, chosen for (-79, 45, 127), walked to (-71, 43, 141). Why cross_level and pillar_up did not get it on: cross_level is a crossing at the bot's own height and ended beside the stack, "1 from it", two below; pillar_up rose two from a column a block off and left the floor "6 blocks across", all six open air, with no block carried that a span is laid with (nether bricks are the pillar's, not the span's), which the option did not say. Why the questions came round every few seconds: the moving place (above), and fortress_leg's back_to_fortress, chosen seven times in five minutes (0.19 to 0.48), offered as "its ways in from here came to nothing: fortress approach: every way it had from here rests", each followed within a second by fortress_approach asked again from the same spot, and from there back to the legs. Why shield_guard spun: it was a piglin, not a wither skeleton (none was about): the stance is offered over biters in sight or unseen within five, and the guard faced only those in sight or unseen within two; the piglin was 3.3 blocks off out of sight, the guard ended at once ("none left"), and the stance ran again, twenty times in a second at 15:06:19. Now, in general. The fortress blocks the bot lays and those of the fortress it digs out are noted as the world says a block changed within reach (src/own-blocks.js, the blockUpdate event, whichever way it was laid or dug), dropped when the ground no longer bears them out, and kept with the fortress search (state.own, state.dug) across restarts; the bot's own bricks are not the fortress (findFortressStep's look and the fortress map's), and a floor is a brick, stair or slab with two clear over it that is not the bot's digging and has another such beside it at its height (fortressFloors), so a lone brick top, the bot's stack and the foot of its shaft are not places to go. The place the way in is asked about is kept while the bot is within sixteen blocks of where it was first asked (tried.js's "from about here") and the place is still one of the floors, so a way tried toward it rests and the next asking is about the same place. walk_route goes on up or down to the floor itself once level beside it, and ends short only where it does not get there, saying how far from the floor. pillar_up says what lies between its top and the floor at that height (open air with no floor, a span, and the span blocks carried; or ground). back_to_fortress is not offered off the fortress's floors where every way into it last offered from here came to nothing (tried.spent), said in the set-aside as from where Jev left it (note 541). The guard faces the biters the stance was offered over (wither-guard.js inGuard, the one rule for both). Shown on the saved ground (test/fixtures/fortress-pier-mid-242-bb.json, x -150 to -50, y 30 to 80, z 90 to 170): the approach from (-84.3, 44, 124.2) with the old place gives the recorded options word for word (walk_route "a whole route of 3 cells ... it ends 3 blocks nearer", pillar_up "from a column 1 blocks from here ... then 6 blocks across"); as now, with the recorded bricks and the pier's open cells as the record, it is asked about (-100, 65, 105), "24 blocks off and 22 blocks up", walk_route a route part of the way, cross_level ending 21 off, the tunnel and keep_searching, no pillar. Tests (test/fortress-pier-613.test.js): the way in is asked about a floor of the fortress's own twenty and more up, not the stack or the stump; a lone brick top and a brick without a floor beside it are no floor; bricks laid within reach are noted, one appearing forty off is not, a dug one is forgotten and the record kept across a restart is read against the ground; a row of three bricks laid by the bot is not taken for the fortress's floor; the place is kept as the bot moves six blocks, where the nearest floor from there is another; the walk goes on to the floor after the level point; the pillar says six of open air and no span blocks; off the floors with every way in come to nothing, back_to_fortress is not offered and is said. test/wither-guard.test.js: the guard holds its time facing a piglin 3.3 off out of sight with the shield up. Each fails on d3039af but the noting of blocks laid, which tests the new module. Changed test: mob-hunt.test.js's two pockets of thirty bricks were laid on a diagonal, no brick beside another; now rows of three, as a pocket is built. npm test 2072 of 2072, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 66 of 68 with the two known gaps. Still open: what was laid or dug before this runs is not known (the floor-beside-a-floor rule stands in for lone bricks and shaft feet of one or two cells, not for a platform); from under that bridge with no pickaxe, 9 bricks and 16 gravel the fortress is twenty-two to thirty up, and whether to tunnel by hand, go back for stone and a pickaxe or search on is Jev's with those facts; nether bricks are laid by the pillar and not by a span (bridging.js MATERIALS); keep_searching still sets aside a circle round the nearest brick, and bricks of the same fortress not linked within eight blocks lie outside it; none of this has run live.
612. *A ghast's fireball pushing the bot off a ledge before anything stepped it back: mid-242-bb-fortress-2 (25587, 15:05:06), with note 610 live, and mid-242-bb-fortress-4 (25584, 15:30:39) and mid-242-ac-nether-3-fortress-5 (25581, 15:32:08) after it; the push model checked against those three and note 610's five.* mid-242-bb-fortress-2 walked a one-wide netherrack path at y 46 over the lava sea. At 15:04:19 a ghast came into sight at 25 blocks; from 15:04:26 to 15:04:52 it drifted 45 to 55 off, survival had the turn by the push claim (note 586) and asked no stance, the encounter looking at mobs within twenty-four only, and the code's own step off the edge (stepOnce) walked for firm ground three times and found no route: it held the cells beside the drop round the feet (holdOffEdge) before walking, and on a one-wide path those are the way off, the edge rule refusing the rest while the ghast could push. With piglins coming, the stance at 15:04:53.4 took Jev 10.6 seconds (none of these 0.47, the fight taken), and at 15:05:04.5 again none of these (0.52): every stance said the fireball was the fall, and the one step off offered was to fight three blocks from any drop, whose netherrack floor a fireball also breaks. The fireball at 15:05:06.58 from 59.7 blocks (20 to 15.2) pushed (-0.28, 0.27, -0.10) a tick, then 0.44 up: the body rose to y 49.1 and came down 4 blocks west and 1.2 north, 18 into the lava, dead at 15:05:10; the save has the 2 by 2 of netherrack under the feet gone. mid-242-bb-fortress-4 stood on its own netherrack span laid on the lava sea at its level; every stance priced a push into the lava beside it as "about 6.1 health of the 20", a second's swim back; the stance after its rail took 9.9 seconds, the ghast came from 55 to 19, and its fireball pushed the body 2.1 blocks north-west into the sea at 15.2: it sank four blocks and was dead three seconds later. lavaFate priced the swim and left out the fifteen seconds of fire after it that lavaTouch counts (note 580). mid-242-ac-nether-3-fortress-5, on the span of note 610's 13:15 death: the ghast came into sight at 44.5, turn_priority was asked at 15:32:04.3 and was still out 4.6 seconds later (Jev answering in 9 to 10 seconds that hour) when the fireball from 35.8 pushed the bot 3.3 blocks south-west and 31 down. The push, from the 26.1.2 jar (ServerExplosion.hurtEntities: along the line from the burst to the eyes, (1 - distance / 2) for a ghast's power of 1, at most a block a tick, with the fireball's own knock) and the eight frames: all eight went away from the ghast, within 12 degrees of its line; 0.27 to 0.42 a tick across, up to 0.45 up; the body back at its own level 2.1 to 4.0 blocks off; five of the saves have the netherrack under the feet gone (one went straight down through it). wallCells' throw of up to four blocks and blastFloor stand; what was not modeled is a push meeting a wall side-on, which goes on along it. Now (survival.js): pushCarries follows a blast's push from a cell, along the line away from the shooter and 15 degrees either side, up to four blocks, x and z apart so a wall met side-on stops one and the push slides on the other, a block at the feet' level stopping it only in the first block (the body is a block up after); blastPushesOver is a ghast in sight whose push carries the bot over a drop that kills, or whose blast breaks the floor over one. pushFooting finds the nearest footing by the walk's own steps (standable, no lava beside, no cell the pathfinder refuses for a mob, safeFromHostiles) where neither holds. A new stance, out_of_the_push: step back from the edge to that footing and stand there, said with the steps, the cells beside the drop walked crouched, the seconds until it is there against one fireball every three, and the jar's aim: a ghast aims at where the bot is and leads no target (Ghast$GhastShootFireballGoal), a fireball meets the body within about 0.8, so a walk across its line takes the body out of where each fireball fired meanwhile comes, and only one already on its way can land (the chance said); a walk along the line is said to be hit as standing is. Its walk takes the cells it was offered along (edgeTaken). Every stance that leaves the bot open says where that footing is, fight_from_footing whether the push still carries it over from its ground. A ghast in sight that can push the bot over a drop that kills is among the mobs the encounter answers, so the stance is asked with it alone. turn_priority says the push, the rate of fire and the footing on the survival claim and on the work ("Where the bot stands now"). stepOnce's step off the edge is the fallback only when Jev cannot be reached, and walks its own way's cells; movement.js lets a walk's edgeTaken cells through the edge hold. lavaFate adds the fire after the swim (fifteen seconds, a point a second, no water in the Nether): at 20 health a push into the lava beside a span is death. The rail with only shooters about is priced with their shots behind the wall, as its words and the span's hold have them (5.8 for fifteen seconds beside a ghast firing every three, now 20.9). Tests (test/ghast-push-footing.test.js on the three saved regions, each failing before): the push away from the shooter, onto four blocks of floor, over a drop two off, sliding along a wall met side-on; on 25587's path the step to the rock's corridor at (-95, 45, 136), 11 steps, 23 in 100, and every open stance saying it; its walk found by the real pathfinder only along the cells offered; the ghast alone asks the stance, out_of_the_push walked, and without Jev the fallback walks its way; on 25581's span turn_priority's two options say the push and the footing, the step to the tunnel through the rock at (-19, 72, 137), 27 in 100, the rail at 20.9; on 25584's span the lava level with the feet is 21.1, death. span-fall.test.js: the sea three blocks from the shore is now 27.6, death. 614. *"It seems like it should charge the thing more" (the user, watching mid-242-aa-fortress-5 on 25581, main 9567384): at 15:16:24 to 15:16:45Z a blaze 3.7 to 4.4 blocks off, three or four more nine to thirteen off behind the walls, the bot at 15 to 20 health with a stone sword, no armour and no shield; encounter_stance chose take_cover (0.41, 0.39) and leave_and_heal (0.37, 0.28), and hunt_target before it deferred single blazes at full health (0.50, 0.42).* Read from the recorded questions. (1) close_in is in both the hunt and the stance (blaze-stand.js blazeStands), and was offered only with a shield in the off hand; this bot had none, so neither question could offer it. Whether ground reached this blaze is not in the record (the fight's own line said a run straight at it stopped after a block, four short). (2) The prices were the game's, but several facts were false or missing. The fight said "about 5.3 seconds and 9.2 damage to kill them all" of the one blaze in sight: four stone-sword swings and a fireball of 5 unarmoured with its fire is about right for one, but "them all" left out the four behind the walls, said only after as "out of sight but about". fight_at_spawner, dig_in_at_spawner, box_here and corner_ambush each said "the shield up" or "where the shield faces" with no shield carried. Every arena row said "measured with the same kit", runs made with an iron sword, a shield and iron armour. The hunt's fitness line said "no sword or axe carried" with a stone sword in hand, beside fights that struck with it (mob-policy's kit is iron or better, and the words said the kind, not the grade). And no option said what it gains toward the rods: cover, heal, retreat and seal were priced in damage alone (4.1 for cover), each a cost set beside the fight's, and nothing said that none of them comes any nearer a rod, nor that the blazes stay. (3) hunt_target at 15:16:14 offered only fights in the open at blazes out of sight 11 to 14 off and 4 up, because the defers at 15:14:09 and 15:14:45 had set the stands (close_in among them) aside for two minutes; each fight led with the arena's spawner row (39.9 damage, 2 deaths in 3), "with the same kit", against defer's rows (21.1, no deaths), and the kit line said no sword. The asking at 15:16:08, a blaze in sight six off, went stale on a 5.2-second answer. The slow answers were the service's, not the question's size: from 15:16 to 15:17:59Z 38 of 54 askings across six trials took over a second (median 2.2 and 1.7 s), questions of 1,500 tokens as slow as those of 8,000, where at 15:15:24 this trial's 8,522-token stance question came back in 199 ms; 15:16:45 was 7,019 tokens and waited 1,736 ms for the response headers. Probes alternating the recorded question and the changed one a minute apart went with the minute, not the size (18,355 characters of state and options at 1.05 to 1.2 s, then 0.17 to 0.33; 24,714 at 0.16 to 0.30, then 1.2 to 1.6). Now, in general. close_in is offered with or without a shield: without one the walk goes straight on (closeIn's walk no longer stops for a volley there is nothing to meet it with; closeInCost prices the walk without the lulls and every fireball at its chance by distance), and its text says so. charge_nearest, the nearest blaze alone, is offered beside it where more than one blaze is about (seen or heard within forty-eight): closeIn with upTo 1, ended at the kill, its rod picked up, asked again; priced by closeInCost up to that one kill, a blaze out of sight counted only with a line to the cell the sword strikes from (bunker.seenFrom), where the close-in, going on to all of them, counts every one within sixteen as before; it is a striking stance. The stance's close-in is priced with the blazes out of sight within sixteen, as the hunt's is. Every option at a blaze fight on a blaze hunt (goal.mobHunt) says what it gains toward the rods (blaze-stand.js towardRods): the close-in, the charge, breaking the spawner and the fight their kills by their own figures and the rods on the average; a hold or a striking stance a kill only if a blaze comes within the sword's reach; cover, heal, retreat, seal, dig down, out of sight, nook, keep working and defer "none, no blaze killed; the blazes stay, and waiting does not send them away", with the rods still needed; lighting the spawner none and no more made; keep working is not said while the work is the hunt itself. The hunt's defer says those left are not offered again for two minutes. The fight's "them all" names the ones in its figures when others out of sight are left out. The shield is said only where one is carried. The arena's rows say their own kit and the bot's where they differ (kitSays). The fitness line names each piece by the grade it asks for and the sword carried ("no iron or better sword carried (a stone sword is)"). The question grew from 7,019 to 8,700 input tokens with the two options and the lines above (the rods line was shortened after a first measure of 9,035). Probed against the live model, the recorded questions, five each: 15:16:45 encounter_stance before take_cover 5 of 5 (0.36 to 0.43), after (close_in and charge_nearest as the code words them for a scene built to match, the rods lines, the kit and the fight named) take_cover 4, retreat 1, charge_nearest 0.11 to 0.17; 15:16:14 hunt_target before defer 5 of 5 (0.48 to 0.58, the nearest hunt 0.14 to 0.23), after defer 5 of 5 (0.42 to 0.44, the nearest hunt 0.21 to 0.27); 15:16:08 (the stale one) before defer 5 of 5 (0.53 to 0.58, the hunt 0.29 to 0.35), after defer 3, the hunt of the blaze in sight 2 (0.38 to 0.45 each way). No replay case: the two questions answer as they did, and 15:16:08 is split. Tests (each fails on 9567384): test/blaze-stand.test.js, the recorded scene with no shield offers close_in and charge_nearest, the walk straight on and no shield claimed, the charge's one kill cheaper than the close-in's run, the four behind the walls not counted for the charge, the rows said with their own kit, and every stand saying its gain toward the rods, none without a rod hunt; test/survival.test.js, the stance with a rod hunt says the gain on every option once, "none" on cover, retreat, seal and dig down, the fight "the one in these figures, not those out of sight below" and its kill; test/mob-hunt.test.js, the defer's none and two minutes, the hunt's kill, and the fitness naming the stone sword. Changed to the new words: the fitness test, the cave-spider fight's "them all" (combat-estimate), and the archer stance's option list (close_in now offered with no shield). npm test 2072 of 2072, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 66 of 68 with the two known gaps. Still open: Jev still takes cover or retreats over the charge at 4.3 with no armour, no shield and four more about, and defers the hunt at full health; that is its weighing of honest prices, not changed here; not run live; whether the ground reached the blaze at 15:16:45 is not known.

615. *mid-242-ae-nether-2-fortress-5 (25584) and mid-242-af-fortress-5 (25587), ended 16:30 to 17:05 on 2026-09-28: "loop: 3× The nether portal at (17, 58, 8) is 158 blocks off and cannot be reached from here: legs of thirty-two blocks on foot toward it made no ground" after ninety-one minutes on 25584, and on 25587 eighty-eight minutes at (-93, 41, 111).* Read from the flight records' no_route frames, whose "around" lists the blocks round the feet. The bot did not move from that cell again. Navigation will not break planks (movement.js keeps every block but soft ground and natural rock in blocksCantBreak, so a route never goes through a house), and working free (unstuck.js) dug natural blocks only, so every walk and every leg found no route, and the portal, the fortress, the warped forest and the food hunt each came back as "made no ground" and rested in turn. Working free offers the dig of a block the bot laid itself, whatever it is made of, beside the natural ones, said as "a block the bot laid itself at 15:32Z"; the planks of a house the bot did not lay are still not offered, and navigation is unchanged. The offer to work free says when the bot is walled in, and how much of it is its own: "walled in where it stands: every side is closed at the feet or the head, 9 of the 9 blocks round it its own (oak planks, laid from 15:32Z), which it can dig through". Tests (test/own-cover.test.js, each fails before): the recorded box offers the digs through its own planks at the feet, the head and over, and before offered only the dig down; with the feet cell open and the head still its planks, the head is offered beside place east, and then the step east; a plank by hand is three seconds; the walled-in line; a placement remembered in the goal across a restart and forgotten once dug. npm test 2095 of 2095. No replay case: Jev was never offered the way out. Not run live; the box's east side and past it, where the step out goes, are from the no_route frames, not probed.

616. *mid-242-af-fortress-5 (25587), the same trial, "loop: flipping detour <-> barter".* The bot carried three gold ingots and six nuggets and wore no gold. Now, in general: the gold a barter can throw is all of it with a gold piece worn or carried, and without one what is left after the four ingots of the boots (bartering.js barterGold, nuggets counted as ingots). The ladder's barter, the pearl route's barter and the bastion's gold ("no gold to throw") all read it; with gold that cannot be dressed for, the barter is not offered and the pearl routes say why: "a barter with piglins: gold for 3 ingots carried and no gold piece to wear: piglins turn on a player in no gold, golden boots take 4 ingots, and one more is needed to throw", and with no gold piece the offered barter says the boots are made from four first. 617. *mid-242-ah-fortress-5 (25586, 17:06:21Z), "burned to death" three minutes after starting from its fortress save: a blaze's fireball pushed it a block off an edge 23 into the lava, as its stance built a wall.* Read from the flight frames. The bot stood at (-217.5, 55, -155.4) on a fortress floor, the edge half a block west of its body and the lava sea's top at y 31, with two blazes 13.6 and 14.8 blocks off to the east; the push claim (note 586) held the turn from 17:06:04 ("Preempted by push" every quarter second), turn_priority gave it to survival, and shield_policy was asked at 17:06:08.3 for a shot on its way. The stance at 08.5 said the drop and its price honestly on every option (a push over it into the lava, death), and priced the walls by the blazes' average rate: rail_and_fight and hold_on_span "about 8 in 100 that a fireball lands first", take_cover 12, from a volley every nine seconds; riskNow said "shotsComingAtTheBot: 1" and nothing tied it to those figures. Jev took take_cover (0.31; box_here and charge_nearest 0.19). The blaze 14.8 off was glowing: its three fireballs are in the frames by 08.79, the first landed at 09.43, 0.9 seconds after the question, before a block was down, with no key held, and pushed the body 0.5 west and up; it came down over the air west of the floor and fell (y 54.5 at 10.02, 50.2 at 10.43, the lava at 11.1). Not box_here: it was asked at 10.0 with the body already falling and never walked. In the lava at 14.6, body_way offered pillar_out, said "about 29.4 in all, more than the 14.6 health the bot has unless it heals" (0.65, none_good 0.33), and it came out at y 32 at 6.0; turn_priority then said "it dies of the burning in about 6 seconds, before the fire ends, unless water puts it out first ... the Nether has none", and eating the beef (hunger 19 to 20) healed a little between the burns until the fire ended it at 17:06:21. Nothing better stood there: no fire resistance carried, the water bucket does not pour in the Nether, no golden apple; the facts were given, and the death was fixed at the fall. The fault was the chance of a shot before the wall: a blaze glows three seconds before its volley (Blaze$BlazeAttackGoal: 60 ticks charging, three shots 6 ticks apart, 100 resting), the client sees the glow (its flags' bit 1, blaze-stand.js charged), and a glowing blaze's three fireballs are due within 3.6 seconds whatever its average; one not glowing has none sooner than the glow and the flight. Now, in general (survival.js): shotsDue says what is known of a shooter's next shots beyond its rate: the fireballs already in the air at the bot (a small fireball or a ghast's between the shooter and the bot within three blocks of that line, read by position since a fireball's velocity often does not arrive; its time left by the fireball's own acceleration, ghast.js flightSeconds), a blaze's volley while it glows (by the glow's clock where volleyWatch saw it begin, the three at once where it did not, said so), and the seconds before any shot not so scheduled can come. shotChanceNow counts each pusher by those shots (a blaze's landing by fireballHit at its distance, a ghast's meeting a body that stands where it aimed) and its rate after them, all the pushers together (before, only the first was counted, here the blaze 13.6 off whose line a fence already cut). The rail's, the hold's and the cover's open seconds (openWhileBuildingSays), an escape's way beside the drop (routeEdge) and the step out of the push (footingStep) are priced so and say the shots due; every stance left open over the drop says "Due now: ..." with the chance one of them lands and when. Tests (test/blaze-volley-due.test.js, the scene as the frames have it; each fails before the change): the glowing blaze's three due within the rail's 1.2 seconds counted by their landing chance, not the rate's 8 in 100; a blaze not glowing lands nothing within 1.2 seconds, and its fireball in the air is counted; the stance's rail says the volley due and 25 in 100, and the fight, the close-in, the charge and keep_working say it due; with neither glowing, 0 in 100 and nothing due. npm test 2092 of 2092, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 66 of 68 with the two known gaps. Probes, 5 asks each through decide: the recorded 08.5 stance take_cover 4, charge_nearest 1 (0.25 to 0.28); with the change's texts written onto it (the rail and the hold 25 in 100, the cover 58, "Due now" on the open stances) box_here 5 of 5 (0.20 to 0.27), take_cover 0.16 to 0.19. No replay case: every stance stays open through the volley's 1.6 seconds but those that walk off the cell, and which of those is right is not one answer. Still open: out_of_the_push (note 612) is offered against a ghast or a breeze only; against a blaze the move off the edge's reach, a block or two east here, is offered only as fight_from_footing's walk to three blocks from any drop (4.1 blocks, ten of its cells beside the drop) or inside the charge; the push of a blaze's fireball is priced "about 2 blocks" on flat ground, not along the body's own place in its cell (half a block from this edge); none of this has run live.
618. *A blaze 4.9 blocks off for a minute and a half, never struck, the stances turning every second or two: mid-242-af-nether-3-fortress-5 (25584), fireballed at 17:12:39Z on 2026-09-28, nine minutes in, one rod carried, iron armour, an iron sword and a shield.* Read from the flight record and the region files as saved (a copy). The charge stays on the blaze it charged: that one set aside or gone, it ends and says why ("the walk to one failed 3 times (No path to the goal!); the blaze it charged is set aside") and is asked again, rather than walking at another. In the recorded scene the stance now says the blaze has a line where the bot stands, offers no cover "already" in place, offers the corner at (-169, 53, 147), one the game's rays do not reach, and offers close_in at 16.5 and at 1 health, walking to the stair run at y 55 beside the blaze, priced by the fight at hand. Tests (test/wart-stair-618.test.js on the saved ground, test/fixtures/wart-stair-mid-242-af.json, stairs and fences with their block state; saved-ground.js reads a palette entry's state and, with `shapes`, stops its ray at a block's shapes; each fails on cd53bf8): the feet on soul sand, over a stair's low half and on a full block; a ray over a stair's low half and through its high half; the line from the blaze to the bot in the wart bed, and no take_cover "already" nor corner at the bot's own cell; the stair cells within the sword's reach and close_in offered at 16.5 and at 1; the charge's walks all at the stair run, three of them, then set aside and said, none at the blaze 38 off. npm test 2093 of 2093, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. 620. *mid-242-ba-fortress-5 (25592), from a fortress save, 17:04 to 17:39Z on 2026-09-28, "loop: flipping hold_box <-> cross_toward": thirty-five minutes by a blaze spawner at about (-199, 56, -154), 17.9 health, hunger 17, nothing to eat, an iron sword, a shield, an iron helmet and chestplate, 0 rods.* Read from the flight records and the bot log. encounter_stance chose box_here sixteen times (take_cover sixteen, seal five), the hunt deferred eleven times and held back_to_wall five, and not one blaze was killed; the box stood 7.2 blocks from the cage, every blaze in sight was 19 to 24 off, the rest six to seven off by the cage out of sight. The last minutes were one cycle every twenty seconds: the rest on the walk back to the portal (257 blocks off, and twice by then "cannot be reached from here") ended at 17:37:44, leave_nether answered go_back, cross_toward found no route and was stopped by the push claim (a blaze in sight, a nineteen-block drop a block off where the box's side was open), encounter_stance chose box_here (0.43 to 0.73), the box's walls went back in and it was held 15 to 20 seconds, turn_priority answered none good (0.54) and the fallback took the work, and the work stepped out again. Three things let it run with nothing above it asking. (1) The ledger counted the box's own walls as getting somewhere: a wait's entry was settled "progressed" by cameOf's "a block was dug or placed" before its scene was looked at, so every box whose walls went back in came to something (the ledger's summary: "box here, 3 times, 2 of them getting somewhere"), and take_cover and seal the same; nothing about the box changed (the same health, the nearest blaze six to seven off out of sight, none in sight within sixteen, no swing). (2) The box's holds were kept nowhere and said nowhere: the stance ran the tactic and threw its stats away, the hunt kept them with no place, and heldHereSays passed over the tactics, so each asking offered the box as the first time, where the hunt's back_to_wall said "Held from about here twice in the last 12 minutes, 4 minutes in all: 0 blazes killed, 0 rods, no blaze came within the sword's reach". The box's own words were honest about what the game does (a blaze more than two off hovers and shoots, the spawner puts its blazes by its cage, the arena's 0 killed in ten runs, "a kill only if a blaze comes within the sword's reach"). (3) The rung's question was lost: its ten minutes ran out at 17:29:41 while a blaze's claim waited to be picked up ("preempted work detour: a blaze came within 4 blocks"); the loop took the rung's stall, answerStall's survey of the next rung's way (surveyRoute, task.check) threw the preemption, inCatch swallowed it, and the question never went out; the rung's clock had begun again, so the next was due at 17:39:41, after the trial ended. Of fourteen rung stalls raised in the day's last forty trial logs, two (this one, and mid-243-af-fortress-4's at its out_of_fire) were followed by another stall with no question between. Offered and priced at 17:38:06: close_in ("the health runs out at about 9.2 seconds in, after about 0 of them killed", 0.01), charge_nearest (5.1 damage for the one blaze 21 off and half a rod on the average, 0.03), corner_ambush, out_of_sight, seal, take_cover, fight_from_footing, retreat ("No way out: ... a run from here fails at once") and keep_working (29 damage in fifteen seconds); leave_and_heal was not offered at 17.9 health with nothing to eat; setting the rung aside is the rung's question's, never asked. Not changed here: keep_working said the work "was making headway when these mobs stopped it" by the stall watch's record, which counts the blocks the walk and the box laid under the rung's one key; leave_nether's go_back said "about 60 seconds at a walk once the way is found" without the two walks there that had come to nothing (the hunt's defer said them). Now, in general. A wait is judged by its world and by what it brought (tried.js waitBrought): a walk off beyond three blocks, or more carried of what is worth keeping; a block laid or dug is its own building, and blocks used up for its walls (planks, wool) are no gain; an answer that is not a wait is judged as before. The box and the corner are waits by what they are when the hunt offers them (WAIT_ANSWERS box_here, box_at_spawner, corner_ambush). Each hold of a box or a corner, the stance's and the hunt's, is kept in the hunt's stand results with its cell, seconds, kills, swings, the most in line and how it ended (the box's quiet as "twenty seconds with no blaze in line with its window or within eight", a hold stopped by a throw as "cut off, something else taking the turn"), and heldHereSays says them on box_here and corner_ambush in the hunt and the stance alike, the stance now given the hunt's holds. The rung's question cut off before it goes out (inCatch's true: a preemption, a threat, air) is put off (stillness.js deferStall, work.js answerOrPutOff), the pass goes on to the turn it was cut off for, and a later pass takes it once no other stall waits; asked, or ended by an ordinary failure, it is not put off, and put off twenty times it is let go. Probed against the live model, five each, the recorded 17:38:33 stance: as recorded box_here 5 of 5 (0.62 to 0.66); with its holds said ("Held from about here 8 times in the last 12 minutes, 3.1 minutes in all: 0 blazes killed, 0 rods, no blaze came within the sword's reach, none in sight; the last ended: cut off, something else taking the turn") box_here 5 of 5 (0.55 to 0.63); as the ledger now has it at that asking (the box resting after two holds that came to nothing, left out with the other ways open, said in waysResting) take_cover 5 of 5 (0.31 to 0.42; fight_from_footing 0.15 to 0.22, seal 0.14 to 0.20, charge_nearest 0.12 to 0.15). As in note 599, the facts alone did not move Jev off a quiet hold; the rest and the rung's question are what end it. No replay case: the box was chosen on true words, and which of the ways left is right here is not one answer. Tests (test/box-hold-620.test.js, each fails before): the box chosen three times with its walls laid between and nothing changed rests after two, said "Held from about here 2 times ... nothing changed", and the ledger's summary says "2 coming to nothing"; a rod picked up in a wait gets somewhere, planks laid for its walls do not, and a block placed by an answer that is not a wait still does; the hunt's box is a wait; the stance's box cut off is kept at its cell and said on the next box offered, in the stance and the hunt; the rung's question cut off is put off and taken after a stall raised meanwhile, and not when asked, when ended by a failure, for the stall's own question, or after twenty. npm test 2109 of 2109, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Still open: the work's "making headway" is read from a record the box's own blocks feed; go_back does not say the walks back that came to nothing; take_cover and seal, the next waits, rest only after two each, so the rung's ten minutes, now asked, are still what ends such a stretch; turn_priority's fallback on none good takes the work into the push claim each time; not run live.

621. *Two ghast deaths on 2026-09-28 with the ghast in sight and the bot's own moves not answering: mid-242-ah-nether-2-fortress-5 (25589, 17:33:03Z, "walked into fire while fighting Ghast") and mid-243-af-fortress-5 (25584, 17:54:27Z, a fall of 32 during unstuck_move).* 25589 came from 20 health at 17:32:36 to 7.4 at 17:32:54 in four ghast fireballs (3.1 each through its iron, then the fire), a ghast 40 to 60 blocks off in sight, piglins 10 to 30 off, standing on its own gravel on a netherrack slope at (-394, 65, -66). The pathfinder lays a block level with its floor from the edge it backs out to (LOSWhenPlacingBlocks, on by default) and keeps the cell it backed from as a place to return to (returningPos); its tick goes to the return before searching any goal, and only reaching the cell clears it. The bot stood on that cell's block up (its own pillar and gravel) and could never get there: an out_of_sight, four retreats and the out_of_fire runs all stood still, and each retreat was taken as done, so the next stance was told "A way is found: 16 blocks to footing 9 blocks further from every mob ... About 4.5 damage" again, to footing the ghast had a line to (it fires from 64). Jev chose retreat 0.60 at 7.4 (nook 0.20, eat 0.12); eating was a fair option (2.5 damage from the mobs while it eats, hunger 16 to 18, health then a point in four seconds) but not against a fireball every three seconds, and no cover was offered but the nook 2.2 off. Then out_of_fire at 3.9 was asked of the fire only: a run of seven steps, said nothing of the ghast, and the fireball at 17:33:02 took 3.9 to 0.8 in the run. A run that never leaves where it began (runAway, leaveReach) is a stance that failed and says so ("the run to the footing at ... ended N blocks short of it, where it began: ..."), instead of being taken as done. The retreat's footing says whether the shooters in sight have a line to it from where they are now and prices the next fifteen seconds with their fire there (survival.js footingSight; the recorded scene now reads "The footing is not out of their sight: the ghast has a line to it ... about 23.3 damage ... from 7.4 health (more than the bot has)", where before 4.5), and the footings out of the shooters' line are tried first (escapeFootings). body_way in fire says the shooters in sight (rate, hit through the armour, shots in the air, how many that land end the bot; vitals.js shootersAtBody, "shotAt" and "shooters" in the state) and each way says whether its end is in or out of the line. 25584 stood two minutes on a few blocks of a fortress ledge at y 65, 32 over the cavern floor, every walk "no route", and worked free with unstuck_move; the ghast at 47 blocks came back in sight and the question's state said "threats: []" (read within sixteen blocks) and no move said the push. step_north at 0.67 took the bot from (-190, 66, -185), where a push from the north is stopped, to (-190, 66, -186), where it carries the body over the drop; the fireball 1.2 seconds later threw it 3.8 blocks south. 623. *mid-242-bc-fortress-2 (25587, 17:56:35Z), "burned to death" three minutes in: break_spawner taken when its own answer put leave_and_heal first; and mid-242-bc (25581, 18:01:45Z), killed inside a box_here with four blazes four to five off.* (1) The answer of 17:56:27 (encounter_stance, health 13.3): the service's judgment said choice break_spawner with probabilities leave_and_heal 0.27, break_spawner 0.26, retreat 0.10, charge_nearest 0.09. There is no tie rule, nested pick, hold or ledger in it: the tree walk (decisions/tree.js) takes the `choice` field as served, and the service documents `choice` as the option with the highest probability; here it named the one a hundredth below. Counted over the flight records of 2026-09-27 and 28 (400 files, 12,070 judgments) 36 have a `choice` that is not the argmax of their own probabilities, each by 0.01 or less, in stance, unstuck, upkeep, fortress and other questions, so the pick and the distribution the log shows disagree about once in 330 answers; nothing had noticed since the logs print the distribution and the tree reads the field. Now (typesafe.js pickByDistribution, applied to every response): a choice is the option with the highest probability, a tie keeps the service's pick, and what the service named is kept on the judgment as `served`. (2) Was break_spawner priced honestly? No. The stance's list held the one blaze in sight (4.3 off); five more were out of sight eight to ten off, hovering round the cage five blocks' walk away, and the option said "1 blaze sees the bot now ... about 7.8 damage over the 7 seconds". Three faults, general: the sum counted only the blazes in sight (close_in and the hunt count every one within sixteen, since the walk in puts the bot in their sight: note 606); it priced the walk and the dig from where the bot stood, each blaze at its distance from there and the shield's cover as faced from there, where the digging is done at the cell by the cage, with the blazes there within two swinging and the rest at their distance from it; and "the N about now stay" said the one in sight. The recorded fight lost 12.6 health in three seconds (two fireballs and a blow, 14.3 to 1.7). With the scene rebuilt in the test the option is now priced at more than the 13.3 health, the cage's cell said ("At the cell by the cage 3 of them are within five blocks, the nearest 3.6 off"), the six about said. The arena row is quoted and relevant (note 606's break row, 2 deaths in 3 against three blazes twenty off, 34.1 damage); it is unchanged. (3) A stance run for more than the six health it holds for: breakSpawner ran its walk and dig with no check of health at all, and only then the close-in's own, which counted from its own start, after the walk and the digging: the frames have 14.3 to 1.7 inside the stance, asked again after. breakSpawner now ends at the same six health lost as every stance (danger.js STANCE_HEALTH) counted from the stance's start, says why, does not go on to the close-in, and the close-in that follows it counts its six from the stance's start too (closeIn takes `startHealth`); the option says it runs fifteen seconds or until six health is gone. (4) At 1.7 health eat was said honestly ("about 6.6 damage from the mobs here while it eats ... more than the bot has", the fire "a health a second whatever is chosen"; retreat 16.9, dig_down 26.7, cover 39.6, leave_and_heal 35.6, every option more than the bot had); the facts were given and nothing was better; the death was the walk into the cage. (5) 25581's box_here: the box was whole (5 blocks placed, the window open toward the spawner; one hold ended 'hurt' at 13.6 to 7.7, then held again at 6.7 on its own choice at 0.41) and the volleys came through the window: with six blazes in line with it spread over some eighty degrees, the shield reflex (blaze-stand.js shieldVolley) turned the bot to face the middle of the blazes due, not the window, so a blaze on the far side of the arc was outside the half the shield covers (frames at 18:01:44: the look at yaw 0.72 to 0.83 from the window's 0.04, then two fireballs of 3.9 each). The option's words say "every shot comes from in front, where the shield faces each volley": true only facing the window. Now shieldVolley takes `face`, and the box's hold (blaze-tactics holdBox) and the bunker's (bunker.js holdBunker) face the window or the door through every volley, since every shot comes in through it; walks and the close-in still face the blazes. (6) mid-242-bc-fortress-4 (25587, verdict "flipping hold_bunker <-> blaze_sortie"): read from its frames, one hold_bunker of 81 seconds at 20 health with seven blazes about and no damage; hold_bunker rewrites goal.step at each look and the hold's own sortie (a step out to strike a blaze just past the sword) sets blaze_sortie, so the audit read the step trading names for the length of the hold. Not a loop, and not in the reach of note 620's ledger, which judges waits by their progress; the general fix is in the audit (scripts/lib/audit.js: a blaze_sortie inside hold_bunker or hold_box is the hold's own swing, not a second step). Tests: test/typesafe-provider.test.js (the recorded 17:56:27 distribution, a tie kept, a noul left alone, the tree taking the highest); test/blaze-stand.test.js (break_spawner priced at the cage with the blazes out of sight counted, more than the health, said; breaking ends at six health lost and does not go on); test/blaze-tactics.test.js (the box faces the window through a volley from a blaze off to one side); test/audit.test.js (a hold's sortie is not a flip; two other steps trading names still are). npm test 2118 of 2118, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. No live probe of Jev on the new break_spawner text and no replay case: the recorded question was answered with false facts (one blaze in sight, 7.8 damage) and what Jev answers with the true ones was not run live; the argmax fix changes no text Jev is told. Still open: which the service means when its choice and distribution differ was decided by its documentation, not measured; whether break_spawner is ever right at 13 health with six blazes about a cage five blocks off is Jev's to weigh with the new price; not run live.
624. *Two trials busy and not progressing, 2026-09-28 18:22Z (main at e1f5819, notes to 623 live): a hoglin across the lava counted as a pusher for sixteen minutes, and a climb up its own shaft taken for standing still.* mid-243-bc (25583, nether, 79 minutes in): from 18:07:22 the bot stood at the south end of a one-wide netherrack ridge over the lava sea at (-77.5, 33, 365.1), the crossing south (cross_toward to (-77, 40, 445): 19 cells, 18 to lay over lava, 18 blocks carried) needing its first block laid over lava. Read from the flight frames and the region files: a hoglin stood 7.7 blocks off at (-83.5, 33, 360.4) on a crimson nylium block of its own in the lava, four cells of air over lava between it and the ridge. Walk-reach (walkersApart, note 560) says it has no way to the bot, run on the saved region (test/fixtures/ridge-hoglin-mid-243-bc.json); immediateThreat already leaves such a walker be (cannotGetToTheBot), but pushersAbout (danger.js, the count behind pushOverDrop, the pathfinder's and staircases' edge refusal and the arbiter's push preemption, note 586) counted every biter within eight blocks in sight, apart or not. So with lava beside the ridge's end the hoglin was a pusher: the arbiter preempted the work four times a second (1,352 'Preempted by push' frames), turn_priority was asked every ten seconds with the survival claim 'escape_threat' and answered survival at 0.89 to 0.96 each time (80 askings; the option said 'a hit's knockback ... into lava', which was true of nothing that could reach it), survival's escape had nothing to do ('its winner did nothing for 10 seconds'), and the crossing's edge cell was refused while something about could push. The stall ladder ran round it: stall strikes to 18, unstuck_move 54 times (34 within two seconds with nothing gained: step_north, step_south, pillar, place_north, dig_south_feet), work_free, until_rest_ends, keep_at_it, set_aside_rung and take_up, none_good 19 times on the moves. The moves were offered and priced honestly for what they were (single blocks: step_north 'stood there 7 times already', pillar a gravel up one, place moves not offered where gravel would fall over lava, dig_down not offered over lava) and the ledger did rest them (waysResting: 'rests 5 minutes more from here'; 4 holds, 3 re-asks, escalations to stillness_detour and rung_progress in the log), but every move answered was cut off within a second by the preemption or walked back by the crossing step at once, and the ladder began again as the rests ran out, each ladder three to four quick answers per way: a ledger that rests what came to nothing cannot rest the cause, and the cause was a fact that was false. The 621 wedge fix (LOSWhenPlacingBlocks) did not touch it: the bot restarted onto e1f5819 at 18:27:08Z and was at the same cell, survival asked every ten seconds, at 18:28. Fix at the rule: pushersAbout keeps the walkers with a way to the bot (cannotGetToTheBot, not for a shooter, not for one that has hit the bot within the attribution window), so every reader of a push (the claim, the preemption, the edge refusal, the option's edge fact) agrees with the threat check. Also found there: the stall's mine_nearby offered the quartz ore in the lava sea's wall to a bot with no pickaxe at every stall ('Dig the nether quartz ore 5 blocks away'), dig() said 'Missing harvest tool', and that error stayed on the goal as lastError, repeated on 1,676 frames; the detour now offers ore only where a tool carried can harvest it (block.harvestTools). mid-243-bd (25581, overworld, 17 minutes in): not stuck. At y 22 with the pickaxe worn out, three planks and no table, it pillared up its own dug shaft 74 blocks with gravel (climb_out 'straight_up', eight blocks a call, a block in six to eight seconds) and was on the surface at 18:21:03, a log taken, a stone pickaxe crafted by 18:23; walked 394, ended 6 from where it began, laid 375 because the shaft is one column. What the audit flagged as pacing was real work the stall watch called nothing: 45 seconds a strike (strikes to 10 on 'rung:stone pickaxe', 14 stillness_detour askings, 9 answered none_good since the answer was to go on climbing, some answered 'differently' and 'mine_nearby' in the middle of it). The watch's progress is new ground (three blocks from every cell stood in the last three minutes), something new carried, a block dug or placed in a cell not worked in ten minutes, or nearer the step's own target: a climb of a block in eight seconds is never three blocks from the cells of the last half minute, its cells are the ones the bot's own dig down marked, and the step named no target. climbStraightUp now names the open sky over the column (the step's and the survival action's target), so each block risen counts as nearer it. Tests: test/push-escape.test.js (the fixture of the ridge: the hoglin across the lava is no pusher and pushOverDrop is null; the same hoglin on the ridge is; one that has just hit the bot is again); test/stillness.test.js (a block in eight seconds up a shaft is a stall with no target and progress with the sky as target); test/surface.test.js (the straight-up step and its survival action carry the target); test/idle-detour.test.js (mine_nearby not offered without a tool that harvests the ore, offered with a stone pickaxe). npm test 2141 of 2141, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow (the test script sets JEV_NONE_GOOD=0; a test file run on its own without it fails 3 tests in surface.test.js and stillness.test.js on the added none_good option, at main too). No live probe of Jev and no replay case: no question text changed, and the turn_priority answers 'survival' were right for the facts it was given, which were false. Still open: nothing here rests the cause when a step's own error keeps coming back (the ledger rests ways from a place, and the crossing came back to the same ridge end each time; a fact such as 'the last four crossings from this ridge each ended at once, refused for a push' was not said to the crossing's question, because with the push fixed there was none); whether the wool a bot carries (four, here) should be a place/pillar block in unstuck.js beside the wart blocks (PLACEABLE lists rock, wart blocks, gravel and sand, not wool, note 619) was left for a trial that needs it; the fix is checked on the saved ground and by unit tests, not yet on the live bot (25583 was running the old code at 18:28).

The bot stood at (-78.3, 38, -88.9) on an island of four warped wart blocks it had laid, at (-80, 37, -91), (-80, 37, -90), (-79, 37, -89) and (-78, 37, -89), one cell (-81, 37, -91) short of the end of its own diagonal span of netherrack at (-82, 37, -91), which runs 50 blocks back over the sea. From 18:21 every walk was "no route" (the pathfinder takes no gap jump in the Nether, and none over lava anywhere: movement.js gapSurvivable), and the unstuck question (18:22:01, none_good 0.51) had steps on the island, a place of gravel (which falls into the lava) and no move that gave it a floor. 626. *Minutes at under 8 health in the Nether with nothing to eat, measured over 2026-09-28, and what was said and done wrong in them: mid-243-ag-fortress-5 (25589, 18:19:42Z) taken down off its own finished pillar into a hoglin at 3.5 health; mid-208-k-nether-3-fortress-6 (25587, 18:37:04Z) sent along a floor past two hoglins that were not priced.* Measured over the day's flight records (in the Nether, health under 8, hunger under 18, nothing carried that is food, broken by a gap of 90 seconds, as in note 607): 58 stretches of a minute or more, 13.3 hours in all, the median 5.8 minutes and the longest 146; 36 ended in a death (a mean 11.7 minutes in), 11 left the Nether, 6 came back over 8 (a porkchop or mutton eaten), 4 were a stage trial's restart at 20, one a gap. Since the food changes of note 607 went live (13:07): 16 stretches, 9 deaths (25591; 25594 twice; 25586; 25600; 25581; 25584; 25587; 25589), 3 restarts, 3 eaten, one left. Where the health went, in the deaths read (25587 at 17:28 and 18:24, 25589 at 17:56 and 13:24, 25591 at 13:15 and 13:22): 10 to 20 health in eight to thirty seconds to fireballs and the burning after them (one a second for up to eight seconds, no water) and to hoglin blows (1.5 to 4.8 through the armour worn), never to hunger. The stage trials start from a checkpoint (scripts/trials/start-stage.sh) with what the source world carried when it reached the Nether or the fortress: 25589's fortress-5 began with two raw mutton (4 food points), 25587's fortress-6 with two mutton at its fortress; the natural crossing of that world at 17:02 was asked the kit (crossing_kit: top_up_cook 0.38, cross_now 0.24) and carried 6 beef and 10 mutton raw, 41 points against the 80 of note 607, so a stay runs on what a stage carries and what the first fight leaves. Hunger at the start of the stretches was 11 to 17, one to seven points under what health needs; with nothing carried and only a hoglin to eat in the Nether, none of it came back. Was that said? On every question, yes: state.healing is on all of them and withoutFood on most (18:17:09's stillness_detour: "health 3.5 does not come back here: nothing carried is food, and in the Nether nothing but a hoglin is food", the trip back with its lava and "3.5 health is what it walks with", the hoglin fight "dead before the hoglin is"); the options that carry health are the stance's, the unstuck moves' and the stall's. What was not honest: (1) The walk back to a portal was priced "about 97 seconds at a walk" for 419 blocks (4.3 blocks a second). Over the day's records the bot's walks back (return_to_portal, cross_toward "the portal back", return_for_food) that began at more than 60 blocks and ran over a minute (181, scripts/nether-trips.js) made 17 blocks a minute in all, 23 for those that moved 20 blocks or more, 30 for those that came out, the stops for mobs, edges, drops and stalls counted; 22 came out in the Overworld, 18 ended in a death, 139 were given up, set aside or stalled. Of the 33 begun under 8 health, 4 came out, 6 died, 23 were dropped (25 blocks a minute). 419 blocks is 14 to 25 minutes, not 97 seconds. (2) The hunt of a hoglin for its meat was offered on the walk's terms and the fight's, and nothing of how it has gone: of the 66 hunts begun in the Nether that day none brought meat, 61 ended at the place a hoglin had been seen with none within thirty-two blocks (huntStep ends when none is within 32; the sighting is old) and 5 in a fight that took six health. (3) The way down to the floor toward the fortress leg, chosen at 10 health (floor_toward 0.48, cross_toward 0.14), said "By the floor that way: 2 hoglins" and nothing more, while the state said all the mobs about were 43 damage; both hoglins hit the bot at the foot of it (10 to 5.9, then to 1.9 under a shield_guard chosen against them, which was priced honestly: "about 8.1 damage ... (more than the bot has)", retreat 12, pillar 44, every option more than the bot had) and it died. (4) keep_on, the answer that leaves the trip back, is offered in that trip's stall and said "go on without the Overworld for twenty minutes"; 25589 had chosen go_back at 18:07:00 (0.52, 3.5 health, the portal 277 blocks off), the crossing stopped at a drop (the walk off got 0 of 8 blocks), and the stall's answers were dirt, cobblestone and keep_on with none good first each time (0.33, 0.39, 0.41): the best listed was taken, keep_on (0.26), which dropped the trip, and the bot went back to the fortress search 130 blocks the other way. Nothing said that keep_on ended the trip Jev chose three minutes before. What was wrong in the code: the edge reflex (survival.js flee, the step off the edge that runs with a stance held) kept a heavy hitter's toss as a reason to leave the bot's own pillar whether or not its blow reaches the top (note 250, "but for a heavy hitter's toss"). At 18:19:37, 3.5 health, a hoglin 8 blocks off, Jev chose the pillar (0.53, priced "about 0 damage ... Two up, none of them reaches it"), the two blocks were up at 18:19:38.65, at 18:19:39.04 off_the_edge took the bot to firm ground, shield_guard (0.82) at 18:19:41 with the hoglin 4 blocks off, struck at 18:19:42, dead. A mob's blow reaches as high as it stands (a hoglin 1.4, combat-estimate.js BODY_HEIGHT, from the jar), so on a top two up it does not: note 113's drills (hoglin_pair, three of three, no damage) and the flight records of 27 and 28 September say the same, 168 pillar stances against hoglins (asked within a second counted once) losing 0.1 health on average against 0.4 said with two deaths inside fifteen seconds, where the 16 shield_guard stances against hoglins lost 1.8 against 2.1 said with three deaths. Now: (1) the edge reflex counts, on the bot's own pillar top, only the heavy hitters whose blow reaches it (position.y plus its height above the feet), as the stance's own price does (survival.js topBody, reachesTop); a hoglin on a ledge as high as the top still moves the bot. (2) The trip back is said at the pace measured (game-progress.js NETHER_TRIPS, netherPaceSays; from sixty blocks, in the Nether only): "about 97 seconds at a walk if nothing stops it", then "In the Nether the bot's walks back to a portal made 17 to 30 blocks a minute over 2026-09-28's trials, the stops for mobs, edges and drops counted: about 14 to 25 minutes, not seconds. Of 181 such walks of over 60 blocks 22 came out in the Overworld, 18 ended in a death and the rest were given up, set aside or stalled", with the 33 begun under eight health when the bot is under eight; the hour it comes out at (arrivalSays) is counted at that pace. It reaches every portalTrip (leave_nether's go_back, the stall's and the pocket's return_for_food, the pearl and kit trips, the healing facts) and the walk to a hoglin seen 60 or more blocks off. (3) hoglinSays adds the day's hunts (nether-travel.js HOGLIN_HUNTS: 66 begun, 0 meat, 61 none within thirty-two blocks at the sighting, 5 a fight that took six health; `node scripts/nether-trips.js --hunts`). (4) A way along the floor prices the mobs by it (walkFloor mobsPrice, said by floorWalkSays, so the way toward a target, the fortress legs and nether_gather's floor way all carry it): "If they all came at the bot on that way, fighting them is about 25.7 damage from 10 health (more than the bot has); nothing carried is food and hunger 14 is under eighteen, so none of that health comes back". (5) keep_on and return_for_food say what they do to a trip Jev chose (goal.leaveNether, food, go_back, within half an hour; standingTripSays): keep_on "ends the trip back for food that Jev chose 3 minutes ago and that has stopped here, 277 blocks from the portal: the walk home is given up, not stalled"; return_for_food "the walk that has stopped here ... this tries the walk again from here, at 3.5 health". Tests (test/pillar-heavy-25589.test.js on the recorded stance, its first case failing before the change; test/low-health-625.test.js: the floor way's price at 10 health, the pace said from 60 blocks and not for 41 or in the Overworld, keep_on and return_for_food with and without the chosen trip and with one chosen 40 minutes before). Changed: nether-healing.test.js (the walk to a hoglin at the pace, the day's hunts, the trip's "if nothing stops it" and its minutes) and pearl-routes.test.js (the pearl trip's minutes; it now comes out at dusk, not by day). npm test 2143 of 2143, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Probed on the live model, the recorded askings as recorded and as told now, 5 runs each (10 for the replay case): 25587's stillness_detour at 18:36:25, recorded floor_toward 5 of 5 (0.44 to 0.49), now cross_toward 3 and floor_toward 2 (0.16 to 0.23 each); replay case floor-way-hoglins-10hp-25587: cross_toward 8, floor_toward 2. 25589's three stall askings at 18:09:58 (none good first, 0.33 to 0.46, then dirt or keep_on) and 18:17:09 (recorded cross_toward 4, work_free 1; now cross_toward 5, return_for_food 0.02 to 0.03 recorded, 0.03 to 0.06 now): no change, and none was expected: with the walk 14 to 25 minutes, a touch of lava on the line death and 3.5 health, the trip home is not a good route and the text now says why in minutes; the stall's missing move is a way past the drop toward the portal, which the surveys (cross_toward, floor_toward) did not find. Still open: (a) nothing in the Nether heals a bot at hunger under eighteen but a hoglin, and the hunt walks up and fights it; a hoglin killed from two up (the pillar stance lost 0.1 health on average in 168 stances against them, and a hoglin drops porkchops) is a real route to food at low health that the hunt does not have; (b) mushroom stew (a bowl from three planks, a red and a brown mushroom, 6 hunger) is a second route to eighteen hunger from what the Nether has, if its biomes have mushrooms near the fortress; I did not check the region data; (c) the stage trials start with what the checkpoint carried, so most stretches begin without the note 607 kit: the kit is Jev's to choose in a natural crossing and never asked in a stage; (d) all 11 hoglin blows that landed with the shield key held had the nearest hoglin dead ahead, but blocked blows leave no record, so whether the shield holds against a hoglin is not measured from this, and 25587's two low-health shield_guard askings had a second hoglin at its side or behind (1171, 1.9 blocks off left of the facing). Not run on the live trials.
627. *Custom dreams: "Jev your dream is to <anything a chat request could do>" (the owner's request).* Until now a dream was one of two, and any other "your dream is to ..." came back as a clarify listing them. dream_operation gains set_custom (option text: any single thing a request could ask for, with the examples "build a castle by the lake", "get me a stack of diamonds", "find a cherry biome"; the hypothetical stays none); it is set at the same 0.65 bar as the built-in dreams and replaces the current dream. Code cuts the text out of the message after "dream is to" (200 characters at most), then checks it with the routing a chat request gets (interpret, called without launching, without build continuation): a text that routes to other, a command, memory, status, stop, resume or another dream, or that asks a question back, is refused with a message asking for something the bot can do (or to say it as a request), and nothing is stored; a request the survival planner cannot do (unworkable, as for a chat request) is refused too. The intake question's dream option now says a dream can be one thing to do, so "your dream is to build a castle" routes to the dream and not to a build. Stored in the existing dream file as dream 'custom' with a text field (version 1 unchanged, old files load). When the bot is idle, the text is read again as a chat request with the world as it is (what is carried, what stands nearby) and launched as a goal with dream 'custom', source 'dream' and the dream's setAt, so a player's request replaces it, stop pauses it, and the cool-down and the two-minute rest after a failed launch apply as for the others. It is pursued once: when that goal completes the dream is marked satisfied, the bot says so in chat, and "chase your dream" starts it again as a new run. Attempts that end blocked, or whose text no longer comes out as a doable request, count one each (a blocked goal once however often it is looked at; Jev being unreachable does not count); at three the dream is paused with a chat message saying so, never retried forever. What is your dream reports the words and how it is going ("done", "working on it now", "2 tries so far"), and status says "Working on my dream: ..." while it runs. Two things found probing live Jev: "make the base nicer" routes as a plain build, so the routing alone did not refuse it, and a new question, dream_text_fit (doable, vague, several), asked beside the routing when a custom dream is set, is what refuses vague wishes and compound texts; and "your dream is to build a castle by the lake" went to memory in four of six asks (objective dream 0.86, but interaction discussion and the memory-statement question at 0.76 took it), so in interpret the memory-statement fallback no longer applies when the objective is the dream (six of six after). Live, after both: castle, diamonds and cherry biome set_custom with the text carried (castle probe routed build, diamonds obtain, cherry find), beat the game and build a village their built-ins, what is your dream query, "if your dream were to build a castle, would you need stone" other (never reaches the dream), "make the base nicer" and "be a good friend" refused, "get a stack of diamonds and then build a castle" refused (the objective was unsure between build and obtain). Tests in test/dream.test.js and test/status-dream.test.js: set_custom carries the text, unroutable texts are refused and not stored, the bar, the storage round trip with an old file, the request handed to the runner, completion, the failure limit, the report. Not run live in a world: the idle launch and the completion chat are session code with no unit test around them.
