The rung's record was also new at 18:01:12: nether_gather's "without" (leave the rods thirty minutes for the pearls) at 18:00:31 and the stall's take_up_obtain_blaze_rods at 18:00:32 replaced it while the ladder stood on the pearls for a second, and the 30 minutes before were dropped (not changed, below). Were the facts honest. The gathering's were: blocks needed against carried, the rock dug by hand with netherrack dropping nothing, lava, where the crossing ends and, for the portal, "Neither the walk nor the crossing with the blocks carried reaches it from here, so going back through it is not offered". The trip back's were not: leave_nether's go_back and the stall's return_for_food said "The nearest portal remembered is 148 (204) blocks off, about 34 (47) seconds at a walk" and the ground of the straight line (6 over lava, 78 on ground, 12 over a drop), nothing of the crossing, the pickaxe or the blocks (the pace text of note 626 was not in these builds). Jev chose go_back at 0.72 at 17:55:01 and return_for_food five times at 0.09 to 0.23 (none good the top or level with it), each choice renewing the ten-minute hold on go_back (chooseReturnForFood), so the way that could not be walked was the one always in hand. The stall's crossing option said "where the work was going" for the gathering's stems. How often the crossing had failed before was said nowhere, and it had not failed as the ledger reads a failure: each stretch moved; it had come to the same place. Nether_gather did not send the bot back to gather blocks or wart: it offered no block or wart source, and Jev asked for stems. Now, in general. (1) The rung's minutes are minutes (tried.js idleSince): within one run a look credits the time since the last, up to the rung's ten; the first look after a start credits 30 seconds, and a gap that began in a wait something was bringing to an end (asleep, a batch cooking, health coming back) credits nothing. (2) A walk toward a place is judged by how near it came, not by how far it moved (tried.js reachOf, settleOne): an answer with a target (option.target) that began within 64 blocks of where the nearest earlier answer of its question toward that place ended, and ended no nearer (by 2 blocks), is not getting somewhere unless something else came of it (something carried, a block dug in a cell not dug in ten minutes, the stall watch's progress); it is settled blocked, said "ended 6 blocks from it, no nearer than the 6 an answer toward it reached 4 minutes before this began", and its way rests after two as any does. The other ways to the same place from about there that came to nothing so are the same failure (about() reads them as kin: on foot and straight across were one tunnel to one stem): left out with it, said. A walk brought from afar is ground made whatever the best before. (3) The trip's facts (game-progress.js wayBackSays, so go_back, return_for_food, the pocket's and the healing question's trips): where the crossing straight at the portal ends and what it digs and lays, from the tool and the blocks carried, in the sentence the gathering says (nether-gather.js reachSays), and "With what is carried that crossing stops 146 blocks short of it." where it does. The stall's crossing names the place the work was going where the step names it (the crimson stems at (-178, 72, -112), nether-travel.js legTarget). (4) A stretch of the crossing that would end no nearer the portal than the bot has come is not walked (nether-travel.js crossToward, beat; work.js approachBest): it is ground made already, and it took the bot away from what the pass needed next; said in the way's words ("a crossing straight at the portal back would go 32 blocks and end 191 blocks from it, no nearer than the 148 the bot has already come"), and the pass goes on to the staircase and the wood. Shown on the saved ground (the fixture, groundBot, the pathfinder's own failure): from the stems' foot with the record at 148, walkToKnownPortal no longer begins a crossing and goes to nether_gather (with the beat dropped, crossToward is called at once and cross_toward is set as the step). Tests (test/flip-629.test.js, each fails with its change switched off): the rung's ten minutes count passes of 4.6 and 4.4 minutes and are due at 11 minutes, count 30 seconds after a restart and nothing after a wait; the recorded round through begin and settle, the first walk to the stems progressed, the second and third blocked with the words above, the summary "cross to 1 ... 1 of them getting somewhere, 2 coming to nothing", read leaving out cross_to_1 and walk_to_1 and keeping another place's way, and from a hundred blocks away nothing resting; a walk nearer than before, one that dug a block in a new cell, and one brought from afar are progress; portalTrip on the saved ground says the crossing's 109 cells, 48 of rock dug by hand, where it ends and that it stops short, and says nothing against a crossing that reaches; crossToward with the record at 148 does not begin, sets no step and says why; the stall's crossing names the stems. npm test 2170 of 2170, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 67 of 70 with the three known gaps. Probed against the live model, six each, on the recorded states (mine_nearby left out of the stall's, as note 624's code does): the stall at 18:16:26, before none good 6 of 6 with return_for_food the best listed (0.21 to 0.26, none good 0.26 to 0.29), after the trip's crossing said return_for_food 0.16 to 0.24 and none good 0.29 to 0.34, cross_toward and return_for_food the best listed in turn; leave_nether at 17:55:01, go_back 6 of 6 before (0.70 to 0.74, keep_on 0.21 to 0.25) and 6 of 6 after (0.67 to 0.75, keep_on 0.20 to 0.26): with the crossing's ending said Jev still goes back, which is not wrong (the way back needs a pickaxe made first), so the facts alone did not change it and the crossing's order and the ledger are what end the loop; nether_gather at 18:14:31, recorded cross_to_1 0.46 (6 of 6), with cross_to_1 resting walk_to_1 6 of 6 (0.44 to 0.57), with both resting leg_west 6 of 6 (0.28 to 0.37, without 0.21 to 0.27). Added to the replay suite as gather-stems-resting-25586 (expect leg_west, without or another place's way; forbid none good), 5 of 5 leg_west. Still open: a rung's record is replaced whenever the ladder stands on another rung, a second included, so the rods lost the 30 minutes they had (a record kept per rung and resumed if left under ten minutes is the shape); the fortress legs have no target, so leg_east and leg_west over the tunnel just dug are still "moved 62 blocks" and getting somewhere, how many of a leg's blocks the bot has stood on before said only on the option; a leg into rock with no pickaxe still digs blind for five minutes on Jev's choice, said; that the mine step at the stems' foot reaches stems 6 up (a staircase dug by hand) is not shown here, only that the crossing no longer takes the pass first; a crossing dug with the pickaxe's last 17 uses does not say what the uses were for; 6 nether bricks, 4 oak planks and 16 gravel were carried and blocksCarried said 0 (bridging.js LAID); none of this has run live.

630. *mid-243-bd (25581, first-days 243), 18:05 to 19:33Z on 2026-09-28, "loop: flipping enter_nether <-> tunnel": seventy minutes on "reach the Nether", a frame begun at (39, 110, -51) and nine buckets of lava carried, never a water bucket, and the Nether never entered.* Read from the flight frames (7,397 of them), the bot log and the code. What "enter nether" needs here: ten obsidian in a lit frame, cast in place (a slot walled, lava poured in, water poured on it, ten times) and then flint and steel. What the tunnel is: the staircase to the frame (tunnelToward, "return_to_frame"), not to a lava pool or to iron (the iron tunnels at 19:12 to 19:15, "steps 166 to 196", are the pickaxe rung's own). The minutes: the rung from 18:22:51; 18:33:42 portal_method craft_buckets (nine buckets from iron), then cast_at_lava (0.44) and flint and steel made; a climb out of the cave for a frame site (none level down there) and the frame set out on a hilltop 43 blocks over the pool; 18:37 to 18:39 nine lava buckets scooped, a slot each with the pack full, so the room question dropped coal, the flint and steel, cobblestone and leaf litter; 18:41:06, room for four sticks, Jev chose the water bucket (its drop note said what it was for). From then no water, and the cast asks for water first at every slot (portal-cast.js). Why it went round: every pass buildPortalFrame, with lava in hand and 8 blocks or more from the frame, walked back to the frame (work.js, the rule of note 481 that fetching lava is the cast's own business), castFrame found no water and called for a water bucket, the search for it (explore, one leg a pass, step fill_bucket) walked ten or twenty blocks toward a heading, and the next pass walked back. The frames show it: enter_nether and fill_bucket trading places, never more than 47 blocks from the frame in the two windows (18:42 to 19:03 and 19:18 to 19:25), 41 search_heading askings for water in 36 minutes with headings west and south-west traded every half minute, and the leg counts starting again at one after a stall 12 times (looseEnds' turnSearch dropped legsByHeading). A river stood 72 blocks south-west in the state of every question (biomesNearby) and in the words of none of the ways: portal_method said "a water bucket (none carried)"; the stall's question said "45 seconds on reach nether without getting anywhere" with "heading south west, 7 times, 7 of them getting somewhere" and no word of what the rung lacked; travel_river was on offer in 7 of 36 stall questions and never chosen (0.02), "walk to the river and carry on from there" being nothing to a bot not told it needs water. The tunnel flips, 19:03 to 19:10 and 19:31 to 19:33: the bot had gone underground (a night-mine detour, the pickaxe rung) and the frame was 85 blocks up. Each pass tried the walk (five to eight seconds to fail) and then one stair, a block up every six seconds ((37, 26, -25) to (37, 37, -38) in 83 s: it gained), so five names in 13 seconds within three blocks read as a flip, and each stall's detour (take_up_bed, look_around, explore) took it off the shaft. The ledger: the tunnel was not what came to nothing, and the rung's ten minutes never ran on one record. The ladder turned reach_nether to the stone and iron pickaxe rungs and back (18:52:00, 19:10:35, 19:12:44), watchRung replaced its one record at each turn, and each record's quiet was cut by new bests (nearer the frame, "new country" from the night-mine detours); rung_progress was asked 0 times in 70 minutes, and the arbiter's rule run over the recorded positions has it due at 18:52:30. Whether the options were complete: for lava yes (a pool 52 blocks off, cast_at_lava, cast_frame, build_new); for water no way was offered as such and no place said; no search for a ruined portal is offered (none was known within 512 blocks; explore says a ruined portal means obsidian). Now, in general. (1) A cast that lacks water is not walked back to its frame: castLacksWater (no water bucket, no obsidian to place as it is, none of the cast's own standing to scoop back) fetches the bucket from where the bot is, the order castFrame itself keeps; stairs begun toward the frame go on without a walk tried first each pass while each pass brings the bot nearer (as the lava's, note 603), which ends the flip. (2) Facts: the ways to a portal say "Water, for a bucket of it: no water in view within 48 blocks; the nearest seen is the river 72 blocks south-west (...)" (water.js waterKnown: a source in view, else the nearest biome seen that holds water, a cave's drowned water not counted); the stall's and the rung's state say what the cast is waiting for (stalled.lacking) and the travel to a biome with water says it is where the bucket fills; the water bucket's drop note says where the trip would be. (3) The rung's record is kept across the ladder's turns to other rungs for three of its budgets (tried.left), the minutes away not counted. (4) The search's legs by heading survive a stall's turn. Probed against the live model, the recorded 18:58:29 stall question: as recorded explore 8 of 8; with the lack and the river said travel_river 8 of 8, and 10 of 10 with the words as the code says them; replay case cast-lacks-water-river-said 5 of 5. Tests (test/water-cast-630.test.js, all but the record's expiry fail before): the lack; no walk to the frame when it lacks water and a walk when it does not; held stairs, and the walk again when they gain nothing; where water is known; the ways say it; the stall says what is lacking and the river's travel says it has water; a rung turned from and come back to goes due across the turn, and one left for long begins new; legs survive the turn; and the drop note in test/inventory-tidy.test.js. npm test 2171 of 2171, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Still open: Jev dropped the water bucket and the flint and steel for room with what they were for said (the pack held nine lava buckets, a slot each; it dropped a made iron pickaxe for raw iron at 19:28 as well and made another, four times), so the fix there is the trip's distance in the note, not a rule, and the cast's fetch does not weigh the slots nine lava buckets need against the water bucket and lighter it will drop; the frame was set 43 blocks over its lava after "cast at lava", a site rule left as note 531 has it; not run live.
632. *mid-243-bf (25581, fresh world from first-days 243), 19:36 to 20:02Z on 2026-09-28, "loop: 3× Repeated server movement corrections at the same position": the view of the blocks had air where the server held dirt, and the server put the body back about a thousand times in two minutes.* Read from the flight frames, the bot log, the world's saved region files and the server's own recording of the packets it sent the bot (recordings/players/.../2026-09-28--15-44-27.mcpr, ReplayMod's format, read with minecraft-protocol's 26.1 decoder). Where and what: the overworld, cell (23, 79, -5), the foot of the bot's own dug staircase down toward a lava pool (go_to_landmark, then the fill_bucket walk to (16, 69, -7)); a walk, not a dig, at 19:57:33.6: the body came down the last step at y 79.23 and from then the server teleported it to y 79.075 every tick (595 position packets in the first minute, 1,075 by 19:59:26). The client's next physics tick took it to 78.996, 0.004 into the top face (y 79.0) of (23, 78, -5); the server refused that and set it back; the client fell again. What the server had: dirt at (23, 78, -5), put there by the bot's own pillar cycle at 19:55:11.6 (block_change dirt, three times) and never sent air again in all the recording until 19:59:26. What the view had: air (the body fell through it; never on the ground in those two minutes). Nothing in the packets ever told the client that cell was air, and the one place mineflayer changes its view without the server is dig: when a dig's time is up it writes air into the world and sends "finished", and the dig resolves on that local write (digging.js finishDigging; the pathfinder's own dig, bot.dig(block, true), is the same call), so a block the server does not break stays in the game and is gone from the view. Why the server did not break that dirt is not in the recording (nothing the bot sends is), and the server ran at 20.0 ticks a second throughout; a dig the server ignored is the one client-side path to this state, and the rest is by elimination, said as such. What it tried, and why none of it could work: the walks (navigate's watch threw at four corrections in half a second, its recovery walked the body inward and refused, y over .05 from the floor), the stall's shake_loose (stage 2 dug stone beside it, moved: false), a stall question that offered footing at (23, 78, -7), then unstuck_move seventeen times (climb, place, dig, bridge and step moves each way, a pillar, dig_down last; eight of them none_good, the missing option taken): every move read from the view, and from a cell that changed with the body's jitter (79.075 floors to 79, 78.996 to 78, so the moves said 'pillar' and 'dig_down' on every other look, and perform refused a move read from another cell); and the ladder's escalation. What ended it: at 19:59:26 recover_1 (return to surface, straight up) put a block against the face of (23, 78, -5) and the server answered, as it always does to a use of a face, with the block it holds there and the block across the face: (23, 78, -5) dirt, (23, 79, -5) air. The view was right from that packet, the body stood on the dirt (y 79.000, on the ground) and went on down. The verdict is not an artifact of a count over a long time: attempts 1 to 6 of the same persist problem in one 2-minute stall (three seen at the frames' one-second sampling), and the stall did end, at 19:59:27, three minutes before the verdict; the rule (three attempts is a loop) is the audit's, and is left. Now: src/server-truth.js. (1) A dig is finished when the server has said so: wrapped after the dig guard, bot.dig waits (a second at most) for the server's block_change or multi_block_change at the cell with a state other than the one dug; with none, it asks the server about the cell, takes the block back into the view if it is still there for the server, tries the dig once more, and then throws DigNotConfirmed with the block in the view (a block the server had already broken answers air, and the dig ends well). (2) Asking: a use of a block's face is sent through a neighbour that is solid in the view and nothing a use would work (doors, chests, tables and the like), toward the cell, with the off hand when it is empty or a shield, else the main hand when empty or a pickaxe or sword, never a block, a bucket, flint and steel or an axe; the server's answers are applied by the client's own handling and what differed is returned. Nothing is placed or broken. (3) The server putting the body back five times in two seconds at one place, whatever the bot is doing, asks about the 36 cells round the body (at most three times a minute); a walk that meets the loop asks too (skills.js navigate) and, if the view was corrected, walks again; if it was not, the failure carries the facts (err.facts: the corrections and that the server's answers matched the view), which persist puts in the step's record and in the question's "failed" text. The problem text stays as it was: the audit groups by it. (4) unstuck_move: when a loop is noted within five minutes and three blocks, the state carries serverCorrections (how many times in how many seconds, where, that the body is held 0.07 over the top of the cell the view calls air, and what an asking found) and a move ask_server, a resync that is exempt from the "read from another cell" check. Jev is the one who chooses it there; the asking by the watcher and the walk is mechanics (making the view the server's), not a choice. Not done: the moves themselves are still read from the cell the body floors to at each look; a body sneaking at an edge, in a boat or on a slab that the server counts differently is not covered by this (no such case in this loop). Probe on the recorded question (19:58:36, unstuck_move, live Jev, eight runs each): as recorded (no serverCorrections, no ask_server) place_north 7, step_north 1; with the facts and the move ask_server 8 of 8. Replay case server-holds-block-view-lacks-ask (evals/replays, 5 of 5). test/server-truth.test.js: 13 tests on a simulated client and server (the dig confirmed, refused and already done; hands; doors; the view corrected and said; the watcher and its three a minute; the walk; the move). npm test 2199 of 2199 (with JEV_ARBITER=shadow the same). Not run live (the trial ports are off limits to this work): the server's half is shown by the recording, the fix's by the simulation, and whether the dirt in the recording was really a refused dig is not shown by either.
631. *Blaze and fire deaths of 2026-09-28, measured from the flight records: 70 of the day's 289 deaths (9 of the 15 from 19:00 to 19:50Z, 22 of the 36 from 17:00), and what the questions said of the fireball that ended them.* Method: scripts/blaze-record.js (`--to 2026-09-28T19:50:00Z`; `--deaths`, `--landings`) reads every connection's frames; a death is health reaching zero and its cause the game's own line (recentDeaths of the next question): 35 "burned to a crisp while fighting Blaze", 28 "fireballed by Blaze", 3 "slain by Blaze", 3 "burned to death", 1 "went up in flames"; a fight is a run of blazes in sight within 24 blocks or hurting the bot, a gap of 30 seconds ending it (415 of them: 79 ended in a death, 42 in a rod, 54 rods). The nine from 19:00 to 19:50Z (health when the fight began; stances in order with the health each was asked at; landings; nearest blaze at death): 19:01:54 25586, 20, take_cover 20, charge_nearest 20, charge_nearest 10.4, three blazes at arm's length (blows 9.6, one landing), 4.5 off; 19:06:03 25587, 10.7, 253 seconds and 26 answers turning back_to_wall, corner_ambush and take_cover from 10.7 to 4.5 at the cage at (-204, 57, -150), one landing at 4.5, 3.5 off; 19:32:23 25584, 1.7 (hunger 8 earlier), take_cover, rail_and_fight, out_of_sight at 1.7, one landing from a blaze 22.5 off; 19:32:24 25589, 3.4, out_of_sight twice, one landing and a tick from a blaze 24.9 off; 19:37:33 25587, 15.6, charge_nearest 15.6, retreat 9.4, take_cover, back_to_wall twice, corner_ambush 4.5, a landing 6.5 seconds before at 9.4, alight 7 seconds, none of 7 blazes in sight, "burned to death"; 19:39:30 25594, 1.7, out_of_sight twice, corner_ambush twice, one landing, 4.3 off; 19:42:01 25584, 20, charge_nearest, retreat, charge_nearest, leave_and_heal 15.5, charge_nearest 18.5, retreat, out_of_sight 13, charge_nearest 9.5 and 6.5, retreat, out_of_sight 3, four landings and 15 ticks of fire in 89 seconds, the last landing at 6.5 with the nearest blaze 27.6 off and four ticks left; 19:44:49 25589, 7.6, charge_nearest, box_here, retreat, fight 5.1, leave_reach 4.1, three landings in 21 seconds, 8.5 off; 19:47:03 25587, 20, twelve answers (leave_and_heal 16.1, take_cover, retreat, corner_ambush, charge_nearest, fight 8.2, corner_ambush 2.3 and 0.3), three landings and 11 ticks, 7.3 off. A way to break the line was offered in the last stance question in 62 of the 64 deaths that had one (take_cover, corner_ambush, box_here, seal, back_to_wall, out_of_sight, nook or bunker); it was chosen in 37 of 64 and the deaths came anyway. (1) Damage: in the last minute of the 70 deaths 1,021 health went: 49% fireballs that landed, 40% the fire they set (on_fire ticks and standing in flames), 7% blows from a blaze at arm's length, 4% other. 39 of the 70 were killed by a fire tick, 31 by a fireball or a blow; of the 63 with a landing in their last fifteen seconds, 38 were alive after the hit and the fire finished them. A landing costs its hit and four ticks of fire: 565 landed in the day, 357 on a bot not alight and burned out before the next, and 293 of those took exactly four ticks (the first a second after the hit, then one a second; five seconds of fire, none at the fifth), hits 2.5 to 3.9 through the iron worn and 5 with none: 6.5 through full iron, half of it fire and more at heavier armor. 44 of the 70 died alight, 44 had burned out at least once earlier in the same fight (142 stretches, 3.9 seconds each, alight a median 12% of a fight). The killing landing came at 6.5 health or less in 48 of the 63 (29 at 4 or less, 19 from 4 to 6.5; 4 from 6.5 to 8, 6 from 8 to 12, 5 over 12), where one landing is the end; the last stance answer was asked at 4 or less in 39 of 64, 4 to 8 in 17, over 8 in 8. Fights began at over 16 health in 42 of the 70, 8 to 16 in 12, under 8 in 16. The nearest blaze at death was within 8 blocks in 36, 8 to 16 in 11, 16 to 24 in 8, over 24 in 14; one was in sight in 63 of 69. (2) Alight at low health with no blaze near, the fire was stated plainly: every question carries burningSays ("it dies of the burning in about 3 seconds, before the fire ends, unless water puts it out first", the Nether has none), and 18 of the 23 stance questions asked at a health no greater than the seconds of fire left said so (the other five were within a tick of it by the code's rounding, or in flames); 25584's 19:41:59 stance at 3 health carried it in its state. Real options: eating, with food carried, outran the fire. Of 8 stance answers to eat while alight at 9 health or less, the three with blazes 13 or more blocks off healed (6.4 to 14.6 in 15 seconds; 5.8 to 9.4; 6.5 down to 2.5 and back to 5.5) and the five with blazes within 7 died (hunger 17 to 20 gives a point each half second while the saturation lasts, twice the fire's rate). But in 14 of the 16 deaths with the nearest blaze 15 or more off and a stance question asked the bot had nothing to eat, at hunger 12 to 17, where no health comes back; one carried two raw mutton (4 points, hunger 15) and one, the fall into lava at 17:06, had food and hunger 19. A golden apple was never carried, no fire resistance, and the water bucket does nothing in the Nether. Read from the 26.1.2 jar, one more exists that no question offers: a water cauldron puts a body out (LayeredCauldronBlock.entityInside applies InsideBlockEffectType.EXTINGUISH; CauldronInteractions' fill from a water bucket has no dimension check, unlike pouring), 7 iron ingots, three fills; whether the bot can stand in one was not tried. Not built: see below. (3) Stances at 8 health or less with a blaze in sight (224 answers; blaze damage in the next 10 seconds, then deaths within 10 seconds): take_cover 91, 1.4, 23 died; back_to_wall 24, 1.1, 5; retreat 23, 2.1, 8; corner_ambush 14, 1.7, 6; eat 10, 4.1, 6; out_of_sight 10, 1.9, 4; close_in 8, 1.6, 3; leave_and_heal 7, 3.9, 4; box_here 5, 2.9, 2; dig_down 5, 2.3, 3; seal 5, none (26 with none in sight counted, 0.1, none died). Not alight (134): take_cover 48, 0.9, 8 died; back_to_wall 19, 0.9, 4; corner_ambush 9, 0.8, 3; close_in 7, 1.0, 2; out_of_sight 5, 1.1, 1; retreat 14, 1.7, 5; box_here 5, 2.9, 2; leave_and_heal 4, 4.6, 3. Alight (90): take_cover 43, 2.0, 15 died; retreat 9, 2.7, 3; eat 8, 4.0, 5. What stood behind a block (cover, the wall at the back, the corner, out of sight) took about half or less of what walking, eating or healing in their line took, close_in among them at these small counts, and none of it did anything for the fire already on the body: the deaths inside them are the fire of a landing before the answer, which is why the killing landing was at 6.5 or less. At over 8 health the same rows: take_cover 586 answers, 2.0; corner_ambush 0.9 (11); box_here 2.3; out_of_sight 2.1; back_to_wall 2.6; charge_nearest 3.0; leave_and_heal 3.1; retreat 3.2; close_in 3.6; fight 5.7; fight_at_spawner 4.6. The prices of the holding stances ran two to three times the damage they took (take_cover priced 5.6 on the mean over 677 answers, 2.2 taken in 15 seconds; at 8 or less 5.2 against 1.6); not looked at here. The fights: begun over 16 health 307, 14% died, 12% brought a rod; 8 to 16, 82, 24% and 6%; under 8, 26, 58% and none; hunger under 18 (no healing) 160, 24% and 6%, at 18 or more 255, 16% and 13%; iron armor four pieces 18% died, two or three 20%, none or one 16% (no difference); one blaze or none within 16 blocks 141, 13% and 11%, two 76, 25% and 13%, three or more (a spawner's) 198, 21% and 9%. (4) The cage at (-108, 77, 155), read from the region files: on a three-high brick pedestal in a walled room, its west wall a row of fence windows on a 5 by 5 antechamber at y 74 to 77 that a straight three-wide corridor from the west runs into; the blazes hover over the room at head height and shoot through the windows at the antechamber's floor. 17 of the day's 70 deaths were within 30 blocks of it (12 in its rooms: 04:03, 04:56, 05:58, 10:55, 15:52, 17:52, 17:56, 18:01, 18:17 twice, 19:01, 19:37), from saves that begin within a minute or two of it (21 of the 70 fights began within two minutes of connecting: the stage saves start at fortresses). It is not the deadliest per visit. Connections that came within 30 blocks of each cage today, deaths and rods gained: this one 120, 17 (14%), 28 rods; (-204, 57, -150), an open cage over the lava sea with no walls, 75, 18 (24%), 19; (297, 57, 199) 27, 9 (33%), 10; (-84, 66, 190) 30, 4, none; (-160, 80, 166) 39, 6 (15%), 23; (-171, 57, 442) 11, 3, none. What the cage does, counted: blazes within 16 blocks at first sight a median 2 (0 to 8), 5 by 20 or 30 seconds, 6 to 8 by a minute in the fights there that lasted so long (04:03:49: 3, 4, 7, 7 at 0, 20, 50 and 60 seconds; 17:56:35: 2, 5, 5, 6; 18:17:02: 8 from the start). Now, in general. (a) A landing is counted with its fire (combat-estimate FIRE_TICKS = 4, landingCost, landingsToEnd, landingsApart, landingsSays). The stance's "At H health, N fireballs end it" was ceil(H / 2.5): "at 3 health, 2 fireballs (about 2.5 each) end it", "at 12, 5". It says now "At 3 health, 1 fireball from the blaze that lands ends it: it is about 2.5 after armour and sets the bot alight for 5 seconds, about 4 more health from the fire (6.5 for one landing)"; at 12 "2 fireballs from the blaze that land from separate volleys end it (...), or 4 in one volley, whose fire is one fire"; alight, "the burning alone ends the bot; a fireball that lands only hurries it", with the fire still to come taken off the landing's. The coin-toss margin of note 628 counts a blaze's blow as the landing ("less than the 6.5 of one fireball that lands (its hit and its fire)"); the pocket's "or N blaze fireballs that land" (hit and 5, ceil(H / 7.5)), body_way's shooters and the crossing kit's and the approach's netherHitSays ("about 2.5 hit and 5 burn", "3 fireballs end it" at 15.6) now say four ticks, the landing whole, and how many end it from separate volleys and within one. (b) The played record (src/blaze-record.js, the day's rows to 19:50Z; the sentence says the row the bot is in by its health and hunger, the blazes about, iron armor, and where the deaths' damage went) is in the state of encounter_stance and hunt_target with blazes about and of fortress_approach with blazes at the bricks (playedRecord), and said in their instructions. (c) The fight in the open at a live spawner is priced with the blazes it puts in over the fight's own seconds (blaze-stand.js spawnerNewcomers, one about every 6.25 seconds up to six, counted at the cage and iterated as the fight lengthens), said with the count at the cage today; and the spawner is said whenever one is near a blaze hunt, not only with more than one blaze reaching. The facts move Jev to walls and lower its confidence, and nothing here says a better answer exists at 3 health alight with nothing to eat: there is none. No replay case: the answers were given on false counts, and which of cover, box and corner is right is not one answer. Tests (test/blaze-record-631.test.js, ten, and test/mob-hunt.test.js, two changed or added, each failing before): the landing's cost and the counts (one at 3 and 6.5, two at 7, apart and in one volley at 12, the fire still to come counted, the burning alone), the stance's sentence at 3, 6.5, 7 and 12 and not at 20, and alight; the margin over a landing; the record's rows by health, hunger and blazes about, in the stance's state with blazes among the threats, and both questions' instructions; scripts/blaze-record.js on frames (a fight by its blazes in sight and its gap, its death, rod and health, hunger and iron rows; a landing's ticks, relit or burned out or alight from the one before; a death's game line, last minute's damage and the health before its last landing); the fight at a cage priced with the newcomers, more than without, and unchanged where no cage is seen, and the hunt's state carrying the record; the approach's state carrying it with four ticks and both counts; test/survival.test.js's pocket expectation (at 7 health a landing is 6.5 and two end it, not one). npm test 2197 of 2197 (main at 8879f22, notes 629 and 630 in), the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Still open: (i) the cauldron: fire is 40% of the damage and 56% of the killing blows, and a filled cauldron a step from where the bot fights would put a fire out for 7 iron ingots and the water bucket the bot already carries and cannot pour; that is a build, a place and a walk into it, and the arena (scripts/arena.js, port 25574) should price it before Jev is offered it; (ii) the fight estimates' burn piece still counts five seconds of fire at a health a second where four ticks land (about a point over per landing; the landings a shield took set none and the 15% whose fire was cut short are in the same average); (iii) the prices of the holding stances run two to three times what they took; (iv) a heal-and-return cycle at a cage that changes health every time is never a cycle to the ledger; (v) the stage saves start beside the cages, so their fights begin at the row they begin at, and a natural run's approach (the three deaths 164 to 205 minutes in) is the one with the choice; (vi) a fight begun over 16 health still died 14% of the time and took a rod 12%; not run live.

636. *"Why don't we go after bastion chests?" The owner's question, and what the code had: no wall, a hidden rule, and no trip.* Read first: the header of src/looting.js said nothing in the Nether is opened and a bastion's chests were never touched, while lootableChests had opened them "whoever is looking" since d2992ab whenever the bot happened to stand within 24 blocks (the gold rung, bartering.js gatherBastionGold, called lootNearby on arrival), the idle trip left bastions out (unlootedLandmarks), and no question ever put the chests against what a lid does. Nobody had chosen; a rule had, without the facts. Read from the 26.1.2 jar: (1) the lid: ChestBlock.openMenu calls PiglinAi.angerNearbyPiglins(level, player, true); it takes getEntitiesOfClass(Piglin.class, player box inflated 16), keeps those idle (Activity.IDLE) and, with the flag, those that BehaviorUtils.canSee the player, and setAngerTarget on each (no armor look at all). So gold armor does not calm a piglin the lid angered, and a piglin brute is not touched by the lid at all (PiglinBrute is not a Piglin); a brute goes after a player it sees within 12 on its own, gold or not (note 576). (2) the loot, data/minecraft/loot_table/chests/bastion_{bridge,other,hoglin_stable,treasure}.json, worked to gold in ingots (a block nine) and chances at the average rolls: bridge about 2.1 ingots' worth, a gold armor piece each 11%, a crossbow 11%, no food, no golden apple; housing about 2.6 (golden apple 10%, golden carrots 13%, cooked porkchop 24%); hoglin stable about 4.5 (gold block 16%, golden apple 10%, golden carrots 10%, porkchops 23%, ancient debris 16%, netherite scrap 8%); treasure about 14.6 (gold block 34%, ingots 34%, netherite ingot 35%, scrap 20%, debris 32%, diamond gear, an ENCHANTED golden apple 5%, and the netherite upgrade template in every treasure chest: its pool has no empty roll; 1 in 10 elsewhere). At the measured nine ingots a pearl a bridge or housing chest is a fifth to a quarter of a pearl, a stable's half, a treasure chest about a pearl and a half: the chests are a real route, not a rich one, except the treasure room. (3) the mobs: the bastion's jigsaw pools fill posts, an ordinary piglin post with a sword piglin 4 in 10, a crossbow piglin 4 in 10, a brute 1 in 10, nothing 1 in 10; a melee post (bastion/mobs/piglin_melee) a brute 6 in 7 (melee_piglin and melee_piglin_always are both piglin_brute) and a sword piglin the rest; hoglin stables have hoglin posts. How many posts a bastion has is in no table: said as not known. Built: src/bastion-raid.js and the question bastion_raid (src/decisions/work.js, area strategy, parent rung_progress, ledgered like the others), asked once per bastion trip at the top of gatherBastionGold and held 45 minutes (or to a death, or to the raid closing), offered only in the Nether with a bastion remembered within 384 blocks whose walk is not resting. Three options: raid_chests (walk there, open the nearest chest, take the loot list, on to the next), gold_only (what the rung did before: the gold blocks and gilded blackstone no piglin is within 16 of, no chest), leave_it (the rung rests thirty minutes). Told: the distance and legs (goToLandmark's leg is up to 120 seconds; the last walk there), the mobs in view now by kind and nearest (brutes first) and that the rest is not counted, gold armor worn or not and what it does and does not do, health, hunger, food, the jar's chest table by room, what the lid does, the fights priced by combat-estimate (one brute, one piglin, three piglins, and everything in view; a brute runs 5.3 a second against the bot's sprint of 5.6) marked as the game's numbers and not a measurement, what the gold and golden apples help with, the record, and the loot code's guard. The record: no bastion chest has ever been opened by the bot in any trial (RECORD in bastion-raid.js, day 2026-09-28), said as not yet tried, with no rate; each raid chosen is an entry in goal.bastionRaids (pending, looted with what it took, nothing, died when a death follows it, declined) and the last three at that bastion are said the next time it is asked and on the raid option. looting.js: a bastion chest is opened only while raidOn(goal) (the flag on goal.bastionRaid, pick raid_chests, not ended, within the hold); a chest among four or more blackstone blocks is inferred a bastion's whichever landmark was written down (before, one fifty blocks from the recorded bastion was "a chest seen" and was opened with no piglin in sight); the TNT-beside-chest shun stays for every chest; a raid looks for chests within 40, not 24; netherite_upgrade_smithing_template and porkchops join the LOOT list. One safety gap closed with it: the survival layer left a piglin be while gold was worn until one struck (danger.js hostileEntities), which after a lid is the opposite of what the game does, so the piglins within 16 that could see the lid are marked provoked the moment the window opens (looting.js angerFromLid). Not changed: the guards in lootNearby (no chest under 10 health or with a mob that bites in sight within 16), trip-kit's light pack, the stances. Priced from the game's numbers only: the arena has no bastion (a drill would need the jigsaw structure or a hand-built copy of a room, piglins with crossbows and a brute, and the lid's anger, which is server-side and needs the real chest; not cheap, not built). Probed live (TypeSafe, five asks, then five again after the brute's chase facts were added; the state from a fake body, a bastion 190 blocks off): full health, gold helmet, iron chest, legs and boots, twelve cooked beef, iron sword: raid_chests 0.63 (confidence 0.50), gold_only 0.30; the same again 0.66/0.28; 6 health, hunger 8, nothing to eat, a stone sword, two iron pieces: leave_it 0.55 (0.66 before the chase facts), raid_chests 0.16; 16 health with a brute 22 blocks off and two piglins at 30 and 34: raid_chests 0.54, gold_only 0.28, leave_it 0.15; 20 health, full iron, diamond sword, no gold worn: raid_chests 0.50, gold_only 0.33. Read: it weighs health and food correctly, and at full health it leans raid even though the estimate it is told says one brute kills a fully iron bot with an iron sword (31.8 damage from 20, about 14 seconds) and that a brute already close is not outrun; with a brute in view it did not change. Confidence is low throughout (0.34 to 0.55). Left as answered: no fact was missing that the state could say; whether Jev is right that the bot can pick chests and leave before a brute closes is for the first live raids to say, and the record will now show them. Replay case bastion-raid-low-health-no-food (leave_it or gold_only, never raid_chests; 5 of 5 leave_it). Tests: test/bastion-raid.test.js (eight: offered only in the Nether with a bastion within reach and not resting; the facts said; gold armor and a brute in view; asked once and held, leave_it rests the rung, no client is gold only; the raid's record ends looted, nothing or died; a bastion chest passed unless chosen, opened when chosen, a TNT chest and the desert temple's never; a chest among blackstone is a bastion's; the lid marks the piglins provoked) and test/looting.test.js (the old "a bastion raid opens its chests whoever is looking" now says unchosen 0, chosen 1). npm test 2221 of 2221 (with JEV_ARBITER=shadow the same). Not run live in a trial: none has yet been asked this question in play.
634. *The cauldron that puts a fire out: measured in the Nether on a disposable server (port 25576, a fresh arena folder, 26.1.2, the_nether at (0, 100, 0) on a netherrack floor; commands only to stage: a floor, fire, gamemode, items), then built as two ways for body_way and one offer for crossing_kit (note 631's open item i).* Verified (a mineflayer bot, every action an ordinary one). (1) Placing: a cauldron item put on the top of a netherrack block with placeBlock: a `cauldron` block, 0.57 s the first time (waiting for the block update, later 0.1 s), its shape the bowl (walls an eighth thick, rim a block high, hollow 0.75 wide, floor at 0.1875 to 0.25). A water bucket used on it (activateBlock with the bucket in hand): `water_cauldron` level 3 in 0.5 s, in the Nether (no dimension check on the fill), the bucket left an empty `bucket` (a bucket of water is one cauldron; the water is not carried on). (2) The fire: a fire block set in the bot's cell lit it (the game's fire, 1 health a second, seconds after it left); the bot stepped in: the fire went out at the moment its feet were under the water (level 3 to 2 in the same tick, the on-fire flag off at most a tenth of a second later), each time; a level-1 cauldron went to an empty `cauldron` after one fire; so three fires a cauldron, one level each. No burning after, no re-lighting inside. (3) Moving in is the hard part, and is what is built. The rim is a block high, so a body jumps onto it (a jump from the cell beside it: 100.75, 101.17, 101.25 in 100 ms steps, down to 101.0 on the rim), and a body 0.6 wide drops into the hollow only with its middle within 0.075 of the cauldron's middle in both directions (bbox in x 3.125 to 3.875 for a cauldron at x 3). It does not just walk in: a hop with forward held (sprinting or not) crossed the whole bowl at y 101 and came down five blocks past it, three times of three (x 3.08, 3.35, 3.72, 4.38 then down at 4.7 to 5.0); walked across the rim in 50 ms pulses it stepped from 3.40 to 3.58 over the 3.425 to 3.575 window and missed; a crouched bot cannot drop in (the edge rule holds it on the rim: not tried, from the physics). What worked, four of four and then more in the built code: line the side up with the cauldron's middle crouched, a tick at a time (about 0.03 a tick), hop onto the rim with forward and jump for about 150 ms, and then look each 160 ms at where the middle of the body is over the bowl and press forward, back, left or right for one 50 ms tick to nudge it into the window (a body 0.1 off sideways stayed on the rim until the sideways nudge was added: one run of the built code burned out at 7.8 seconds beside a cauldron it stood on the rim of); gravity drops it in. Out again: jump and forward until the body is on the ground past the far wall (1 s, or the 0.5 s of a hop onto the rim and off it); the first try's exit ran five blocks on because its stop asked for the rim's height. (4) The cost, timed on the built code (src/cauldron.js) from the call to the fire being out: a cauldron and a water bucket carried, standing in the open: 0.8 to 1.0 seconds (put down, filled, lined up, hop, drop), the whole way with the step out 1.7 to 1.8 seconds; a filled cauldron placed 3.9 blocks off: 1.8 to 2.7 seconds to the fire out (the walk 1.2 of it), 2.6 to 4.0 all told. What it needs: 7 iron ingots (the recipe is 7 in a U at a crafting table; the planner crafts it: `craft 1 cauldron at a crafting table` from 7 iron and a table, one slot), one water bucket kept (a bucket of water in the pack in the Nether is the fill for it, and not a fall or a cast then), and for the bot to be alight where there is 3 by 3 of open floor beside it and room to jump (two cells over the cell it goes in from and over the cauldron). Also seen: the arena's Nether floor had lava pooled 3 to 4 blocks east of the test cell, and motion.move refused the hop out at the first tick that read the drop ("lava at (4, 99, 0) ahead; not walked into": the deep check reads a drop into lava from the bowl's floor cell): the guard held there, as it should. Built. (a) src/cauldron.js (the placing, the filling, the crouched line-up, the hop and the rim steps by motion.move, the hop out; `plans(bot)` says whether a water cauldron stands within 6 blocks with a cell to go in from, or a cauldron and a water bucket are carried with a side of the bot's own cell open). (b) vitals.fireWays, alight out of the fire: `extinguish_in_cauldron` (the cauldron near: its distance, level of 3, the hop and why it is a hop, the seconds, the fire left and the health it saves, the level it costs, a drop or lava beside the cell it goes in from, and whether that cell is in a shooter's line) and `set_down_cauldron` (the set carried: the seconds measured, that the bucket is left empty and no water bucket is left for a fall or the portal cast, what it saves, what it spends: the water and the cauldron staying where it is put with two levels in it, a pickaxe takes it up again without water; the drop and the line). `burn_out` says "in the Nether only a cauldron's water puts it out" when one is on offer; fireToAnswer is true with a way to put it out in the Nether (it was false there but for an enchanted apple); the burning said in every question (body.burningSays, conditionSays) names the cauldron near or carried, and only then. Nothing chooses for Jev: the fallback order is unchanged and the cauldron is never first. Not offered while standing in fire (the flame relights it), with an empty cauldron, or with no room. (c) crossing_kit: a `cauldron` item in the kit said when the set is carried or makeable (a cauldron or 7 iron, and a water bucket or an empty bucket), never short, with its price (7 iron ingots, an iron pickaxe is three; a slot or two; what it does; the seconds to put down and step in, worth most set down before a fight away from the blazes; the bucket emptied into it), and `top_up_cauldron` on offer with nothing else short (it makes the question worth asking; the fallback never picks it): it crafts the cauldron, then fills a bucket, one step a pass. kitSummary names it as an option, not a gap. (d) inventory_drop notes the cauldron ("for a fire on the body in the Nether: put down and filled from a water bucket") and the water bucket when a cauldron is carried ("and the water for the cauldron carried: emptied into it, it fills it, in the Nether as anywhere (a poured bucket evaporates there)"); the option lists and the decisions doc carry the new keys. Probed against the live model (5 asks each, body_way through the real fireWays and the same state the step builds, a Nether floor): before (no cauldron, the only way is burn_out, taken without asking, "[one way]"); after, with the way present: a set carried at 4.5 health and six seconds of fire left set_down_cauldron 5 of 5; a filled cauldron three blocks off at 4.5, extinguish_in_cauldron 5 of 5; the set carried at 12 health and four seconds, set_down_cauldron 5 of 5; the set at 18 health and two seconds left (the burn costs about two health, the set its water and its place), set_down_cauldron 5 of 5 (Jev spends it where it costs more than the fire does: the price is in the words, and the way is still Jev's; a note for the next look is whether the play spends its set on the small fires); 6 health with twelve seconds of fire, an enchanted golden apple and the set: set_down_cauldron 5 of 5 (with the apple alone before, eat_golden_apple 5 of 5); recorded replay case body-alight-nether-4.5-health-cauldron-carried (appended): 5 of 5. No trial has played it yet: the bot must first come to carry the iron and a bucket at the crossing, and the way must be reached while the reflex is what asks (an alight body in a blaze fight is the stance's question first, whose burning sentence now names the set; the fight itself is not stopped for a cauldron). Tests: test/cauldron-634.test.js, nine (the way near and carried, said with its facts; not offered empty, far, roofed, carried without water; a drop into lava said; the burning's sentence; the aim and the side; the kit's set said and never short, offered with nothing short and never the fallback; the drop note); npm test 2219 of 2219 with and without JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Still open: (i) the fights where a body alight is asked at all (a body in a blaze fight at 20 health with a set carried has the option only when the fire question is asked, which fireToAnswer now makes true); (ii) whether Jev spends the set on small fires (18 health, two seconds) and then has none for a fire that kills; (iii) a cauldron put down before a fight, at the hold, is not offered as a stance option yet; the bot has to be alight to be told of it; (iv) mining a cauldron back up (it drops itself without water) is not a way; (v) the entry has been measured on netherrack only (soul sand and slabs alter the rim's height).
637. *Trial infrastructure so results can be measured (Fable's design review, 2026-09-28): the stage start's pick, the commit in the flight record, and the stance prices against what the stances took. Tooling only: no gameplay code, nothing said to Jev, the saves not edited.* (1) Stage saves. start-stage.sh picked the save least started from. Read from each save's own player data (world/players/data/*.dat; the bot's state files hold no health, hunger or food): the 28 fortress saves come from 13 source worlds (a save's world through its -nether-N and -fortress-N trials: 242-ac, 242-af and 242-ah three each, several a few minutes apart), 9 of 28 (a third) were saved at hunger 17 or lower and 4 below health 20, 18 of 28 carry 9 food points or fewer (mid-243-ag-071048 4, mid-235-p-213634 none), and only 2 carry 40 or more at health 20 and hunger 18 or more (mid-242-bb-143450 82 points, mid-242-aa-020157 63); of the 30 nether saves, 23 are at health 20 and hunger 18 or more. The pick (scripts/lib/stage-select.js, scripts/trials/stage-pick.js, start-stage.sh) now prefers saves at health 20 and hunger 18 or more and, for a fortress start, 40 or more food points carried (raw and cooked at their hunger points; rotten flesh, spider eyes, poisonous potatoes, pufferfish, chorus fruit and suspicious stew not counted); of those it takes the source world with the fewest starts so far (the sum over its saves), then that world's save least started from, so every source world starts once before one repeats; with fewer than three fortress saves qualifying it falls back to the nether stage's saves by the same rule (health and hunger only), and prints the rule and why (`stage-pick: fallback-nether: only 2 of 28 fortress saves qualify (needs 3); fell back to the nether stage: 23 of 30 nether saves at health 20, hunger 18 or more; took the source world started least (mid-242-bb-142608 ...)`). `sh scripts/trials/start-stage.sh --list [stage]` prints every save with health, hunger, food points, source world, its starts and its world's, why it does not qualify, and the next pick; STAGE_ANY=1 keeps the old pick; JEV_ROOT reads another checkout's saves. Today's consequence: with two of 28 qualifying, fortress starts are nether starts until the checkpoints keep more saves with stock (the 28 will not get better by themselves: checkpoint.sh keeps a fortress save on the first fortress a trial reaches, wherever its food stands); the change is in the selection and does not touch what checkpoint.sh keeps. Not selected on: a save beside a live blaze spawner (the state does not say; the fortress saves' first fights are at the cages, note 631 (4)). (2) The commit. The flight record's connection frame carries `commit`, the short SHA of the checkout the bot loaded (src/recorder/commit.js: `rev-parse --short HEAD` in the repository root, once per process, null where it fails), so a run is known by its build, not by its clock time; progress-audit.js --by-commit [--since ISO] [--to ISO] [--json] groups the flight records' runs (a bot process: its file and -partN continuations; commit read from the first part's head) by commit: runs, ports, bot-hours (gaps between frames under a minute), deaths (health from above zero to zero) and rods per bot-hour, runs that gained a rod (a rise in blaze rods carried between two pocket samples, so a rod picked up again after a death counts), Nether entries (a frame in the Nether after one elsewhere; a run begun there by a stage save is none); blaze-record.js --by-commit gives the fights row per commit. None of today's records has a commit (the change is not deployed), so the whole of .bot-state/flight, 1,850 runs from 2026-09-26T17:39Z to 2026-09-28T21:32Z, is one row: unknown, 317.5 bot-hours, 354 deaths (1.11 an hour), 80 rods (0.25 an hour), 52 runs with a rod, 153 Nether entries in 93 runs; the table fills as bots restart onto the build. (3) Price calibration, scripts/price-calibration.js: per encounter_stance option, the damage the chosen option's description priced for its window ("about N damage from the mobs here in the next fifteen seconds this way"; the fight's "about N of it in the first fifteen seconds"; a charge's or close_in's "over the N seconds"; a run's and a meal's over their own seconds; the arena's measured sentences are not the price) against the damage events taken in that window after the answer was given (blaze-record.js's hurts()), the price also held to the health the bot had. Over all 17,412 answers by Jev in the record (14,587 with a stated figure and a whole window; 2,512 chosen options state none: leave_and_heal 122, return_fireball 147, box_here 75, corner_ambush 49, creeper_dance 70, get_out_of_water 33; 313 dropped as unfinished): mean priced (capped) against mean taken, and the answers that took any damage: fight 11.5 against 1.2 (5,193 answers, 1,027 took any; medians 10.4 against 0), take_cover 3.0 against 1.9 (1,985, 696), out_of_sight 1.7 against 0.9 (2,266, 353), retreat 4.7 against 0.7 (606, 134), rail_and_fight 6.6 against 1.4, seal 2.8 against 0.9, pillar 3.2 against 1.1, dig_down 4.2 against 1.6, bunker 4.2 against 1, nook 5.8 against 1.7, shield_guard 5.1 against 1.9, charge_nearest 5.3 against 1.7, eat 2.6 against 0.9, close_in 3.8 against 2.1, charge_shooter 4.1 against 2.2, keep_working 13 against 1.8, hold_on_span 5.3 against 1.5, block_creeper 1.4 against 0.9, back_to_wall 2.4 against 2.2 (within 50%), fight_at_spawner 5.2 against 5.8 (within), break_spawner 5 against 8.1 (n 3), strike_from_above 1.7 against 7 (n 5: UNDER). By the flag (over 50% on the means): all but back_to_wall, fight_at_spawner, break_spawner and low_ceiling are OVER, take_cover 1.6 times and the fight ten; by the medians most windows took nothing, so the median rows say only that a price over half a point is more than nothing. What it can measure: a stated figure against the damage events of its window, per option. What it cannot: (i) the price is from the mobs and the taken is all damage (fire, falls, lava, mobs not counted); (ii) a stance ends before its window when it fails or the fight is won, so the figure is a ceiling on what one that ran the whole fifteen seconds took, and part of the gap is the stance ending (a fight priced at killing three mobs that dies with the first is not mispriced); (iii) what was chosen is not random, so a row says what happened where Jev picked the option, not what it would take anywhere, and an option Jev picks only when it looks cheap will look cheaper taken than priced; (iv) nothing here says what another option would have taken; (v) a window the record does not cover whole is dropped unless the bot died in it. Note 631 (3)'s "two to three times" reads here, over the whole record, as 1.6 for take_cover, 1.9 for out_of_sight, 6.5 for retreat and 10 for the fight; whether those are prices to lower or a fight over too soon to take what it priced is (ii) and is not settled by this table. Tests (test/trial-infrastructure.test.js, 18, each failing before): the source world from a save's name, food points, what qualifies and why not, the rotation over source worlds and within one, the nether fallback and its reason, STAGE_ANY, the vitals read from synthetic player data with the save left unchanged, the commit read once and null on failure, the connection frame carrying it, a run's bot time, deaths, rods and Nether entry, the grouping by commit with 'unknown' and rates, a directory of records with a part and an old record, the price sentence shapes, the window's taken against priced (capped, dropped, died in) and the table's flags. npm test 2256 of 2256 (main at 2c16ae7, notes to 636), the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Open: (a) fortress saves worth starting from (checkpoint.sh keeps the first at each fortress whatever the stock); (b) --by-commit fills as bots restart, then reruns of the calibration by commit say whether a price change moved the ratios; (c) the stage saves' blaze-spawner nearness is not read; (d) the options that state no figure (leave_and_heal, box_here, corner_ambush, return_fireball) cannot be calibrated until their text does.

638. *Should this visit happen now: a design review's two findings (Fable, 2026-09-28), a hidden gate on going out of the blazes' sight and no question at the level of the visit itself.* (1) Note 631 measured that what moves a blaze fight's death rate is the health and hunger it begins at (over 16 health 14% died and 12% brought a rod, 8 to 16 24% and 6%, under 8 58% and none; hunger under 18 24% and 6%; iron armor made no difference), yet fortress_approach had a dozen ways in and no "not yet", and leave_nether was asked only when the hunt was short of its fitness. (2) blaze-stand.js offered leave_and_heal only `if (hp < 20 && about.length && (food || hunger >= 18))`: hidden in exactly the state where walking out of sight is the whole of it. At hunger under 18 with nothing to eat no health comes back, but out of sight the volleys stop and the fire burns out; note 631 counted 14 of the 16 deaths with the nearest blaze 15 or more blocks off and a stance asked as bots with nothing to eat at hunger 12 to 17. Now. (a) The gate is gone: leave_and_heal is offered whenever a blaze fight is on, health is under 20 and a cell out of every blaze's sight exists (the geometry, the walk and the price unchanged). Whether health can come back is worked out from the food carried (healing.js foodCarried: eating all of it brings hunger to min(20, hunger + points)) and the text says what it is. Where it can, as before ("eat the cooked beef (about 1.6 seconds) and stay until the health is full ... from about 9 to 20 takes about N seconds"); where it cannot, "Go out of their sight (no health comes back at this hunger): ... stay only until the fire on the body is out: at hunger 14, under eighteen, no health comes back (nothing carried is food), so healing there would take never. It gets the bot out of the fire and the volleys and no health back: it stays at about 0.2 health, and each point lost from here on stays lost until the bot has eaten to eighteen", with no seconds to full and expects.heals 0. Food that does not reach eighteen is said too ("eat the potato (it brings hunger only to 11)"); the old `fast` rule counted any food carried as bringing hunger to 20. The run (blaze-tactics.js leaveAndHeal) is ended honestly: its loop already broke out on arrival at hunger under eighteen with nothing to eat, with 'no food' as its whole account and even with the fire still on the body, out of the fire checks; it now waits for the fire to be out (at most eight seconds; nothing else standing there can change) and ends saying "out of their sight and the fire out; at hunger 14 nothing comes back". The `when` texts of encounter_stance and hunt_target say the same. (b) A new question, fortress_visit (parent rung_progress), src/fortress-visit.js, asked before fortress_approach when a fortress in view is about to be approached (mob-hunt.js findFortressStep, off its floors) and on a blaze hunt when blazes not in sight are about to be gone at (huntObserved; with one in sight the fight is on and the stance is asked), with the state: health, hunger, food carried and whether health comes back at this hunger, armor, weapon, shield, rods still needed, the played record, and that it is one day's record whose health and hunger rows were counted apart (there is no row for both) and are what happened to bots that began a fight there, not what getting to another row first would do. Options, all real routes, none forced: go_in ("Go in now, at health 5 and hunger 14 ... at health 5: under 8 health, 26 fights begun there, 58% died, none brought a rod; at hunger 14: under 18, 160 fights begun there, 24% died, 6% brought a rod", and whether health comes back on the way); heal_first, offered where it changes something (health under 20 and health can come back, or hunger under 18 with food carried): eat what is carried and wait until the health is full, at most three minutes, with the seconds at the pace that applies and how the record's rows move if it works ("the health row moves from 8 to 16 health (24% died, 6% brought a rod) to over 16 health (14% died, 12% brought a rod): fights begun in that row, not a trial of waiting"), a mob in sight ends it; go_back, offered in the Nether where health cannot come back (hunger under eighteen and the food carried does not bring it there) and the way back is at hand: the trip at note 626's measured pace (portalTrip: 17 to 30 blocks a minute, minutes not seconds, of 181 such walks 22 came out and 18 ended in a death) with the food known on the other side, run as leave_nether's go_back is; hoglin_hunt, offered in the Nether at hunger under eighteen with a hoglin in view or seen: hoglinSays as the food answers word it, plus both facts of note 626, the pillar stance against hoglins losing 0.1 health on average over 168 stances (0.4 said, 2 deaths inside fifteen seconds, the 16 shield-guard stances losing 1.8) and the 66 hunts begun in the Nether of which none brought meat, and that this hunt goes at the hoglin on foot (survival.foodHunt's plan: two minutes or six health lost) and does not stand on a pillar; leave_fortress, on an approach: the fortress shunned ten minutes as keep_searching does, said to change neither health nor hunger and to gain no rod. No health threshold refuses a visit (go_in is on offer at 1 health), and the wait is not offered where nothing would come back, which its neighbors say. Held once per visit (goal.fortressVisit): until the bot dies, its hunger falls two points, or its time is out (five minutes for going in, three for a wait, two for the trip back and the hunt); a wait ends when health is full (the visit then goes on as chosen, not asked again) or a mob is in sight; the ledger rests it as any question (decide, tried.js). With Jev unreachable, or JEV_FORTRESS_VISIT=0, the visit is not asked and goes on, as the code did. With one way (go_in alone) decide takes it and says so, so at 20 health fed on a hunt, with no fortress to leave, it is not asked. Probed against the live model, five asks each, options as the code words them: health 20 fed (six cooked beef; go_in and leave_fortress) go_in 5 of 5 (0.99); health 5, hunger 14, nothing to eat, a hoglin in view (go_in, go_back, hoglin_hunt, leave_fortress) go_in 4 and go_back 1 (go_in 0.41 to 0.49, go_back 0.31 to 0.41, leave_fortress 0.08 to 0.13, hoglin_hunt 0.03 to 0.04, none_good 0.04 to 0.07); health 12, hunger 18, four cooked beef (go_in, heal_first, leave_fortress) heal_first 5 of 5 (0.93 to 0.95). Recorded encounter_stance askings where leave_and_heal was hidden, asked as recorded and with leave_and_heal added as the code now words it (the text from a scene built to match, not the recorded geometry): 25594 at 19:38:40Z (1.7 health, hunger 13, blazes about) out_of_sight 5 of 5 both ways (0.83 to 0.87 recorded; leave_and_heal 0.04 to 0.05 with it added); 25584 at 19:31:59Z (1.7 health, hunger 6, nothing carried) take_cover 5 of 5 both ways; 25589 at 19:32:10Z (3.4, hunger 14) out_of_sight 5 of 5 both ways. So the option is on offer and Jev does not take it at these states: out_of_sight is the same walk out of sight without the promise to heal. Replay cases fortress-visit-hurt-with-food-heals-first (heal_first 5 of 5) and fortress-visit-full-health-fed-goes-in (go_in 5 of 5), both built scenes. Tests: test/fortress-visit-638.test.js (the offerings at 20 fed, at 5 health and hunger 14 with nothing to eat, at 12 health and hunger 18 with food, at hunger 14 with food that does and does not reach eighteen; the honest text at hunger 14 with no food; both hoglin facts; the pace; the state; the hold's breaks; the wait eating and ending; leaving; no client), test/blaze-tactics.test.js (leave_and_heal at hunger 14 with nothing to eat offered with the honest text and no seconds to full; with a cooked chicken and with a potato; the run ending once the fire is out, not at sixty seconds), test/mob-hunt.test.js (the visit asked before the way in and leaving shunning the fortress; the hunt path with and without a blaze in sight), and the test stubs that answer the way in answer go_in to the visit. npm test 2254 of 2254, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; docs/decisions.md regenerated. Still open: (i) go_back is offered only on an approach (the hunt's actions carry no returnOverworld), and the pillar hunt itself is not built: hoglin_hunt is the existing on-foot hunt with the pillar figure beside it; (ii) the record's rows count fights begun, not visits, so a visit that ends in no fight is not in them, and go_in has no rod figure of its own; (iii) the rates are one day's counts of fights whose starting health was not chosen, so what healing first would do is an association, said so in the options that use it; (iv) at 5 health and hunger 14 Jev splits between going in and going back, going in by a little: not changed, the facts are what they are.

639. *Food as a resource of the Nether stay, as blocks became one: what the Nether has to eat (read from the 26.1.2 jar), the step restock_food with each way priced, the stay's food kit asked inside the Nether, the hoglin hunt from a pillar, and "health does not come back" on the options of a hurt bot.* The design review of 2026-09-28 (Fable) found that in the Nether health was a fact the questions reported and never a resource they managed: note 626 measured 58 stretches of a minute or more under 8 health with hunger under 18 and nothing carried that is food, 13.3 bot-hours, 36 ended in a death; blocks had been made a rung's resource (restock_blocks, blocksCarried) and food never was; the stage saves begin with what their source world carried (25589's fortress-5 with two raw mutton) and are never asked the crossing's food question; of the 66 hunts of a hoglin for its meat begun in the Nether that day none brought meat (61 ended at the sighting, 5 in a fight costing six health), and 168 pillar stances against hoglins (two blocks up, where a hoglin's blow, 1.4 blocks sideways and none up, does not reach) lost 0.1 health on average with 2 deaths. What the Nether has to eat, read from the server jar (data/minecraft loot tables, recipes, tags and worldgen features, extracted from versions/26.1.2/server-26.1.2.jar of a trial server; verified): a hoglin drops 2 to 4 raw porkchops (looting adds 0 or 1 a level) and 0 or 1 leather, the porkchops cooked as they fall when the hoglin is on fire or the killing weapon smelts loot (raw 3 hunger, cooked 8: about 9 raw or 24 cooked a hoglin, a hoglin having 40 health); red and brown mushrooms have placed features (red_mushroom_nether, brown_mushroom_nether: half the chunks, 96 tries each within 7 blocks, on a solid floor in the dark) in the nether_wastes and basalt_deltas biomes only, not the crimson and warped forests or the soul sand valley, and mushroom stew is a bowl (3 planks make 4; crimson and warped planks serve) with a red and a brown mushroom, 6 hunger; chests: a bastion's hoglin stable chest holds about 17 food points on average (a golden carrot roll 10% of 8 to 17 at 6 each, a golden apple 10%, and 3 to 4 rolls of a pool with porkchop and cooked porkchop 2 to 5 each, 1 in 14 apiece), its other chests about 12 (golden carrots 12 in 89 for 6 to 17, a cooked porkchop 1 in 13 of 3 to 4 rolls), a treasure chest has an enchanted golden apple (2 in 112 of 3 rolls), a ruined portal's chest about 4 (golden apples 15 in 398 of 4 to 8 rolls, golden carrots), a fortress's chests and the bridge bastion's none; nothing else: piglin barter's 19 items hold no food, a strider drops string, chorus fruit is the End's, and cake, golden carrots and golden apples are made of an apple, a carrot, milk, sugar, wheat and eggs, all of the Overworld. Cooking, from the jar: a furnace is 8 cobblestone, blackstone or cobbled deepslate, 10 seconds an item, its fuel coal or charcoal (8 items each) or a blaze rod (12; fuel.js), and crimson and warped stems and planks do not burn (the jar's non_flammable_wood: fuel.js already had it, work.js cookable did not: its FUELS took every stem and plank, so a bot with crimson planks was told a furnace was fuelled; fixed); a campfire (3 logs or stems, 3 sticks, a coal) and a soul campfire (soul sand or soil for the coal) cook 4 items at once, 30 seconds each, with no fuel, but the bot does not cook at a campfire and it is not built here. Not verified: how many mushrooms stand in a nether wastes or basalt deltas chunk (the feature's tries are not the survivors) and whether the bot gathers and crafts them in the game (gatherSpanBlocks over the two mushroom blocks and acquireStep for the stew, never run on a server); a lava bucket as fuel (not in the jar's data files); how a hunt from a pillar goes end to end (the 168 stances are the review's figure from the flight records, not re-measured here; whether a hoglin comes to a pillar is measured by no hunt, none has been made), and no way to set a hoglin on fire is built. What was built. src/nether-food.js: foodNeed (in the Nether, Survival, monsters about, under 8 food points carried, or hunger under 18 with health under 20; said in the option as the facts it is offered on, never a gate on Jev), foodRoutes (each way priced from where the bot stands and left out with its reason when it is not real: the hoglin on foot, said as hoglinSays says it with how this trial's hunts went; the same hoglin from a pillar, with two blocks that can be laid carried; mushroom stew, with a red and a brown mushroom in view within 48 blocks and a bowl or three planks' worth of wood; the raw meat carried cooked, with a furnace or eight stone and fuel that burns; the trip back with the measured pace of the Nether's walks and the food known on the Overworld side), restockFoodOption (one option, restock_food, offered at the food question of a hunt short of fitness (leave_nether, mob-hunt.js foodLeave) and at the stalled Nether step (nether-travel.js netherAnswers), said with why it is on offer, the stay the goal still wants (crossing-kit.js netherStay: about 120 minutes and 80 points from nothing, at 40 hunger an hour) against what is carried and how long that lasts, and the yield of each way; chosen, it asks the question restock_food with each way in full and the state's waysNotOffered and whatTheNetherHas), askStayKit (the question nether_food_kit: the first Nether question of a stay in the fortress search or the blaze hunt, with fewer points carried than the stay wants and none of the mobs in sight, and each hour of the stay after: go on, get food here (restock_food) or go back, said with the points carried, the minutes they last and the minutes the goal wants; nothing is given), and the pillar hunt. The pillar hunt is a method of the food hunt the survival layer already runs (survival.js huntStep, plan.method 'pillar'): walk to within 12 blocks of the hoglin, put two blocks under the feet by the stance's own pillarFrom, wait on the top up to 45 seconds for the hoglin to come within the sword's reach and strike from there (defendNearby), and on no block going down go on the ground with the pillar's failure kept; the pillar stays for the work's own descent (descendPillar) and the drop is picked up as the hunt picks it up. It was modest because the machinery was there: the encounter stance's pillar (pillarFrom, onPillarTop, pillarWait) and the hunt's step; what is missing is a measurement of it (only stubs and a mock survival layer test it) and the hoglin's coming. The hunts' outcome is kept and said on the next offer: huntHoglin walked to a sighting and began the hunt whether or not a hoglin was there (61 of the day's 66); it now begins nothing at a place none stands within 32 blocks, forgets the sighting and says so, and noteHunt records each food hunt's method, kills, porkchops gained and how it ended in goal.netherFood.hunts, said on the way's option ('Made in this trial: N, M brought meat'). Health not coming back: healing.js noHealSays says it in one sentence (health under 10, hunger under 18, and what is carried not bringing hunger to 18; 'Health 3.5 does not come back at hunger 13: nothing carried is food, and in the Nether only a hoglin, a mushroom stew or what the bastions hold is, so whatever this costs in health stays lost.') and withNoHealSays adds it to every option of the stall's question (work.js answerStall, which covers work_free, cross_toward, differently, mine_nearby and the rest) and of the fortress leg's (mob-hunt.js chooseLeg) that does not say it already; withoutFood no longer says nothing but a hoglin is food (nor the crossing kit's food line). What was not done: fortress_leg's own catalogue is in src/decisions/travel.js, another change's, so restock_food is not among the leg's options (restock_blocks is): the leg question still has none, and the stall and the hunt's food question carry it; fortress_visit and leave_and_heal are that other change's. Probed against the live model on the recorded question, mid-243-ag-fortress-5 (25589) stillness_detour at 18:17:09Z, 3.5 health, hunger 13, nothing to eat, 159 coal carried, a hoglin pair seen 45 blocks off, five asks each: as recorded, cross_toward 5 of 5 (mean weights cross_toward 0.44, work_free 0.37, mine_nearby 0.09, hoglin_food 0.03); with the options as this branch says them (the sentence on differently, work_free, cross_toward and mine_nearby, and restock_food offered), cross_toward 5 of 5 (cross_toward 0.38, restock_food 0.27, work_free 0.20, differently 0.06, hoglin_food 0.03): the pick did not change, the weight moved a quarter of it to the food step. The question restock_food on the same facts (hoglin_walk, hoglin_pillar, return_for_food, keep_on): hoglin_pillar 5 of 5. The stay's kit question for a stage save (2 raw mutton, 20 health, hunger 20, a hoglin pair seen 45 blocks off): restock_food 5 of 5, go_on none; it is the replay case nether-stay-kit-stage-save-2-mutton (expect restock_food or return_for_food, never go_on). Tests: test/nether-food.test.js (11: the offering facts, the step's text and the ways offered and left out with why, the stew, the furnace's fuel and cooking, the hunt that finds no hoglin at the sighting, the hunts' record, the pillar hunt's steps and the survival layer's run of it, the stay kit asked once an hour and not with a mob in sight, restock_food asked and its fallback, the health sentence), test/stillness.test.js (the stall at 3.5 health says it, once), and the expectations that gained restock_food (mob-hunt, stillness, idle-detour). The decisions doc is regenerated.

640. *Two "missing after 3 hours" that were 33 and 29 minutes of play: nothing started the bot again after a restart.* mid-242-bd (25590, first-days 242, from 19:11Z) and mid-243-be (25593, source 243, from 19:15Z) were judged "missing after 3 hours: nether, fortress, blaze_rods, ender_pearls", no death, no loop. Their flight records end at 19:44:22Z and 19:44:23Z: the logs' last lines are "[restart] asked for, and quiet now: quitting for the new build" (`touch .bot-state/restart-requested`, the quiet restart of notes 338 to 361), uptime 33 and 29 minutes. Neither port had a supervisor (`supervisor.sh` for 25590 and 25593 last logged on 26 and 28 September before the trial began; only the ports someone started one for are watched, and `midgame.js start` started none), so no bot ran there until the next trial's on the same ports at 22:12Z and 22:15Z. The verdict counted wall clock: 180 minutes, 147 of them with no bot. Run clock of bd, minutes by step over its 32.9 played: night_mine 5.3, reach_nether smelt 4.3, mine 3.0, go_to_landmark 2.5, fill_bucket 2.3, tunnel 2.0, food 3.6, iron_pickaxe 3.4, shelter 1.6, the rest under a minute each; nothing was waiting, no rung_progress was due (ten minutes on none), no death. It ended at 32.7, 47, 57.1 at hunger 20, health 20, with a bucket, a water bucket, flint and steel, a bed, 128 cobblestone and no obsidian (its lava bucket at minute 10 went with the second bucket when the shelter was stashed at 17: 9 minutes of night, 9 more of iron for a new bucket by 26.5, the crossing kit again by 30.7), so at minute 33 it was where the 15 worlds that entered the Nether (median 28 minutes) were at 20. be ended at minute 29 with 5 lava buckets, a water bucket, flint and steel and 10 raw iron on the way to the frame, closer than most. The same restart took down more: 25594 (mid-242-bb-fortress-6: 4 minutes played of 155 on the record), 25595, 25597 and 25598 (about 14 minutes of 114 each) and 25585, 25588, 25591 have no supervisor and a silent bot now. Nothing Jev was asked or told was involved, so nothing about what it is asked changed. Changes, all in the harness: (1) a bot asked to restart quits only where a supervisor is watching its port (`pgrep -f 'supervisor.sh <port>'`, asked every 15 seconds), else it stays up on the old build and says once "no supervisor is watching port N (sh scripts/trials/supervisor.sh N starts one, and the restart follows)"; quiet-restart.js, `port` from session.js; (2) `midgame.js start` and `first-days.js start` start the port's supervisor when none runs (scripts/lib/supervise.js, log artifacts/supervisors/<port>.log), as retry.sh did; (3) the midgame verdict carries `playedMinutes`, `absentMinutes`, `absences` (gaps of 5 minutes or more with no flight frame, the tail counted once the window closed) and `unplayed`; a timed-out run with a tenth or more unplayed says "missing after 33 minutes played of 3 hours (the bot was not running for 147; not a verdict on play)", where bd's verdict now reads so from its own record; (4) progress-audit's `silent` flag says when no supervisor is watching the port. Tests: test/quiet-restart.test.js (a restart is not taken with no supervisor and is when one appears, said once), test/supervise.test.js (a supervisor started when none runs; the absences, bd's shape), test/progress-audit.test.js (the silent flag with and without a supervisor). Needs the owner: `sh scripts/trials/supervisor.sh <port>` for each live port without one (25585, 25588, 25591, 25593, 25594, 25595, 25597, 25598, 25590 at the time of writing); the running supervisors read the old script and are not affected by this change.
