(3) Classification. Mostly a bad test: five of seven deaths in the lava and the choices Jev made were among options that ended alike, because the place had no good one (with nothing carried every leg is a dead end, and the nearest footing, 8 steps, is along the same span). A test that begins on a lava span with the last blocks and a fortress overhead measures one situation, and measures it as a ghast's aim. Two things were the code's: the cross_level text (which said 'ends 16 blocks nearer, 2 from it' for a span that ends 38 under the bricks, so a plan to lay the last blocks toward a fortress it cannot reach at that height read as arriving), and the pick (three saves qualified, all one map, one of them this, started from 9 times). The two blaze deaths are the known spawner fight (note 631: charge_nearest into four blazes at 2 to 3 blocks, 20 to 0 in 8 to 12 seconds), not caused by the start. The stance prices were not the trouble: the calibration table (price-calibration.js, all 15,007 recorded answers with a figure) shows hold_on_span priced 0 median against 5.9 mean taken and 10 deaths in 102 answers, and out_of_the_push 14.6 against 9.6, but on this span every option said death for a push and the choice among them did not change what a hit did. (4) Changes. (a) scripts/lib/save-spot.js reads a save's spot from the world files (the player's position; the block under the feet, the floor round it in the nine cells, what lies under it down to 80 blocks; anything unreadable is unknown and counts against nothing) and stage-select.js leaves out of the pick a save whose player stands on a floor one or two blocks wide (at most four of the nine cells) with lava at the bottom of a drop of three or more, or any drop of 23 or more, and says so (`fortress stage: 1 on a span over lava or a deadly drop left out`); of today's 33 fortress saves one qualifying save is left out (this one), of the 35 nether saves 6 (mid-242-bc-174126, mid-243-bg-205157, mid-243-ca-212804, mid-243-cb-214533, mid-243-af-053834 and mid-244-ab-031342), and the fortress pick falls to the nether stage (2 of 33 qualify). (b) A save started four times in the last hour rests (STAGE_MAX_PER_HOUR, 0 turns it off): start-stage.sh logs each start to .trial-checkpoints/stage-starts.log (a line beside the saves, not in one; hours of history before this change are not in it), stage-pick.js reads it, --list shows a 'last hour' column, the pick's reason says how many were left out. (c) cross_level, where the fortress is four or more blocks above the end of the span, now says 'It stays level: it ends 37 blocks under the nearest brick (y 74), and the 37 blocks up are still to be made from the end of the span, with 0 blocks left, over the lava it was laid across; the way up is asked again from there'. Probe of the recorded question (25591, 22:47:19Z), 10 runs each: as recorded cross_level 10 of 10, with the sentence cross_level 3 and tunnel 7; replay case span-toward-a-fortress-38-up-ends-under-it (expects tunnel, other_way or keep_searching; 5 of 5, 5 of 5, 4 of 5 in three runs of the suite). Nothing is said to Jev about the save, nothing is added to a start, no save is edited. (5) Not done, said plainly. A better selection than the hourly rest: keep the checkpoint from being taken mid-span at all (checkpoint.sh keeps a fortress save on the first fortress a trial reaches, wherever it stands; a save should be taken on ground at least three blocks wide, with the same reader), and treat the saves of one map as one source (level.dat's seed or the fortress's coordinates), so the rotation over 'source worlds' is over maps; with 242 the map of 16 of 33 fortress saves, the pool is a few situations either way. A way Jev is not offered on a span with none carried: taking up the span's own blocks behind it (26 cells of cobblestone and netherrack, a pickaxe carried, none dug today because 'under a span's floor' is refused) would give the blocks for rails or a way up; it is a new action, and where the bot has no other way it is the only one, so it is a proposal, not a change. The calibration of hold_on_span's price (0 for a hold whose failure is a lava death) is noted, not changed: the text already prices the push by the fall. Tests: test/stage-spot.test.js (a synthetic region file read for the span, a wide floor, unknown spots, the pick, the fallback, the hourly rest, the log), test/mob-hunt.test.js (the climb sentence, and its absence at a level fortress).
642. *mid-243-ah-fortress-7 (25589, a fortress-stage start 20:26:44Z, ended 23:26Z at the three-hour limit: no death, no loop, 180 of 180 minutes played, no rod, no pearl): a stall, not care. The bot spent its 90 blocks in three minutes with no pickaxe to get any back and stood on 15 blocks of its own span for two hours fifty.* Read from the flight records (11 files, 17,884 frames) and the audit's own measures at fixed times. Minutes by step of the run clock over the 181 played (start of the trial to its end; about 16 not clocked): obtain blaze rods: detour 61.3, find fortress 49.4, cross toward 29.8, nether gather 19.6, food hunt chosen 2.3, work free 1.5. It began at (-271, 52, -255) beside a fortress floor 21 up and 1 block off, 90 blocks carried, no pickaxe (a save's inventory: 31 iron ingots, 3 sticks, 3 oak planks, 148 coal, 16 gravel, 6 buckets, no food), health 17.3, hunger 17. What happened: (1) 20:26:57, fortress_approach: pillar_up (21 blocks of the 90, 69 left after) 0.34, keep_searching 0.36 (taken: "leave this fortress for ten minutes"; its text said nothing of blocks). (2) 20:27 to 20:30, the sweep's leg east and two cross_level crossings laid basalt on the lava sea: 29 cells east at y 52, 45 cells south, a pillar of five to y 57 beside a second fortress at (-218, 66, -308) ("the pillar would not rise"), and 15 more west along y 57: 77 blocks at 20:30:00 and 0 carried, the last crossing priced "15 blocks carried, 0 left after". (3) From 20:30:00 to the end the bot stayed between x -233 and -218, z -306, y 57 (15 by 2 blocks, every 15 minutes' extent measured in the flight): fortress_leg 388 askings (leg_east 109, leg_west 92, none_good 129), stillness_detour 189 (127 none_good), nether_gather 142 (without 64: the warped forest 21 blocks north with "no path"), fortress_approach 142, rung_progress about 89 (keep_at_it 28, until_rest_ends 24, work_free, differently, restock_food 9 each, set_aside_rung 7 which sent it to leave_nether wait_here 13 times), restock_food 33, fortress_visit go_in 14 of 14 (never heal_first, go_back or leave_fortress), unstuck_move about 150 (step, place, dig_feet: gravel placed and taken up again, 16 to 1 and back), walked 6210 blocks in all with a net of 65. Fights: encounter_stance fight 3 times and rail_and_fight once (21:05, 17.3 to 10 to a fireball; 21:53, 10 to 6.4), take_cover 12, out_of_sight 15, hold_on_span 6, out_of_the_push 8; no blaze ever in reach, no rod. (4) Health 17.3, then 10 from 21:05, then 6 from 21:53 to the end, hunger 16 all three hours (walking a 15-block span spends none), nothing to eat and no hoglin nearer than 122 blocks across the sea: it did not starve, it sat at 6 health with health that could not come back, and every question said so (healing on all of them) and none said what was true of the blocks. Every answer to "what now" was priced in blocks (the leg "stops at cell 0", "0 blocks carried: it stops at the first cell needing one"), and the only things the state said of the pickaxe were on fortress_approach and fortress_leg ("none carried: rock and nether bricks cannot be dug"), not on fortress_visit, leave_nether, rung_progress or the stall's questions. The way out was closed: no pickaxe means no block dug or taken up (netherrack, basalt, bricks and blackstone drop nothing by hand), a crafting table needs four planks and it carried one, the warped stems 21 blocks north had no path, and every way that lays a block stopped at its first gap. The audit did flag it, from the first fifteen minutes (run over the record at 20:50Z, 15 min: newGround 0 of 5 columns, pacing 558 blocks walked and 7 net, noneGood 33 of 112, quickNothing, stallShare 11%, netherGround, firstRod, rungTarget; at 22:00Z, 60 min: the same and milestone 90 minutes, none_good 179 of 507, stallShare 32%; over the three hours it flagged milestone, noneGood, quickNothing, stallShare, netherGround, firstRod, rungTarget and not newGround or pacing, which the first half hour's new ground had spent), so the flags existed and nothing read them (no `waitShare`: 0, the time was in a rung set aside and in detours, not in a shelter or a hold; no `noRodInHours` flag exists, firstRod says it). Verdict: a stall, physically closed by minute 3 and worsened by the questions being answered in the same words 1,000 times. What would have made it take the fight: at 20:26:57 the pillar (69 left, the floor 1 block across) or a walk to the fortress on the ground it stood on; with 15 blocks left at 20:29:45 nothing, and after 20:30 nothing that Jev could choose. What changed, as facts (Jev's choices are not made for it): src/block-stock.js says, in the Nether with no pickaxe carried, how many blocks can be laid and that none comes back or can be dug (a laid block taken up drops nothing), what making a pickaxe takes and what is carried toward it (heads carried, sticks, planks, logs, table), and with none carried that every walk, crossing or climb that needs a block stops at its first gap; it is on every gameplay question's state as `blockStock` (decisions/index.js, said in the guidance), where the pickaxe was said only on two; and the price of every way that lays blocks (crossing, the fortress leg, the pillar, covering lava, the span round) says after "N left after" that with no pickaxe none of them comes back, and for the last blocks ("0 left after", a leg that runs out) that none is left to lay and none can be had, so every way that lays a block from where it ends is closed. Not changed: no route home or out is added (none exists on those facts), and the choice to end an attempt on purpose is not offered (whether a stranded bot may be told that a death returns it to the Overworld with nothing is the owner's to decide: it changes what a death means in the trials and the audit). Probed against the live model on the recorded question, mid-243-ah-fortress-7 fortress_approach at 20:26:57Z (1 block off, 21 up, 90 blocks, no pickaxe), eight asks each: as recorded, keep_searching 4 and pillar_up 4; with the stock said (pillar_up "no pickaxe: none of the 69 left comes back", keep_searching "every leg over the lava sea lays a block a cell and the 90 are all there will be", blockStock on the state), pillar_up 7 and keep_searching 1: it is the replay case fortress-1-block-off-21-up-90-blocks-no-pickaxe (expect pillar_up, never keep_searching); the as-recorded question is kept out of the suite (it is the case before). keep_searching's own text now says it too (the probe's copy carried the same sentence). Tests: test/block-stock.test.js (6: the fact with 31 iron, 3 sticks and 1 plank; left out with a pickaxe and in the Overworld; blocks carried counted and said not to come back; the sentence after a crossing and a leg with 0 left; the crossing's and the leg's text; the state carrying it on a real decide()); test/mob-hunt.test.js expectations (the pillar and cover_lava texts). The decisions doc is unchanged.
645. *What the blaze fights that brought a rod did differently from the ones that killed the bot, measured from the flight records (2026-09-28, 511 fights to 23:59Z: 61 ended with a rod, 106 in a death, 10 in both), and made visible to Jev as rows by situation.* Method: scripts/blaze-record.js now describes every fight (`--records <file>`: the setting, gear, stances in order with time and health, blazes seen, kills, damage, sight, the rod's timing; `--wins`, `--sequence`, `--answers`; fights() keeps the frame indices; a kill is a blaze within 6 blocks in one frame carrying mobs and gone from the next within 10 seconds, an estimate: of the 37 rod fights with a kill seen, 31 had the rod within 1.6 s of it). Table, medians (rod and alive n=51, died with no rod n=96, neither n=354): health at the start 20, 20, 20 (over 16: 88%, 56%, 79%; hunger 18 or more 76%, 53%, 64%); seconds 34, 35, 24; blazes seen at the start 2, 2, 3; within 16 at the peak 2, 3, 2; a live blaze spawner within 16 45%, 59%, 45%; shield carried 94%, 91%, 92%; iron sword 94%, 89%, 89%; a span underfoot 0%, 19%, 14% (ground 96%, 68%, 74%); blazes 4 or more blocks over the bot: 4 rods in 69 fights; a kill seen 65%, 41%, 2%; health lost 7.9, 17.5, 7.9; blazes out of sight for 3 seconds or more at some time 37%, 42%, 42%. Not the setting, the gear, or breaking sight: the shield was carried in 92% of all fights and the 41 without one took 3 rods and died 9 times (7%, 22%, against 12%, 21%); breaking sight 11% rods and 21% died against 12% and 20% without. What differs is the answer: of the 61 fights with a rod 56 had close_in or charge_nearest in them; the 360 fights with neither took 5 rods (1%) and 17% died, and 60 of the 96 deaths with no rod were in them (never struck: cover, retreat, out of sight, healing, until the fire or a volley ended it; 51 of 94 last asked under 4 health). A rod is one blaze killed at 2 to 5 blocks by the sword, picked up at once: median 9 seconds from the first strike (42 of 55 within 15; 90th percentile 52), 18 seconds from the fight's start; 32 rod fights at a live spawner (with 2 to 8 blazes about at the kill), 29 with none within 16, 18 with one blaze about: not one blaze wandered off a spawner and not a shield timed to a glow (the record does not show a glow; the shield is carried in all groups alike). First stance, all 511: close_in 28 fights, 54% rod, 18% died; charge_nearest 50, 46%, 28%; take_cover 151, 5%, 16%; back_to_wall 58, 7%, 21%; retreat 45, 2%, 31%; leave_and_heal 27, 15%, 30%; defer 27, none, 26%. Holding is no safer (cover first 18% died, strike first 24%) and takes a ninth of the rods. The deaths differ two ways, counted: 60 held and were finished by fire and volleys at low health; 46 struck and died, mostly at a live spawner (a strike there 34% rod and 40% died, n=85, against none within 16, 41% and 18%, n=66) and late or hurt (the first strike within 15 seconds of the fight's start: 97 fights, 43% rod, 27% died; later: 54, 26% and 37%; a first strike under 8 health: 8 fights, 1 rod, 7 died). By the situation and what followed each answer (--answers; a fight counted once per kind and cell; the health, blazes and spawner at the answer; a rod after it, a death after it): no spawner, one blaze or none, over 16 health: a strike 34 fights, 15 rods, 4 died (12%); cover 81, 5 rods, 9 died; a spawner, four or more, over 16: strike 19, 6 rods, 3 died (16%); cover 75, 2 rods, 11 died; the same spawner at 8 to 16 health: strike 12, 2 rods, 6 died (50%); cover 77, 2 rods, 15 died (19%); heal 45, 2, 12; retreat 29, 1, 7. So the strike pays where the bot is healthy or the blazes few, and at a spawner hurt it is the worse of five bad answers. Sequences repeated: one strike segment (close_in or charge_nearest, separated from the next by another stance) 111 fights, 32% rod, 31% died; two 28, 43%, 25%; three or more 12, 67%, 42% (survivorship: a bot that lives long enough strikes again; not a trial of a retreat between strikes). No lure option: the 26.1.2 jar (note 606) has a blaze that sees the bot hang back and a blaze that loses sight chase for five ticks, so a retreat pulls nothing out of a spawner's reach, and the corner_ambush arena rows (note 606: the blaze never came round in ten holds) agree; the 29 rod fights with no spawner near are blazes already away from one, which the hunt's charge_nearest and close_in already reach. The arena was not run: its rows for these stances exist (notes 577 and 606), and the record's cells are the same shape as they were (one blaze in the open, close_in 5 of 5 kills; four at a spawner about 7 rods in 10 and 3 deaths, with the arena's kit and no hunger). Now, in general (src/blaze-record.js; the price functions are unchanged): `answersSay` is in the state of encounter_stance and hunt_target as playedAnswers: in the situation the bot is in (a spawner within 16 or not, the blazes within 16 as one or none, two or three, four or more, the health as over 16, 8 to 16, under 8), each kind of answer (a strike, a fight from a stand, cover, a retreat, going away to heal or eating, carrying on) with its fights, rods after and deaths after, only where at least 5 fights are in the row (the finest row, else the one at any health, said so), the kinds left out named, that these are what came after such answers and not what an answer caused, and how the rods came, above. `optionSays` puts the row of an option's own kind at the end of its text in the stance (survival.js stanceOptions) and in the blaze stands of both questions (blaze-stand.js). The instructions of both questions say what they are; docs/decisions.md regenerated. No rule pre-empts any question and nothing is refused. Probed against the live model, 5 each, recorded encounter_stance questions as recorded and with playedAnswers and the option sentences added from the recorded situation: no spawner, no blaze within 16, 19.4 health (2026-09-28 12:59:40Z, recorded take_cover) take_cover 5 of 5, then close_in 3 and take_cover 2; two blazes, no spawner, 20 health (20:25:27Z, recorded charge_nearest) charge_nearest 3 and shield_guard 2, then charge_nearest 5; four blazes at a spawner over 16 (20:53:05Z, take_cover) take_cover 5 both ways; at 9.6 health (20:57:14Z, back_to_wall) back_to_wall 5 both ways; 3.6 health at a spawner (13:06:51Z, close_in) close_in 5 both ways, so the row (spawner, one blaze, any health: a strike 20 fights, 5 rods, 11 died) did not turn it. The facts move Jev toward the strike where the record backs it and not where it does not. No replay case: the one answer that moved is a choice between two defensible ones. A data point from the coordinator, port 25581 fresh world mid-243-cb, 21:06 (the world begins at 21:05:47; the lava death at 21:05:05 was the port's world before) to 23:47Z, 180 played minutes, no rod: not a careful loser of fights. It began none (no blaze in sight within 24 in any frame; 36 blazes ever heard or seen at 3.6 to 64 blocks, the median nearest 37; no blaze damage; health never under 18.6); 137 of its minutes were in the Nether, 135 fortress_approach questions (keep_searching 58, walk_route 23, cross_level 9, other_way 6) and 100 fortress_leg (back_to_fortress 21, the legs), go_in chosen at all 17 fortress_visit questions, the last at 29 blocks from the floor and 2 above it, "No path to the goal", no pickaxe, no blocks carried, within a 60 by 70 block area at y 71 for the last 70 minutes: a stall in reaching the fortress, before any fight, which the fight record cannot see and the 0.5 of a rod a kill cannot help. Tests: test/blaze-record-645.test.js (7: a fight described with its stances, kill, rod and spawner; a span; the answers' rows, once per fight and kind, a rod only after the answer; the five-fight floor and the any-health row; the paragraph; --wins and --sequence), test/blaze-record-631.test.js (2: each option's row in the stance, the state's playedAnswers and both questions' instructions); one anchored expectation in test/survival.test.js loosened. npm test 2311 of 2311; under JEV_ARBITER=shadow the same (one run showed test/cauldron-634.test.js failing under load, and it passes alone and on rerun). Still open: (i) the terrain (room, corridor) is not in the record, only a drop at the feet and span frames, and the height of the blazes against the bot; (ii) the rows are one day's, over builds that changed all day (the commit is in the connection frame for the last 53 fights only), and the answers were chosen by Jev in states they do not hold alike; (iii) a strike at a spawner with four or more blazes at 8 to 16 health is the worst row we hold: whether a heal first then a strike at over 16 is better is 14 fights (spawner, four or more, over 16 health after a heal answer: 0 rods, 4 died); (iv) the stall of mid-243-cb is the approach's and not looked at here.

644. *Why most fresh worlds never reach the Nether, 2026-09-28: 60 fresh worlds (mid-<n>-<letters>, no -fortress or -nether), 29 of them in the Nether (median 30 minutes on the wall clock, 7 to 160), 31 not; read from artifacts/midgame, the flight records (analysed by trial window, each capped at the next trial on its port) and the run clocks.* Three saves feed the trials and they are three different games: the 242 saves stand in the kit at "reach nether" (13 of 18 in the Nether, median 17 minutes); the 243 saves are 68 blocks down a mine with the pickaxe worn out and three planks, at the stone pickaxe rung (10 of 20, median 30); the 244 saves are mostly at y 4 at dawn with no bed, at the bed rung (6 of 19, median 128 minutes on the wall clock, two of those with 62 and 106 minutes of no bot running). Where 2,647 played minutes before the Nether went: ascend_to_surface 14 percent (all 20 243-save trials spent 10 to 23 minutes on it, straight up 64 blocks by hand at 8 to 9 minutes on the recorded question, the climb_out prices right), mine 13, enter_nether 12, fill_bucket 10 (the cast's lava trips), tunnel 5, craft 5, gather_wool 4, food steps (food_near_frame, food_known, hunt_food_for_nether) 6; the slowest, mid-242-ab (143 minutes), stood 126 of them at a frame near (19, 72, 59) in the staircase-pacing loop that note 603 ended. Deaths before the Nether: 23 in 18 trials, none by starvation, and since 13:10Z none to a zombie on land: zombies 8 (one drowned), creepers 5 (each a blast that took the bot from full health), skeletons 3, spiders 2, falls 2, suffocation in a wall 1, fire and lava 2; 9 at night (ticks 13000 to 23000), 3 at dawn within a minute of the start, 11 by day; 15 of 23 wore full iron and a shield, so armour was not what was missing (the ladder has the shield rung, the four armour rungs, golden boots and the bow and arrows before nether_first, all deferrable, and the Nether-first option says what each costs; there is no golden apple rung, an apple being a leaf's chance). Two eras: 20 of the 23 came before 13:10Z, when shield_guard (note 601) and the creeper run (note 604) went live (the guard against zombies, with a shield: when it was chosen, 55 askings, 0.5 health was lost in the next 30 seconds, against 1.7 for fight with no guard on offer (283 askings) and 1.8 for pillar (92), different hours and so a hint and not a trial; it was offered in 65 of the 119 zombie-only shield askings after 13:10Z, the rest, as far as the states show, with the zombie out of reach or the bot in water); since it, 29 trials began and 3 died before the Nether: 244-ca at 11 minutes (in water at y -51 with six zombies, where the guard is not offered), 244-cc at 10 (mining gravel beside a 21-block drop with skeletons about: a fall took 18 of its 20, the push watch having preempted the work for the drop a moment before, and the skeletons finished it), 242-bg at 24 (in a pocket it had walled against zombies, its seal reported failed, at the cast, in lava for four seconds with no water carried and not moving, "leave_lava" running in place). The top two causes, by what the fresh worlds lost: (1) the bed rung's wool hunt begun from deep in the ground (stretches of the rung in the flight records: 29 begun below y 40 ended in a death 5 times and took 8.4 minutes; 20 begun at or above it, once and 3.6 minutes; 6 of the 23 deaths were in a wool hunt), for which "get bed" said what a bed is worth and nothing of the way (no sheep seen, the climb, the night), and (2) the Overworld's mobs met on foot with no company: 18 of the 23, wolves in the entity lists of about one flight file in fifty, tame_wolf offered 3 times in 2,858 win_strategy askings on 27 and 28 September and chosen never (bones carried in 12 of the 23 death inventories). Now: strategy.js woolTrip, said with the bed rung (rungOption, and the carried bed) whenever the step is a wool hunt: the nearest sheep in view or remembered with its walk, or that none is known; how far under open sky the bot is and the climb's minutes before any walk; the night above and the minutes to dawn, with what spawns on open ground; and the record above (WOOL_HUNTS: the hunts begun as low as this one, and the higher ones). Wolves: sightings.js keeps wild adult wolves as it keeps flocks (thirty minutes; a tamed one beside the bot or a pup is not one), wolves.js tameReady is true for one seen within 64 blocks and out of view, tameWolf walks to where it was seen and forgets it, and sets it aside twenty minutes, if it is gone, and the option (tameSays) says where the wolf is, the odds the bones carried give (one in three a bone: 33 percent for one, 70 for three), that a tamed wolf follows and comes to the bot, fights what attacks it or what it strikes, goes for skeletons unasked and does not attack a creeper, two at most, that it sits before a crossing and does not go through a portal, and what the Overworld cost the fresh worlds. Probed against the live model, five asks each on the recorded win_strategy of mid-244-aa (00:25:44, 72 blocks down at dawn, creeper, zombie and skeleton about, no sheep known): rung_bed 5 of 5 as recorded, and 5 of 5 with the way to the wool said; with a wolf seen 48 blocks off added under side_trip, rung_bed 5 of 5: the facts are Jev's to weigh, the choice did not move, and no replay case was added (the bed or the Nether first is a matter of taste on that state, and the deaths were the stance's and the creeper's). Tests: test/strategy.test.js (3: the hunt from 71 blocks down at night with none seen, the surface with a flock known or sheep in view, and not said for another rung, a bed in wool or the Nether); test/wolves.test.js (4: the sightings keep a wild wolf and not a tamed one or a pup; a remembered wolf is a trip within 64 blocks and not beyond, set aside, with no bone or with two kept; the option's words; a remembered wolf walked to and tamed, and one gone forgotten and set aside). Still open, from the same records: the 242-bg lava death (a pocket walled against zombies, the cast's clear_top, lava at the feet, no water carried, four seconds without a step), the 244-cc fall from an arrow's knockback at a 21-block drop while mining (shield_policy said nothing of the drop), 243-ac suffocating in a wall for ten seconds after a reconnect mid-climb with no pickaxe (dig_out_of_block cannot finish a cobblestone by hand in the ten seconds the damage allows), the 243 saves' 68-block climb by hand (a pickaxe worn out at depth with one plank short of a table), water fights where the guard is not offered, and none of this has run live.

646. *What the ledger counts as progress: the rung's own measure, not motion (a design review's advice, 2026-09-28; notes 571, 599, 620, 629, 631; and 25598, mid-242-bb-nether-1-fortress-9, 23:22 to 00:02Z).* The ledger's unit of progress was motion: an answer of the work's own was "getting somewhere" when the bot moved more than three blocks, carried something different (any change, a meal eaten included) or laid or dug a block (decisions/repeats.js cameOf). Note 629 fixed the walks that had a place to go; fortress legs (no target), boxes built and heal-and-return cycles still counted. 25598, from a save at a blaze room: 352 blocks walked for a net of 55 in forty minutes, 83% of them in the stall's detour, unstuck_move asked 86 times, fortress_leg 53, rung_progress 68 (keep_at_it 28, until_rest_ends 32), and the measure did not move; a flint or a quartz picked up now and then was "what is carried changed". Now (src/rung-measure.js, tried.js measureOf and settleOne, repeats.js mark and cameOf) each rung has a small vector of numbers, each with a direction, read from what watchRung tracks and a little more: `items` (what the rung is for: rods, pearls and eyes, obsidian and flint and steel, the piece of gear), `step_items` (what the step in hand is for: its item, drops, resource, block, when not the rung's), `kills` (blazes or endermen dying within sixteen blocks of the bot, counted from entityDead), `food` (food points carried), `frame` (the portal frame's blocks standing), `milestones`, all counts, more is better and fewer is neither (eating, or a box's walls, spends what is carried and is no loss and no gain); `ground` (columns looked over at fortress heights, nether-coverage seen, four new columns make new ground: a tunnel dug blind sees none); and distances, nearer is better (the fortress found, the nearest place blazes were seen, the nearest blaze cage known, the nearest portal or frame for reaching the Nether, the step's own target), each judged by a new nearest as the rung's budget judges it (a nearest kept in goal.tried.bests, stale after thirty minutes, credited to any answer that was in force when it was set), the first time a fortress, sighting or cage is known counting once. An answer to a question of the work's own under a rung (workBelowRung; not the stall's, which keep the rung's best and now carry the measure to say why, not the survival layer's stances, not a wait, which keeps note 620's scene judgment as it was) records the measure when it begins (entry.rung, entry.measure) and is settled by what changed over its life: motion counts only through ground and the distances, so two hundred blocks walked toward a fortress in legs of thirty are a new nearest at each answer and thirty along a tunnel already dug are not, and a walk toward a place of its own (option.target) is judged by its nearest approach as note 629 has it, nearer that place than it began and than any answer toward it has come since it was left. One that gained nothing says so in the rung's words on its entry and on the option next time (tried.js triedSays), "Tried 2 times from here in the last 3 minutes, and it came to nothing: nothing gained on the rung: killed nothing, no rod, no new ground looked over, no nearer the fortress (162 blocks off, the nearest yet 100), ended 62 blocks from where it began", and the rest, escalation and hold rules run on it as before. The repeat rule's cameOf takes the same measure for these questions (a look a few seconds apart, by values), and outside them a change of what is carried counts only when there is more of it (a meal eaten is no progress: the heal cycles), the dug-and-placed count and the walk as before. Measured on the day's flight records (scripts/ledger-replay.js, `--since 2026-09-28T00:00:00Z`: 23 bots, 1,187 runs, 269 bot-hours, 104,708 answers each ended by its question asked again within ten minutes, 28,086 under a rung, 10,815 waits left as they were), old rule against new on the answers under a rung: 8,841 getting somewhere and 19,245 to nothing become 5,046 and 23,040; 4,969 change class, 4,382 to nothing (moved N blocks 2,906, a block dug or placed 898, what is carried changed 578) and 587 to getting somewhere (a new nearest with no walk, a blaze place learned, new columns looked over, 4 food points); the old rule here already carries note 629's, so the change is not those walks. Per bot-hour, under the rung, old to new: came to nothing 71.6 to 85.7, the audit's quickNothing 54.1 to 54.8 (a quick answer moved nothing before and moves nothing now: the change is in the slow ones), the repeat rule's quick holds 15.1 to 16.4, answers chosen while their option would have rested 46.3 to 47.6, answers asked again within two minutes after a hold at the same place 41.1 to 41.8; over every answer judged, with the meal change, quickNothing 142.2 to 146.8 and holds 37.4 to 40. Those are counterfactual on the recorded answers, not what the bot would have done: it would have rested and left out some of them. By question, to nothing: fortress_approach 1,965 of 10,424 answers, fortress_leg 1,030 of 8,891, sheep_search 331 of 636, portal_method 269, search_heading 209, climb_out 152, crossing_kit 150, portal_way 91 (20 to getting somewhere), hunt_target 79 (13 the other way, the rod). The examples asked for: 25598's forty minutes, fortress_leg and fortress_approach, 96 answers: 74 to nothing before, 90 now (the fixture test/fixtures/ledger-25598-detour.json carries its 192 answers; replayed through the ledger 29 of 100 were getting somewhere, 9 now, and a leg that walks eight blocks out and back each pass at a blaze room is asked twice from there and then escalated to the rung's question with the reason said, where under the old rule it was never); 25586's gather walks (walk_to and cross_to the crimson stems, 18:23 to 18:29) were already nothing under 629 and stay so, the 63-block leg_east at 18:35 is "13 new columns" in the replay and would be nothing in the bot, whose blind tunnel looks over none; the crossing walks (crossing_kit cross_now, portal_way) come out as 45 to 191 nothing of 447 and 288 to 359 of 418; 25587's eleven heal cycles at the cage (18:11 to 18:17) are the survival layer's stance answers (leave_and_heal, take_cover), not the work's, and are not judged by the rung: what changes for them is that eating no longer counts, and the cycle is the rung question's to catch, ten minutes without a new best, and the hunt's hunt_target answers there are judged (charge_nearest with the rod 'more', hunt_257 twice 'nothing gained: killed nothing, no rod'). Not measured in the record, so the replay is generous to the new rule on ground and cages and cannot see option targets except by the step's own: kills (zero throughout, so a kill shows as the rod it may drop), the columns seen from a distance (it counts columns stood in), the cages, the portals known. Guard against too strict a rule: the slow approach is the distance parts (tests: two hundred blocks toward a fortress, nearer at every step; taken back and walked over again is not; past the nearest yet is; a nearest set in another life goes stale), a walk to a place of its own is judged by its approach, what a step is for counts, a rod, a kill, new ground and food count; what does not count is a block dug or placed, a walk that ended where an earlier one did, a meal eaten, a flint picked up on the way. Tests: test/rung-measure.test.js (each rung's measure, the judging, the ledger's settle and its reasons, the repeat rule's mark, decide() escalating a leg that walks and gains nothing from a blaze room, the 25598 fixture through the ledger under both rules, the replay script on a synthetic record) and test/flip-629.test.js (the walk with a block dug is no longer getting somewhere, one that carried what the step is for is). Replay suite: 78 of 82 passed, 3 known gaps, and span-toward-a-fortress-38-up-ends-under-it failed once (cross_level 2 of 5), failed on one rerun of ten (cross_level 4) and passed on another (cross_level 1): a borderline case, and the suite asks with no bot, so neither the ledger nor the repeat rule is in it and this change does not touch its text.

649. *Three reachability fixes from the live audit of note 643: the cauldron and a bastion's chests asked inside the Nether, and a shelter shell that counted a portal it cannot dig.* (1) The cauldron (note 634): top_up_cauldron was a line of the Overworld crossing kit only, and most trials begin inside the Nether (saves), so no trial ever reached it; where it was seen Jev took cross_now at 0.5 to 0.6 against 0.1 to 0.2. It is now a line of the stay's kit question, nether_food_kit (nether-food.js askStayKit, at the first fortress-search or blaze-hunt question of a stay and each hour after), as `top_up_cauldron`, offered only when the set can be made there (crossing-kit.js stayCauldron): 7 iron ingots, a water bucket already carried (the Nether has no water to fill an empty bucket, so an empty one is not a set), no cauldron carried, and a crafting table carried or the wood for one (the recipe in data/vanilla-26.1.json is a 3 by 3 shape, so the inventory's 2 by 2 cannot make it; a log or stem makes four planks). The question is now asked when food is short or the set is makeable: with food enough, only go_on and the cauldron are put, with the go_on line saying food is not short and the note saying the food and cauldron lines. Said with what it saves and costs (fire about 40% of the damage in the fatal blaze fights, 44 of 70 blaze deaths alight at the end, a landed fireball its hit plus about four ticks of fire: note 631; the iron, what else the iron makes, the slot and the table; about a second in the open, one cauldron of three levels puts out three fires and stays where it is put, the water bucket is spent; it puts a fire out only where it stands, so it is set down near the fight before the bot is alight, or carried and set down when it is (set_down_cauldron, body_way); the table's few seconds not timed in a trial) and that no trial has played it. Chosen, the cauldron is crafted through the planner (makeCauldron: acquire cauldron, a failure kept on goal.netherFoodKit.cauldronFailed and the stay goes on); nothing is given, and the fallback stays go_on. (2) A bastion's chests for food (note 636, food per chest note 639): bastion_raid was asked once in 2.7 hours, only at the pearl step with no gold. bastion-raid.js foodRoute now builds a route from the same facts (the walk and its legs, the mobs in view and that the count is not known, gold armor and what it does not do, what a lid does, the brute and three piglins priced from the game's numbers and marked as not measured on a bastion, the record: never tried), with what the chests hold in food (a hoglin stable's chest about 17 points, the housing units' about 12, the bridge's none, golden apples and carrots among them), offered as `raid_bastion` at restock_food (foodRoutes, so also the stalls' restock_food step and its description) and at nether_food_kit when food is short, only in the Nether with a bastion remembered within 384 blocks whose walk is not resting, no raid already on, and a way to walk. Chosen, it is the raid Jev chose (beginTrip, shared with bastion_raid's chooseTrip: goal.bastionRaid raid_chests with via 'food', an entry in goal.bastionRaids), one leg is walked toward the bastion, the chests within 40 blocks are opened by the loot pass while the raid is on, and the raid closes as the gold rung's does when the bot has arrived and no chest is left in reach. restock_food offers keep_on beside it (before, only at hunger under 18) so the raid is never the only thing to take, and the fallback never picks raid_bastion first. Never taken by the fallback, never a gate. (3) `seal_shelter failed: Cannot dig nether_portal`, 128 times in mid-244-bg: shelter.js missingShell counted a portal's sheet as a missing cell (no collision box, so not solid), the seal pass dug every missing cell that is not air and dig threw on a block that is not diggable, each pass. A cell holding a block the game never lets be dug and that is not water or lava (nether_portal, end_portal, end_gateway, a light block; bedrock, a barrier, an end portal frame and a command block are full blocks and were walls already) is not in the ring to be closed (shelter.fixed); water and lava stay gaps (both are diggable in the game's data), and so does any open cell. This covers dig_in and the pocket plan, which read missingShell too. Probed against the live model (TypeSafe, five asks each, the state from a fake body in the Nether with the real option text, iron armor with golden boots, a hoglin pair 45 blocks off, a bastion 190 blocks off): the stay kit at 2 raw mutton and full health, before (go_on, restock_food, return_for_food) return_for_food 5 of 5 (weights 0.52 return, 0.44 restock, go_on 0.03), after (plus raid_bastion and top_up_cauldron) restock_food 1, return_for_food 4 (0.48, 0.45; raid_bastion 0.03, top_up_cauldron 0.01, go_on 0.02); fed (12 cooked beef, the set makeable), go_on 5 of 5 (go_on 0.66, top_up_cauldron 0.31); restock_food at 12 health, hunger 15, no food, a hoglin seen, before hoglin_pillar 5 of 5 (0.53; return 0.37), after hoglin_pillar 5 of 5 (0.56; return 0.34, raid_bastion 0.03); at 5 health, hunger 10, no hoglin, a bastion 190 off: return_for_food 5 of 5 (0.86, raid_bastion 0.05, keep_on 0.07). Read: Jev prices the raid honestly (a brute kills an armored bot in the estimate, no chest ever opened by the bot) and leaves it at 0.03 to 0.05 everywhere, moving no answer; the cauldron at 0.31 against go_on 0.66 when nothing else is short is a defensible answer for a set that costs 7 iron and is not played yet; no case was answered wrongly given the facts, so no replay case is added. Reachability is what changes: both are now on the list at the start of a stay and at the food question, where Jev can take them. Tests: test/shelter-649.test.js (three: a portal, the end portal and gateway, a light block are not missing, bedrock, a barrier and a frame were walls already, an open cell, water and lava still are, a portal beside a real gap leaves only the gap) and test/nether-cauldron-bastion-649.test.js (seven: the set offered only where it can be made there; its price; the kit asked for the cauldron alone with food enough, the pick crafting it, once an hour; a failed craft said and the stay going on, the fallback never making it; the kit with food short carrying the cauldron and the bastion beside the food ways; restock_food offering the bastion route only with one remembered, choosing it the raid Jev chose, the arrival closing it, a raid already on not offered again, the fallback never picking it; the stalls' step naming it). npm test 2352 of 2352 with and without JEV_ARBITER=shadow.
648. *Two definitions of "enough blaze rods", one of them hidden, and what the bot did once it had seven (mid-235-p-nether-4-fortress-6, 25589, Fable's design review of 2026-09-28 at 00:20Z, checked against the flight records): the ladder wanted eight, the stay's text said six, and a bot holding seven went back into the Nether for the eighth and died there with all seven.* Verified, not assumed. The rung's target was in the record the whole time: `goal.mobHunt.targetCount` 8 from the first frame (the state's `nowOn` read "obtain blaze rods" from 18:52 to 19:08), from src/game-progress.js `target = neededEyes or 16`, `rods = ceil((target - eyes - powder) / 2)` = 8, while crossing-kit.js `STAY_FOR.rods.count` was 6 and `pearls` 12 (the kit's "The goal still needs 12 ender pearls" said 16 times) and GOAL.md and scripts/midgame.js measure six rods and twelve pearls; the ladder's pearls were `target - eyes` = 16. What the design review read as "kept working at the fortress" was two lives. First life (file 18:51:59): rods 1 at the start, 2 and 3 at 18:53, 4 at 18:56:35, 5 and 6 at 18:56:48 to 18:57:01 (`close_in` at a live spawner, a `body_way` out_of_fire at 9.7 health), 7 at 18:57:12; then no route (`return_to_portal`), `hunt_mob` at 19:06 asked `leave_nether` (food: hunger 14, nothing to eat, health 9.7) and answered go_back, and the bot came home with seven at 19:08 (no rod in the record was lost there). Second life, same process (file 19:10:41): the ladder saw 7 < 8, went `stone_pickaxe`, `reach_nether` (19:13), entered at 19:16 with seven, `return_to_blazes` at 19:19, and `fortress_approach` was asked 32 times (`keep_searching` 13, `walk_route` 7, `cross_level` 6) with no fact in any of them of what was carried against what was wanted (its state had the run clock, "nowOn: obtain blaze rods", and nothing of rods); it died at 19:32:24 holding the seven, the next stage start had 1 rod (the save the trial used), and the life after that died at 19:44 with that one. Fable's reading was right on the cause and off on the sequence: the eighth rod was not being hunted at the fortress after 18:57, it sent the bot back in.
**One number, and its reason** (src/eye-need.js, read by the ladder, the stay, the hunt and every question that says what is needed): an End portal has twelve frames, an eye is one pearl and one blaze powder, a rod makes two powder, so twelve eyes are six rods and twelve pearls; but stronghold.js never throws the twelfth eye (it keeps twelve for the frames, "needs another spare Eye of Ender") and the ladder starts the search only at thirteen (`>= 13`), a thrown eye comes back four times in five, so the eye the search throws with is the thirteenth: **13 eyes, 7 rods (14 powder), 13 pearls**; once the portal is found, its empty frames (`neededEyes`, some come filled). Not sixteen (eight rods and sixteen pearls was an unstated reserve for throws, each further rod one more fortress fight), and not twelve (the search would begin blocked on its first throw). A shatter mid-search leaves twelve and the ladder asks for the one eye again, which is the self-repair a constant twelve would not have. GOAL.md's milestone (six rods and twelve pearls, scripts/midgame.js) is what a run is *measured* by and stays; the ladder's number is what the search can begin on, said so in the texts. **The rung ends at it**: `rodsShort = rods carried < rods wanted` with powder and eyes counted, so seven rods (or four and six powder) carried, `nextGameStage` no longer returns `obtain_blaze_rods` or `reach_nether`: in the Nether the pearls (barter, bastion gold, warped forest) or the way home, in the Overworld the pearls' routes (test: the 19:13Z state, seven rods in the Overworld, gets `obtain_ender_pearls` count 13). The hunt counted to its own saved `targetCount` (eight when the step began, the count at that moment, and wrong after a powder is made or a rod lost); for the ladder's own hunt (win goal, rods rung) `blaze-stand.rodsNeeded/rodsTarget` read the same number from what is carried each time (a request's hunt, "get me 3 blaze rods", keeps its own count), `huntObserved` ends the hunt at it and no blaze question is asked after it.
**What Jev is told**: `rodsTheGoalWants` on hunt_target, fortress_visit and leave_nether (both askings): "The goal wants 7 blaze rods in all for 13 eyes (an End portal takes 12 eyes, an eye is one pearl and one blaze powder, a rod makes two powder, and the stronghold search throws only the eyes above 12 ..., so 13 eyes are what it begins on: 7 rods and 13 pearls). Carried: 4 blaze rods, 0 ender pearls; 3 rods still needed." and, when done, "no rod is still needed: the rods are done, and the fortress has nothing more the goal needs"; every "Toward the rods" line ends "; N rods still needed (the goal wants 7 in all for 13 eyes, C carried)"; the Nether stay says "wants 7 rods and 13 pearls in all, for 13 eyes"; fortress_approach and fortress_leg carry a brief line at the end of the state: "Blaze rods: 1 carried, 7 wanted in all (13 eyes for the portal and the search), 6 still needed." The brief line and its place are measured (live Jev, the recorded 19:19:11Z fortress_approach, options as recorded, 10 asks a variant): the state as recorded, cross_level 5 of 5; the full sentence first in the state, keep_searching 5 of 5 at zero rods carried and at seven; brief, first: keep_searching 6 of 10 at one rod carried; the fuller reasons ("a rod makes 2 powder") anywhere near the front turned ten in ten to keep_searching, and the same brief line at the end of the state, cross_level 10 of 10 at 1 carried and at 6. A question about how to reach a fortress is a near thing to Jev (0.41 against 0.25), and reasons about eyes read as "the goal is far, leave": so the reasons sit where the question is about the rods or the leaving (hunt_target, fortress_visit, leave_nether: recorded hunt_target 5 of 5 defer, then 8 of 8 defer and charge_nearest 8 of 8 with and without the sentence; leave_nether at seven rods go_back 5 of 5 both; encounter_stance with "(the goal wants 7 in all for 13 eyes, C carried)" on every option, retreat/charge_nearest 4/4 before and 5/3 after, noise), and the fortress ways carry the number and nothing to argue with. fortress_leg with the brief line at 7 carried (done) moved go_to_blazes 8 of 8 to 4 of 8 (leg_north 4): a bot that was told the rods are done, in a question that has no way home, walks somewhere else; the ladder does not ask it once the rods are done, so this is the answer to the fact and not a loop. No replay case: no answer was wrong given the facts; the code's target was.
**The funnel** (scripts/blaze-record.js `--runs`, 2026-09-28 00:00Z to 24:00Z from the flight records; a run is one life of the bot, from a file's first frame or a respawn to the death or the end of the record; rods carried, a rod made into two powder counting as a rod): 1,468 runs, 856 in the Nether, 280 of them died there, 61 gained a rod in the run. Reaching 1 rod: 107 runs (54 alive at the end, 53 died, median 237 seconds from the last rod to the death); 3 rods: 10 (1 alive, 9 died, median 158 seconds); 6 rods: 2 (1 alive, 1 died); 7 rods: 2 (1 alive, 1 died: the 25589 second life, 1,302 seconds after it entered with them). Counting only rods gained in the run (a stage start from a save carries some): 1 rod, 61 runs (23 alive, 38 died); 3 rods, 6 (1 alive, 5 died); 6 rods, 1 (alive, the 18:52 run). To 2026-09-29 12:00Z the same: 1,501 runs, 874 in the Nether, 284 died there; reaching 1: 109 (54 alive, 55 died); 3: 10; 6: 2; 7: 2. The bot that reaches three rods is dead within about three minutes of its last rod nine times in ten; and the one run that held seven rods alive at 18:57 was sent out again by the ladder.
Tests: test/eye-need-648.test.js (the number and its arithmetic with powder and eyes made and a portal found; the ladder at seven rods in the Overworld and in the Nether, at six asking for one more; the hunt's target read live and a request's own; the sentence; the fortress_visit state and the "of the N" line; the brief line; the funnel over frames with a death, a rod made into powder and a stage start with rods in hand), the hunt ending at seven with a stale saved count nine and the question's state and options short of it (test/mob-hunt.test.js), the leave_nether state (test/game-progress.test.js); test/nether-healing.test.js, test/stillness.test.js and test/tried.test.js said 6 and 12, 16 pearls.
647. *The stance prices against what the options took, by situation (the review of note 637): which models ran high and why, corrected at their source, and what is left. Note 637's table re-run on every flight record (17,946 answers to 2026-09-29T00:22Z), split by the mobs about, the health band and the dimension.* Method (scripts/price-calibration.js, extended): the taken side is said which it is (--taken all, mobs [without falls, lava, walls and hot floors, which "from the mobs here" never counts], whole [only the answers whose mobs were still about at the end of the window: a fight priced over fifteen seconds that was won in four is not compared at all] or prorated [the price cut to the seconds an early-ended engagement lasted]); the window is always the priced window; each answer carries the situation (state.threats' kinds by priority blaze, ghast, wither skeleton, piglin, hoglin, creeper, skeleton, zombie, spider, magma cube), the health band, the dimension, the seconds to the next ask, how near the priced kinds came, and when in the window each hurt fell; --episodes counts the first ask of a stretch of the same option in a run (under two minutes between its asks) once. What the record itself said before any price was touched. (1) The 10 times is mostly loops: while mobs are about the stance is asked again every second or less (the median next ask came 0.3 seconds later, 90 in 100 of fights and out_of_sights inside fifteen seconds), each afresh; one run asked the same fight 1,273 times about two spear piglins 14 blocks off that never came (priced 20 to 32, taken 0.03), and three more runs 440, 317 and 163. Counted once per stretch (4,670 episodes for 15,058 answers) the fight is 2.35 times (11.2 by answers), take_cover 1.76 (1.55). (2) The records are priced by several builds: note 602's blaze cadence reached the bots at 12:46Z on 2026-09-28, before it a blaze in sight was a shot every two seconds and alight throughout (a 3.4 second run 7.4 to 8 for one blaze); the model of the build at 2203407 reproduces 96 to 100 in 100 of the take_cover answers from 13:00Z (within 15% or 0.3, 71 to 77 in 100 before), so the table is also given for the 1,863 episodes from 13:00Z ("current build"), which is what the prices of that build were; and the repricing below adds what the model changes to a recorded price, so it means most on those. (3) Of the biters that were about but not coming at the bot (none nearer by a block a second), 156 fights' worth (biters 4 to 16 blocks off in sight): one within three blocks inside fifteen seconds in 37 in 100 (21 in 100 of 29 on the current build), 2.3 taken against 8.3 priced (0.94 against 12.4); of those coming, 75 in 100 arrived, 3.96 against 8.1. Where a mob did reach the bot the fight price was near: zombie 4.9 against 4.8, skeleton 3.2 against 2.9, spider 3.9 against 3.2. (4) The measured rates, per shooter or biter in sight, over all the bot did (scratch scripts over the same records): blaze landings 0.106 a second within 4 blocks, 0.060 from 4 to 8, 0.044 from 8 to 12, 0.030 from 12 to 16, 0.03 to 0.05 beyond, with total fireball and fire damage a blaze in sight put on the bot 0.60 a second from 4 to 8, 0.48 from 8 to 12, 0.27 from 12 to 16; a skeleton 0.24 hits a second within 4 blocks, 0.18 from 4 to 12, 0.09 from 12 to 16, none past 16 (2,000 skeleton-seconds, 450 hits); a ghast 5 in 35 seconds from 12 to 16 blocks, 15 in 165 from 16 to 24, 23 in 314 from 24 to 32, 52 in 929 from 32 to 48, 46 in 1,517 beyond; a piglin's bolt 0.054 a second within 4 blocks, 0.03 from 4 to 8, 3 in 3,143 seconds from 8 to 12 and none in the 13,000 beyond; melee at arm's length (under 2 blocks) 0.77 a second from a zombie, 0.8 from a wither skeleton and a spider, 0.43 to 0.56 from a piglin and a hoglin (one blow every two seconds), which the model has right. What was wrong, at the source. (a) The fire of a landing (combat-estimate shotPieces, blazeRate, closeInCost, tacticOptions): a blaze's shot was priced as a steady chance of being alight, 1 - e^(-5 x its landing rate), from the first second, for five seconds past its last shot, a health a second; the game (note 631: a landing sets five seconds, the first tick a second after it, then one a second, four in all) puts a tick at t only if a landing fell in the four seconds ending a second before it. A stance of 1.2 seconds of building with a blaze 10 blocks off was priced 2.8 where the hits and fire of its landings in those seconds come to 0.8, and the fifteen seconds in the open 0.79 a second where the record has 0.48 for a blaze 8 to 12 off (now 0.67; the model runs 1.0 to 1.5 times what the bot took in sight from 2 to 40 blocks, 2.1 at 14, where it ran 1.2 to 1.7, 2.6 at 14). Now burnChance and burnRamp (per-shooter pieces from a second in, climbing for four), burnBetween for the close-in's phases and the tactics' setups, FIRE_TICKS in the steady figure (blazeCadence burns 0.29 at 15 blocks, was 0.34). (b) The fire already on the body (note 631 open item ii) was a health a second for its seconds left; its ticks are a second apart and the last a second before it ends (4.9 seconds left is four more, 3.5 three): bodyBurn, in the fight's and every stance's figure and in the words ("about 5 seconds of fire left ... 4 more health from it"). (c) Every shooter but the blaze was a shot every two seconds, every one landing: a bow is drawn twenty ticks and waited on forty (Normal), a shot every three seconds, its arrow scattered as a triangle of 0.0172275 x (14 - 4 x the difficulty's id) of its direction, started 0.2 of the distance high and falling (gravity 0.05, speed 1.6), landing within 0.6 sideways of the middle and inside the body's height: every arrow within 6 blocks, 72 in 100 at 10, 56 at 14 for a bot standing still (arrowHit, from the jar; the record's bot, which also walks and shields, took about two thirds of that: 0.17 a second at 4 to 12 blocks where every two seconds and every arrow said 0.5). A crossbow (pillager, piglin) a shot about every 2.75 seconds (25 ticks charged and 20 to 40 waited), scattered as the bow's; a piglin's bolts are the record's rates above, since the game's numbers say nothing of when a piglin attacks (hostile piglins by the bot's own rule at 11 to 14 blocks, priced 10 to 19 in fifteen seconds standing in their fire, took 0.65 and 0.12). A ghast a fireball every three seconds (ghast.js GHAST) landing as the table above, 43 in 100 within 16 blocks to 9 in 100 beyond 48 (it was 100 in 100 every two seconds: a ghast about 43 blocks off, standing in its fire with nothing to swing at, was priced 5.8 in fifteen seconds by episodes, 10.9 by answers, and took 0.95). Said on each mob in the state (every, lands, shots: "a shot every 3 seconds, 72 in 100 landing from 10 blocks on a bot standing still (the game's scatter ...)", "a fireball every 3 seconds, 17 in 100 landing from 40 blocks (measured: 52 landings in 929 seconds ...)"), and in the instructions (an expected damage, an average over a few large hits). (d) A biter out of sight within eight blocks (danger.js unseenBiters) was at the bot as any other; the game gives a mob a target only in sight and drops it sixty ticks after losing it (NearestAttackableTargetGoal mustSee, TargetGoal unseenMemoryTicks): in the 272 stance windows with only such biters about the price was 3.06 and the taken 0.73 (a fight 6.8 against 0.39), a quarter landed: counted at 25 in 100 of their blows (combat-estimate UNSEEN, arrival), said beside the figure with why; the ones counted by when they could be there before a build is done (far, note 581) are left whole. (e) "Behind it, none of them reaches it": from the fourth second on, the stances that hold (take_cover, seal, dig_down, pillar, out_of_sight, the rail) took 0.11 of the open rate behind cover from a blaze, 0.17 to 0.22 from a skeleton, 0.04 to 0.25 from a ghast, 0.2 from a piglin (the open rate what the model gives for that shooter standing in the open), 0.15 in all; the first three seconds 0.3 to 0.6 of it from a blaze or a skeleton, which is the setup's seconds counted. A shooter kept off by what stands between is priced at 15 in 100 of its open rate for the seconds after the setup (COVER_LEAK, stanceCost `leaks`), said beside the figure; not for a stance over in its own seconds (a meal, a run). (f) The fight with nothing to swing at (survival.js shotsIn15) and keep_working each summed hit over the shot's interval for every shooter in sight, twice a second for all and, for a blaze, without its fire: keep_working in one recorded scene with three blazes in sight and more about 61, a fight standing in the fire of those three 10.6; now stanceCost's figure for the fifteen seconds, the fire in (107 and 18.6 there; a ghast 32 blocks off, fight 23.3 to 2.6). (g) A magma cube or a slime was priced as the big one and its whole family (13 mobs, 52 damage in fifteen seconds through two iron pieces) whatever its size; they spawn as sizes 1, 2 and 4 (Slime.finalizeSpawn), health the size squared, a hit of the size (a magma cube's two more), about three of half its size where it dies: slimeOf, slimeSplits, the size read from metadata 16 (slimeSize) in the stance's estimate and state: a small one 1 damage, a medium and its three smalls 8.6, the big 52; the record's fights with them (priced 9.6 to 16.7, taken 0.3 to 0.9) carry no size, so the calibration cannot show it and it is the game's rule; unknown size is the big one. (h) Said, not changed: a fight priced with biters 4 to 16 blocks off that are not coming now says "the figure counts each as coming: ... about a third had one at arm's length inside fifteen seconds (a fifth on the latest builds), and the bot took about a quarter of what was priced (those coming arrived in three of four)" (survival.js idleSays); the price still counts them, because the record says how many stood off and not why (a portal or a fungus a hoglin will not pass, no way in, not its target: the traces show a hoglin 4 blocks off for 17 seconds and one that came to 3.2 and stood).
