On the real record of 25598 it fires at 00:05Z (about 40 minutes after the bot came to the tip: the 30-minute box, and a run of ten from 23:54:46 to 00:02:10Z), not at 23:45Z, and again at 00:30Z and 00:59:50Z (12 none_good in a row, 3 blocks). On 25585 it fires at 01:33Z (30 minutes within 5 blocks of (117, 46, -358), none good in 54 of 119 answers; not at 01:15Z or 01:25Z, the bot having walked a hundred blocks until 01:00). **The second case, 25585 (mid-242-ca-nether-1, 116 minutes in at 01:32Z), read the same way while it ran (read only): the same pattern at a span's end, with a different cause for the stall.** It walked a bar of netherrack one wide at y 42 (floor top 43) along x 117 (its cells z -335 to -374 are in the saved region; the bot's trail runs 110 blocks north on it) over the lava sea, 11 above the lava, ran out of netherrack at about 01:00Z (7 carried at 00:40, 3 from 00:44, 1 at 01:00, 0 at 01:04), and its unstuck moves (place, pillar, dig) put netherrack and gravel down round it at z -358 to -356: netherrack at (117, 43, -358), gravel at (117, 43, -357) and (117, 43, -356) and a column of gravel to y 47 at z -356, a wall that cuts the bar 2 to 4 cells behind it. Two hoglins were 8 and 10 blocks off at the last question, seen; the survival layer held the span (hold_on_span 8 of the last 40 minutes, turn_priority 19 and shield_policy 16 askings). It stood at (117.5, 43, -360) to 01:33Z. **Carried at 01:33Z**: no pickaxe (an iron sword, a stone axe, a wooden hoe, flint and steel), 6 gravel (15 at 01:04, 12, 9, then 6: the wall and the pillar), 15 oak fences, a crafting table, a furnace, a white bed, an oak plank, a water bucket and a bucket, 29 gold nuggets, 108 coal, 5 cooked mutton and a cooked beef, health 20 hunger 20. **Beyond the end**: the bar goes on 14 cells north of the bot to (116, 42, -374), where a nether wart block hangs at head height west of it (115, 44, -374: dug by hand in half a second, one block that holds and that PLACEABLE names), and the crimson land of a forest island (nylium, wart blocks, stems, weeping vines) lies west and north-west of it: the nearest ground that is not part of the bar is (112, 41, -368), four cells of gap from the bar cell at (117, 42, -368), eight steps north along it from where the bot stood, twelve cells of gap from its own cell, and twenty-four to the east. **Offered** at the recorded question of 01:23:20Z: step_north, place_north, step_south, place_south (gravel into the cell at the feet), pillar (gravel), none_good 0.23; at 01:04:45 bridge_east, bridge_west and bridge_south while netherrack was carried. The answers were not the stall: step_north was the answer 10 of 10 on the recorded state (0.62) and the bot took it; what held it was the survival layer (the hold on the span against the hoglins), its own wall behind it, and the legs and walks that could not start (fortress_leg north "no route" with no goal, the walk to the warped forest "the way passes along a drop that would kill", the portal 381 blocks off "legs of thirty-two blocks made no ground"): every one a question about a walk, and no move it had crossed the eight cells to the land west, which the fifteen fences would have crossed (12 of 15 from its own cell, 4 from the bar cell eight steps north). The crossing kit is the second place the fences are missed: bridging.js LAID (rock kinds, wart blocks, nether woods) is the stock the crossing prices and lays, so "0 blocks carried" was said of a pack with fifteen fences there too, as in note 635; not changed here (a fence span is walked crouched and the pathfinder does not walk one; the unstuck moves do). With the same code on the saved ground (test/fixtures/span-tip-mid-242-ca.json): here.floor "a floor of 18 cells, joined to no ground; the nearest ground that is not part of it is 4 cells of gap from the floor cell at (117, 42, -368), 8 steps along it from here, at (112, 41, -368)", bridge_west "12 cells of gap away, at (112, 41, -368): 12 of the 15 fences carried would reach it", bridge_east "24 cells ... 15 fences carried, 9 short of it. The shortest of the ways from here is west, 12 cells"; live Jev, ten asks: as recorded step_north 10; with these options and the floor line bridge_west 9, step_north 1. At the tip itself the bridge west is not offered (a fence needs three cells clear over the floor cell and the wart block is at the second): the block is dug (dig_west_head) instead. **Probes** (live Jev, the recorded questions with the options as they are now, state as recorded with `here.notOffered` from the new code, ten asks each): 00:37:12Z, before: none_good 10 of 10 (the fallback took take_floor); after: bridge_east 10 of 10. 00:48:01Z: before none_good 10 of 10; after bridge_north 7, step_south 3. 00:59:40Z (at the tip, the post two under): before none_good 10 of 10, the fallback step_north; after bridge_north 9, step_west 1 (before the step said what it lands on: step_north 5 of 5, bridge 0.16). Replay cases span-tip-fence-bridge-25598, span-tip-step-onto-post-25598 and bar-out-of-netherrack-fence-bridge-25585 (5 of 5 each; the whole suite 79 of 84 before the third, the other five are the known gaps and two encounter_stance cases this change does not touch, retreat-from-spider-at-7 and bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, run once). Tests: test/fence-bridge-650.test.js (the real ground: the bridge and its price, the shortfall, the table, no take_floor and its line, the island of 21 cells and the rock as ground, the rise's fence line, the bridge's placement against the floor stood on, the step onto the post, the shortest way said), test/stranded-650.test.js (the audit function), test/island-bridge-625.test.js (take_floor over lava is not offered, the table floors the one-cell gap). npm test 2374 of 2374, the same with JEV_ARBITER=shadow. **Open**: (a) not run in a world: the fence bridge (placing against a fence's side, the crouched walk, the drop of 1 onto the rock) is checked on the physics and on unit tests only; the next stranded trial that carries fences is the check; (b) the 'away' aim ("off this spot, onto dry ground at least eight blocks away") can be met by walking nine blocks along the same span (the span is 21 cells and dry footing is any floor), so the work_free spell can end "out" while the bot is still on the span it is stranded on; it should be met by leaving the floor the bot is on (islandOf), not by a distance, and is not changed here; (c) a fence bridge is a walk of a quarter block's width over a drop that kills: a ghast's fireball push or a hoglin over it is as deadly as on any span, and the question says a touch is death; (d) the bed and more of the pack's full blocks (planks and logs of the burning woods, furnace, barrel) are not counted as bridge blocks; (e) 25585's stall is the survival hold and the walks, not the unstuck answers (see above); whether the bot, told the floor and the price, walks eight cells north and bridges, is the next trial's to show; (f) the two cover planks on the span (-112, 52..53, 143) cut it for the pathfinder ("no route", "around" lists them) and are not offered as blocks to take (they drop onto the span, where they can be picked up).

653. *Gold walked past in the Nether: 462 blocks open to the air within eight blocks of the paths walked, 55 taken (an audit of 94 flight records from 2026-09-29, 27 worlds, about 1,125 Nether minutes, each record set against its trial's Nether region files; which record is which world is approximate).* Pearls were under 16 the whole time, so the pearl condition never kept the bot from stopping. Within eight blocks of the walked paths: 3,536 gold blocks (3,510 nether gold ore, 26 gilded blackstone), 462 of them touching air (145 within 4 blocks, 152 at 4 to 6, 165 at 6 to 8). Where the bot was at its closest pass to air-touching gold within 6 blocks: find_fortress 189 (77 within 4), cross_toward 46 (24), warped_search 26 (12), tunnel 17 (15), stalk_mob and close_in 4 (3), return_to_blazes 1 (1). In 70 of those 297 near passes health was under 16 at the closest point. **Why**: (1) the look ran only on the fortress sweep's own walks (leg, go-to, patrol, spawner wait) and the walk back to the blazes; crossToward, the warped search, approachFortress, goDown and the floor walk, the gather walks, corpse runs and the return to the portal never looked; (2) a walk that stopped for gold was booked as a failure: goToWay's stopped walk was not "close", so it went on to approachFortress and asked Jev about the way with "the walk came no nearer", and the in-fortress patrol's walk ended more than 1.75 blocks off, so `map.failed` marked that floor as failed; only return_to_blazes undid the stop; (3) the radius was 4 with no Jev option (the client was null), the ore test `/_ore$/` left out gilded blackstone and gold blocks, and health under 16 or food under 14 took every candidate away without a word; (4) the shortage line said only "nine gold ingots barter a pearl": not the nuggets a block, the share of a pearl, or the seconds. **Change**: `navigate` (skills.js) takes `passing`: the walk runs with a stop for gold in reach; stopped for it (and not for the caller's own stop), it mines the gold (opportunistic-mining.js mineInPassing) and runs the same walk again, its time given back the detour's seconds, up to eight detours a walk. The stop is not the walk's end, so no caller sees it as a failure. The walks with `passing`: all of the fortress sweep's, return_to_blazes, approachFortress's walk_route, the warped search, both nether-gather walks, goDown and the floor walk, corpse runs and the return to the portal in the Nether; crossToward lays and digs its own way, so it looks once before the crossing. mob-hunt's own stops (stopWhen: goldInPassing and the look before each walk) are gone. Within 4 blocks, nether gold ore and gold blocks are taken as a rule while pearls are short and health is at least 16 and food at least 14. Everything else in reach is the new question `passing_gold` (asked at most every 15 s; without Jev, nothing is taken): gold to 8 blocks, gilded blackstone, and gold within 4 while health or food is low, which the option now states ("Health 9 of 20 and food 18 of 20: under the 16 health or 14 food at which gold this near is taken without asking"). Each option gives the block's gold ("2 to 6 gold nuggets, about 4, about 0.44 of an ingot, about 1/20 of a pearl at nine ingots a pearl"; gilded blackstone "a 1 in 10 chance of 2 to 5 gold nuggets (about 0.35 nuggets a block on average), otherwise the block itself", about 1/231 of a pearl), the distance and walking steps, the seconds of the detour there and back with the dig (steps at 4.3 blocks a second plus the dig time with the tool carried), and how many such blocks and minutes of detours a pearl is. The safety checks stay: dry standing, the hostile check, a tool and room, no piglin within 16 blocks of the gold, a route of at most 16 steps that digs and lays nothing. Two are new: no lava against the block, and no standing on the block being broken. The opportunistic_ore shortage line now gives the nuggets and the share of a pearl. Diamonds, iron and lapis in passing are the rule's alone, as before (within 4, at 16 health and 14 food). **Probe** (live, the new question, 5 asks each, 2 more with confidence): nether gold ore at 6 blocks with a 5 s detour, continue 5 of 5 (0.82); gilded blackstone at 3 blocks, continue 5 of 5 (0.89); nether gold ore at 2 blocks at health 9, continue 5 of 5 (0.78). The same with how many blocks and minutes a pearl is: unchanged. So with Jev asked, the gain is the 145 near blocks the rule takes (about 7 pearls' worth over those 1,125 minutes, if every one were reached and mined), plus the walks that now look at all and no longer fail when they stop. Tests: test/gold-passing-653.test.js (the tiers, lava and the block underfoot, what Jev is told and that continue leaves the gold, gilded blackstone's price, the walk that mines and walks on to the same goal), test/companion.test.js (the fortress sweep's walks look in passing and the step digs nothing itself). **Open**: (a) not run in a world; the next Nether trial's flight record (`opportunistic.history` entries with `passing: true`, and `lastDecision.question: 'passing_gold'`) is the check; (b) Jev passes every offer in the probe, at full health too; whether 1/20 of a pearl for 5 s is worth it is a judgment, and it is Jev's; if the trials show pearls are the bottleneck, the fact missing may be what a pearl costs by the other ways (the enderman hunt's measured minutes a pearl); (c) the reasons the old stops failed (`opportunistic.lastError`) are not separable in the flight records from the goal's own lastError, and were not tallied; (d) the tunnel keeps its own mining question and does not look in passing; the crossing looks only where it starts; (e) the audit's 3,074 gold blocks not touching air are not reachable without digging and are not offered.

654. *A pickaxe promised and never made (25581, mid-243-ch, 22:45 to 23:03 local, flight records 02-39-13, 02-51-51 and 02-57-56Z, commit 53ce77b running).* Asked: why "A fortress! I'm heading for it." at 23:00:14 was followed 5 s later by "I'm looking for a fortress (leg 39)", and why it was then stuck at (-45, 55, 514). The sighting was real and is remembered: 1,180 nether bricks at fortress heights, first said at 22:47:49 ("a nether fortress at -82, 505"), the step's `found` (-68, 62, 537), bricks at (-105, 52, 517), 31 to 60 blocks from the bot, its region (x -432 to -1, z 432 to 863) marked as holding it; the only bastion known is at (89, 43, 324), a region away, so it is not a bastion mistaken. Every ask after carried it: `fortressInView` with its bricks, floors and set-aside, and `back_to_fortress` offered. What kept the bot off it was the pickaxe. Its iron pickaxe (239 uses at 01:53Z) wore out on the legs by 02:20Z; from then it carried 12 iron ingots, 4 planks, 2 logs, 16 gravel, no block that holds and no pickaxe. `blockStock.makingAPickaxe` said so ("The wood carried is enough for the table and the sticks"), and restock_blocks and blocks_then_cross each said "a wooden pickaxe is made first from what is carried (2 logs, 4 planks), a few seconds, and the rock is dug with it". Neither made one: restockStep went straight to `actions.mineAt`, work.js `mine` with a selected block, which digs with what is in hand, and dig() refused each block ("Missing harvest tool for netherrack"); three in a row ended it, gained 0, and the offer said so each time after ("the mining ended: three blocks in a row gave nothing"). The approach at 02:57:57 to 02:58:06: keep_searching, walk_route ("No path to the goal!" at once, though surveyed as a partial route ending 15 blocks nearer), blocks_then_cross three times, each 0 dug. Then every leg ended at its first cell, "out of blocks (0 carried)": north, west, the staircase west ("no ground made": no pickaxe) and south in 11 s, which is legs 36 to 39; the leg count is legs begun, not ground made. At 03:00:12 Jev answered none_good (0.33) over leg_west, seek_fortress_height and back_to_fortress: the missing move was making the pickaxe, which no question offered. The stuck spot is the same cause: seek_fortress_height chosen at 03:00:14 dug nothing, the unstuck moves (work_free) rose from y 48 to y 55 by rise_through and a three-block gravel pillar, and there every step rested ("step east: tried 2 times ... nothing") and until_rest_ends waited; at 03:02:51 it was on the gravel at (-45, 55, 514), no route west. The "No way on in this direction" turns before it (legs 2 to 17, 22:09 to 22:33) were with the pickaxe, and not looked into here. **Change** (src/mob-hunt.js): pickaxeFirst names the pickaxe that is made, the best head carried (iron from three ingots, stone from cobblestone, cobbled deepslate or blackstone, else wooden from nine planks' worth), with what from ("an iron pickaxe is made first from what is carried (3 of the 12 iron ingots; 2 logs, 4 planks)"); makePickaxe makes it through the craft steps (actions.acquireStep, one step a call, up to eight); restockStep makes it before any digging, and where it cannot be made the restock digs nothing by hand and its `lastRestock.why` says "no pickaxe to dig with: an iron pickaxe was not made: ..."; blocks_then_cross mines through restockStep, so it too; and fortress_leg offers make_pickaxe wherever no pickaxe is carried and one can be made, said with which, from what, and that without it rock and netherrack dug by hand drop nothing and N blocks can be laid (src/decisions/travel.js declares it; restock_blocks' and blocks_then_cross' definitions say the pickaxe made). The mid-242-ab fixture (note 591), with 11 ingots carried, is now offered an iron pickaxe, not a wooden one. Tests: test/fortress-wall.test.js (blocks_then_cross with no pickaxe makes the iron pickaxe first and digs its 49 blocks with it, where dug by hand throws; the pickaxe not made, nothing is dug and why is said; with 25581's inventory the legs offer make_pickaxe with its wording and choosing it makes it; no head and too little wood promises none, nine planks' worth promises a wooden one, blackstone a stone one). **Open**: (a) not run in a world: the next Nether trial with a worn pickaxe (`goal.step.action: 'make_pickaxe'`, and `make_pickaxe` in fortress_leg's options) is the check; (b) fortress_approach itself does not offer make_pickaxe: its tunnel is still offered with no pickaxe (said in its state as "a staircase ... digs nothing") and only blocks_then_cross makes one; (c) walk_route was surveyed as a partial route 15 blocks nearer and failed at once with "No path to the goal!": the walk and its survey disagree, not looked into; (d) the pickaxe wore out on legs through rock with no spare made while ingots were carried: the night mine replaces its pickaxe from the pockets, the fortress legs do not.

655. *The Nether bots that stood still (25583 mid-243-cg, 25589 mid-243-cd-nether-1, 25592 mid-243-cc-nether-1, 25585 mid-242-ca-nether-1, and 25581 mid-243-ch; progress audit and flight records around 03:00Z on 2026-09-29, all on commit 53ce77b; region files as saved at 03:06Z).* What each was doing. **25583**: 30 minutes on one cell of blackstone at (-21, 101, -19) in a basalt delta, 1.8 health, hunger 13, no food, no pickaxe, no block that holds (14 gravel), 30 iron ingots and no wood. Every walk was "no route" (noPath, no goal height): in the Nether the pathfinder takes no cell with lava in any of the eight cells round it at the feet, head or floor (movement.js besideLavaRefused), and in the delta the lava lies in pools level with the floor, so from its cell the walkable set was that cell alone (a walk over the saved region without the rule reaches 328 cells, 56 blocks out, 39 of them beside lava). unstuck_move offered single steps (north, west, east), gravel that falls and a pillar; the steps went a cell and back ("nothing changed"), rested, and rung_progress answered until_rest_ends, which held it still 95% of the last 15 minutes (the audit's persist/detour 12.8 of 13.4 min); none good 54 of 75. A walk of nine cells, two of them beside lava, reached dry ground with no lava round it eight blocks north; nothing offered it. **25589**: 17 minutes at (-163, 38, 150), near the far end of its own span at y 37 over the lava sea at y 31 (a bar west along z 155 from the shore at x -134, a diagonal north-west, a bar on west), no block carried, an iron pickaxe with 170 uses. Every leg rested "out of blocks (0 carried)"; fortress_leg offered seek_fortress_height (a staircase from a span: "no ground made") and return_for_blocks (a portal 219 blocks off, itself "cannot be reached from here"); restock_blocks was not offered because the restock looked for rock within 16 blocks and a walk of 32, and the shore netherrack was a walk of 30 along the span but more than 16 blocks off. unstuck_move 64 asks (17 pillar), none good 70 of 163, 12.8 of 57 minutes held until rests ended. **25592**: no pickaxe, three oak logs, six planks, two sticks and a crafting table carried (33 raw iron, a furnace, coal). 48 of 50 minutes "cross toward": a crouched crossing at y 52 through basalt dug by hand, 19 cells in 4.5 minutes; blocks_then_cross and restock_blocks said "a wooden pickaxe is made first" and gained nothing ("Missing harvest tool for basalt"), the note 654 fault. The upkeep asked eight times, block_reserve ("comes out in a moment with any pickaxe") or carry_on: a pickaxe was offered only as a spare beside one carried (work.js spareDue, `pickaxes.length > 0`). It sighted its fortress at 03:07Z. **25585**: not stuck in place (458 net in an hour) but no pickaxe and one plank: legs of 96 blocks tunnelled by hand at y 54 (4 minutes a 32-block leg, "nothing is seen from inside it"), and at 03:06 Jev chose leg_west, back through its own tunnel (said: "stood on 60 of the 96 blocks"). restock_blocks was offered as "Dig 35 blocks ... about 78 seconds" with "none can be made from what is carried: netherrack dug by hand drops nothing" in the same line. **25581** (note 654) carried 12 ingots and oak logs with no pickaxe. So five of seven Nether bots had no pickaxe. **Root causes**: (1) a Nether region the walks refuse whole (the lava-beside rule) with no whole walk ever offered, only single steps; (2) a restock that looks only 16 blocks round the bot, blind to the rock its own span joins; (3) no pickaxe made when none is carried: the upkeep's spare needs one carried, and the restock promised one it never made (note 654 fixed the latter on the fortress search); (4) a restock offered that cannot gain a block; and behind all of them the rest/hold loop (rung_progress until_rest_ends) waiting where the ways had emptied. **Change**: unstuck.js walkOffPlan and the move `walk_off` (unstuck_move, for the 'away' aim): the nearest cell 8 or more blocks from where it got stuck that is dry ground with no lava in its eight cells, over the ground as it stands (level, one up, down to three, nothing dug or laid), taking the fewest cells beside lava, within 16 blocks; said with its cells, the height, how many cells have lava beside them, the lava touch priced for this body ("a touch is death" at 1.8), and that the bot's own walks take no cell beside lava in the Nether. Walked a cell at a time through the single-step move, crouched where the cell has lava beside it and the step is level; stopped and said where the body is not in the cell. Hard rules kept: no drop of two or more and no jump up onto a cell beside lava, no cell in lava. Single moves now say "lava beside the cell it ends on" (25583's step north said only "ends on dry ground"). mob-hunt.js blocksPlan: where nothing can be dug within the near reach, it looks along the floor the bot stands on to 64 blocks and a walk of 96 (at most 800 cells, bridging.js spanBlockSources `cells`), said as "a walk of 30 blocks from here, back along the floor the bot stands on (nothing can be dug from ground within 16 blocks of here)", and the gathering uses that reach (its walk timed by its cells). restock_blocks is not offered where no pickaxe is carried and none can be made. mineThenCross makes the pickaxe (note 654's makePickaxe) before the crossing when the blocks were carried already and the restock did not run. surveyCrossing priced with a pickaxe to be made is not said as "no block comes back". work.js upkeep offers `make_pickaxe` whenever no pickaxe is carried and one can be made (note 654's pickaxeFirst: iron, stone or wooden, what from), said with its uses and what digging by hand costs where the bot is; without Jev it is made first; block_reserve says when none is carried. Tests: test/nether-stuck-655.test.js on two new fixtures from the saved regions (test/fixtures/basalt-delta-mid-243-cg.json: the pathfinder's noPath, the walk off's nine cells and two lava-side cells, no airborne step onto one, walked and stopped cell by cell; test/fixtures/span-end-mid-243-cd.json: nothing within 16, the shore a walk of 30, restock_blocks offered from the span end with the portal 219 off beside it, no restock where no pickaxe can be made, the restock making the wooden pickaxe it said before any dig), the upkeep's make_pickaxe with 25581's pockets; test/mob-hunt.test.js's restock tests carry a pickaxe. Replay cases: basalt-delta-walk-off-25583 (walk_off 5 of 5; before the lava-beside fact on single steps, step_north 3 of 5) and no-pickaxe-upkeep-25592 (make_pickaxe 5 of 5). **Open**: (a) not run in a world: the next basalt-delta stall (`unstuck_move` offering `walk_off`, `goal.step.move: 'walk_off'`) and the next span end with a pickaxe and no blocks (`restock_blocks` "back along the floor") are the checks; (b) the rest/hold loop itself is unchanged: until_rest_ends still holds where every way rests from here; with the walk off, the far restock and the pickaxe offered, fewer ways should empty, and the audit's persist/detour share is the measure; (c) 25583 carries 30 ingots and no wood; the warped forest was 32 blocks west and its nether gather could not walk there (the same lava rule); the walk off leaves the delta's cell, not the delta; (d) the fortress search's other walks (legs, gather walks, the return to the portal) still refuse every cell beside lava with no whole-walk offer of their own; a leg or return_to_portal priced by its lava-side cells, as walk_off is, would be the general form; (e) 25585's legs tunnel by hand with no pickaxe and no wood: stems from a nether forest for one are not offered from the search; (f) the pickaxe wore out on legs with no spare made in the Nether (note 654's (d)); the upkeep now makes one when none is carried, not before.
656. *Fire resistance, the one answer to a blaze's fire (the day's top killer: fireballs and burning), was never recognized, kept, bartered for or drunk.* Before: a barter kept only the names in KEEP (pearls, obsidian, string, fire charges, quartz, soul sand, iron nuggets, books), so a fire resistance potion a piglin threw was left lying with the gravel; nothing read a potion's contents (a water bottle and a fire resistance potion are both `potion`); body.js `fireResistant` counted the effect as on however little was left, and terrain.js priced a fall into lava as harmless on it; no price of a blaze fight (combat-estimate, blaze-stand) knew of it; and the only source offered was the enchanted golden apple. **What the 26.1.2 jar says** (read this time, not remembered): the barter table (loot_table/gameplay/piglin_bartering.json) is 469 in weight a throw, a fire resistance potion 8 and a fire resistance splash potion 8 (both the three-minute kind), a water bottle 10, ender pearls 10 (two to four): 16 in 469, about 3.4 in 100 a throw, about 29 ingots a potion on the average. Potions.FIRE_RESISTANCE is 3600 ticks (3:00), LONG_FIRE_RESISTANCE 9600 (8:00); their potion_contents ids are 11 and 12 (the jar's registries report). LivingEntity.hurtServer returns before any hurt or knockback for damage in the is_fire tag (in_fire, campfire, on_fire, lava, hot_floor, fireball, unattributed_fireball) with the effect on; SmallFireball.onHitEntity puts back the fire it set when the hurt did not land. So with it a blaze's fireball does nothing at all (no hurt, no push, no fire), burning and lava nothing; a blaze's swing within two blocks, a ghast's blast (its direct six is `fireball`, the explosion is not), arrows, blades and falls hurt as ever. A splash potion acts on each body within four blocks, cut by the distance from where it breaks to the body's box. **Change**: src/fire-resistance.js (new) reads the potion from its potion_contents (or the old Potion tag), the potions carried, the effect's seconds left (combat-estimate effectLeft, which now matches the registry's "FireResistance"), the barter's odds and a drink (the potion drunk in 1.6 s, a splash thrown looking straight down). bartering.js keeps a fire resistance potion from any barter (the pearl barter included) and counts it, and barterForFireResistance throws round after round until one is carried, the gold is gone or no piglin is in view. fortress_visit offers drink_fire_resistance (a potion carried and under a minute of the effect on: its minutes against the walk ahead; drunk, the visit goes on as go_in) and barter_fire_resistance (none carried, in the Nether, gold to throw once a gold piece is worn and a piglin within 32: the table's odds, the chance with the gold carried, the pace; asked again after). encounter_stance offers drink_fire_resistance where a blaze shoots in sight or the body is alight, priced over its 1.6 s (0.5 for a splash) as the meal is, with the fight here over fifteen seconds as the bot is and with the effect on (on note 617's ledge: about 5.4 against 0). body_way offers it in lava, alight and on a hot floor, a splash first. The prices: fightEstimate takes fireproofFor, and a blaze's fireball pieces and the fire on the body count only from when the effect ends (a partial effect prices the rest of the fight in full); burnBetween takes the same; blaze-stand's close-in, stands, box, corner and away-to-heal split their fire at the effect's end, the swings of a blaze within two left whole; a ghast is priced as it was (its blast was never measured apart from its hit). Burning out of the fire is nothing only while the effect outlasts the fire left, and then no body_way is asked for it. **In a world** (a scratch vanilla 26.1.2 server on port 25710, the scene staged from its console: a glass room at y 100 in the Nether, 128 gold ingots and golden boots given, three piglins summoned): barterForFireResistance threw 54 ingots in 159 s and stopped with a fire resistance splash potion carried (potionId 11 as the bot read it) and 7 pearls; a water bottle was picked up in passing (walked over, not sought). Now (src/stance-scene.js): the stance's scene is what its outcome turns on, each in words: the health in whole hearts, the hunger, each mob by kind within the sword's reach (combat.canStrike), within 8 blocks, within 16, farther or unable to get to the bot, and in sight or not; a hit taken, the blocks carried, the shield in the off hand, the block stood on, the rods carried. A book is kept per scene (a scene come back to within holds.js's five-minute cap is the same book). While the scene is unchanged: an answer that came to nothing in it (failed, or a striking stance that struck nothing, with nothing else done) is left out while two or more other ways stay on offer, said in notOfferedNow, as note 596 leaves one out; an answer that held (a wait that ran its time, a fight that struck) is taken again without asking ("[scene hold]" in the log), except where the stance before was ended by one of its physical triggers (a newcomer, a hit, a line to where it hid, a creeper's walk, a shot on its way, the bot off its spot, a way new on offer) or by holds.js's cap; keep_working, eating, drinking and the runs are never held so, as holds.js does not hold them on. At five minutes from the last asking the question is asked and the rung's question is due (tried.rungDue), holds.js's cap. Asked, the question says it: sameSceneSoFar (nothing a stance turns on has changed for so long, the facts, each answer in that time and what it came to, the none-good answers, and what would change the scene), or what changed since the last scene and how its answers went. The none-good answer to the stance is counted by the scene (decisions/index.js `situation`, repeats.js noneGoodAfter `anyWeight`): twice in one scene, at any weight, and the question is spent there five minutes and escalated to survival_priority through the ledger (tried.escalate, the stall raised), as note 599 meant; before, it was never spent on the ledge. Note 596's test of the 06:27:21 burst changes with it: the hoglin a block and a half along below the ledge, still unable to get to the bot, is the same scene, and the fight comes back when a heart is lost.

The measured rows of note 645 (playedAnswers) were already said with every stance and hunt at a blaze fight and are unchanged; "passes" (the fortress patrol's) are not said here.

660. *Lava beside a cell priced, not refused (the Fable check-in at 04Z and note 655's (d): 25583 mid-243-cg stranded 174 minutes with one walkable cell, 25589 mid-243-cd-nether-1 325 minutes without sighting a fortress; worked on the saved regions and in a scratch world).* **The rule before**: movement.js besideLavaRefused (note 516) refused, in the Nether, any cell with lava in any of the eight cells round it at the floor, the feet or the head (24 cells), whatever the health, the armor or what was about; `lavaRefusals` made every walk's failure "No route ... the way passes beside lava". Every walk through the pathfinder takes it: fortress legs' walks, the gathering's walks, walk_route, the portal walk, the tunneling stairs (which ask the same rule of each step). Only walk_off (note 655), the crossing's floor walk and the portal frame opted out by name. **What it guarded against** (notes 514, 516, 220-e, 580): a step's drift or a push putting the body into lava, and a fall or jump carrying it past the cell it aimed at. What each part is physically: lava level with the floor beside the cell (a pool's edge) is an edge, and a crouched body is held on its floor at an edge by the physics (prismarine-physics clips a sneaking body's move off its floor), so without a push it is no danger; lava corner to corner is out of the body's width (0.6 wide in a cell, 0.2 from each side at the middle) unless it drifts; lava a block to a side at the feet or the head is walked into as easily as the next cell, which a crouch only slows; a hit's knockback is not clipped by the crouch at all, and a touch in the Nether is the lava's hits and then fifteen seconds of burning with no water to put it out (terrain.js lavaTouch: 23 at full health with no armor, about 18 in iron). Landing on such a cell after a drop of two or more or a jump up carries the body on past it. **Change** (movement.js): `lavaRound` gives the lava round a cell and how much of it is a block to a side; `besideLavaRefused` refuses the cell only (a) where a touch is death to this body now (lavaTouch with the health, the armor worn and fire resistance with 30 s or more left) and the lava is a block to a side, or (b) where something that can push the bot (danger.js pushersAbout) is in line with the lava: lava on the far side of the cell from it, within seventy degrees of its line (a shot in flight by its heading); under fire resistance neither. The deadly-drop part (note 541) is unchanged except that lava level with the floor is now the lava rule's, a drop being a block or more. Otherwise the cell is walked at a cost of 6 more than open ground (LAVA_SIDE_COST; lava a block to a side keeps note 516's 4 as well), so routes take as few as the ground allows. Kept as hard rules: no drop of two or more and no jump up onto any cell with lava round it (now the whole 24-cell set in the Nether, as walk_off counts it), no block laid where a miss is lava, no cell in lava. skills.js: the walk crouches on any cell with lava round it in the Nether (crouchOnEdge, as walk_off walks its cells; released before a step down, as for edges); a pathfinder "No path to the goal!" (a search that found part of a way) is said as the empty route's no-route when the rule refused cells, and both now say why ("where a touch of it is death at this health", "in line with something that can push the bot"); surveyRoute carries `lava: { beside, touching }` for the route in the Nether (movement.js lavaAlong), said by lavaAlongSays with how it is walked and what a touch costs this body, in the gathering's and the portal trip's "On foot" (nether-gather walkSays), fetch_stems' route survey, the rung's landmark and target surveys (work.js), and walk_route (mob-hunt, replacing its "within two blocks of lava" count; "the pathfinder walks upright" is now "upright on open ground and crouched beside lava or a drop that kills"). walk_off and the no-way texts say the rule as it now is. **Measured on the saved regions** (every cell reachable over the ground as it stands, nothing dug or laid): 25583's delta from its cell, the old rule 1 cell at any health; now 97 at its 1.84 health in iron (cells with lava only corner to corner or at the floor's corners), 208 at 20; a ghast 21 blocks east in sight: 1 again, every cell with lava west of it refused, those with lava only east, north or south walked. The pathfinder now finds the walk off's dry ground eight blocks north at 1.84 (7 cells, lava round some, none a block to a side). 25589's span end was not collapsed by this rule (171 cells before, 173 after: its trouble was blocks, note 655); its shore cell (-134, 32, 153) with the sea west and north is walked with nothing about, refused with a blaze over the sea to the south-west (its push toward the lava north), walked with one due west, refused at 1.8 health (a touch is death). **In a world** (a scratch vanilla 26.1.2 server on port 25760, peaceful, staged from its console: a one-wide blackstone causeway 25 cells long through lava pools level with the floor on both sides, in an obsidian box in the Nether; the bot in iron at 20 health): the survey found 28 cells, 27 with lava round them, 25 with it a block to a side; the walk arrived in 21 s, crouched on 412 of the 413 ticks it stood on such cells (the first tick before the crouch took), no part of the body in lava on any tick, 20 health throughout. Dropped to 5 health (a touch is death), the walk back was refused: "No route from here to (1, 100, 10) (noPath): the way passes beside lava where a touch of it is death at this health". Server stopped by its own PID and deleted. Tests: test/nether-lava-660.test.js (the delta at 1.84 and 20 health, the ghast's line, the shore's four cases, fire resistance, the crouch on a cell with lava at the feet or head only, the no-path reason); nether-stuck-655 and nether-wood-658 say the rule as it now is. The saved-ground test bot has no world floor (`game.minY` undefined), so the pathfinder's drops never land there: 655's "noPath" assertion was partly that, and is dropped; the 660 tests set y 0. npm test 2441 of 2441, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 85 and 86 of 89 on two runs, the two known gaps open each time, the known flake bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up once, and once basalt-delta-walk-off-25583 (walk_off 2, none_good 3; ten more runs gave walk_off 8 of 10: its recorded options carry the old text, so this is the case's own spread). **Open**: (a) not seen in a trial: the next Nether bot in a delta or on the lava sea's shore (walks with `lava` in the survey, "passes beside lava where ..." in a no-route) is the check; (b) unarmored at full health a touch is 23 of 20, so such a body still refuses cells with lava a block to a side (honest by lavaTouch; whether two hits for a touch is right at a crouch's pace is unmeasured); (c) the seventy degrees of "in line" and pushersAbout's reach (a ghast in sight to 64) are the push's rules as they stood, not measured for the delta; (d) nether-travel.js's own way down to the floor (wayDown) and the fortress legs' line survey (surveyLeg) still count lava beside a cell as no step; (e) the crouch holds only on the ground and is let go for a step down, so a one-down step onto a cell with lava round it is walked upright for that step.

661. *The blaze and fire deaths of the overnight run, and what the new code paths did (2026-09-29T04:49Z to 11:37Z, commit 3c1af18 running; flight records of every port, scripts/blaze-record.js, scripts/after-rod.js, scripts/death-timeline.js; 248 blaze fights, 73 of them ending in a death, 76 of the 115 deaths with a blaze about, 63 by the game's own line a blaze or its fire).* **What killed** (the last minute's damage of the 145 deaths by a blaze or its fire over the two days: 48% fireballs, 32% the fire they set, 16% blaze blows at arm's length; overnight alone the blows were 17%, up from 7% on the first day, since the bot now walks in). Grouped by root cause, not by symptom: (1) **38 deaths in a fight begun healthy (15 health or more) among four or more blazes**, 16 of them within a minute of a rod: the same fights the rods come from. Overnight, a fight at a live spawner with four or more blazes within sixteen (114 fights) ended in a death 49% of the time and in a rod 45% (79 rods, 56 deaths: 1.4 rods a death); every other fight (134) in a death 13% and a rod 50% (98 rods, 17 deaths: 5.8 rods a death). With one blaze about at most, 61 fights, 10% died; two or three, 62 fights, 13%. A fight brought a rod as often among four or more blazes as among fewer: what the number of blazes changed was the deaths. Of the 56 deaths with a healthy start and four or more blazes within sixteen at some time in the fight, the median was 115 s in the fight, 43 s to fall under 10 health and 54 s more to die, four fireballs landed, each 3.5 health through a helmet and chestplate and five seconds alight at a health a second (the fire ticks outnumbered the landings 459 to 172 in the last minutes of the 76). (2) **28 deaths with fewer than four blazes about at the end**: the tail of a burn, a wither skeleton or a skeleton's arrows on top of a fireball, blows at arm's length after a strike; 15 within a minute of a rod. (3) **10 deaths carried on at 8 health or less for a minute or more with health unable to come back** (hunger under 18 in all ten, nothing to eat in seven): 25590 stood at 2.7 health with five rods and hunger 15 for fifteen minutes (fortress_visit go_in 0.66, keep_on, restock hoglin_pillar) and was killed by one fireball; the question said the row (62% died, 3% a rod), that health does not come back, and offered go_back at 227 blocks (12% of such walks reached the Overworld) or a hoglin it could not fight: the lost state is upstream of the fortress (no food carried, note 639), not something a fortress question can fix. Across all 76, hunger was under 18 twenty seconds before the death in 29 (19 of them at exactly 17, one point short of regeneration). **The gear**: 245 of the 248 fights were begun in an iron helmet and chestplate and nothing more (the trial saves defer the rest, DEFERRABLE, and no iron was carried: median 0 ingots), none with a bow (0 of 161 read), a potion (0), a golden apple (0) or a cauldron; a water bucket was carried in 160 of 161, and water does not stand in the Nether.

**Did the new code help?** (a) *Fire resistance (656)*: no. 0 potions carried in 161 fights; barter_fire_resistance offered 2 times in the run, never chosen; drink_fire_resistance never on offer. The barter needs gold and 1 potion in about 29 ingots (8+8 in 469), and the only way to have one is brewing, which nothing in the bot does (below). The cauldron ways (634): top_up_cauldron offered 101 times, chosen 3; extinguish_in_cauldron and set_down_cauldron never (no bot carried a cauldron: seven ingots). (b) *strike_at_arm (657)*: fired, and did not help: 42 chosen of 58 offers; over the two days, with four or more blazes about, 25 answers, 52% died within thirty seconds and 6.2 health lost, against burn_out 11 answers 36% (the same question); it is among the last eight answers in 17 deaths and the very last in 7. Not clearly a backfire (asked at 9.9 health on average, at arm's length of a blaze) and not a rescue. (c) *Scene holds (659)*: the scene was in 4,829 of 4,897 stance questions and a held answer in most; the asks per fight-minute went from 7.7 (09-28) to 7.1: the holds cut the same-scene repeats, not the asking. (d) *After a rod (659)*: **it backfired on a small sample**. The table said to Jev after every rod had those that went away first at 5 deaths in 20 (25%), those that stayed at 42%; the 185 rods that followed had those that went away at 24 in 43 (56%) and those that stayed at 33 in 107 (31%); at over 16 health at the rod, 46% against 27%. The table is now the whole record (284 rods: away 29 of 63, 46%; stayed 54 of 157, 34%; no answer 17 of 62) and each answer is also said within the bot's own health (over 16: stayed 33 of 101, away 12 of 33; 8 to 16: stayed 15 of 48, away 11 of 22). Rods picked up under 8 health (both days): 22, 18 died, median 13 s after. (e) *The record itself (631, 645)* was the 09-28 fights: it told Jev a spawner's fight ended in a death 21% and a rod 9%, the strike answer at a spawner with four or more blazes and over 16 health a death 16% and a rod 32% (19 fights), cover a death 15%; and "Iron armour made no difference". Counted over both days the strike row is 78 fights, 32% a rod and 40% a death (cover 77: 6% and 19%), a spawner's fights overall 34% and 30%, and iron does take health off a fight (17.1 with a helmet and chestplate, 380 fights over 16 health; 11.5 with three or four pieces, 105) while the deaths barely moved (24% and 26%): armour takes a third off a fireball's hit (3.9 to 2.5 through all four) and none off the fire.

**The biggest measured difference between two answers Jev is offered in one question** (body_way, standing in fire, both offered together, 427 answers over the two days): with four or more blazes about, putting out the flame where the bot stands was followed by a death within thirty seconds in 45% of 111 answers (7.6 health lost) and running out of the fire in 26% of 97 (5.1 lost); each of the two days alone the same way round (27% and 11% on 09-28, 48% and 26% overnight). With fewer blazes the two are level (17% and 15%). Jev chose the punch 111 times to the run 97, its text saying "no step taken, about a quarter second a flame". Not a trial of either: the answers were given in states these rows do not hold alike.

**Now** (src/blaze-record.js, src/body.js, src/after-rod.js): (1) every way out of fire in a fight with blazes (blaze within 24 in sight, the Nether) ends with its own row, by the blazes within sixteen (WAYS, from `scripts/blaze-record.js --ways`, only where eight answers are in the row): how many answers, how many died within thirty seconds, the health lost, and that these are what followed and not what the way caused; the question's guidance says so. (2) The played record (fortress_visit's playedRecord and the stance's state, which is where "go in" is priced: it had said 14% died at 20 health, 307 fights) is counted again over both days (624 fights: at over 16 health 22% died and 34% a rod; hunger under 18, 33% and 16%; three or more blazes 34% and 30%; the deaths by a blaze 145, 128 with a landing in the last fifteen seconds, 83 of them at 6.5 health or less), and says the newest trials' rows beside it, with the rods each death cost. (3) The stance's answer rows (ANSWERS) are the 624 fights (`--answers`), dated from-to; HOW, counted only on 09-28, says so. (4) "Iron armour made no difference" is gone: the fireball's arithmetic through the armour worn, the fire not reduced, the health lost per fight by the pieces. (5) After a rod, the whole record and the comparison within the bot's own health. (6) scripts/blaze-record.js: `--ways`, `--recent` (the rows RECENT and IRON_LOST hold) so none of this is typed by hand; eachFile skips a record archived while it reads (the janitor). Tests: test/blaze-record-661.test.js (the ways rows said by blazes about and only where eight answers are in them, body_way's tree ending in them, the two script tables on constructed frames, the record's sentences, the after-rod bands adding up), the old literals of 631, 638, 645, 659 and mob-hunt moved to the counted rows (read from the constants where the number is a row's).

npm test 2459 of 2459, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 87 of 91 with the two known gaps open, the known flake bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, and once pocket-nether-no-food-blazes-drifting-25592 (go_for_food 3, stay 2; 15 of 15 go_for_food on a rerun: its recorded text is unchanged by this note). **What was not done, and why** (the largest groups are not a facts problem): the spawner's fights are a treadmill (up to four blazes every ten to forty seconds while the bot is within sixteen, a supply the fight cannot end) and every answer that gets a rod at one costs a death about as often: holes, boxes and corners got no rod in 42 box_here answers, 2 dig_in_and_fight (offered 993 times), 5 fight_at_spawner (744), 7 break_spawner (727), because a blaze that sees the bot hangs back and shoots (the arena measured it: held two minutes in a hole, 0 killed). Those are two features (a Nether stance with the bow, and a brewing route in the tree), each needing a live server, and are the next cycle's top two; **Open**: (a) the ways rows are counted over two days and one code era each; the next trial day says whether Jev's picks move from the punch to the run, and whether the fights' deaths follow; (b) the healthy-start deaths are unchanged by facts alone unless Jev moves off the strike at four or more blazes, which the rows now say costs a death 40% of the time for a rod 32%: if it does not move, the option missing is a way to have fewer blazes shoot at once (every fight not at a live spawner ended in a death 13% of the time overnight) or a ranged one; (c) 10 deaths at 8 health or less with no way to heal wait on the food work; (d) 29 of 76 deaths had hunger under 18 twenty seconds before, 19 of them at 17.
662. *Twenty deaths "tried to swim in lava" and two falls in the overnight run (04:49Z to 11:37Z on 2026-09-29, code to 3c1af18): every one a knock over the lava sea, none a walk onto a lava-side cell, and what the new code did.* Method: scripts/death-timeline.js on each of the 25 deaths of the slice (ports and times from artifacts/overnight.log, the local server clock four hours behind the Z of the flight frames), the seconds before the first "hurt: lava" read frame by frame with each answer and its options; scripts/knock-record.js (new, reproduces the tables below from the flight records; `--dir` for a checkout without its own .bot-state) for the throws and what followed each stance; a pass over the flight records for the Nether hours and lava deaths per hour in three windows. **The groups** (25 deaths, 22 lava): (1) a ghast's fireball landed on the bot at 4 to 64 blocks up over the lava sea (or beside a lava-side ledge) and threw it over: 10 lava plus the two "doomed to fall" (25597 mid-242-de, y 64; 25591 mid-242-ee-fortress-3, a blaze's, y 56); it was in `keep_working`/crafting/mining/`cross_toward` at the first fireball in six (the ghast 26 to 55 blocks off and tracked for 2 to 7 seconds before), in `seal`/`take_cover`/`hold_on_span`/`rail_and_fight` (3.6 s to wall) in the rest. (2) a magma cube's hit: 7 (25598 mid-243-da-nether-1 04:59, 25581 mid-243-ff 06:41, 25583 mid-243-eg 10:26, 25593 mid-243-ed 08:50, 25593 mid-243-eh 11:06, 25589 10:38, 25583 mid-243-fe): the bot on a span at y 33 to 58 over the sea, `pillar` chosen in four of them (0.71 to 0.77), `fight` in two; five of the seven in the worlds started from first-days-243, whose Nether spawn is a basalt delta and lava sea with cubes: one crossing east at x 70 to 240, z about 10 to 20, replayed in every trial of that seed. (3) a hoglin's blow (25588 mid-244-dh, ledge one block over the lava, `shield_guard`), a piglin's arrow (25597, `pillar`; 25592, tunnelling a block from the lava): 3. (4) two overworld falls, both `way_down` -> `ride_water` down a 53 and a 55 block tower (25595 mid-244-eb 05:54:47Z, mid-244-dg 10:51:36Z): 20 health to none in one frame. In lava the body barely moves: over 88 stretches of 1.5 seconds or more in the records of 09-27 to 09-29, the horizontal pace was 0.39 blocks a second (median; 0.59 nine in ten), 62 died and the 26 that lived came out within a block and a quarter; from 15 health to none took 2.5 to 5 seconds with the bot 0.2 to 1.4 blocks from where it fell. **Did the new code help or backfire.** Lava pricing (3c1af18, running from 04:45Z): lava deaths per Nether hour 1.66 (09-27 to 09-28, 3.6 h, too few), 1.54 (09-28 04:45Z to 09-29 04:45Z, 30.6 Nether hours, 47 deaths), 1.58 overnight (14.5 hours, 23 deaths): no change; none of the 25 entered by a step onto a cell priced as lava-side (the last frames show the bot standing, or on a span it built, when the hit came); what moved is the mix (a hit in the seconds before: fireball 19 to 9, magma cube 4 to 7, hoglin 5 to 0; a death with no hit in the nine seconds before 16 to 3, per hour 0.52 to 0.21), so the price rule neither helped the knock deaths nor caused them, and the walk-ins fell. Fire resistance (1099ad7): no death in the slice had the effect on or a potion carried (0 mentions in the event log); it would have turned the lava into a survivable fall, and it is still never in hand. `strike_at_arm` and the scene holds: nothing in the slice; the one held answer that mattered was the `pillar` hold on 25598 at 04:59 (fifteen seconds at 20 health while three cubes closed from 7 to 3.4 blocks and the first hit threw it), which is the pillar's own price, below. **Root causes and what changed.** (1) `pillar` was priced at "about 0 damage from the mobs here" against magma cubes while its own text said "Two up does not stop a magma cube (jumps higher than two blocks, and its hit throws)": REACH_UP had them, CLIMBERS did not, so the price left them out, and against 13 cubes with hold_on_span at 35.6 damage the pillar was the cheap stance (0.71 to 0.77) taken four times on a one-wide top 20 to 27 blocks over lava; each cube hit threw the bot off it (the same as mid-211-h on 09-27, which had only the text fixed). CLIMBERS now holds magma_cube and slime: the pillar is priced as the fight it is from the top, "Two up, 78 magma cubes still reach it", 83.7 damage in the recorded scene (test/lava-knock-662.test.js; fails without the change). (2) The drop was looked for three blocks off for every pusher; a landed fireball threw the body a median 1.7 blocks, nine in ten within 4.2, 6.1 the most (106 landed, 30 into lava = 28%; magma cube 55 landed, median 1.4, 18 into lava = 33%; hoglin 64, 10 lava; a skeleton's arrow 200, none), and the deaths went over at 4.1, 4.2, 4.3 and 4.5. 25593 mid-243-fc at 04:31 stood seven seconds with a ghast 37 blocks off in sight and the work went on, "no drop within three", until the fireball. src/knock-record.js holds the measured throws; danger.pushOverDrop looks for the drop as far as the throw of the kinds about (5 for a ghast, 3 otherwise), survival.shotOverEdge and the stance's own drop the same, BLAST_THROW (pushCarries, the footing search) 4 to 5; the stance's drop sentence carries "Measured: a ghast's fireball that lands: of 106 that landed on this bot in the Nether, the body went 1.7 blocks (half of them), up to 4.2 (nine in ten), 6.1 the most, and 30 ended in lava". (3) What followed each stance in this situation, said on each option with a lethal lava drop within three blocks and a ghast or cubes about (as blaze-record.js does for blazes): per stretch, ghast: take_cover 10 of 195 into lava within 30 s, out_of_sight 10 of 152, rail_and_fight 8 of 85, seal 3 of 81, fight_from_footing 5 of 80, out_of_the_push 2 of 63, hold_on_span 5 of 53, keep_working 3 of 36, retreat 1 of 32, fight 4 of 27, pillar 2 of 9; cubes: fight 1 of 54, shield_guard 2 of 47, pillar 4 of 31, fight_from_footing 2 of 25, retreat 1 of 22. Small samples, confounded by where the bot stood, and said as counts. (4) `lavaFate` priced a swim to the shore at one block a second, "not measured", while lavaWays used the jar's 0.4: every fall into lava with ground three blocks off said 12.6 health in it and 27.6 with the fire (7.5 seconds, 31.5 and 46.5 in fact); it is 0.4, measured (88 stretches, 62 deaths, the survivors out within 1.2 blocks), and says so. (5) `ride_water` down a 55-block tower: the step off the top was made and the survival watch took the turn a second or two down (a push about, then the air: `Preempted by push`, `Preempted by air: swim up`), the stance or swim up ran in the falling water and the body left the one-wide stream and fell 50 blocks; 11 of 11 rides of 4 to 17 blocks came down. way-down.js `sinkDown`: from the step until the ground, nothing takes the turn but a cancel (interruptCheck and stallCheck set aside and put back), and the body is steered to the stream's middle when the current carries it off; the option says what the rides came to. Tests: test/lava-knock-662.test.js (the pillar priced against cubes and slimes; the pace in lava; the drop looked for as far as a ghast's throw and a zombie's not; the measured throw and the stance table on the question), test/ride-water-662.test.js (the turn kept, a cancel lands, the steer), the record sentence in test/way-down.test.js; span-fall, ghast-push-footing updated to the measured pace and the five-block throw (five blocks of floor west stays on it). **Open**: (a) not seen live: the next ghast at a lava sea and the next cubes in a delta are the check (the stance table will show whether pillar leaves the cube choices and whether pushOverDrop's five blocks stop the work sooner); (b) the blast's throw is the body's ground covered in 1.5 seconds and includes what the bot did itself; a cleaner one needs the velocity at the tick; (c) first-days-243's delta and sea crossing kills every trial of that seed at the same place: the fortress leg question does not say a leg's length over lava with cubes or a ghast about (the ledger has it), worth offering; (d) fire resistance never in hand: the barter path is offered but the bot has no gold in the Nether at the crossing; (e) a fireball's throw over open ground (25591's blaze at y 56, 25597's ghast at y 64, both "doomed to fall") is priced by the fall's damage only and its own text says nothing measured; the throw table has no blaze row because a blaze's small fireball landed 523 times with 2 into lava.
663. *The melee deaths of the overnight run (2026-09-29 04:49Z to 11:37Z, main at 3c1af18): 25 by a mob at arm's length, and the alert that stood at six health where a blow is 4.8 to 6.7. Loops and strandings grouped.* Read from the flight records (the server logs had rotated away for two thirds of the deaths, so each death was found as a danger frame at health none, 115 in the window, and its cause read from the last "hurt:" label; scripts/death-timeline.js reads a window from the server log's death line and finds none for these). The 115: on fire 40, lava 21, fireball 17, and 25 in my slice: mob attack by blaze 10, by wither skeleton 5, piglin 3, zombified piglin 3 (one a spear), magma cube 1, piglin brute 1, a drowned's trident 1 (at 3 health, 21 blocks off), a creeper's blast 1 (at 20 health beside a skeleton, "block_creeper" chosen at 0.93 and then none-good). Where and how: nine of the ten blaze ones are one place, the spawner room of the fortress checkpoint (x -107 to -116, y 74 to 78, z 150 to 158) that five ports were started at (25592 twice, 25594, 25585, 25590, 25598 four times; the tenth, 25591's, is at the other fortress): blazes at one to four blocks, each swinging once a second for 6 before armour, 4.8 through an iron helmet and chestplate (flight frames: 20 to 15.5 to 10.8 to 6.3 to 1.6 to none at 05:05:33.5 to 37.5 on 25594; the same 4.5 to 4.8 a blow on the five others read). The wither skeleton ones are three ports at another fortress (x 146 to 158, y 61, z 343 to 365; 25584 four times, 25591 once, and 25589's magma cube): 6.7 a blow through the same armour, 20 to none in three blows (25591, 09:36:02.8, 03.5 and 05.6, the stance shield_guard chosen at 03.2 and the second blow landing 0.3 seconds after its answer). The piglin, brute and zombified piglin ones: 20 to none in three to five seconds at arm's length (25597 at 08:40 from 20 by two piglins while retreat then pillar were answered; 25598 at 06:00 by a brute, 19.5 to 14.7 to 5.6 to none in two seconds under shield_guard; 25593 at 10:13 a brute and piglins). Common to most: from the first blow to death 2 to 5 seconds, four or five blows; 16 of the 25 were above 8 health at the start of the last 45 seconds (at least 8 of them at 17 or more) and 9 were at 8 or under throughout (four of those flat at 0.3 to 3.2 health for 47 to 167 seconds at hunger 15 to 17, where health does not come back: 68 of the 115 deaths were at hunger under 18, 36 with nothing carried that is food, note 626's stretches still). Did the new code fire, and did it help? strike_at_arm (3b81c71): offered 58 times in the window's 474 body_way questions, chosen 42; it was among the last dozen answers of 3 of the 25 (25585 at 05:13, 25584 at 07:14 and 09:15, one of them none-good 0.64), never the difference: six of the ten blaze deaths were in close_in or charge_nearest, a stance, and a body question was asked only once a hit had taken the bot down. The scene holds (63cefa1): 43 stance questions in the window carry a held-scene mention; no death of this slice was a held answer retaken without asking (the 10:59:12 charge_nearest at 16.1 was asked at 0.31 to leave_and_heal 0.28 and every later blow came before the next asking); the fixed re-ask did not change an outcome here, the asks came too late for it to. Fire resistance (1099ad7) and the lava pricing (3c1af18) do not touch this slice. What did the killing: the alert that hands the bot to Jev when a mob is at arm's length (arbiter.js observeReflexes, "arm", ALERTS) stood at health six or under (danger.js STANCE_HEALTH), where a blow through the armour is 4.8 (blaze), 5.4 (piglin), 6.7 (wither skeleton) and 12 (brute): on 25594 the hunt's close_in, begun at 20 by a hunt_target answer, was first preempted "by arm: escape threat" at 36.75, 3.2 seconds and three blows after the first, at 1.6 health; the stance the health-down break (blaze-stand.js closeIn, six health since the stance began) returns to had nothing to ask for either. Changed: (1) the alert holds when the bot has been hurt within four seconds and at most three of the blows of the hardest mob at arm's length (`blowOf`: combat-estimate MOBS through the armour worn, a blaze's swing only within its two blocks, no shooter and no creeper) are left in the health, as well as at six or under; its facts say the blow through the armour and how many end the bot (blowThroughArmour, blowsThatEndIt), still an alert (Jev is asked who acts, no rule takes the turn), still held two blocks past the line. On 25594 that is the asking at 34.5 with 10.8 health instead of 36.75 with 1.6; on the wither skeleton's it is the same asking as the newcomer rule's. Fixture: the recorded health tracks (test/arbiter.test.js). (2) The shield_guard option says what the bot's own runs of it came to by the kind faced (wither-guard.js RECORD, recordSays), where it had only the arena's five-run rows against wither skeletons in a rock corner with no deaths: against wither skeletons 107 runs, 14 took a blow, 17 blows, 4 ended in death; against a piglin brute 5 runs, every one took a blow (7 blows, 58 health lost), 2 ended in death within 20 seconds, and it carries a golden axe, not a sword, which the arena did not include; piglin, hoglin and zombie rows too. Not changed and left open: (a) the hunt's answers re-enter closeIn with a new baseline after its health-down break (startHealth is read at each call), so "asked again once six health is gone" is per call, not per fight; the alert above covers the blow-by-blow case, the loop itself is not proved from these frames; (b) charge_nearest's price counts only the blazes with a line to where it strikes ("2.8 damage over 3.7 seconds" at 19.6 health, chosen 0.53 over close_in's 19.8) while the spawner's others came in the same seconds, six of the ten blaze deaths were in close_in or charge_nearest; the record of 2026-09-28 it quotes gives 16% died after it, the overnight fights with three or more blazes, all stances, 42% (blaze-record.js, 154 fights); (c) shield_guard's timing against a blow every 0.7 to 1 second (the swing routine lowers the shield for the sword after each blow, AFTER_BLOW_MS 600) is not measured; (d) three of the ten at low health were held on corner_ambush or box_here at 0.3 to 4.7 health for a minute or more with nothing to eat, note 626's problem, unchanged. Loops and strandings of the run (each trial's end event; 11 loops, 2 stranded in the window): the flips between find_fortress and detour, cross_toward or persist, 8 of the 11 (25584 at 06:08 for 71 minutes, 25593 at 06:38, 25585 at 08:46 and 10:30, 25584 at 10:44 mine to detour, 25591 at 10:54, 25594 at 11:36, all fortress-stage or Nether-stage trials: the fortress found and the leg to it answered by stillness_detour's cross_toward or differently, then find_fortress walking it again); "No loaded return portal observed in the Nether; saved progress retained" 3 times (25592, 04:51) and "Took to long to decide path to goal" 3 times (25588, 10:47: a pathfinder timeout, the walk asked again); go_to_landmark and stalk_mob (25598, 04:53, after two deaths); nether_gather and mine (25583, 04:49, the one that was also stranded 30 minutes within 6 blocks of (-21, 104, -19) with 13 none-good answers to stillness_detour: the one-walkable-cell ledge of note 660, fixed at 3c1af18 after it began). The second stranding, 25583 mid-243-ec at 09:58, 30 minutes within 5 blocks of (343, 55, 171) with 11 none-good answers in a row to rung_progress (09:49 to 09:54): not read further.
664. *Food before the fortress: what the bot carries at the crossing and at each blaze fight, where it goes, and what the questions now say about it (flight records of 2026-09-28T00:00Z to 2026-09-29T11:40Z, main at bb91b3d; scripts/food-audit.js, new; src/food-facts.js, new).* Asked after notes 661 to 663 (68 of 115 deaths at hunger under 18, 36 with no food carried): what food does the bot have when it crosses, when it meets blazes and at each fight, and how is it lost or never gathered. **Measured** (567 blaze fights, 185 Nether hours, 168 crossings from the Overworld; the script prints every figure and takes `--from`, `--to`, `--dir`): (a) *At the crossing* 42 of 168 carried no food (25%), 36 carried 1 to 7 points, 44 carried 8 to 23, 46 carried 24 or more (median 9 points); 50 crossed at hunger under 18. The kit's stay count is 24 points at the least (more the longer the goal's stay), so 122 of 168 were short of it; of the crossing_kit's 868 askings 621 were answered cross_now, 82 of the 112 askings at nothing carried and hunger 18 or more among them. (b) *At the first fight of a visit* (252) 34 carried nothing, 35 carried 1 to 7, 32 carried 8 to 23, 151 carried 24 or more; 39 began at hunger under 18. (c) *At each fight* the row that stands apart is nothing to eat carried at hunger under 18: 92 fights, 47% died, 12% brought a rod; nothing carried at 18 or more, 22 fights, 23% died, 27% rod; food carried at hunger under 18, 45 fights, 4 deaths (the bot ate first, and heal_first was picked 82 of 708 times); every fight begun at 18 or more with food carried, 408, 24% died, 40% rod (24 or more points carried: 310 fights, 22% died, 44% rod; 1 to 23: 143 fights, 22% to 24% died, 21% to 22% rod). Fights, not a trial of carrying food; a bot with food differs in other ways. (d) *Time*: 36% of the Nether hours were at hunger under 18 and the same 36% with nothing to eat carried; hunger 6 or less never showed (the bot eats or dies first). (e) *Spend*: fights over twenty seconds (369, 433 minutes) lost 0.9 hunger a minute; a blaze fight's median length is 0.6 minutes (three in four under 1.1, nine in ten under 2) and a visit is several; 37% of the 430 fights begun at 18 or more ended under 18; over the whole Nether time the food bar fell 22.8 an hour and 33 points of food were eaten an hour (eating past 20 wastes the rest and saturation is spent first; the code's 40 an hour is an upper figure). (f) *Where carried food went*, in food points over the window: 6,254 eaten, 6,216 in the pack at a death (150 deaths, about 41 a death: every death restarts the stay at the portal with nothing, which is why 531 of the 955 lives that began in the Nether began with none), and 6,608 that left the pack with no eating and no death frame (raw and cooked beef and mutton, 594 mutton, 425 beef, 403 cooked mutton; the record does not say whether they were dropped for room, stored, lost to lava or burned: unexplained, and worth its own audit). (g) *What Jev chose*: fortress_visit was asked 708 times, go_in 624, heal_first 82, go_back 2; at nothing carried and hunger under 18 the answer was go_in 125 of 127, with go_back on offer in 115 askings in all, because the way home was offered only where health could not come back at all, and never at hunger 18 or more with an empty pack (the 22 fights above) and no other way to food (restock_food's hoglin, stew, cooking, bastion chests) was on that question, only a hoglin hunt at hunger under 18. The entry-to-first-fight chain could be matched for only 21 crossings (a file per life does not continue across every crossing) and is not read. **Now**: (1) src/food-facts.js says, from one place, hunger and whether health comes back (only at 18 or more; none below; sprint gone at 6 or less; starvation at 0), the food carried in hunger points with what cooking the raw would add, the minutes of fighting it holds at 0.9 a minute (an upper bound: the bar caps at 20) and the minutes to hunger 18 with no eating, the played row the bot is in (its food carried and hunger, the numbers above and the caution that they are fights, not a trial), and the ways to food each priced: the Overworld's cows (1 to 3 raw beef, 3 each, 8 cooked), sheep (1 to 2 mutton, 2 and 6), rabbits, fish and crops, with cooking at a furnace (ten seconds an item) and that pigs and chickens are never hurt; in the Nether a hoglin (2 to 4 porkchops, 40 health, none of 66 hunts on 2026-09-28 brought meat), stew, bastion chests, the trip home; and that piglin barter gives no food (none of its 19 items). (2) fortress_visit's state carries all of it as `foodBeforeTheFight`; go_in and heal_first say the hunger clock and that what heals holds only while hunger stays at 18 or more; go_back is offered where health cannot come back OR the food carried is short of the stay (nether-food stayFacts, the kit's own measure) and says the Overworld's ways and the bot's own record row; get_food_here (restock_food's ways) is a new option where under 8 points are carried or the bot is hurt at a hunger that does not heal. (3) The crossing kit's food line and the crossing_kit state carry the same regen state, clock, row and ways (`foodBeforeTheNether`); leave_and_heal in a blaze fight says what its healing holds for. (4) healing.js's "no food known on the Overworld side" no longer names pigs. Nothing gates an answer; the thresholds compared (a stay's points, 8 points) are the code's existing ones and said in the option. **Not done, and why**: the 6,608 points that left the pack unexplained (needs the record's drop and chest frames read by hand); the ladder has no rung that makes food before the first crossing (crossing_kit is the place and Jev answered cross_now 621 times; whether a hard rung is right is a judgment for Jev's next reading of the row above, not a threshold here). Tests: test/food-before-664.test.js (the record adds up, the clock and rows at hunger 20, 19 and 14, food carried, the ways without pigs or chickens, fortress_visit's state and options at an empty pack and at twenty steaks, the kit's line, the pig-free text); test/fortress-visit-638.test.js and test/mob-hunt.test.js now expect the new option where they carried nothing.

665. *The fight at a live spawner with four or more blazes about (half of them ended in a death): what the record separates, the count told at the entry, and the one route the game allows to a smaller count (flight records of 2026-09-28T00:00Z to 2026-09-29T11:40Z, 567 fights, scripts/blaze-record.js `--records`, `--counts`; main at bb91b3d; the server jar's Mob.checkDespawn, BaseSpawner and MobCategory read with javap).* **What the record says.** A fight is at a live spawner when a decision's state had a blaze spawner within 16; counted by the most blazes within 16 of the bot at once: three or fewer, 85 fights, 22% died, 53% brought a rod, 0.9 rods a fight (4.0 rods for each death), 13.7 health lost; four, 29, 52% died, 41% a rod; five or six, 85, 49% and 40%; seven or more, 130, 30% and 22%. With no spawner within 16 (238 fights): none or one 144, 13% died; two or three 75, 13%; four or more 19, 32%. The count is a result of the stay, not only of the entry: the spawner tries up to four blazes every 10 to 40 seconds while a player is within 16, until six are about (BaseSpawner, read in note 606), so of the 163 fights at a spawner that began with one to three blazes in sight, 82 reached four or more within 16, a median 32 seconds after the start (nine in ten within 65). The clock inside a fight at four or more (244): the first rod came a median 16 seconds in (76 fights), a death a median 58 seconds in (a quarter within 32, three quarters within 95); fights under 30 seconds 20 of 77 died (11 rods), 30 to 60 s 31 of 69 (22 rods), 60 to 120 s 27 of 56 (32 rods), 120 s and more 18 of 42 (47 rods). **What separates survivors from deaths at four or more** (all differences are among fights the bot played, chosen in states the rows do not hold alike): no blaze killed in the fight, 130 fights, 23 died (18%), 13 rods; a blaze killed, 114 fights, 73 died (64%), 99 rods: the rods and the deaths come from the same act, the strike, and the record has no fight that took rods without close blazes; begun over 16 health 74 of 210 died (35%, 107 rods), at 16 or under 22 of 34 (65%, 5 rods); hunger 18 or more 70 of 188 (37%), under 18 26 of 56 (46%, 14 rods); the nearest the bot came to the cage within 8 blocks 74 of 178 died (42%, 102 rods), 9 to 12 blocks 16 of 47 (34%, 8 rods), 13 to 16 blocks 6 of 19 (32%, 2 rods): farther off lost hardly fewer fights and took no rods; iron pieces three or four 8 of 30 died against 88 of 214 with two, the same as note 661; terrain (ground, span), blazes above or level, the height, the sight breaks, the first stance: no separation (rows in `--wins`). The stance chains that ended more often without a death were the passive ones (box_here 8 of 35 died and 5 rods; seal 3 of 13 and none; defer 12 of 44), and the ones that took rods were the strikes (charge_nearest 79 of 172 died, 89 rods; close_in 43 of 75, 48 rods): a trade the record prices at 1.2 rods for each death at four or more against 4.0 at three or fewer, and no stance in it removes the death rate. (A measure fixed on the way: scripts/blaze-record.js `moved` (how far the bot went in a fight) ran on into the frames after a death, which carry the respawn's position, so every death "moved" 30 blocks and more and a first reading said no bot that stayed within 30 blocks ever died; it now stops at the death, and the death rate is the same for a bot that moved under 10 blocks (55%), 10 to 30 (47%) and 30 and more (33%, 9 fights).) **The routes asked about.** (1) A window or a cage so only one or two blazes see the cell: the box (box_here) and the hole (dig_in_and_fight, dig_in_at_spawner) exist and say how many blazes have a line in; offered 1,063 and 758 times at a live spawner with four or more in 1,271 stance askings, chosen 73 and 0 (the hole's text says "in the hole, 7 blazes still reach it": the ones above the mouth see in). Blazes hover where they see and shoot and come to a window only within two blocks (the goal's rule, note 606), so a box is a way to live, not to take rods: 5 rods in 35 fights. (2) Blocking the spawner's other sides or lighting it: built, measured in the arena at 3 and 4 deaths in 5 with no rod, offered only under BLAZE_TACTICS_ALL (note 606); not changed. (3) One at a time at a doorway: corner_ambush (28 of 47 died, 17 rods) and bunker; the same rule, a blaze that loses sight of the bot flies toward it a quarter second and then hovers. (4) Retreat to heal at a distance: leave_and_heal 66 of 168 died, 76 rods, chosen 271 times at four or more, and the health it heals the spawner's refill undoes when the bot comes back inside 16. (5) Another spawner, or a moment when the count is lower: every spawner does the same, four in the first 10 to 40 seconds and six after, so the count at the entry to a spawner is not a property of the spawner; the fortress_visit question's leave_fortress is the only "another one", and its state (blazeCounts) says now that a spawner elsewhere is the same rule. (6) Bows and snowballs: a bow is three sticks and three string, string comes from spiders (none in the Nether) and in the Nether only from a piglin's barter (about 4 in 100 rounds); a fortress's skeletons drop arrows and now and then a bow; a snowball (three damage to a blaze) is dug from snow, which the Nether has none of. 8 of the 567 fights began with a bow and arrows (2 died, 1 rod), none with snowballs; the shoot_<id> options are offered when a bow and arrows are carried, and nothing offers to fetch either before the Nether that the ladder's bow rung (a night rung of the Overworld) does not. Said honestly in the facts, not built. (7) **Waiting far off** (new): the one route to a smaller count that the game allows without killing them. Mob.checkDespawn (26.1.2): a monster with no player within 32 blocks and 600 ticks idle is removed by chance, one in 800 a tick (mean 40 seconds: 78 in 100 gone at 90 seconds, 89 at two minutes), and at once beyond 128; BaseSpawner and Blaze set no persistence, so a blaze a spawner made is an ordinary monster to it; the spawner makes none while no player is within 16. **Now** (src/blaze-record.js, src/blaze-tactics.js, src/blaze-stand.js, src/survival.js, src/mob-hunt.js, src/fortress-visit.js, src/decisions/survival.js, docs/decisions.md): (a) `blazeCounts` on encounter_stance, hunt_target and fortress_visit (`entryFacts`): the blazes in sight now, how many within 16 in sight or not, how many have a line to the cell the bot stands in (blaze-tactics `seeing`), the spawner's distance and the seconds the bot has been within 16 of it (a gap of a minute begins a new stay) against the median 32 seconds at which four were about, the spawner's rule, the rows by count with their N (COUNTS, from `--counts`), the rows by the nearest the bot came, the clock, that a row is what a fight that got that many came to and not what entering with that many would do, that another spawner is the same rule, and the ranged kit carried now with what makes it. No threshold gates anything. (b) `wait_far_off` (kind far, in TACTICS): offered wherever a live spawner is within 16 and a blaze is about, at any count, when a route was found before the question (the retreat's scouting calls `scoutFar`: a route survey to any cell past 34 blocks of the cage plus the blazes' spread about it, GoalInvert(GoalNear), that passes no blaze nearer than the nearest is now and is under 120 blocks of walking; refused with its reason otherwise); priced with the walk in their fire, the lava along it, the shield; said with the despawn rule, that a blaze following in sight keeps its clock at nothing, the spawner's first four on the return, and that no bot in the records has done it, so what is left of the room after 120 seconds is not counted; run by walking there and waiting 120 seconds eating (health comes back at hunger 18 or more), ended sooner by a biter at arm's length or health under eight. Kept: every physical-safety rule (the retreat, the fire reflexes, the knock rules). Not done: an "another spawner" walk (the rule above makes it no different), fetching a bow or snowballs (needs the Overworld), and no hidden cutoff on entering a spawner room at any count.
