Open, to read in the trials: whether wait_far_off is chosen, whether the walk out finds a route in the fortress (the scout says why not when it does not), how many blazes a return finds, and whether the 120 seconds is enough (the wait's own stats carry `blazesTracked` at its end, but the server tracks entities only within its range, so the count of the return, in blazeCounts, is the read). Tests: test/blaze-count-665.test.js (counts table, the respawn's frames out of `moved`, the entry facts on an open floor and behind a wall and on the recorded crossing mid-243-ch, the stay clock, the scouting with a route through the blazes refused, no route, a route too long, the despawn arithmetic, the option offered at one and at four blazes and not without a way or without a live spawner, the wait walking out).
666. *Two-arm trials: main against a pinned baseline, same hours, same starts.* Deaths per Nether hour did not move across the nine fixes merged overnight, and nothing could say whether any of them helped: the commit changes every hour, the worlds differ (fresh sources 242, 243, 244; fortress saves picked by stage-select), and `blaze-record.js --by-commit` and `progress-audit.js --by-commit` compare one hour's commit on one hour's worlds with the next's. Nothing Jev is asked or told changes; this is harness only. (1) An arm per port: `.bot-state/arms/<port>` names the checkout that port's bot runs from (none: main, ROOT's own). A baseline is a detached git worktree at the pinned commit under ROOT/.arms/<name> (`node scripts/lib/arms.js setup <name> <commit>`) with node_modules, .env and .bot-state linked to ROOT's: the bot keeps its state, pid file, flight records and restart request under its own `__dirname/.bot-state` (index.js, session.js), so the link puts a baseline bot's in ROOT's, where the supervisor, the verdicts and the quiet restart look; an arm whose .bot-state is not that link is refused (not run as main). supervisor.sh, midgame.js start and first-days.js start all start the bot through `arms.js launch`: node on the arm's index.js by absolute path, cwd ROOT, JEV_ARM set, the start logged in `.bot-state/arms/starts.log` (time, port, arm, commit, pid, checkout). A quiet restart reaches a baseline bot through the link and its supervisor starts it again from the baseline, so it never moves onto main's code; the commit in the connection frame is read by git in the checkout the code loaded from, so it is the baseline's; builds from this one on also carry `arm` in the connection frame; the midgame record and verdict carry `arm` and `commit`. (2) Pairing: a start-stage.sh start on one arm takes first the save another arm started in the last six hours (asked as the same stage) and this arm has not (stage-select rule 7, `pair`); `start-fresh.sh <port> pair [fallback]` takes the first-days source this arm owes the other, by the trial records. (3) `node scripts/ab-report.js [--since <iso>] [--to <iso>] [--json]` (scripts/lib/ab.js): per arm, runs and commits, bot, Nether and fortress hours (in the Nether with a blaze seen within 24 in the last 30 s or within 48 blocks of a fortress the record names) and the blaze-sight hours, deaths per bot hour and per Nether hour by the game's cause (the record's recentDeaths, else the server log), rods per fortress hour, blaze fights (blaze-record fights()) with the share at four or more blazes and the deaths in those, and the trials begun with their passes, loops, strandings and deaths from the verdicts; rates with 95% Poisson intervals, shares with Wilson's, and main over each other arm as a ratio with its interval and the exact p. A run's arm is its frame's, else the start logged just before it, else the arm at its commit, else main; a trial whose port changed arm mid-trial is "mixed" and counted for neither. Checked end to end on scratch servers 25700 and 25701: a baseline at 3c1af18 and main at bb91b3d ran side by side, their records carried 3c1af18 and bb91b3d, a touched restart-requested brought each back on its own arm, and a midgame start on the baseline port recorded arm baseline-3c1af18. Tests: test/ab.test.js. Deploying it needs the supervisors of the baseline ports restarted (a running supervisor keeps the old script, which starts ROOT's index.js).
670. *Sealed in, fed, and the way out told as a trip nobody was making (bucket 3 of note 667: shelter sitting, obtain blaze rods, wait in shelter, 2.45 bot-hours in 31 trials; flight records 127_0_0_1-25583-Jev-2026-09-29T10-27-08-580Z (mid-243-fa), 25593 04-52-04-888Z (mid-243-dd), 25595 2026-09-28T23-52-10-644Z and 2026-09-29T00-20-11-834Z (mid-244-cd)).* **What the bot did**: mid-243-fa at 10:58:19 answered the food kit return_for_food (the stay short of food points), its walk to the portal found no route (partial) at 10:58:30, and at 10:58:31 the kit, asked again, got go_on; it searched on, ate to hunger 20 at 11:00, and at 11:03:02 sealed in against three magma cubes 4, 7 and 20 blocks off, 19 blocks from the fortress. From 11:03 to 11:16 it stood at (91, 35, 22) and did nothing: pocket_next stay 13 of 13 (0.51 to 0.73), turn_priority survival every minute (0.74 to 0.86, the work 0.12 to 0.23). The leave every time was "go on with the way back to the Overworld for food, as Jev chose at 10:58, before this pocket was sealed on it ... The nearest portal remembered is 84 blocks off ... Of 181 such walks of over 60 blocks 22 came out in the Overworld, 18 ended in a death"; by 11:14 one magma cube was left within 16, 12 blocks off, never having seen the bot in the wait, priced 42.5 damage as the big one. mid-243-dd (05:18 return_for_food at hunger 17, then fortress legs; walled off from a ghast 21 blocks off at 05:22 at hunger 20) and mid-244-cd (hunger 19, nothing within 16 for the last seven minutes) sat 8 and 7 minutes the same way, the leave the trip back 138 and 73 blocks. **Root cause**: the trip back for food held (goal.leaveNether, note 589) was told as the pocket leave's work while it was held, but the work makes the trip only in the hunt's rule (mob-hunt.js prepareMobHunt: hunger under 18, nothing safe to eat, not kept on); fed or with food carried, leaving went on with the fortress search, so the leave named a long, deadly walk that leaving did not do, and no option said "back to the fortress 19 blocks off". The held clock stops at the seal (note 597), so a pocket kept the trip held for as long as it stood. And a later answer at the food kit (go_on) did not end the trip. The ledger saw the stay gain nothing ("It rests 5 minutes more from here, kept on offer: fewer than two other ways are open") and could not escalate: the only other way was the false one. Over 2026-09-28 to 09-29 (all flight records): of 257 stay answers in Nether pockets, 93 had the trip as the leave with hunger 18 or more, in 6 ports; by the gaps between asks (up to two minutes each), 2.25 bot-hours of Nether pocket stays had a leave told as the trip while the bot was fed or had food with it, 0.18 hours with the trip real (hungry, nothing to eat), and 2.8 hours with the leave back to the work. **Changes**: (1) *The trip is the leave's only while the work would make it* (game-progress.js `foodTripDrives`: held, hunger under 18, nothing safe carried, not set aside by keep_on; survival.js pocket_next and tunnel_out). Held but not so, the leave goes back to the rung and says why: "The trip back to the Overworld for food Jev chose at 10:58 is not what leaving does now: hunger is 20, so the work goes on here, and food is asked about again when it is short." (2) *The leave back to the work says where the work is from here*, by the rung's measure (rung-measure.js parts: the fortress, the nearest place blazes were seen, the cage, the portal): "From here that work is the fortress 19 blocks off." (3) *A later answer at the food kit ends a trip chosen before it*: go_on, restock_food or raid_bastion (nether-food.js `kitEndsTrip`); return_for_food and the cauldron do not, nor the rods' own go_back. (4) *A magma cube or slime outside is priced at its size* on the pocket's leave and in riskNow (survival.js outCost and risk.js now pass slimeSize, as the stance's estimate has since note 647 (g)): one magma cube 12 blocks off, over 80 damage at an unknown size against 7 for a small one in the test scene. **Tests**: test/pocket-fed-trip-670.test.js on test/fixtures/pocket-fed-trip-mid-243-fa.json (the 11:14:11 pocket: the bot, the carried food, the two magma cubes, the seal and the trip's times, the fortress and the portal): fed, the leave is the rung with the fortress 19 blocks off and the trip said not made; hungry with nothing to eat, the trip as note 589 had it; hungry with food carried or kept on, not; the size priced; the kit's answers that end the trip. Replay case `pocket-fed-food-trip-ghast-gone-mid-243-dd` (the 05:25:31 question with the new leave): recorded stay 0.56 (the window's asks 0.50 to 0.60), now leave 8 of 8. The mid-243-fa question with the new leave still got stay 8 of 8: its magma cube is priced as the big one because the record carries no size, and live the size is read now; not added as a case. npm test 2513 of 2513, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 90 of 93 (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, a known flake, pillar 4 of 5; the two known gaps). **Not measured live**: no trial was run (starting the bot runs index.js). Left: the 2.8 hours of Nether stays whose leave was already the work (the longest 14 minutes beside three or four piglins held off out of sight, 25590 mid-242 08:08Z, golden boots worn) are not touched; turn_priority still answers survival while a pocket holds the turn, its work option naming only the step.
671. *The start of every midgame trial from first-days-243, 23 minutes to leave it (mid-243-fg, -fh and -ga, 2026-09-29 15:47Z; flight record 127_0_0_1-25593-Jev-2026-09-29T15-47-09-622Z, artifacts/midgame-mid-243-ga.log; the saved world and player file read from .trial-sources/first-days-243).* **The start**: 72 blocks under open sky at (48, 28, 8) beside its furnace, a stone column to the grass at y 99; the only pickaxe an iron one at damage 79, **171 uses left (68%)**, not worn by the ladder's rule (a fifth or 64); 3 oak planks, one short of a table and two sticks (3 planks short, one log); 5 iron ingots, 15 raw iron, and a saved batch of 64 raw iron in the furnace (640 seconds). **Timeline**: 15:47:11 upkeep offered the spare pickaxe and wood with the pickaxe budget ("45 more digs than the uses carried ... no other pickaxe can be made") and Jev chose to go up for wood; `gatherWood` went through `acquireStep`, which finishes a saved batch first, so the climb waited on the 64 iron; while_cooking was asked (Jev said none of the options was good; its next best, mine_nearby, was taken) and the walks to ore within 32 blocks, each dug through rock by the pathfinder, wore the pickaxe 171, 154, 137, 115, 85, 35, 19 and broke it at 15:50:13 (161 cobblestone dropped for room on the way); the walks went on by hand to lapis and iron that drop nothing until 15:57. The ladder, with no sound pickaxe and 31 to 69 ingots carried, asked for "another stone pickaxe" (15:51:34), whose sticks and table want the same log. At 15:53 work_free: in a two-high tunnel the moves offered were "put a dirt east, at the feet: a step up" (no room over the head to jump onto it) and then the dig of that dirt; Jev answered none good 0.92 each time and the next best was taken: place north, dig north feet, place north, place west, dig west feet ... fifteen moves in fifteen seconds, the same cells. 15:57:51 "no pickaxe and no wood: digging out by hand"; 15:59 a staircase by hand, 16:02:18 straight up from y 35. **The climb at 9 s a block is the physics of a bare hand**, not overhead: the flight record's heights give 8.0 s a block of stone (7.5 to dig, the jump and the block under the feet) and 15.4 and 17.1 s at y 43 to 45, which the saved column shows are copper ore (hardness 3, 15 s by hand); the turn and upkeep questions at each call of eight blocks cost under a second. At 16:09:41, 22.5 minutes in, it was at y 86 of 99 when the restart came. **Changes**: (1) *while_cooking says what the digging costs* (work.js whileCooking): every way that digs says that each block dug, the ore or the rock on the way, wears the pickaxe a use, with the pickaxe budget (uses left, the way home to open sky, what the pockets make and the wood short, `pickaxeBudget` in the state); after a walk that wore the pickaxes the question is asked again with the walks so far (`walksSoFar`: trips and uses); standing says it wears none. (2) *leave_cooking* (new option): a batch saved earlier that other work came to finish first may be left to cook while that work goes on; `localBatch` holds it until it is done and the bot is back within 16 blocks of the furnace, or 20 minutes (`LEAVE_BATCH_MS`). Not offered when the work in hand is the batch's own. (3) *Only ore a carried tool takes a drop from* is walked to or dug while cooking (and the stone only with a pickaxe): an ore dug by hand drops nothing. (4) *The pickaxe the ladder asks for is the best the heads carried make* (game-progress.js ladderRung): with no sound pickaxe and three iron ingots carried, the rung is the iron pickaxe (the same sticks and table, 250 uses against 131, and it mines the diamonds); stone as before with fewer, or with the iron rung set aside. (5) *The pickaxe rung with none carried* says the budget too (strategy.js spareSays), and the budget says the wood short in planks and logs (pickaxe-budget.js `plankShort`). (6) *No place-then-dig churn in working free* (unstuck.js localMoves): out of water a block at the feet is offered only where the bot can climb onto it (room over the head to jump and two open cells over the block); otherwise it is in `here.notOffered` ("no step it could climb onto"); and no move is offered that takes back the move before from the same cell (a block put there dug again, a cell just dug filled again), said in notOffered. The offer to work free says how far open sky is and that no pickaxe is carried (aimFor `says`). The test of note 615's 25587 flip is changed with it: the cobblestone put back under its own planks is no step. **Tests**: test/start-underground-671.test.js on test/fixtures/start-underground-mid-243-ga.json (the saved world round the start and its columns to y 106, the pockets with their damage, the batch); replay case `while-cooking-72-down-only-pickaxe-mid-243-ga`: the old text got mine_nearby 5 of 6 and wait_here 1; the new, leave_cooking 5 and dig_in_reach 3 of 8, mine_nearby none. **Not measured live**: starting the bot runs index.js, so no scratch trial was run; with the wood climb left free of the batch, the iron pickaxe's 171 uses cover the 72 digs straight up the column at about a second a block, against the 22.5 minutes above.
667. *The time before the blazes: every bot-minute from a trial's start to its first blaze fight, called progress or waste and put to a pattern, a step and a question (the user, watching trials: "a lot of times the bot is just struggling to even get there"; flight records of 2026-09-28T00:00Z to 2026-09-29T16:30Z, 580 trials, main to bb91b3d; scripts/wasted-minutes.js, new; a measurement, no behavior change).* **Method**: a trial is its artifacts/midgame record, cut at its first blaze fight as blaze-record.js has it (in the Nether, a blaze in sight within 24 or a blaze's hit); bot time is the frame gaps under a minute, charged to the trial's clock minute. A minute is *progress* when a milestone came (the bot's own, the Nether entered, a fortress walked to), a rung distance ended the minute a new nearest by more than rung-measure.js NEARER against both the kept nearest and the minute's own first look (the fortress in a question's state, a fortress found, the step's target), a ladder item rose above the most carried this life up to what the ladder uses (one flint, two pickaxes), a fortress or landmark was first seen (a point within 96 of a fortress seen before is that fortress), or 8+ block columns not stood on in this life were stood on. It is a *crawl* when that progress was only a distance or new ground and under 10 blocks of it (a walk covers about 250), unless the answers flipped, a wait or a fight held 30 s of it, or it walked 20+ (pacing or old ground). *Upkeep*: food carried up, eating, health up 2+, wood or coal, blocks stocked, a mob that is not a blaze fought. The rest is *waste*, by the first of: died, night wait, shelter sitting (a shelter, bunker, box, pillar top, span or nook held 30 s), waiting out a rest (the until_rest_ends detour, rods_waiting), stuck/unstuck (persist, a detour, shake loose, unstuck_move, stillness_detour, climb_out, two navigation stalls), failed route again (the third failure to one goal in ten minutes), flipping (the work step or one question's answer trading between two, 4+ changes), re-asking (one question 3+ times), bridging with no advance, tunneling, digging in place, pacing (20+ walked, under 6 net, height counted), standing still (under 3 walked), old ground. The pockets are read only from the observations' (they sum the stacks; a decision frame's cobblestone flickered 61 against it three seconds apart), and as the minute's net change. **Measured**: 218.5 bot-hours before the first blaze fight (245 of the 580 trials reached one, median 3.9 minutes in, most of them fortress checkpoints); progress 137.2 h, crawling 24.2 h (11.1%), upkeep 4.7 h, waste 52.4 h (24.0%): 35% of the time before the blazes was not getting there. By start: fresh 117.0 h, 19.0% waste and 9.6% crawling; Nether checkpoints 40.4 h, 24.1% and 9.4%; fortress checkpoints 61.1 h, 33.3% and 14.9%. By pattern: crawling on a span 14.7 h, waiting out a rest 13.2, stuck/unstuck 9.5, old ground 7.5, shelter sitting 7.5, crawling up a climb 6.0, pacing 4.4, flipping 4.0, crawling on foot 2.4, re-asking 1.8, died 1.8, standing still 1.4, failed route again 0.8. By pattern and step: crawling (span) at cross_toward 10.0 h and at find_fortress 3.9, waiting out a rest in the rods' detour 9.7 and the pearls' 2.6, crawling (climb) at ascend_to_surface under the stone pickaxe rung 5.1 and on foot there 1.8, shelter sitting in wait_in_shelter 3.7. **Without a pickaxe**: 83.8 of the 218.3 bot-hours with pockets read were spent carrying no pickaxe at all (242 of 580 trials had such minutes); 27% of those minutes were crawls against 1% of the minutes with one, and 22.8 of the 24.2 crawl hours had none; every crawl bucket above is 99-100% without a pickaxe. A climb out of a mine by hand: 25583 mid-243-eg 10:02Z on 2026-09-29, y 13, climb_out offered "about 12 minutes with bare hands" for 92 blocks, 3 oak planks, no stick, table or pickaxe, 285 cobblestone and 23 iron ingots carried; it rose a block every 7 s (stone by hand is 7.5 s), 87% of the time standing on the pillar. A span by hand: 25598 mid-242-cf-nether-1-fortress-17 13:24-13:34Z, a straight tunnel north through a basalt delta at 4 blocks a minute, a one-second bridge_step and 12 s standing per cell (basalt by hand 6.25 s a block, two a cell), with blazes and the fortress's nether brick behind it at the start (trail map); the question state says "pickaxe: none carried". 8.7 of the 14.7 span-crawl hours are one checkpoint, mid-242-cf-nether-1, replayed at the fortress stage: it was saved without a pickaxe. **Waiting out a rest**: 215 windows, median a minute, 90th percentile 6, longest 63; 10.2 of the 13.2 hours had a none_good answer in the minute, and the labels are "no route (noPath)" (4.4 h) and "the nether portal ... cannot be reached from here" (1.2 h): every way rests and holdForRest (work.js) stands waiting in 5 s sleeps when no detour is on offer. **Shelter sitting**: 144 windows, median 2 minutes, longest 46; 1.2 h said a ghast, 1.2 h a piglin or hoglin, 4.2 h named no mob in the minute (pocket_next stay asked again and again, "I keep getting stuck on the obtain blaze rods. I'll come back to it."). **Validation**: 120 minutes drawn at random were read against their raw frames (positions every 15 s, controller, step, survival action, decisions, labels) and four windows against trail maps (trail-map.js's render over audit.trialWindow at a past end, scratch only). The first three draws of 30 were used to fix the rules (a wait that crept, a flint past the one needed, a mark looked at again after minutes on another step credited as nearer, flips between a survival action and its own step, a descent of 13 counted as pacing by its flat net, a death called pacing, legs east and west on a span called progress). On the last draw, judged before its fixes: 2 of 30 on the wrong side of progress against not (both a fortress re-seen from a new spot counted as a sighting, fixed after), 1 questionable, 2 in the right class with the wrong pattern (a hand climb called old ground or standing still, not a crawl). The class error is about 7% (a 95% interval of roughly 1 to 22% at n 30) and leans toward counting waste as progress; the 10-block crawl line leaves 11 and 12-block-a-minute spans as progress, so the crawl hours are a floor. The 25589 trail map (mid-243-ah-fortress-7, 20:28-20:38Z on 2026-09-28) shows the east-west pacing on one short span that the minutes call flipping and pacing, and one minute of it (20:32) called progress for a new leg target 13 nearer. **Not done**: no behavior change; what the three largest buckets suggest is for the next notes (a pickaxe lost with no wood to make one, a rest waited out on the spot, a shelter held with no threat said). Tests: test/wasted-minutes-667.test.js on test/fixtures/wasted-minutes-flight.jsonl (ten made-up minutes, a pattern each, the blaze that ends the window).
668. *Climbing out of the mine by hand, the top bucket of the wasted-minutes measure (note 667: "crawling (climb), stone pickaxe: ascend to surface", 4.3 bot-hours in 41 trials, 87% of it standing still, all of it without a pickaxe); flight records 127_0_0_1-25583-Jev-2026-09-29T09-58-42-291Z (mid-243-eg), -2026-09-28T20-04-28-768Z (mid-243-bh), -2026-09-28T22-06-35-054Z (mid-243-cc), and every `climb_out` asked 2026-09-28 to 09-29 (424 askings).* **What the bot was doing**: the long climbs (60 to 92 blocks) are the first-days-243 start of note 671: the iron pickaxe (171 uses) wore out on the ore walks while the saved batch cooked, within three minutes, at y 11 to 20, with 3 oak planks and no table (no pickaxe can be made; a log is on the surface). mid-243-eg: pickaxe gone at 10:01:45, climb_out at 10:02:45 at (57, 11, 2), straight_up 0.83 ("92 blocks up, 89 blocks to dig ... about 12 minutes with bare hands"), then 8 blocks a minute to the grass at 10:13:43, the stall watch's rung measure (nearer the open sky over the column) counting each minute as a crawl, not a stall. bh the same, 84 up from y 19, 20:08 to 20:18. cc stood in a pit it had made (26 unstuck questions at 22:11) on a dirt block it had put under itself, the column overhead ruled out by gravel. **Root causes**: (1) *the staircase was priced by the block under the feet*: `climbOptions` took the dig time of the ground block and multiplied it by 3 digs a block of height, so on dirt or gravel a staircase of stone read as a few minutes: cc's "about 249 blocks dug ... about 5 minutes with bare hands" (half an hour of stone), and 13 of the 27 staircases chosen with no pickaxe said 4 or 5 minutes for 207 to 249 digs; Jev took them over straight up (9 minutes), and the next climb question came 36, 59, 18, 22 and 46 minutes later (25581 01:04, 06:48, 09:53; 25593 06:48, 12:40; not all of it climbing), and after 2.4 to 4.9 minutes and 6 to 12 blocks risen in the rest; (2) *the climb started where the pickaxe gave out*, at the bottom of the mine: no way was offered to walk back up the mine's own open stairs first, where the rock overhead was thinner (eg: 89 blocks to dig at y 11, 67 at (48, 22, 10), 25 cells back along its tunnel); (3) *a way kept was never looked at again for running long*: chooseClimb asked again only when the tools or the ways on offer changed, so a staircase said as 4 minutes was kept for an hour. The ledger (tried.js) and the rung measure did not end these because the climb did gain, a block every 8 seconds by hand, which is the physics of a bare hand (note 671); the waste was in the way chosen and where it began. **Change** (src/surface.js): `stairwayCost` reads the blocks on the staircase's way from the world (the headroom over the stair left and the two cells stepped into for each block of height, two a stair across; open cells cost nothing, a cell not loaded counts as stone), each at its own dig time with the pickaxe uses worn a block and then by hand, and the staircase says the blocks and their kinds: cc's is now 234 blocks (stone, gravel), about 30 minutes; eg's 261, about 35 (said 36 before, on stone). `walk_then_up` (new climb_out option): the open mine round the bot is walked over (level, a block up where the head has room, down to three, nothing dug or laid, no cell in, over or beside water or lava, 24 blocks and 600 cells at most), the 24 highest columns reached are looked over as straight_up would (natural ground only, nothing that falls or flows), and the quickest is offered where it saves a minute or more on the quicker way from here, the walk counted at 0.4 s a cell: said with the cells walked, the rock overhead against here, the blocks and minutes; taken, the walk is made with digging off and the climb goes on straight up there, kept, not asked again; a walk that does not arrive leaves that cell off the ways from there (`surfaceReturn.walkedAway`). eg now: straight_up about 12 minutes, walk_then_up about 10 (25 cells to (48, 22, 10), 67 to dig). A way kept that has run past twice what it was said to take (two minutes at least) is asked about again, with `climbSoFar` ("the staircase chosen 14 minutes ago, said then as 5 minutes, has risen 12 blocks since"). The decision registry says both. **Tests**: test/hand-climb-668.test.js on two fixtures of the mine as it stood at the decision (test/fixtures/hand-climb-mid-243-eg.json and -cc.json: rock from .trial-sources/first-days-243, the tunnels from the trial worlds under y 40, the cells the bot stood in before the decision from the flight record, cc's cells dug after it put back, eg's headroom cell (57, 13, 2) open as the recorded 89 digs show): cc's staircase over 25 minutes by hand with the dirt block under the feet, no walk offered from its pit; eg's straight_up said as recorded (92 up, 89 to dig) and walk_then_up two minutes or more quicker; the walk taken without Jev, then straight up the column walked to, asked once; a walk that does not arrive not offered again; a kept way asked again past twice its word, kept within it. test/surface.test.js: the shaft's staircase is 67 blocks dug, not 72 (the stairs reach the grass before the last digs). Replay case `hand-climb-walk-then-up-mid-243-eg`: the recorded state with the new tree, walk_then_up 5 of 5 (recorded: straight_up). **Not verified live**: no scratch trial was run (starting the bot runs index.js). With note 671 the first-days-243 start should mostly keep its pickaxe, and then these climbs are a second a block; the change is for the climbs by hand that remain and for any staircase priced on soft ground. The walk's 0.4 s a cell and the pathfinder's walk with digging off through a pathfinder-dug stair (its descents leave the headroom a climb back needs) are read from the code and the fixture, not measured; the column search reads about 10,000 blocks in a mine and 24,000 in an open cave (about 0.1 to 0.3 s a question, asked each call of eight blocks or six stairs). Check: `climb_out` answered `walk_then_up` and `goal.step.method: 'walk_then_up'`, and the staircase's minutes against the minutes it took.
669. *The crossing straight at a fortress dug by hand, and the floor a block up "reached" without a step (mid-242-cf-nether-1-fortress-9, 25598, 2026-09-29 09:51-10:13Z; flight record 127_0_0_1-25598-Jev-2026-09-29T09-10-53-412Z; bucket 2 of note 667's wasted-minutes ranking: crawling (span) | obtain blaze rods: find fortress | fortress approach -> cross level, 2.93 bot-hours in 26 trials, still 86% of it, no pickaxe 99%).* **The window**: in the basalt deltas with no pickaxe, 23 blackstone, a crafting table and no wood (the nearest warped forest 327 blocks off, the portal 292), the walk to the fortress refused ("the way passes along a drop that would kill"). fortress_approach offered cross_level "39 blocks, digging 67 blocks of rock ... about 421 seconds", and the state said `pickaxe: "none carried: rock and nether bricks cannot be dug, so a staircase, a tunnel or a crossing through rock digs nothing"`, which was false beside it; Jev took it (0.52, none_good 0.39). The crossing dug by hand, a block every six to eight seconds, the body creeping a cell and standing while it dug, for seven minutes, to 2 blocks from the floor, with no question asked (the answer holds; the rung measure said nearer each minute, so it was progress by the ledger, only slow). At 09:58:51 the patrol said "Walked what I can reach of this fortress" and offered unwalked_1, the floor at (160, 62, 268), a block up and two across from the bot's tunnel at (161.6, 61, 266.7): its goTo counted 2.3 blocks from the cell's corner as reached, so it returned "reached it" three times in three seconds without a step, rested, and the bot left for the bricks at (190, 60, 306), 48 blocks off, by another hand-dug crossing "about 782 seconds", 43 to 4 blocks in thirteen minutes; there the patrol found nothing to walk and a leg south was dug by hand from 10:12. **Over two days** (every fortress_approach answered cross_level in the flight records of 09-28 and 09-29): 1,851 answers, 591 of them with no pickaxe; those that ran more than 20 seconds came 8.9 blocks nearer a minute against 27.3 with a pickaxe (7.6 and 7.2 bot-hours); the seconds said held (ran 1.14 times the said); 39 had the pickaxe to be made in a few seconds from what was carried (blockStock.makingAPickaxe "the wood carried is enough"), and on 25592 at 03:44Z the bot dug 18 blocks by hand for 104 seconds and then took the leg's make_pickaxe. The legs offered make_pickaxe and fetch_stems (notes 654, 655); the way in never did. **Change** (src/mob-hunt.js, src/decisions/travel.js): (1) the `pickaxe` fact with none carried says what is true: rock is dug by hand and drops nothing, the seconds a block by hand of netherrack, basalt, blackstone and nether bricks and with a stone pickaxe (the game's hardness x 5, and ticks of 4 / hardness / 30), and that the staircase digs by hand only rock softer than basalt. (2) cross_level with no pickaxe and rock to dig says how much of its time is the rock dug by hand and what the same crossing takes with the pickaxe that would be had (the one made from what is carried, else a stone one; surveyCrossing with that tool), and whether it can be made here. (3) fortress_approach offers `make_pickaxe` (from what is carried) and `fetch_stems` (nether-wood.js, as upkeep and the legs offer it) where no pickaxe is carried and a way in digs rock (the crossing or the staircase), each with the crossing's seconds by hand and with a pickaxe; a pickaxe had asks the way in again rather than counting a failed way (pickaxeWays). The fallback order puts make_pickaxe before the crossing and fetch_stems after the staircase. (4) Floors seen across a gap (the unwalked goTo) are reached when stood on: at their height and within 1.5 blocks of the cell, not 2.5 from its corner at any height; from below, the walk there is tried and, where it finds no way, the way there is asked (fortress_approach with the stretch and its crossing along the ground). **Tests**: test/cross-by-hand-669.test.js (the deltas as in the window: a basalt wall 54 blocks by hand at 6.25 s against 0.5; make_pickaxe offered and taken and the way in asked again with the pickaxe; no wood, fetch_stems offered and the crossing says none can be made; the unwalked floor a block up from 25598's own tunnel walked to and asked, and reached only when stood on); replay case `fortress-approach-pickaxe-before-hand-dig-25592` (the 03:44Z question with the new texts: make_pickaxe 5 of 5). **Not measured live**: no scratch trial was run (starting the bot runs index.js); the window's own fortress had no wood within 300 blocks, so there the crossing by hand stays the likely answer and the gain is the arrival (the floor a block up walked to or asked, not left); whether the patrol finds the floors by the second arrival's bricks at (190, 60, 306) was not reconstructed; the 8.7 hours the ledger put on mid-242-cf-nether-1 come from a checkpoint saved without a pickaxe, which this does not change.
673. *The crossing's kit made before the portal: a spare pickaxe, blocks and food as rungs (approved by the user, 2026-09-29).* Why: at the crossing the kit was one question (crossing_kit) answered cross_now 621 of 868 times; 42 of 168 crossings carried no food and 122 of 168 were short of the stay (note 664); five of seven bots in the Nether had no pickaxe left (notes 654, 655); spans stopped where the blocks ran out (650, 655). **Change**: three rungs, last on the ladder before the portal (src/crossing-kit.js kitRungs, src/game-progress.js ladderRung), open only in the Overworld in Survival while the goal still needs blaze rods, not while the Overworld's endermen are the pearls' route or rods, powder or eyes wait in the home chest: `nether_pickaxe` (two pickaxes of stone or better with 24 uses each, the one in use and a spare; iron when three ingots are carried), `nether_blocks` (cobblestone to the 128 of NETHER_BLOCKS) and `nether_food` (food points to the stay's, crossing-kit.js netherStay: 80 for the whole goal, 40 hunger an hour). The numbers stay where they were (crossing-kit.js, food-facts.js RECORD). Each is DEFERRABLE: Jev weighs it in win_strategy with the other open rungs and nether_first, said with what it is for, what it takes from the pockets and what going without costs (strategy.js rungOption, crossing-kit.js kitRungSays); the food's ways are priced where known (the cook, the nearest known food). A kit rung set aside, by Jev, by the stall question or by its own stall, waits out its rest: preparationRung and gearStage no longer hand it back when nothing else is left, so the crossing goes on (no loop). The food rung, taken, asks the new kit_food question (src/work.js kitFoodStep): the crossing question's food ways moved there unchanged (top_up_food, top_up_food_near, top_up_cook) with go_without (set aside half an hour as a choice, offered back at the portal as take_up_nether_food); ten working minutes with no food point more set the rung aside. crossing_kit shrinks to health, gold, wood, the cauldron and the valuables, and says what the kit rungs left short in one line; it is no longer asked when only those are short. The unused hungerSays is gone. Replay cases crossing-kit-cow-in-view-no-frame-244ah and crossing-kit-cook-among-zombies-242ab moved to kit_food (cross_now read as go_without): top_up_food_near 5 of 5 each, both pass. **Tests**: test/crossing-kit-673.test.js (a bot at the portal with no food, with no spare pickaxe, with 10 blocks; all three with nether_first; a failing kit rung not handed back; the crossing question without them; go_without and the take-up); the crossing's food, cook and kit tests moved to kitFoodStep; ladder tests at the portal now pass through the kit rungs or set them aside. npm test 2516, one timing test under load (load average 141) passing alone, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 87 of 92 with 3 known gaps, the flaky bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up and span-toward-a-fortress-38-up-ends-under-it (fortress_approach, not touched here, 3 of 5). **Not measured live**: no trial was run; home-stash.js NETHER_FOOD_POINTS (80) still drives the survival layer's stocking while the food search runs, the same as the whole stay's figure but a second number.
674. *A bow and 32 arrows for the blazes: where arrows come from and what they cost, from the record (flight records 2026-09-26T17:38Z to 2026-09-29T16:45Z, 1,491 files, read by script: 153.5 Overworld hours, 47.3 of them at night by the clock where a decision's state held it, 101.2 by day, 5.0 unknown; 218.4 Nether hours; the loot tables, barter table and fletcher trades read from the 26.1.2 server jar).* **The bow rung**: open (phase `bow`) in 13 records, all on 2026-09-26 between 19:09 and 20:39Z (25596, 25599), the `arrows` rung in 3 (25601 to 25603, 17:39Z that day); never since, while the day's diamond_sword rung after it is in 48 records to 2026-09-29 (the rung needs dark, a spider within 32 or three string). No bow was crafted in the record; a bow came into the pockets 12 times by pickup, and 186 records carried one from their save. **Arrows**: the most ever carried was 6 (430 records carried some, from their saves). Gained: 77 in the Overworld and 37 in the Nether; 242 spent. Skeletons that died within five blocks of the bot: 73 in the Overworld (22 at a known night), 41 in the Nether, about one arrow picked up for each, as the loot table says (entities/skeleton: 0 to 2, mean 1, plus 0 to 1 a Looting level). Distinct skeletons in sight within 24 blocks: 200 in the 47.3 night hours (4.2 an hour), 266 in the 101.2 day hours (2.6, in caves). The seven skeleton hunts (`hunt_mob`, 2026-09-26) took 4.2 minutes and no arrow; skeleton arrows hit the bot 747 times. **32 arrows from skeletons** is 32 kills: at the record's deaths near the bot (0.47 a night hour) 68 night hours; killing every skeleton seen (4.2 a night hour) 7.6 night hours, 55 nights of 10,000 ticks (8.3 minutes each at 20 ticks a second), about 18 hours of play with the days between; a hunter that saw three times as many would still spend 18 nights, six hours. **Other sources** (26.1.2): *feathers* only from chickens, never; *piglin barter*: spectral arrows weight 40 of 469, 6 to 12, 0.77 a gold ingot, so 32 for about 42 ingots (the same table gives a pearl for about 16 ingots; the bot's measured 160 for 18); a spectral arrow shoots from a bow with an arrow's damage, but bartering.js leaves them lying and `bowReady` and every count read `arrow` only; the record has 6 barter rounds and 47 approaches in three and a half days, and the pearl rung comes after the rods; *fletcher* (villager_trade/fletcher/1/emerald_arrow, stick_emerald): an emerald for 16 arrows, 32 sticks for an emerald, so 32 arrows for 64 sticks (8 logs) and a bow for 2 emeralds at level 2, the cheapest by far, but no village was found in any record of the window (`landmark_found` village: 0); *chests*: a bastion's (arrows 5 to 17, spectral 10 to 28, with its piglins and brutes) and a pillager outpost's (2 to 7); dungeons, desert pyramids, mineshafts and fortresses have none. **The blaze fight with a bow** is already there: the fight question offers `shoot_<id>` for a blaze in clear view 4 to 20 blocks off with a clear arc (combat.js shotTargets, survival.js), and mob-hunt.js shoots a blaze from 4 to 20 before closing to the sword when a bow and arrows are carried. It is priced at 4 arrows a blaze (20 health over 6, every arrow counted a hit; a full draw is a critical, 6 plus 0 to 5, so 2 to 4, and a player's scatter at 15 blocks is about a quarter block, inside a blaze's 0.6: the misses would be the lead on a bobbing blaze, not measured). Offered 16 times in 3 records (25584 2026-09-29 01:16 to 01:30Z, 25589 2026-09-28 17:13Z) with 1 to 3 arrows carried, against "about 4 arrows bring it down"; never chosen, and no arrow was shot at a blaze in the window (of 1,115 shots: skeletons 432, ghasts 391, piglins 136). A blaze gives a rod one kill in two (entities/blaze: 0 to 1), so seven rods are about 14 blazes, about 42 arrows if every one hits; 32 arrows are about 10 blazes, five rods. **Decision: not built.** The bow is cheap (three string, 110 spiders seen at night) but 32 arrows by skeleton hunting is some 55 nights at the record's rate, and the cheap sources are gold the bot does not yet spend before the blazes, and a village the trial worlds have not shown. Open for the user: (a) keep the spectral arrows a barter gives and count them as arrows everywhere (bartering.js KEEP, combat.js bowReady, the fight's counts); (b) a fletcher route (sticks for emeralds, emeralds for arrows) offered where a village is known; (c) the arrows rung's 16 (game-progress.js), which by this record is about four night hours even killing every skeleton seen, is left as it is (deferrable, and it has not opened since 2026-09-26).
672. *How much Jev is asked, and what in the asking moves his answers (Fable's review of 16:40Z: 6.6 asks a bot-minute, a median question of 6.3k characters; flight records of 2026-09-28T00:00Z to 2026-09-29T12:40Z, 1,088 files, 20,638 bot-minutes; the replay suite's cases and 160 recorded asks re-asked of TypeSafe's jev-latest; main at 065606c, then 787f56d).* **The asking.** 108,743 asks with Jev's answer (decision frames with judgments), 5.27 a bot-minute; the request as sent (state and questions, rebuilt from the frame's state, options and asked instructions) a median 8,215 characters, p90 20,552, the largest 88,836; input tokens a median 3,054; latency a median 186 ms, p90 258. By question: turn_priority 21,507 asks (1.04 a bot-minute, 20% of all), a median 4,666 characters; encounter_stance 15,270 (0.74), a median 21,325, p90 44,451, the largest 88,836 (6,770 tokens); fortress_leg 11,246 (0.55), 13,225; fortress_approach 9,952 (0.48), 6,996; unstuck_move 8,090 (0.39), 8,405; upkeep 7,518 (0.36), 7,713; survival_priority 6,088 (0.30), 9,388; hunt_target 930, a median 27,663. Of all the bytes the state is 37%, the options' words 37%, the instructions 25% (the glosses decide() appends to every question about playing the game about a thousand characters of each). The state's largest: healing 6.6% of all bytes, runClock 4.8%, recentPositions 2.7%, deathWouldCost 2.1%, riskNow 1.9%, stalled 1.6%, estimate 1.5%. The stance is half options (51%), its guidance alone 5,561 characters. **What moves the answers** (each field dropped, or each option cut to its first sentence, N=5 each; two asks of the same question differ in their top answer 5 times in 247, a mean total-variation distance of 0.018): the options cut to a sentence moved 135 of 247 top answers and lost 42 replay passes. Dropped whole: runClock moved 21 of 206 (4 passes lost), healing 14 of 216, riskNow 14 of 151, recentPositions 10 of 119, estimate 7 of 43 (3 lost), playedAnswers 4 of 12 (distance 0.17: without it hunt answers went from the strike to defer), playedRecord 4 of 32 and 3 of 12, sameSceneSoFar 1 of 10, hereSoFar 1 of 3; at the noise, deathWouldCost 5 of 124 (0.031), biomesNearby 2 of 50 (0.023), whatFailedBelow 0 of 10 (0.033) and afterTheLastRod 0 of 8 (0.039). Rewritten shorter, the records moved answers too: all of them as prose lines, 26 of 247 (4 passes lost); on 34 near-even cases runClock alone 10 (6 lost), riskNow, recentPositions and healing 9 or 10 each, against 7 with nothing changed; runClock cut to its four biggest ways moved basalt-delta-walk-off-25583 to none_good 3 in 10, playedRecord cut to its rows moved span-toward-a-fortress-38-up to its forbidden cross_level, and a sentence every option said, said once beside the question, sent span-ghast-walled-toward-push to none_good 17 times in 20 (2 in 20 as built): what is true whichever option is chosen still bears on how each ends. The glosses cut to a line each moved 12 of 248, no pass lost. **Now** (src/decisions/lean.js, src/typesafe.js, src/decisions/index.js, src/arbiter.js, src/survival.js, src/mob-hunt.js): (1) The request goes out from the client through `leanRequest` (JEV_LEAN=0 sends it as built), keeping every option's words and every record's shape: numbers to a tenth, null fields left out, the same words twice in a list said once with how often (whatFailedBelow carried one escalation five times), deathWouldCost's note and recentPositions' held places run together, playedAnswers cut to its rows for this situation and what the rest says that is not a count of past fights; runClock, playedRecord and blazeCounts (note 665, too new to measure) go whole. The decision record keeps what was built; the 'sent' stage says the characters sent. (2) afterTheLastRod is no longer built (the stance and the hunt) nor glossed. (3) The glosses in a line each. (4) turn_priority's answer is given again to the same scene within thirty seconds (sameScene: each claim's layer, alert and action, the kinds of mob within sixteen, the food band), when the ruling fell only for having gone (no ruling after a reflex or a single claim, its winner's claim gone, the claims changed and changed back) and health is not four lower; a newcomer, a stopped or idle winner, a minute, a mob at reach and the rest ask as before; said "(scene: ...)". Replayed over the 21,501 recorded turn_priority asks, 2,451 would have been held (163 of them had been answered otherwise): 1.04 to 0.92 a bot-minute, all asks 5.27 to 5.15. **Sizes as sent** (324 fixtures: main's 95 replay cases and 229 recorded asks; afterTheLastRod left out as the builders now do): a median 10,648 characters to 9,947, p90 23,801 to 21,840, the largest 55,014 to 50,324; the stance a median 19,825 to 18,535, the hunt 28,662 to 25,606, turn_priority 4,359 to 4,017. The 2.5k asked for is not reachable by the client without changing what Jev answers: the words that move him are the options' and the questions' own guidance, and they are to be cut builder by builder with the replay suite. test/lean.test.js holds each question to a ceiling as sent on the replay fixtures (CAP 2,500 for any question not named; the named ones at what they come to now, a ratchet to lower, never raise). **Replay suite** (5 runs a case; main's 95 cases): main 91 of 95 (2 known gaps open; fails bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, flaky, and span-toward-a-fortress-38-up-ends-under-it, cross_level 2 of 5); lean, 90 of 95 (3 known; fails bridge-sword-piglin and span-ghast-walled-toward-push, return_fireball 3 and none_good 2, both on the flaky list) and 92 of 95 (2 known; fails bridge-sword-piglin only). Before the rebase, 065606c's 91 cases had gone 87 and 86 as built. Tests: test/lean.test.js, test/arbiter.test.js (the scene held), test/decisions.test.js.
675. *Waiting out a rest, the largest waste pattern before the first blaze fight (note 667: 12.7 bot-hours, 5.6% of the time before a fight, in 'obtain blaze rods: detour' and 'obtain ender pearls: detour'; flight records 127_0_0_1-25598-Jev-2026-09-29T00-20-11-834Z (mid-242-bb-nether-1-fortress-9), 25583 2026-09-29T02-53-12-672Z (mid-243-cg), 25585 2026-09-29T01-32-11-244Z (mid-242-ca-nether-1), with their artifacts/midgame logs; all flight records of 2026-09-28 and 09-29 read by script).* **What the bot did.** 25598, 00:19 to 00:34Z: on a ledge at (-110, 52, 141) over the lava sea (lava under (-109, 51, 140), a 20-block drop into lava to the west), an iron pickaxe with 118 uses, no block (2 oak planks), the fortress's bricks 10 blocks across and 21 up. Every leg of the fortress search ended "out of blocks (0 carried)", walk_route "No path to the goal!", the staircase came no nearer, and working free's floor digs were refused by the dig guard (note 600: "the body would fall into lava"). Upkeep had offered the netherrack at about 00:25 and been answered carry_on, which holds five minutes. At 00:26:05 rung_progress offered differently, until_rest_ends and none good (keep_at_it resting; setting the rods aside not offered, ways untried below: fortress visit, upkeep's block reserve, nether gather, listed but not offered): none good 0.40, until_rest_ends 0.35, taken. The hold's catalog in the Nether had nothing ("[still] holding step:rung:obtain_blaze_rods until its rest ends; detours: none"), so the bot stood; after 45 seconds the stall watch struck the hold itself, work_free and differently came to nothing in a second, the rung's question came again, and until_rest_ends was taken again: by 00:19:44 the ledger said "rung progress: until rest ends, 13 times, 13 coming to nothing". 25583 mid-243-cg, 02:56 to 03:01Z: on blackstone at (-21, 101, -19) among a basalt delta's lava, 1.84 health, hunger 13, no food, no pickaxe, no wood, 30 iron ingots; rung_progress none good 0.55 (until_rest_ends 0.29) four times, the walk off refused "the way passes beside lava". 25585 mid-242-ca-nether-1, 01:32:27Z: the rods set aside and the pearls' sweep refused (noPath), leave_nether offered wait_here as "Other work in the Nether until the rods step's rest ends, taken up again in 27 minutes, then the rods again; what the work is, is asked then" (0.87 against go_back 0.07, a 385-block walk back); nothing was on offer, and it stood 20.5 minutes on its span at (118, 43, -360), with no pickaxe and one plank, a hoglin about, turn_priority and the shield asked each minute. **Why every way rested at once**: each way of the fortress's questions tried twice from here and come to nothing rests five minutes (tried.js REST_MS), and every one of them had failed for the same missing thing, blocks (25598) or a pickaxe and the health to walk past lava (25583); none of them could come to anything until that changed, and nothing on offer changed it. **The pathfinder's refusals were real** in these windows: the lava under the ledge and the 20-block drop into it (25598), and at 1.84 health in iron a touch of lava is death, which note 660's rule refuses and does not price (25583). **Across the record** (steps whose `waitingFor` says a hold with nothing on offer, gaps under a minute): 31.7 bot-hours in 3,904 windows over the whole trials, all but 0.5 of them in the Nether; 23.1 with a pickaxe carried, 19.6 of those with fewer than sixteen building blocks; by what rested: step:return_to_portal 15.0 h, the rods rung 7.9, rods_waiting 5.1. **Root cause**: the "other work until the rest ends" was an unnamed promise: the hold's catalog (breakStillness: the night mine, the Overworld's day work, a look around, ore a carried tool takes) is almost empty in the Nether, the option did not say what the work would be, and a hold with nothing on offer stood in five-second sleeps in the work's name; upkeep's blocks, stems and pickaxe, the work that would have ended the rests' cause, were only upkeep's, held by its carry_on. **Change** (src/work.js, src/game-progress.js): (1) *The hold's work is one catalog* (`detourWork`, what breakStillness offered), and while a rest is held it takes upkeep's work too (`upkeepOffers`, split from upkeepStep: make_pickaxe, fetch_stems, spare_pickaxe, wood_reserve, block_reserve; netherrack is not offered with no pickaxe and none to make now: dug by hand it drops nothing). (2) *The option that chooses the hold says what it has on offer from here* (`restWork`, the same catalog read without running, and `restWorkSays`): until_rest_ends "Work on offer meanwhile from here: Mine netherrack for building blocks now: 2 carried"; with nothing, the wait itself with its cost and why: "Wait here for the 2 minutes until the first of the fortress leg's ways comes off its rest here. Nothing else is on offer from here meanwhile (the Nether, where the day work of the Overworld is not on offer; no ore within 16 blocks that a carried tool takes; 34 building blocks and a pickaxe carried): chosen, this is standing here idle about 2 minutes, until about 00:27Z." leave_nether's wait_here the same ("Wait here until the rods step's rest ends, taken up again in 27 minutes, then the rods again. Nothing else is on offer ..."), through the game's `rest_work` handler. (3) *Upkeep's work is offered beside the wait* at the stall's and the rung's question when every way rests until a time, each its own answer ("... The obtain blaze rods is taken up again after it; the rest runs on meanwhile."). (4) *A hold chosen as work whose work runs out ends*, and the question above is asked again ("[wait] the work on offer while ... rests has run out; the question above is asked again"; goal.restHeld and a held wait_here are dropped), rather than a silent wait under the name of the work; a hold chosen as the idle wait is held to the rest's end as before (note 609's one "[wait] waiting for" line). A detour that was tried and failed is not "nothing on offer". **Asked of Jev** (TypeSafe, the recorded questions rebuilt from their flight frames): 25598's rung question as recorded, none good 6 of 6; with the hold's work said in until_rest_ends, none good 6 of 6; with the netherrack beside the wait as its own answer, block_reserve 8 of 8 (its source line, "the nearest netherrack ... 1 blocks off, with footing", assumed: the region was not read). 25585's leave_nether: wait_here 6 of 6 as recorded, with the work said (the stems for a pickaxe), and said as idle 27 minutes; with the change the hold then offers fetch_stems, the one way, taken. Not added to the replay suite: the recorded rung question comes to 14,112 characters as sent, over rung_progress's ceiling of 5,000 (note 672's ratchet). **Tests**: test/rest-wait-675.test.js on test/fixtures/rest-wait-675.json (the three windows' bots, pockets and what they were offered and answered): 25598's question says the netherrack on offer and offers it beside the wait; with 32 netherrack, the idle wait said whole; the hold offers block_reserve, and with it set aside a hold chosen as work ends at once, not stood out; a hold chosen idle holds to its end with one "[wait]" line; 25583's says the stems and no netherrack; 25585's wait_here said with its work, and as idle with a pickaxe and blocks carried, the idle passed to the hold and a hold that came back early asked again. test/rung-aside.test.js and test/ruined-portal.test.js read the new words; test/idle-detour.test.js rests upkeep's ways with the rest. npm test 2545 of 2545, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 91 of 95 with 2 known gaps (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up pillar 5 of 5 and span-ghast-walled-toward-push none good 3, return_fireball 2, both on the flaky list). **Not measured live**: no trial was run (starting the bot runs index.js), so the ledger's minutes for this pattern on these windows are not re-measured; the gather at 25598's ledge is not proven to find a face the dig guard allows. Left: a way resting for a cause the work has since made up (blocks gathered, the legs rested "out of blocks") keeps its rest to its end; the pathfinder's refusals were not priced further than note 660.
680. *One span walked four times, the warped sweep's chat in a second, and a step aside that stopped with the head still in the gravel (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260929T1901Z.md, findings 3 and 4; flight records 127_0_0_1-25593-Jev-2026-09-29T18-16-30-556Z (mid-242-gb) and 127_0_0_1-25595-Jev-2026-09-29T18-47-45-505Z (mid-242-hb), read by script).* **What the bot did.** 25593, 18:58 to 19:03Z: it laid a span of about ninety blocks east from (436, 53, -257) to (530, 54, -260), 103 blocks carried and 8 left, and then chose leg_west, leg_east and leg_west again along the same span (19:00:42 at (440, 53, -261), 19:01:56 at (528, 54, -261), 19:03:16 at (438, 53, -261)). The leg texts read each line at the feet's height alone: from the east end, a block up, the span a block below was "82 of open air ... no floor: it needs 90 blocks laid ... the blocks run out at cell 9"; from the west end the span's own blocks were "61 of rock to dig". The ground stood on is kept in columns of 4 by 4, and the line from the east end ran one block off the span, over the next row of columns: "stood on 6 of the 96 blocks" at 18:59:27, 92 of 96 from the other end. "Back the way the last leg came" was said on each walk back (the critic's reading that it was missing was wrong: it is by heading, not height). At 18:58:03 to 04 it said "Looking for a warped forest" and "No warped forest found" three times each: the known forest at (529, -290) had just set its walk aside (noPath), and each pass of the sweep counted a leg as found because a warped forest was remembered (`warpedKnown`, any distance), while the step walks only to one within 512 blocks whose walk is open; eight "legs" in under a second, the sweep rested, started again. 25595, 18:58:30Z (not drowning, as the critic had it: air 20, the head in gravel): hurt "in wall" at 20 health, body_way answered step_aside (0.51 against dig_out 0.43; the critic read the confidence as the probability), and the step stopped as its feet crossed into the cell beside, the head's box (the game's test, 0.24 either side of the eye) still in the gravel's column: four hurts, 20 to 16, before the dig took it. "Crafting a bread." was the loop's narration of the step the air had stopped, not a craft; the work's own interrupt check was the threats alone, and only digs, walks and the window's sync looked at the air. **Root cause**: each fact was read in a frame the walk does not keep: the leg at one height where the walk steps a block, stood-on on the line's own column where a span runs a block off it, a forest remembered where the step walks only to a near one, the step aside by the feet's cell where the head's box is the test. **Change**: (1) `surveyLeg` (src/nether-travel.js) follows the ground a block up or down from the height it starts at, where the cell ahead steps up with room over the head or down onto a floor, as the pathfinder walks the leg first; the leg says "It steps a block up or down N times where the ground does." and "N of its cells are on blocks the bot laid itself: its own span, walked before." (own-blocks.js `laidAt`); leg_* in src/decisions/travel.js says so. (2) `headingCoverage` (src/nether-coverage.js) counts a block of the line as stood on when a column within a block to either side was; the coverage watch keeps the ground walked every tick while the search runs, not only in the minute its looks are kept to (a crossing of ninety blocks outlasts it). (3) The warped sweep (src/warped-pearls.js) counts a leg found only on ground made or a forest the step itself would walk to (the same 512-block, walk-open test). (4) `headWays` step_aside (src/vitals.js) walks until `suffocatingBlock` is clear, not until the feet are in the cell beside or the last hurt is two seconds old. (5) The work's interrupt check (src/work.js runGoal) is the air (`checkAir`: the head in a block, breath short, the body in lava) and then the threats, so any step stops, a craft at the table included; the step's narration is not said while `needsAir` (src/narration.js). **Tests**: test/nether-coverage.test.js (a span a block below the feet: stepped once, floor to walk, nothing to lay; from the other end no rock; stood on counted a block beside the line), test/warped-pearls.test.js (a forest remembered past 512: no leg counted standing still, one "Looking", no "No warped forest found"), test/vitals.test.js (step_aside walks on past x 4.24 until the head's box leaves the gravel's column), test/narration.test.js (no step line with the breath short). npm test 2549 of 2549, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 92 of 95, 2 known gaps, and bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up (pillar 5 of 5, on the flaky list). **Not measured live**: no trial was run; Jev was not asked the corrected leg texts. Left: the finding 5 pattern (answers overridden by the next question, 25584) is not touched here.
678. *Go back, and a question a second later asking again: the way back that wanted a pickaxe it did not need (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260929T1901Z.md, findings 1 and 5; flight records 127_0_0_1-25591-Jev-* (mid-242-ch-fortress-10) and 127_0_0_1-25584-Jev-* (mid-242-fg), read by script).* **What the bot did.** 25591, 17:20 to 19:03Z: at 1.6 health, hunger 10, nothing to eat, no pickaxe and no blocks, it stood on netherrack at y 81 with its portal at (-20, 71, 19), 8 across and 10 straight below. It chose leave_nether go_back (0.75 at 18:56:22) and nether_food_kit return_for_food over and over; within a second nether_gather asked for a warped stem and its portal_trip, "back through the portal for wood", was taken, ended in no route, and without set the rods aside, and leave_nether was asked again. The trip back was said as "10 blocks off, about 2 seconds at a walk", and portal_trip as reached "straight across at this height", a crossing that ends 10 blocks above the portal. 25584, 18:59 to 19:02Z: nether_gather without set the rods aside and leave_nether's search_on took them up again in the same second, round and round. **Root cause.** The go_back was carried out: returnFromNether's walk failed, and the staircase to the portal (`tunnelToward`) wanted a stone pickaxe before any step, though the stair already digs a block under hardness one by hand (netherrack, 2.0 seconds a block by hand by prismarine's digTime, 0.3 with a wooden pickaxe, no drops). Getting that pickaxe asked nether_gather, whose portal_trip was the very trip that wanted it, and whose without set a rung aside without saying from where, so the question above took it straight back. The portal's distance was flat everywhere (portalTrip, nether_gather, portal_way), and the crossing's reach was judged across only. **Change.** (1) `stairFromHere`/`stairSays` (src/tunneling.js): whether a stair step from here gains ground with what is carried, about how many steps and seconds, and what is dug by hand. (2) `tunnelToward` (src/work.js) digs the stair by hand where the target is within sixteen across (as the pillar's rule) and a step gains; the pickaxe first otherwise, and while it is got what it is wanted for is kept (`bot._wantedFor`). (3) nether_gather (src/nether-gather.js): the portal's distance across and up or down; the crossing reaches it only at this height; a stair down or up to a portal within sixteen across is a way to it, said with its seconds; portal_trip is not offered when the wood is wanted for the way to that portal itself, and that is said; without says the trip it ends and records `goal.rungAside` from here (as set_aside_rung does), so search_on is not offered back from the same spot (asideStands). (4) `portalTrip` (src/game-progress.js) and portal_way say the portal's height and, within sixteen across in the Nether, the stair. (5) recent.js prints the answer's probability beside the runner-up's, with the service's confidence apart (25595's step_aside printed 0.27 against dig_out 0.43 when the distribution had them 0.51 and 0.43: `pickByDistribution` is right; the display mixed the two measures). Test: test/way-back-678.test.js. **Measure next.** In the next Nether trials: go_back followed by a return_overworld step that is a stair and not nether_gather; the leave_nether/nether_gather alternation per bot-minute.

676. *Shot with a shield in hand and its back to the blazes (25589, mid-242-dc-fortress-22, 2026-09-29 18:47 to 18:49Z, main at ed01268): 71% of the shots that landed on a bot carrying a shield came with it down, because the shield rose only inside the survival layer's own turn; each shooter's warning is now asked about as it begins, beside whatever step runs, and a shot already in the air with no answer meets a reflex.* The person watching saw the bot shot again and again without its shield or facing the right way: fireballs of 3.9 at full health and burning ticks while the step was work, take_cover, leave_and_heal, out_of_fire, shield_at_shots and charge_nearest, shield in only one of fifteen hurt frames, and a 3.9 landing a second after shield_at_shots was chosen. **Measured** (scripts/shot-record.js over 1,112 flight records since 2026-09-28, every damage frame whose direct cause is a projectile): 2,555 shots landed (1,468 small fireballs, 907 arrows, 173 ghast fireballs, a trident), 2,415 on a bot with a shield in the off hand, and at the impact the shield was up for 700 and down for 1,715 (71%). Of those 2,415: not raised at all 1,462; lowered within the second before 253; raised under the quarter second a shield takes to block 201; up and facing away 89; up, facing the shot and landing anyway 410. 714 came from behind or the side (more than 90 degrees off the look); 2,125 came with the bot standing still, 290 moving. The standing choice shield_at_shots was in force for 1,870 of them: the choice was made, and nothing carried it out where the shots came. Unraised by who had the turn: a question out to Jev 460 (encounter_stance 263, turn_priority 110, shield_policy 44, body_way 19), stances that never raise it (take_cover 150, charge_nearest 99, charge 90, dig_in 57, close_in 54, eat 49, leave_and_heal 36), the hunt 88, the work's steps (stalk_mob 69, dig_bunker 25, and others). Decision latency was not the cause: 1,269 of the 1,715 came with no question out, 394 with one out under a quarter second. Nor the event loop: the recorder was silent over 1.5 seconds in the three seconds before only 4 of them. Two faults under the 410 that were up and facing: the code's flag (`_shieldRaised`) is not the server's, and any main-hand use ends the shield's use on the server while the flag stays up (on a scratch 26.1.2 server: the bot's own living-entity flags read 3 with the shield raised and 2 after a main-hand deactivate, the flag still up), so a meal or a bow's draw in a fight left the code believing a shield that was down; and mineflayer divides a shot's velocity by 8000 as the older protocol wanted while 26.1 sends blocks a tick, so projectile-guard read every shot as still and judged it by its moves, which the server sends every half second for a fireball. **Change.** (1) src/shot-reflex.js, installed with the survival layer, looks every tick whatever holds the turn: each shooter in sight, or within 24 blocks unseen, that begins its warning (a blaze's glow, three seconds before its shots at 3, 3.3 and 3.6; a ghast's open mouth, half a second; a skeleton's, stray's or bogged's draw, about a second) is asked about aside (`shot_answer`, the work keeping the turn; Jev answers in about a fifth of a second): shield_up (face them and hold the shield while the shots are due, the step waiting; said with how long, whether the shooters are split, and the measured rates below and this run's own tally), behind_cover (a cell one or two level steps off out of every warned shooter's line, with no lava or drop beside the way), strike_first (a warned shooter the sword reaches, its swings and seconds against the seconds to its shot) and keep_on (what each shot that lands costs through the armour). The answer holds for that warning only; the next is asked again. Without Jev (no client, JEV_ENCOUNTERS=0) a warning is answered shield_up by rule. (2) A shot in the air on a line that hits (the server's own spawn and velocity packets, its owner from the spawn's data) whose shooter's warning has no answer is the reflex's: the shield up, the head turned to it, the walk's keys and looks refused while held (a body lock on setControlState, look and lookAt, bounded by the shot), let go a quarter second after nothing calls for it, then the step goes on (the navigate watchdog does not count the wait as a stall). Where the shooters are split the facing covers the most of them. The physical exceptions, where the turn is not made and why is kept on the frame (`shotRefused`): in the air over lava or a drop of more than three, laying a span or a pathfinder block, in water or lava, on a ladder, eating or drawing a bow (the raise ends them), a biter at arm's length (projectile-guard meleeClose). Answered otherwise (behind_cover, strike_first, keep_on), the shots are left to the answer, and projectile-guard deflect and blaze-stand shieldVolley leave them too. (3) combat.raiseShield reads the server's flags and raises again when the flag says up and the server says down (not within half a second of its own raise, which would start the quarter second over); lowerShield does not lower under a hold. (4) shield_policy, the standing choice, is gone (its question, the survival method, the policy reader); the replay case becomes a shot_answer case. (5) The recorder: the frame's shield key is the server's word, a hold's why (`shotHold`) rides the frames, and each shot on a line is a `shot` frame (landed or not, shield up or down, answered or the reflex's), which shot-record.js reads. **Verified** on a scratch 26.1.2 server (port 25700, scripts/shot-reflex-probe.js, two minutes a round: iron and a shield, walking eight blocks with the pathfinder and standing three seconds facing away, blazes summoned seven blocks to the side, free to move): one blaze, the shield never raised 11 of 39 fireballs landed; the reflex alone (no answers) 7 of 42, late where the blaze had come close; each glow answered shield_up by a stand-in answering after 0.2 seconds 2 of 45. Three blazes: never raised 13 of 126; answered 3 of 128, the walk 8 laps against 13.5 (the holds' cost, said on the option). Two faults found there and fixed before those rounds: a blaze that loses its line keeps its glow and shoots the moment it has one again, so a warning is asked and held for shooters within 24 blocks seen or not, and an answer holds while its warning lasts, not for a fixed time; and a warning whose shooter went out of sight was never seen to end, holding the step behind cover for twelve seconds. Of the 5 landings with an answer, 2 came with the shield up a second or more, faced within two degrees (the leak the records' 410 also hold, not explained here), and one where the server had ended the shield's use during an eleven-second glow and the raise came again a moment late. behind_cover with a wall beside each end: walked to the cell behind it and held there until the glow's shots were past; the blaze lost its line and fired nothing. Stationary with the shield up and facing: a sword swung or a blaze struck let nothing through; a dig 0 of 9; a block placed 1 of 9; a meal ended the shield's use as above. Tests: test/shot-reflex.test.js on 25589's frames (18:48:19.334, the work stalking with its back to six blazes and ten fireballs in the air: raised, turned to them, the walk's keys and looks refused while held and given back after; 18:48:19.838 in the air over the fortress floor still raised; over lava, laying a span or eating refused with why; the glow asked aside during work, keep_on leaving its fireball be, the next glow asked again; shield_up raising at 2.4 seconds into the glow with no shot yet; the rule without Jev; an answer lapsing; strike_first offered at reach; split shooters; the stale flag raised again; the tally), test/body.test.js (deflect leaves a shot answered keep_on and meets one unanswered). **Measure next.** In the trials: the `shot` frames' landed-with-shield-up and landed-with-it-down against these 700 and 1,715; how often a hold is refused and for what (`shotRefused`); how many shot_answer questions a minute skeletons' draws cost, and whether Jev picks keep_on where the step matters more. Still open: a pillager's or a piglin's crossbow gives no warning read here (the reflex meets its bolts in the air); the 410 up-and-facing landings are read by the old flag and a shooter chosen by nearness, and the next records will say how many were the stale flag.

687. *No pickaxe in the Nether, said where it bites; the last pickaxe's wear said before it breaks; two chat lines that were not so; a failure pinned on the wrong answer (the live critic's items 1 to 3 in artifacts/critic/critic-20260929T2008Z.md and item 1 of critic-20260929T2032Z.md; 25585 mid-242-dh-fortress-22, 25589 mid-242-dd-fortress-22, 25590 mid-242-hd; flight records since 2026-09-29T12:00Z read by script).* **Measured.** Of 3,346 Nether bot-minutes since 12:00Z, 1,686 (50%) were spent with no pickaxe (25589 231, 25585 215, 25591 214, 25598 158, 25584 144, 25581 137, 25597 126, the rest under 115). In them upkeep was asked 541 times and answered carry_on 260 (48%), fetch_stems 188, make_pickaxe 88; fetch_stems was offered 433 times and make_pickaxe 106. carry_on's words were only "Carry on with the X and see to this later; asked again in five minutes" (149 with cross toward, 96 find fortress, 84 go without, 52 nether gather). (2) upkeep's carry_on with no pickaxe says what the five minutes cannot do ("No pickaxe is carried: the next 5 minutes cannot dig or stair through basalt, blackstone or nether bricks, or pillar or span a gap; netherrack is dug by hand (about 2 seconds a block) and drops nothing", or the blocks carried), and that the hold ends when a way chosen fails for want of one; the hold is kept with noPickaxe, and the ledger (tried.js settleOne and record) ends it when an answer settles blocked "no tool for", "harvest tool", "out of blocks", "none to lay" or "no pickaxe" with none carried (block-stock.js `pickaxeWanted`); the next asking says "The last carry-on ended early: tunnel failed for want of a pickaxe (...)". The upkeep's situation leads "No pickaxe is carried: fetch_stems gets one first." (3) The questions above lead with getting one: fortress_leg with no pickaxe and make_pickaxe or fetch_stems offered puts them first and its first fact `withoutAPickaxe` says what the ways lack and which were not offered for want of one; rung_progress, when answers under it settled blocked for want of a pickaxe in the last ten minutes, offers upkeep's ways to one, puts them first and leads its situation with them and those failures. (4) Wear as a fact (pickaxe-budget.js `wearOf`, `wearSays`, `lastPickaxeSays`): the uses carried sampled every half minute over a quarter hour at each upkeep pass and question, a new pickaxe starting them again; in the Nether the pickaxe fact of fortress_leg and fortress_approach is the pickaxes with uses, the uses spent lately and how long the rest lasts at that rate, and whether another can be made; with one pickaxe and no other to be made, each leg, the crossing (cross_level), the staircase and seek_fortress_height say the blocks they dig against its uses ("it breaks on the way, the rest dug by hand"). In the Nether on the ladder, with one pickaxe and the pockets making another (mob-hunt.js `bestMakeable`: iron, cobblestone or blackstone, else planks, the head and the wood for sticks and a table; makePickaxe now makes one beside one carried), upkeep offers spare_pickaxe said with the wear, and carry_on says the wear too. (25590 at 20:08:04, 16 blocks from it). **Replay** (two cases added, upkeep frames of real trials, no pickaxe, stems known and walkable, the texts as changed): upkeep-no-pickaxe-stems-58-steps-25585 (17:52:22Z, recorded carry_on 0.66) and upkeep-no-pickaxe-fortress-25589 (20:08:20Z, recorded carry_on 0.58): with the recorded words carry_on 5 of 5 each, with the new fetch_stems 7 of 7 each. **Tests**: test/note-687.test.js (the 25589 upkeep frame, test/fixtures/upkeep-no-pickaxe-25589.json: carry_on's words and the lead, the hold held and ended by "no tool for nether bricks", not by "No path"; a leg stopped at bricks with no pickaxe and dug with one; the staircase gate; 25585's saved fortress map, test/fixtures/fortress-map-25585.json, and its chat; the chat for a found fortress; fortress_leg on a basalt ledge at y 36 leading with make_pickaxe, three legs and the staircase closed; 25589's 117 to 3 uses as wear, the spare offered and made; the misattributed failure); test/mob-hunt.test.js, nether-wood-658, tried and rest-wait-675 updated for the new rules (a staircase no hand digs is not offered; the rung's lead; a spare beside one pickaxe is work on offer). **Not measured live**: no trial was run. **Open**: the critic's items 2 (fortress_approach asked on the fortress's floors) and 4 to 5 are not touched; spareDue's Overworld rule (cobblestone) is unchanged; how long a carry_on hold now lasts in practice (each failure for want of a pickaxe re-asks upkeep) is not measured.
682. *An answer carried out, or failed with its reason said to the next asking; a fortress left, not found again from the same spot (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260929T1923Z.md, findings 1 and 2; flight records 127_0_0_1-25585-Jev-2026-09-29T19-09-37-511Z (mid-242-dh-fortress-22), 127_0_0_1-25581-Jev-2026-09-29T18-18-12-815Z (mid-243-gf) and 127_0_0_1-25598-Jev-2026-09-29T18-58-18-018Z (mid-242-ee-fortress-18), read by script).* **What the bot did.** (a) The make_pickaxe answers were carried out: 25585 at 19:18:22 had no pickaxe and 1 log, 1 plank, 2 sticks; the wooden pickaxe was in its pockets by 19:18:26, and 25581's by 19:00:44. The hunt's record said each as "walked to where 1 hoglin seen ... and none was within thirty-two blocks", hoglin_walk said "None made yet in this trial", and each asking came from a new place, so the ledger's "from here" (four blocks) said nothing. "Leaving this fortress for now" and "A fortress! I'm heading for it" were said together eight times in eight minutes. **Root cause.** A failure reached the next asking only from within four blocks of where it was chosen, or toward the same target. The hunt's own record did not say how it ended, and a fortress set aside by its extent could be found again from the spot where it was left. **Change.** (1) `tried.justNow` (src/tried.js), read on every ledgered question: an answer to the same question that came to nothing in the last two minutes, from wherever the bot stood, is said on its option ("Chosen 21 seconds ago 57 blocks from here, and it came to nothing: ..."). A walk to a hoglin is the same walk however it is hunted, so recordSays says it on both hoglin_walk and hoglin_pillar. (3) A fortress set aside from a spot is set aside, all of it, from within four blocks of that spot while the set-aside lasts (`leftFromHere`, src/mob-hunt.js; remembered fortresses elsewhere are not touched). fortressInView reads the latest set-aside from here, else the latest over the bricks, so back_to_fortress is said and not offered from where Jev left it. keep_searching says when the look was cut short and the fortress runs on past it. (4) upkeep: a pickaxe made puts the work's step back (src/work.js upkeepStep). **Tests.** test/answers-682.test.js: the walk that finds no way is recorded as that, the place rests and is said, and both hunts say it; a blocked answer from 57 blocks off 21 seconds ago is said, not rested, and not said after five minutes; the hunt's failure is kept on restock_food's answer. test/fortress-wall.test.js: left from the bot's spot a second ago with a radius of 4, fortress_leg is asked, not fortress_approach, and back_to_fortress is not offered (before: fortress_approach). npm test 2572 of 2573; the one failure (push-escape, a stance on a span) passes alone.
