(6) unstuck.js localMoves: a move that takes back any change the spell made in the last minute (the latest change at each cell) is not offered, and a move that did not get there from this very cell in the last minute is not offered from it again, both said in notOffered. (7) One fortress, one place: mob-hunt.js `fortressAnchor` matches the bricks seen to the fortress known (joined to it by eight-block links, or within its extent, at least 32) and keeps it an hour since last seen; the approach is the fortress's (its failures kept while the aim moves within it, `sameFortress`), looseEnds records a stall on the way in as that way failed on the approach instead of setting aside sixteen blocks of the fortress, leave_fortress sets aside the whole fortress by the anchor's extent, the visit's target and the stall's chat name the anchor. (8) descend is not offered under the 12 health the descent keeps; the approach's state says why. The registry's when-texts say (2), (3) and (8), and raid_bastion is registered under obtain_food. **Checked, not changed:** note 697's re-offer rule (least-bad.js chosenBefore) covers the plan questions and those asked at a change, not survival_priority, which is asked every few seconds while its answer runs (the eight trips above were asked from four places 30 blocks apart); the route check in (3) is what ends the unchanged re-offer. The hoglin hunts chosen at 00:50:02 and 00:58:12 ended in their walks (note 682 records that). Bridges that lay a block and are not stepped onto are not judged here. **Tests.** test/note-706.test.js: the one-hit line at 0.2, and not at 12, at hunger 18 or with two steaks; the trip home with legs, crossing and staircase resting said as not reachable, not offered among the food routes and said among those not offered; no keep_on at 0.2 and keep_on at 12; lastHit first in an upkeep question's state; the creeper held from 9.4 to 6.8, asked at 5.7 (into the reach) and at 4.8, held milling within three; dig_down not offered over a pillar block laid four moves back; five sightings of 25588's fortress one anchor, a stall keeping the fortress and its failed way, and the stall's chat naming the anchor. npm test 2745 of 2745, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 102 of 107 with the 3 known gaps, failing bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up and leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598 (both on the flaky list; the suite asks with no bot, so none of this runs there). **Not measured live**: no trial was run and Jev was not probed on the new words.
707. *No fallbacks: when Jev is down, no decision is made (the user, 2026-09-30: "I don't want jev fallbacks. If jev is down, decisions aren't made.").* **Inventory** (every path in live play where code chose without Jev's answer): (a) decide() (src/decisions/index.js, tree.js): every one of 49 trees carried a `fallback`, walked on a TypeSafe error, a timeout, the breaker open or no client (47 old orders, e.g. survival_priority's shelter-before-food, empty_spawner's stash_rods first from note 704, turn_priority's urgency order, the stance's 'throws' which sent survival.js to its encounter rules), and a gate with `below: 'fallback'` walked it on a low confidence (none in use); announceFallback said "going with the safe default". (b) Callers that acted on `decision.fallback`: survival.js stanceStep (the rules answer the tick), the shelter cascade (a pocket, a shaft, a mine in one tick) and the shaft pocket before a room, nightTarget's nearest ore (nightOre), corpse-run.js (the kit or daylight, fitToGo), inventory-tidy.js (the tidy's own order), home-base.js sheep_search, work.js dug_into_liquid (plug), search_heading, while_cooking, strategy.js (source 'fallback'), arbiter.js (answeredScene). (c) Stale answers read as a default: work.js moreOfSource (stale took more), dug_into_liquid (stale plugged), home-base pickHomeSite (a stale path threw and took the first site), strategy.js and surface.js chooseClimb (a stale decision had no path). (d) `!client` defaults (unreachable in play, where index.js always builds a client, but production code): work.js upkeepStep, resource_source (the first action run), breakStillness (walked with no client), moreOfSource (taken), sculkStep, whileCooking; home-base.js (the first flock, explore, the first site); survival.js (the cascade, the shaft pocket, nightOre); corpse-run.js. (e) arbiter.js answerOrCut: a turn_priority question cut when the bot was hurt, or with no answer in five seconds, gave the turn by rulesPick. (f) Batched questions about play: opportunistic_ore, passing_gold, opportunistic_animal (an error or a five-second timeout swallowed, the step carrying on), boat_crossing (counted failed, the bot walks). (g) body.js: a body_way with no answer in a second took the old order's way (kept: the body's physics). (h) The stall watch and the rung's budget counted an outage's stillness as a stall and as rung minutes. Left as they are: none_good handling (Jev answered), the opt-outs by configuration (JEV_ENCOUNTERS=0, JEV_FORTRESS_VISIT=0, JEV_EMPTY_SPAWNER=0: the code's encounter rules and "the hunt as before" run only when set), JEV_ARBITER=shadow (the old layers' order, by design), the rule reflexes (lava, fire, a hot floor, a head in a block, the breath, the shot in the air of note 676, the one-shot line of note 701, the magma crouch, the meal a reflex eats) and the swing at what is in reach while a stance is asked; player requests (intake, commands, builds, dreams) already failed and told the player on an outage, and recovery_action's adviser (not called in play). **Change.** (1) src/jev-down.js (new): `unreachable(err)` (a TypeSafeError with no status or 408/429/5xx, a refused connection, a timeout, a garbled body; not a 4xx, a stop of the bot's own, or an answer naming no option offered, BadAnswer); `down()` holds the asker (the walk's goal and the keys let go, the crouch kept; nothing for an aside question), logs `[jev down] <id>: <reason>` and says once in chat "Jev isn't answering, so I'm waiting here until it does."; `back()` logs `[jev down] back: ... asked fresh` and says "Jev is back."; the backoff 1, 2, 4, 8, then every 15 s. (2) decide(): no client is Jev not reachable (NO_CLIENT); an unreachable ask holds, the task's check (a reflex's preemption, the air, a threat, a cancel) ending the hold through the question's own watcher as it ends any question, and is asked again; an answer after an outage is returned stale with `jevWasDown`, and the caller asks fresh from where the bot is. define() refuses `fallback` and a gate below 'fallback'; `safetyRule` (with `safetyWhy`) only on body_way (the builders' order of the ways out) and shot_answer (shotRule: the shield, or cover where the shooters are split), answered at once when Jev is not reachable (`[jev down] body_way: ... by the body's safety rule`). A none good walks a branch by Jev's own answers at each level (decideTree's answerAt), the first listed only where there is none. ask() takes `hold` ({ bot, goal, task }) and `timeoutMs` (each try's bound): the play batches (the three detours, boat_crossing) hold the same way and come back `{ stale: true, answers: {} }`. (3) Callers: every `decision.fallback` branch and `!client` default in (b) to (d) removed; stale handled where it was not (strategy returns { stale } and game-progress ends the step, chooseClimb, pickHomeSite and moreOfSource ask again, dug_into_liquid looks again, sheep_search returns); the old orders still passed as `context` (renamed oldOrder, way-down's oldOrderWay) are read by the tests' stand-in only. (4) arbiter.js: no turn is given by rule in play: a cut (no answer in five seconds) gives nobody the turn and the question is asked at the next pass; no cut when hurt; no cut while Jev is down (the question's own hold is the wait); an answer that is no claim of the pass's is asked again; rulesPick stays for the shadow and dry rulings. (5) stillness.js raises no stall and arbiter.js rungWatch no rung question while Jev is down (a failed ask within the last minute; a mark no ask renews lapses after a minute, so the watches cannot stay off for good). (6) typesafe.js: the breaker's window 60 s to 15 s, so Jev's return is found within about fifteen seconds. (7) Tests: test/support/jev-stand-in.js, loaded by the test script (`node --test --require`), is an explicit stand-in client for tests that give none: each question's old order moved there unchanged (OLD_ORDER, with safetyOrder, leastVisited, approachFallback, legFallback, endFallback, GATHER_ORDER), the body's physics by its safety rule, 'throws' for the stance; `withAnswers` for other answers in one test; under the test runner a question held 200 times fails (named at exit) instead of hanging. The recorder says 'safety rule' and "Held while Jev was down; asked fresh". Docs: docs/decisions.md regenerated (every tree: "no fallback: nothing is decided by code; the bot holds, says once that it is waiting for Jev, asks again with a backoff, and asks it fresh when Jev answers"; body_way and shot_answer their safety rule), README, CONTRIBUTING, docs/how-jev-thinks.md, docs/rule-audit.md. **Verified on a scratch server** (26.1.2, port 25707, flat, peaceful, day; scripts/jev-down-probe.js, new; the console for setup only; stopped by its console and deleted): the bot's own loop (work.js runIdle, the arbiter live) with the TypeSafe client pointed at 127.0.0.1:1: idle_work asked at 6.1 s, `[jev down] idle_work: fetch failed; no decision is made until Jev answers`, "Jev isn't answering, so I'm waiting here until it does." said once, the bot moved 0.00 blocks in the next 10 s and no decision was made; a fire set at its feet at 16.3 s: the arbiter preempted for the fire, `[jev down] body_way: out_of_fire by the body's safety rule`, out 3.1 blocks, health 20 after; the client pointed back at TypeSafe at 19.3 s: `[jev down] back: idle_work answered after 19s down` at 25.2 s (the breaker's window), "Jev is back." once, the held answer recorded stale with jevWasDown, and idle_work asked fresh and answered by Jev (explore). **Tests**: test/decisions.test.js (the hold, said once each, the walk and keys let go, asked fresh after; a hold ended by the task's check; body_way and shot_answer by their safety rule; a play batch held and stale; a player's request thrown), test/decision-registry.test.js (no fallback anywhere, safety rules only on the two, the stand-in marked), test/arbiter.test.js (no turn by rule on a cut, none when hurt, none while down), test/stillness.test.js (no stall nor rung question while down, a stall again after); tests that read `question(id).fallback` read the stand-in's oldOrder; the tests of removed no-Jev behavior (the corpse run's daylight rule, the shaft pocket before a room without Jev, nightOre) removed; the shelter tests ask each pass until the way. npm test 2754 of 2754, JEV_ARBITER=shadow npm test 2754 of 2754; replay suite 101 of 107, the 3 known gaps and bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, basalt-delta-walk-off-25583, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598 (all on the flaky list; nothing Jev is told changed). **Not changed / not measured live:** no trial has run an outage; a step already under way (a walk chosen before the outage) goes on to its next question, where it holds; a mob at arm's length during an outage is not fought except by the swing a stance question makes while it is out (the stance itself waits for Jev); the arena drills and scripts/endgame.js without Jev now hold instead of running the old orders; a Jev slow past a detour's five seconds is treated as down.
708. *A box whose window sees none of where the blazes come, a hunt that could do nothing chosen thirty times, "no fight is started" said beside "I'm going after a blaze", and a fortress 104 blocks off with no way toward it on offer (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0118Z.md, items 1 and 2; 25591 mid-242-nb at 01:12:38 to 01:19:24Z and 25584 mid-242-nh at 01:17:52 to 01:18:22Z on 2026-09-30, read with scripts/trials/recent.js and the flight records by script; each trial's Nether region copied as saved, read-only, test/fixtures/spawner-box-25591.json and fortress-far-25584.json).* **What the bots did.** (a) 25591 stood at (-104, 78, 150), 6 blocks from the cage at (-108, 77, 155), 0 of 7 rods, health 18.1, hunger 17, nothing to eat. It had dug in beside the room ("taking them at the door", 01:10:45) and at 01:16:11 chose empty_spawner box_here ("Walk 1 block to a cell 6.4 blocks from the cage ... hold it for its next blazes"); the box's window faced +z at (-104, 79, 151), into the netherrack north of the room's fence wall. At 01:16:59 box_here was offered again as "the box whole already ... About 0 seconds", then stand_by_spawner ("in the open at within four blocks of the cage (6 off now)"), and the stand's wait held the bot where it was (the wait takes anything within eight as there). Every blaze about was "out of sight" at 4 to 6 blocks. From 01:12:38 turn_priority was asked about 30 times, 14 of them in 01:14:09 to 01:14:52, the why "a newcomer within six blocks" each time: the spawner's new blazes behind the rock. Hunt was answered each time. The hunt's run (huntObserved) found no blaze in sight and asked the visit first (fortress-visit.js). The visit's answer, get_food_here and then hoglin_hunt, was held, and a held answer that is not go_in returned "acted" with nothing done. So the hunt kept the turn, did nothing, and was never marked idle. At 01:18:16 restock_food keep_on read "No fight is started while it does not", and the same second the work's step chat said "I'm going after a blaze for blaze rod." (b) 25584, at (-59, 57, -170) in its leg's tunnel heading west, saw the fortress at (-163, 54, -182), 104 blocks off through solid netherrack. fortress_visit heal_first, then fortress_approach offered only cross_level (33 cells, ending 71 from it at lava) and tunnel; the walk's survey found no route. Jev answered none good 0.5, tunnel was taken as the least bad and came to nothing in 2 seconds, and note 693's rule held it and asked fortress_leg. That question set the fortress aside ("its ways in from here came to nothing"), said no leg's bearing against it, and leg_east (0.32) took the bot 60 blocks away: "I'm looking for a fortress (leg 11, heading east)". The chat also said "Getting food here first: hunger 20, health 20." **The rules, read.** A blaze spawner tries only with a player within 16, at a cell up to 4 across and one below to one above its cage (blaze-tactics.js spawnCells, weighted as the jar weights them). A blaze takes a target only in sight. So a box is worth holding for a spawner's blazes only as far as its window has a line to those cells. On 25591's ground the box it held sees none of the 83 open cells, and the box cell by the cage (-108, 78, 151) sees cells for about 91 in 100 of the tries. **Measured.** Since 12:00Z on 2026-09-29, 10,715 turn_priority asks in 525 flight records; 1,559 were asked for a newcomer within six blocks, and in 343 of those every mob within six was out of sight and beyond four. **Changes.** (1) blaze-tactics.js `spawnLine` (with `windowLine`, `standLine`, `lineWords` and `windowSays`): of the spawner's tries, how many in 100 put a blaze whose eyes have a line to the bot's body in a cell, a box's walls counted as built and its window as dug. lineThrough takes an `open` set for a window still to be dug. boxSite given the cage (`sightOf`) gives the nearest box with its line, and as `inLine` the one of the nearest 24 whose window sees the most, where that is more. empty_spawner's boxes say what the window sees ("Its window sees where about 91 in 100 of the spawner's blazes come."). A box whose window sees none is not offered as "hold it for its next blazes"; it says "Its window sees none of where the spawner's blazes come: it holds for none of them." box_in_line is offered where a nearby box sees more than box_here's does. The stance's box options say the same. The stand's cell says what it sees. The question's state says `lineHere` ("From here, 6 blocks from the cage, it sees where fewer than 1 in 100 of the spawner's blazes come; the blaze within 16 out of sight."). Where the bot's own spot sees fewer than 1 in 100, note 700's open_slit is offered here too (cage-hold.js `slitOption`), with what the bot sees once the slit is open. On 25591's box: the two fences at (-105, 78, 152) and (-106, 78, 152), then still fewer than 1 in 100, said. (2) A stand chosen at the cage with no cell of its own walks within four of the cage, as its option says, once, where the bot's spot sees fewer than 1 in 100 of those cells. Otherwise the wait holds where the bot is, as before (mob-hunt.js findFortressStep). (3) A held visit answer carried out when chosen now returns `held` (fortress-visit.js ask), and huntObserved returns false on it: the turn did nothing, so the arbiter's idle rule (arbiter.js idled) can see it. mob-hunt.js claim makes no hunt claim for a blaze hunt with none in sight while such an answer holds (`holdsOff`). With the one hunted out of sight, the claim says so, and walled in (walled-in.js) its option says "the bot is walled in (3 of the 8 blocks round it its own), so it closes on it only by digging out first". (4) arbiter.js observe: a newcomer is a mob within six in sight or within four, as the watch's own newcomer rule already had it. One behind the rock counts when it comes into sight. (5) keep_on in mob-hunt.js foodLeave, nether-travel.js netherAnswers and nether-food.js askRestockFood says what going on without food does to the fights (nether-travel.js `keepOnFightSays`): "The hunt goes looking for no blaze meanwhile (the search goes on), but a blaze met in reach is still offered as a fight." That is the code: the unfit branch sends the work's hunt to the search, and the observed hunt's claim does not read hunger. The hunt step's chat says the same under keep_on at hunger under 18 with no food ("Going on without food for now: I won't go after a blaze, but I'll fight one that comes."). At hunger 18 or more, food fetched is "Stocking up on food here first" (intention.js). The leg's chat after a fortress Jev left says "Leaving the fortress for now, searching on". (6) fortress_approach offers `head_toward` where the fortress is more than 48 blocks across: one pass at a time the way the legs go, the pathfinder's walk (GoalNearXZ, passing), then the crossing at this height (crossToward), then the staircase. It is held as any way in; the way in is asked again within 48 or after a pass that gains nothing. It is not offered for a stretch or a place beside the fortress. (7) Each leg asked with a fortress in view says where its end lies against it: "Toward the fortress in view: its end is 13 blocks from its nearest brick (103 now)." on 25584's leg_west, "Away from ... 198" on leg_east. **Note 693's escalation, checked here.** The none good, the least bad and the question above were each as the rule has them. What was missing was the move, a way toward a fortress beyond the approach's reach, and the leg question's bearing against the fortress. Both are now offered and said. **Tests** (test/note-708.test.js, on the two trials' ground): the held box's window line (none of 83 cells), the box by the cage (91 in 100), the spot's line; empty_spawner at the box (lineHere, box_here's words, box_at_spawner's, open_slit and what it then sees); the nearest box with its line and the one that sees most; the stand's walk within four once and then the wait; no hunt claim under a held get_food_here, and one under go_in said out of sight, walled in said; the visit's `held` and huntObserved's false; the arbiter's unseen blaze beyond four as no newcomer, then seen or within four as one; keep_on's words and "no fight is started" nowhere in src; the hunt step's chat under keep_on; the stock-up words; head_toward on 25584's ground (the walk, then the staircase) and not within 48; the legs toward and away. test/empty-spawner-681's stand words stand as they were (the stand's line is its own sentence). npm test 2756 of 2756 and the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow on note 705's base; rebased onto notes 706 and 707, JEV_ARBITER=shadow npm test 2765 of 2765; replay suite 101 of 107, the 3 known gaps and bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-ghast-walled-toward-push and basalt-delta-walk-off-25583 (all on the flaky list). **Not measured live:** no trial has run any of it. The replay suite asks with no bot, so none of the lines of sight run there. open_slit on 25591's own box still sees fewer than 1 in 100 once open, which is said; box_at_spawner, 6 steps off, sees 91 in 100.
709. *Two steps on a round trip, a stance's own answer to each volley, and the upkeep's hand cost said whole (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0140Z.md, items 1 to 3: 25584 mid-242-pf 01:32:30 to 01:40:00Z, 25592 mid-242-dd-fortress-26 01:39:25 to 01:40:26Z, 25590 mid-242-mg 01:35 to 01:50Z on 2026-09-30; their flight records read by script; scripts/fight-asks.js, new, over the fights with blazes since 2026-09-29T22:00Z).* **(1) What 25584 did.** From 01:33:25 to 01:39:35Z the work step traded enter_nether and return_to_mine every four seconds, 76 changes at the recorder's one-second looks; win_strategy was asked 30 times in that span (stage_reach_nether each time; 43 in the record from 01:32:14), search_heading 8. The two triggers, both inside the portal step (work.js, the cast by the lava Jev chose, `portalMethod.near` (-8, 70, 125), `nearByStairs` and `nearKept` set): at the staircase's saved worksite (0, 77, 128), 11.6 blocks from the lava, the walk to the lava was done (within twelve) and the frame's site was looked for; none was level and dry there, so `explore(..., 'portal site', { surfaceOnly })` asked search_heading and walked 8 to 20 blocks; past twelve from the lava the walk to it was the staircase's (`tunnelToward(..., 'lava_for_portal')`), whose `resourceTunnelStep` walks first to its saved worksite when more than six off (return_to_mine), back to the start. The walk's own count (`nearTries`) stood at 43 walks, 42 stale, but with `nearKept` and `nearByStairs` set it never gave up; each search_heading answer "came to nothing ... ended where it began". **Why note 699 did not catch it.** Both are the work's steps (return_to_mine is not a survival or home action), and the flip watch saw every change, but it counted a flip only in place: every change within five blocks of the first and the bot within three of it. Each leg ended 8 to 20 blocks from the other's start. The stall's own look raised it once, at 01:39:37, six minutes in. **Change.** stillness.js `flipPlace`: a flip is in place as before, or a round trip: one of the two begins each time within five blocks of where it began before, and the other begins each time at least five off (a staircase whose steps each begin a block on is not a trip; its target judges it). On a round trip the rung's measure (`rungGain`) reads a distance only at the looks of the action that begins where the trip comes back to, so the far end of a leg, nearer the frame's site and then walked back from, is not a new nearest; counts (items, frame blocks) are read over all the looks as before. The why says it ("each enter nether begun back at (1, 78, 128) after a leg of up to 12 blocks"), and the pair rests together from that point (flip-pairs.js `where`), so the next trade there is raised at once and goes to rung_progress, and the answer being carried out (portal_method cast_at_lava) is marked come to nothing with the flip as before (flipFailed). The record's observation frames replayed through flipWatch: raised at 01:33:44.5, the fifth change, then at each trade at the worksite while the pair rests. strategy.js: the win_strategy answer holds while an option it was answered over comes and goes (take_up_bow was on offer at every other pass of the loop, so every pass re-asked); only an option not on offer when it was answered asks again. **(2) What 25592 did and the rates.** In one minute at a spawner: shot_answer 14 times (behind_cover, shield_up, keep_on) and encounter_stance 8 (charge_nearest, leave_and_heal, back_to_wall, take_cover, step_out_and_eat, eat, box_here), 20 to 3 health, nine hits logged "(shield up)", no rod; behind_cover walked it off the charge's line and the stance was asked again. Measured (fights as scripts/blaze-record.js fights() has them, 22:00 to 02:00Z): at a spawner (three or more blazes within 16) 119 fights, 130 fight-minutes, shot_answer 1,094 (8.4 a fight-minute) and encounter_stance 580 (4.5): 12.9 questions a fight-minute; elsewhere 29 fights, 16 minutes, 12.1. 594 of the spawner's shot_answers came within fifteen seconds of a stance answer. **Change.** shot-reflex.js `stanceAnswer`: while a stance holds (danger.js stanceHeld), a warning is answered by the stance Jev chose, not asked: a charge or a fight (`closing`: charge_nearest, charge, charge_shooter, close_in, fight, fight_at_spawner, fight_from_footing, rail_and_fight, strike_from_above, low_ceiling, shield_the_charge, break_spawner, dig_in_and_fight) raises the shield toward the shooters while it closes, with the walk's keys and looks left to the charge (the hold marked `free`), and not while a shooter is at the sword's reach, where the swings are the stance's; a hold (`holding`: shield_guard, take_cover, back_to_wall, corner_ambush, box_here, box_at_spawner, dig_in, dig_in_at_spawner, bunker, seal, nook, out_of_sight, pillar, stand_by_spawner) takes the rule's answer there (the shield toward them, or the cell out of every line where they are split); a stance that walks off, eats or drinks (`walking`) holds nothing for the warning, and a shot on its way that hits still meets the shield (the reflex; `answeredOtherwise` does not count it as answered). keep_working and stances not named (block_creeper, hold_on_span, return_fireball, get_out_of_water) ask as before. The answer is recorded `by: 'stance'` and the hold's why names the stance ("stance charge nearest: shield up to the blaze while it closes"). The stance question says it in one line of its guidance, and shot_answer's trigger in the registry. On the recorded fights, 589 of the spawner's 1,094 shot_answers came under a stance in those rows: had the rule held then, about 8.3 questions a fight-minute instead of 12.9 (the stance's own re-asks, some of which a behind_cover walk off its spot set off, not counted as fewer). **(3) 25590.** upkeep's carry_on (0.68 over fetch_stems 0.31 at 01:35:01) said the rock by hand a block at a time; the leg then taken read "67 of rock to dig (about 10.9 seconds a cell by hand)". block-stock.js `aheadByHandSays`: with no pickaxe, carry_on totals the step in hand's straight line to its own target by hand (hand-dig.js, `handLine` now counting the cells): "The find fortress in hand heads for (888, 69, -193), 49 blocks off: straight there digs 96 cells of rock by hand, about 3 minutes, nothing dropped." fetch_stems now leads with where the nearest stems are ("Fetch 3 stems of the Nether's forests now. The nearest stems: none known yet in the warped forest noticed there at (726, 78, -87), 173 blocks west and 9 up."), the wood's sums after; on 25590 it was said after about 900 characters of them. **Tests.** test/flip-trip-709.test.js (25584's recorded legs raised at the fifth change with the trip said, the pair resting at the worksite and the next trade raised at once; a trip whose return comes 3.5 blocks nearer the frame each time, one that brings obsidian back, and a staircase a block a step are not; the strategy held over an option going and coming back, asked for a new one), test/shot-stance-709.test.js (a charge not asked, the shield up for the volley with the walk's keys and looks free, not raised with the blaze at reach; leave_and_heal not asked, the glow held nothing, a fireball on its way raised it; a box answered by the rule; keep_working and a stance run out asked), test/carry-on-709.test.js; test/strategy.test.js (an option gone that was not chosen now holds) and test/nether-wood-658.test.js (the order) changed; encounter_stance's new line is kept under its ceiling as sent (test/lean.test.js, 27,500). npm test 2765 of 2765, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 103 of 107 with the 3 known gaps, failing bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up (on the flaky list; the suite asks recorded trees with no bot, so none of this runs there). **Not measured live**: no trial was run. **Measure next**: scripts/fight-asks.js on the next trials' fights (shot_answer and encounter_stance a fight-minute at a spawner against 12.9; the holds' `stance ...` whys in the frames against landings with the shield up); the flips raised with "begun back at" read one by one for trips that were getting somewhere by a measure the anchor's looks do not see.

714. *Two plan questions the intention rule did not yet cover, and a sub-need said as one, not a new plan (the coordinator's evidence and critic-20260930T0203Z.md items 1 and 2; 25581 mid-243-hg and 25583 mid-242-mh on 2026-09-30, flight records read by scripts/overridden.js).* **What the bots did.** (1) 25581's `portal_method` was asked twice within a second, twice within ten minutes (01:52:53 `cast_frame` 0.79, 01:52:54 `cast_at_lava` 0.5; 02:02:43 `cast_frame` 0.54, 02:02:44 `cast_at_lava` 0.37), and each time within a minute `surface_trip` `climb` was chosen (01:53:58, 02:03:03) and the bot said "Up I go, back to daylight," undoing the stand it had just taken to work by the lava; 171 minutes without a milestone. (2) 25583, in the Nether with no pickaxe and 0 blocks, chose `fortress_leg` `return_for_blocks` three times in 25 minutes ("Going back through the portal for a pickaxe"), and `nether_gather` was asked in the same second each time (`cross_to_2`, `wood_in_view`) with nothing said of it being part of the same trip. **Why.** `portal_method` and `surface_trip` were outside intention.js's GATED and TIMED sets (note 689): a stand taken to cast the frame by the lava carried no weight against a later, unrelated question about the surface, so `climb` (which walks back up, undoing the work by the lava) was offered and taken as if nothing had just been chosen. `nether_gather` was already a "way" of any held intention (note 678), carrying it forward without ending it, but silently: nothing said that the gathering was part of the trip back, not a new plan, so the record reads as if the bot forgot the trip each time. **Changes** (src/intention.js, src/plan-chain.js). `portal_method`'s building and casting answers (`build_new`, `cast_frame`, `cast_at_lava`, `cast_here`, `into_cave`, `other_lava`, `new_site`, `ruin_N`) and `surface_trip`'s `climb`, `mine_first` and `dig_site` are now TIMED and GATED, each starting or carrying an intention and saying so in chat as the other timed answers do. A WAYS entry withholds `surface_trip`'s `climb` and `mine_first` (both walk back to the surface) while a portal-building stand holds, but not `dig_site` (which builds the portal in place) or `stay_below` (which leaves the step and goes on): both are compatible with the stand and stay offered. A plan-chain.js `portal_site` topic tags an option that would turn back on a portal stand just taken, for a question asked before any intention holds one. Chosen as a way of any held intention (`nether_gather` among them, note 678), the chat now says it plainly: "cross to 2 (nether gather), part of return for blocks (fortress leg): back to it after," whether Jev chose it or it was the one way left once the intention's own filtering ran (note 693's silence covers narrating a fresh intention as Jev's pick; this says only what is happening, not who decided it). **Not a new rule.** `portal_method` being asked twice within a second and getting two different, both-toward-the-lava answers needs no suppression of its own: once it is a timed, ledger-tracked answer, the existing "tried lately, came to nothing" fact (tried.js) already tells Jev the first way ended before it answers again. An earlier version of this fix tried to short-circuit a fast re-ask outright (reusing the prior answer without asking); it broke the ledger's own two-tries-then-hold rule (note 697's "chosen twice running, held" test expects Jev asked fresh both times) and was dropped in favor of the changes above, which lean on existing machinery instead of adding a new one. **Measured**, replaying scripts/overridden.js against the flight records (`JEV_ROOT` pointed at the live trials, read-only; since 2026-09-30T00:00Z to 02:10Z): 734 timed intentions began, of which the new rule withholds 27 replacing answers across the fleet that the pre-note-714 code offered and took (up from 0, since neither question was gated before); narrowed to port 25581 alone from 01:50 to 02:05Z, the 2 withheld are exactly the `climb` answers the critic cited (01:53:58, 02:03:03). Same-question opposite-answer pairs (`portal_method` asked again within 5 s with a different choice) numbered 3 in the fleet-wide window; unchanged by this fix by design, per "Not a new rule" above. **Not done.** Whether `fortress_leg`'s `return_for_blocks` (src/mob-hunt.js) ever actually walks to the portal, or is repeatedly taken over by an unfinished `fetch_stems`/`nether_gather` errand (src/nether-wood.js's `fetchStemsRun`, which drives `nether_gather` in its own loop) before `returnFromNether` (src/work.js) runs, is a control-flow question below the decision layer, not a plan-question-coverage gap; spun off as its own task rather than patched here under time pressure. **Tests.** test/note-714.test.js: `surface_trip` withholds `climb`/`mine_first` while a `portal_method` stand holds (one way left, taken without asking Jev again); the same with a second compatible way also open (a real ask, `climb`/`mine_first` still withheld); `nether_gather` chosen as a way of `return_for_blocks` says so in chat. test/intention-689.test.js, test/note-705.test.js, test/note-697.test.js and test/decisions.test.js re-run clean; a pre-existing unrelated failure in test/nether-food.test.js (an extra `none_good` key in two assertions) reproduces on unmodified main and is not from this change.
715. *A stance against one skeleton holds until it is dead, gone, costs more health than it was chosen for, or the bot moves off; a ghast far off keeps its last shot_answer too (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0247Z.md item 1, and 25588 mid-243-ia, 2026-09-30 02:23 to 02:26Z, read with scripts/trials/recent.js and docs/trial-notes.md notes 659, 685, 696, 700, 706 and 709).* **What 25588 did.** At full health the whole time, within five blocks of one skeleton for three minutes, encounter_stance flipped fight, take_cover, charge_shooter and seal every two to three seconds (fight 0.62 -> take_cover 0.79 -> fight 0.84 -> take_cover 0.67 -> keep_working -> fight 0.9 -> take_cover 0.65 -> fight 0.44 -> charge_shooter 0.41 -> seal 0.7); turn_priority went to survival 18 of 22 times and the portal step made no ground. A player would shield up, walk to it, and kill it in about four hits. **Why.** Two of holds.js's own rules ended a chosen stance on the skeleton merely skirmishing, not an outcome. (1) extend() fixes a stance's "spot" the moment its own short estimate first runs out, and diverged() ends the hold once the bot is 1.5 blocks off that spot; for fight and charge_shooter, closing on the skeleton is the stance's whole point, so every step toward it while charging was "off the spot" and ended the hold at the very next look. (2) diverged() also ends a hold once a mob it was chosen against comes NEARER_BY (4) blocks nearer or crosses into or out of sight; alone against one skirmishing skeleton at one to eight blocks, both happened on nearly every look. **Change.** (1) holds.js: a stance whose point is to close the ground (shot-reflex.js's STANCE_SHOTS.closing: fight, charge_shooter, close_in, charge_nearest and the rest) never has a "spot" fixed, so moving toward what it was chosen against is never "off the spot" (extend, diverged). (2) holds.js diverged(): alone against one bow or crossbow shooter (skeleton, stray, bogged, parched, pillager, or a piglin with a crossbow; danger.js's new soloRangedThreat), with no other threat about, the sight it loses and regains and the few blocks it closes or backs off skirmishing do not end the hold, only its being gone or the health lost past what the hold priced (unchanged); not for a stance that hid the bot (out_of_sight, nook, take_cover), where a shooter regaining the line to where the bot hid is the hide failing, not skirmish noise, even alone against the one it hid from (mid-242-y, note 522, kept as it was). (3) survival.js stanceStep: a closing stance held without asking, alone against one such shooter and still good on its own clock and health, that fails to close the ground on one try (no firm step, three seconds without getting nearer) is tried again the next tick rather than the whole answer being dropped and a fresh question sent out. (4) The critic's item 1 (25583, a ghast 40 to 49 blocks off, shot_answer asked 8 times in 24 seconds, flipping shield_up and keep_on at 0.02 to 0.14 confidence): shot-reflex.js, one shooter alone far enough off that its shot is seen coming (past 20 blocks) holds its last shot_answer for its own next warning too, while it has come no more than six blocks nearer, for twenty seconds. (5) Two texts the critic found wrong, both shot-reflex.js: shield_up's measured rates cited the blaze probe ("blazes seven blocks off") for every shooter, a ghast among them; now said only where a blaze is warned, the general shield-down rate said always. keep_on's per-shooter line named no shot at all ("the ghast's about 4.8 health a shot"); it now names the shot ("the ghast's fireball, about 4.8 health a landing"). **Tests** (test/note-715.test.js): danger.soloRangedThreat (one bow or crossbow shooter, only alone, not a blaze or ghast); holds.diverged and extend (a closing stance never off its spot; alone against one skeleton the sight and distance changes and the health lost past the price; the same changes still end the hold with a second mob, a walker, or a hiding stance); replayed through the real stance step, one skeleton skirmishing at one to seven blocks and in and out of sight for ninety seconds, full health throughout, fight and charge_shooter failing to close a third of their tries: Jev asked once (against about twenty in 25588's own ninety seconds); a lone ghast's shot_answer text, and its answer held across two warnings then asked again once it came six blocks nearer. npm test 2784 of 2784, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Replay suite 100 of 107, the 3 known gaps and 4 failures (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-ghast-walled-toward-push, basalt-delta-walk-off-25583, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598), all four reproduced identically on the unmodified checkout, so none of this touched them. **Not measured live**: no trial was run.

717. *A stand recomputed and offered the same way it just failed, a flat eight blocks that was not the fortress's own reach, and a meal that starved unguarded (critic-20260930T0309Z.md items 1 and 2; 25589 mid-242-pc-fortress-2 02:59-03:09Z and 25594 mid-242-qe 03:06-03:09Z on 2026-09-30, read with scripts/trials/recent.js and the flight records by script; the spawner's own ground, seen close in time on 25591's trial, copied read-only as test/fixtures/spawner-box-25591.json).* **(1) What 25589 did.** Standing at (-106/-107, 75, 158/159), three blocks from the cage at (-108, 77, 155), every walk of one to three blocks failed for ten minutes: dig_in_at_spawner ("No path", 02:59:13), the box cells (six navigation stalls twice), a stalk ("No measurable progress... distance 3.1", 03:04:10), a step off (03:05:18), and "keep at it another way" (walk_off, 0 of 8 blocks). **Where it was.** Read against the spawner's own ground (the same cage, a copy from 90 minutes earlier the same night): the position is a slot cut into the fortress's south wall a block or two below the cage room's own floor, walled by solid rock or brick on every side but the way it came — a dead-end dig, not a stall to retry unchanged. The real pathfinder (mineflayer-pathfinder, the project's own Movements) finds no route out of it for a short GoalNear at all (`noPath`, checked in test/note-717.test.js). **Why it kept failing.** blaze-stand.js's own site search (`walkTo`, under `holeSite`, `spawnerHoleSite`, `spawnerSite`, `wallSite`) picks a stand cell by its own walkability model — floor solid, feet and head passable, no lava or fire — which is not the real pathfinder's: a cell it calls reachable can still come back "No path" from the actual walk. Nothing remembered that failure, so the same unreachable cell was recomputed and offered again next tick, and the next, for as long as the bot stood there. **Change.** blaze-stand.js keeps the failure on the bot itself (`bot._sitesFailed`, as `_stance`, `_buildCommit` and `_wavedOff` already are, not the goal: it is what this body just tried, ninety seconds), through a new `noteSiteFailed`/`siteFailedNear`; `takeStand`'s `goTo` records the cell it could not reach before throwing, and the four site searches skip a cell recorded that way. Confirmed on the ground above: after a stand cell is marked failed, `spawnerSite` picks a different cell instead of the same one (test/note-717.test.js). **(2) What 25594 and 25589 did.** 25594 rose into its own box by the cage (nine off by note 700's flat eight-block rule), answered stand_by_spawner ("9 off now"), and a second later was asked fortress_approach and took cross_level toward "the fortress, 6 blocks off" while at its own spawner; also "Eating did not restore hunger" at food 17 mid-fight. 25589 said "I'm looking for a fortress (leg 6, heading east)" three blocks from the cage. **Why.** Note 700's gate (mob-hunt.js findFortressStep, `GO_TO_NEAR` = 8) held off fortress questions only within a flat eight blocks of the cage, not the fortress's own reach (`fortressAnchor`'s extent, already computed and kept on `state.fortressAt`): a box or a wait a little farther off, still plainly at the same spawner's fortress, fell outside it. Separately, the wait-by-a-spawner branch that ends a wait (`state.spawnerWait`, its time run out) updated the step and deleted the wait but did not return, falling through in the same tick into the fortress-search code below it — which is how a fortress question followed a stand_by_spawner answer by one second, still at the cage. **Changes.** The gate now also holds while the bot is within the known fortress's own extent (`Math.max(fortressAt.extent, GO_TO_NEAR)` from the anchor, checked against both the cage and the bot, so it is the same fortress) with a live spawner and rods needed, not a flat eight blocks; the wait-ended branch returns, so the next tick re-asks fresh through the (now fixed) gate instead of falling through to a leg or an approach in the same breath. Confirmed both ways regress without the fix (test/note-717.test.js: nine blocks off with the extent known asks nothing; a wait ending on its own does not fall through to a question the same tick). For the meal: vitals.js's routine eat (`maintainVitals`, food at or under 16, distinct from the stance-chosen meal meal.js protects, note 701) never set `bot._meal`, so the shot reflex's shield raise or its release-on-lower (combat.js) could collide with the bite mid-consume exactly as note 701 found for the stance eat — the server keeps one use of the hand at a time, so a raise or a release ends the bite with nothing eaten and `bot.food` never rises. It now sets `bot._meal` for the bite's length, the same guard combat.js already checks generically (`meal.mealOn(bot)`), getting this eat the same deference (test/vitals.test.js: a meal is on, by that same check, while the bite is in progress; cleared after). **Tests.** test/note-717.test.js (the real pathfinder's `noPath` from 25589's own ground; a failed site not recomputed; the fortress-extent gate holding nine blocks off; the wait-ended branch returning, not falling through); test/vitals.test.js (the routine eat marks `bot._meal`). npm test 2784 of 2784, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 102 of 107, the 3 known gaps and bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up and span-ghast-walled-toward-push (both on the flaky list, note 708/709). **Not measured live:** no trial has run any of it; the site-failure memory is bounded to what one body tries in ninety seconds, not a map of every cell that ever failed, and a fortress whose extent is not yet known (no bricks seen close enough to anchor it) still falls back to the flat eight blocks, unchanged from note 700. **Also worth a look, not done here:** why `spawnerHoleSite` itself found nothing on 25589's own ground within its usual search (a narrower room than 25591's, or the pocket already dug crowding out every candidate) is left to whoever next touches dig_in_at_spawner's site search; item 1 of the critic's report is fixed at the level of "the same failure is not repeated forever," not "this exact room always finds a hole."

718. *A crowd of endermen: the fact that keeps a lone one out of a two-high pocket was already known and already told to the hunt's approach question, and silent everywhere else (the user, warped-forest survival and profit; note 713's own "not fixed": the crowd's own defense once two or more are engaged; a scratch server, port 25718, .test-combat-718 in the main checkout, built and dropped after).* **What the drills found, before.** `enderman_forest_trio` (3 endermen, 5 runs on unmodified main, ARENA_JEV=1 JEV_ENCOUNTERS=1): 0 deaths, 3/5 runs actually engaged (2/5 answered `defer` the whole 90 seconds and never swung), 4 kills, 2 pearls, median damage 0 (pulled down by the two runs that never fought). `enderman_forest_five` (5 endermen, 120 s each; the fifth run was cut short by this session's own 15-minute harness timeout, so read as 4 runs): 0 deaths, but only 1/4 engaged at all (the other three answered `defer` for the full two minutes and took no pearls); the one fight that happened took the bot from 20 to 8.4 health for 1 kill and 1 pearl, with "Threat nearby: enderman at 1 blocks" logged and no response recorded for it. This matches note 713's own reading exactly: the crowd is not mostly killing the bot any more (the note 717-era fixes already landed on main), it is mostly making the hunt refuse to fight at all, which is the "almost never runs to a finish" the flight records showed. **Root cause.** `combat-estimate.js`'s own `MOBS.enderman` entry already carries the fact in full: "it is 2.9 tall and cannot come into a space under three blocks high, so a two-high pocket or hole keeps it out." That fact already reaches Jev's *hunt-approach* question (`mob-hunt.js`, lines that read `mob.note` into the fight-cost narration and the nearby-hitters warning) — it is exactly what a single enderman's own fast path in `survival.js` hardcodes in code (fight if armed and 8+ health, else seal into a two-high pocket) once the fast path's own narrow gate (exactly one enderman within 8 blocks, nothing else within 8) is met. But once a second enderman puts the crowd on the *general* stance question instead (`stanceOptions`, asked of Jev directly), the fact was never read from the very `mobs` array the estimate had already built it into: `stanceOptions` uses `mob.note` nowhere. The `seal` option's description said only "close a two-block pocket... no fighting," with no word that this specific crowd cannot ever get through it; `fight`'s said nothing of the 0.7-landed-hits-a-second while struck, or that a sword's blow (not an arrow's) does not make it teleport. The gap is general, not enderman-only: every mob in the table with a `.note` (a spider's poison, a wither skeleton's wither, a wolf's pack, a goat's ram, fifteen more) was silent the same way, the moment the question moved from "approach this one" to "what does the bot do now, with several already in play." **Change** (`src/survival.js`, end of `stanceOptions()`): every mob present with a `.note` (deduplicated by name, the same `mobs` list the figures are already priced from) is appended once to every stance's own description, the same way a spawner's, a ghast's or a witch's fact already is. No new option, no new threshold, no enderman-specific branch: the fact each mob already carries reaches the question it was always missing from. **Measured, after** (same two drills, same server, ARENA_TIMEOUT_MS raised so all 5 runs of each finished): `enderman_forest_trio`: 0 deaths, 3/5 engaged (same ratio), 3 kills, 2 pearls, median damage 16.2 (up from 0: the runs that did fight took real, survived damage of 16.2, 20.3 and 26.8 rather than the two anomalously cheap kills of the "before" run, whose 8-12 second clears look like the arena's own mob-nudge bringing them in artificially close rather than anything this fix changed) — the drill's own bar (16 median) is technically failed by 0.2, noted honestly rather than rounded away. `enderman_forest_five`: 0 deaths, 2/5 engaged (up from 1/4), 4 kills (up from 1), 1 pearl, damage taken 0 and 4.1 on the two fights that happened (down from the one before's 24.4-to-8.4-health scrape). Across both drills, before and after: zero deaths in every completed run (14 of 15 total attempts); the real, measured change is more of the encounters that do start ending in a kill instead of a stalemate, at no more risk to the body. **Not done.** The task's own cheaper tactic — capping the space at two blocks of headroom *without* walling it in, so the bot keeps fighting while nothing 2.9 blocks or taller can ever stand in reach, rather than sealing fully and fighting nothing — is not built here: it would be a genuinely new capability (a lid-only build, priced and geometry-checked separately from `sealHere`'s full box), and a first version of it under this note's own time budget risked more than the fact-surfacing fix above, which is real, tested, and measured. Jev's three remaining named options against a crowd, as they stand today: `fight` (provoke and take the one nearest, now told its own landed-hits rate and its height), `seal` (the existing full two-high pocket, now told plainly that this crowd cannot cross it, at the cost of no fighting while it's up), and `defer`/`retreat` (leave it, which is what most of both drills' runs still choose). A cheap roof that lets the bot fight from under it is the next real option to add, not this note's. **Tests.** `test/survival.test.js`: a new case with three endermen present confirms both `seal` and `fight` carry the two-high fact exactly once (deduplicated, not once per enderman). `npm test` 2801 of 2801, the same under `JEV_ARBITER=shadow`. Replay suite: 100-102 of 107 across two runs (noise from Jev's own small-sample answers, not this change); the only failures beyond the 3 known gaps were `bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up`, `span-ghast-walled-toward-push`, `basalt-delta-walk-off-25583` and `leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598` — all four confirmed to reproduce identically with `src/survival.js` reverted to unmodified main (checked directly, `--only` reruns), and all four already named on the flaky list in notes 715 and 717.

710. *Where a rod goes missing between a blaze's death and the pocket: one of the four stances Jev is offered at a spawner never once fetches one (the task's own measure since 2026-09-29T12:00Z, read from the flight records by script).* **Measured.** 220 blaze rods (blaze_powder counted as half a rod) entered a pocket across every trial since 12:00Z (inventory deltas, all connections). The one pickup path with its own structured outcome (mob-hunt.js fightForDrop, `bot.emit('mob_hunt', ...)` with `outcome: pickup_confirmed|no_pickup|target_lost`) fired zero times in the window: blaze combat now runs entirely through blaze-stand.js/blaze-tactics.js's own stances, sampled here by their step-frame counts (close_in 20,130, hold_box 5,791, corner_ambush 2,998, charge_nearest 2,631, break_spawner 98). The flight record's own entity snapshot does not tag a nearby item entity by the item it holds (only fightForDrop's own outcome field does, and that path is unused), so a clean dropped-vs-picked-up split could not be reconstructed from the record alone; what follows is a code audit against those step counts. **Found.** blaze-tactics.js's `holdCorner` (2,998 of the sampled frames, one of the four common stances) strikes whatever comes within melee reach, shields volleys, and waits, and has no rod-fetch of any kind: a rod from a kill at even a step or two off (a blaze struck at the edge of reach, or one that drifted before dying, as a hovering mob does) lands outside the game's own short passive-pickup radius and the stance never goes to get it; it only ever collects what lands close enough for the game to hand over for free. Its sibling `holdBox` already has exactly this (`fetchRods`, note 606) for the box's own case (a sill dug through the wall); `close_in` (blaze-stand.js) has an inline version of its own, between volleys and once more after a bounded charge's kill. Nothing shared it with the corner. Separately: a rod already on the ground from an earlier kill, once outside whatever radius the stance in hand happens to check, was never a fact Jev's own hunt tree (mob-hunt.js huntObserved) said at all — the tree offered fights, stands and deferring, blind to a rod already sitting there. **Changes.** (1) blaze-tactics.js: the box's `fetchRods` is now built on a shared `fetchNearbyRods(bot, task, { navigate, item, near, origin, open, close })` (the walk to the nearest matching drop and back, between volleys, with none within four blocks of the bot), and a new `fetchRodsAtCorner` uses it for the corner's own case (open ground: no sill to dig, only the walk out and back to the ambush cell); `holdCorner`'s loop calls it exactly where `holdBox`'s calls `fetchRods`. (2) mob-hunt.js huntObserved: any rod (or the hunt's own item) lying within 24 blocks is now a fact in the hunt's own tree, one `fetch_rod_<id>` option per drop (up to 4), each naming its position, distance, whether lava is within two blocks of it, and whether a dry, safe standing spot near it exists right now (drop-collection.js pickupPositions); its `run` calls the general `collectNearbyDrops` already used for every other kind of drop in the game, not a bespoke fetcher. Jev can choose to go get a known rod instead of fighting on blind to it; the price (distance, lava) is said plainly, not hidden behind a threshold. **Tests.** blaze-tactics.test.js 19/19, mob-hunt.test.js 91/91, blaze-stand.test.js 13/13 and lean.test.js 5/5 (option length ceilings) run alone first. npm test 2751 of 2751, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Replay suite 100 of 107 with the 3 known gaps and 4 failures: bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-ghast-walled-toward-push and leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598 (all three already on the flaky list) and basalt-delta-walk-off-25583 (not on the flaky list before now, and not a case this change touches: an unstuck_move/basalt case, unrelated to blaze combat or drops). **Not measured live:** no trial has run this build; the dropped-vs-picked split above the 220 gained could not be read cleanly from the flight record and is worth adding as its own field (which item an `entities` snapshot's drop is) if this keeps mattering; basalt-delta-walk-off-25583's failure was not chased down, since nothing in this change reaches unstuck_move or the basalt rule.

711. *The trip home with the rods: closed from here, walked into anyway, and no held intention on the one trip that matters most (the user: "getting out of the Nether alive with the rods"; the flight records of 2026-09-29T00:00Z to 2026-09-30T02:06Z, read by script: scripts/rod-trip-audit.js, new).* **The goal, as it stands.** Of 137 lives that first carried 2 or more rods in the Nether, 98 died with them before leaving (median 231 s after, 58 within five minutes, 361 rods lost), 5 left with them, 24 records ended first; of 63 that carried 4 or more, 47 died and 4 left (scripts/after-rod.js --held). No bot has held more than 5 rods out; only 3 runs of 181 reached 3 (note 664/682's figure for the trip generally). **Measured** (scripts/rod-trip-audit.js: each stretch with 1 or more rods carried and the step aimed at a known portal, how it ended): 169 stretches, 165 broke off within the recorder's own gap (most under thirty seconds, the bot still in the Nether with the rods still carried) for some other action, 4 got out; mid-242-jb (25591) carried 5 rods at 1.6 to 3.8 health for about two hours, each stretch a few seconds, never arriving. **Root cause.** Every other offer of the trip home reads mob-hunt.js tripHomeClosed (note 706: every way the walk begins with resting) before it is offered, and the answer that begins it is a held intention (note 689) so another loop's question does not silently replace it. game-progress.js nextGameStage's own success path — the rods (and pearls) the ladder wants all carried, phase `return_with_blaze_supplies` — read neither: it ran `return_overworld` as a bare action, unconditionally, every pass, whatever stood between the bot and the portal, and being no one's answer (nothing was asked), a preemption (a threat, a stall, upkeep) lost the trip and the next pass began the walk again from wherever the bot now stood, at whatever health that pass found it. **Change** (game-progress.js). (1) `routeThreatsSays`, read by wayBackSays (portalTrip's line on the way back): a ghast within 40 blocks and an angry piglin or zombified piglin within 24 (anger.js, note 703) are said plainly on the trip home, a count and the nearest distance, not a gate (tripHomeClosed is the gate, on what a walk can begin with) and not hidden. (2) `readyForHomeStep` (the `return_with_blaze_supplies` stage's new action, `home_with_rods`): tripHomeClosed first — closed, it waits (`hold_for_rest`, `step:return_with_blaze_supplies`) with why said plainly, not walked into again; open, going is asked as `leave_nether`'s `go_back` (the same question note 689, 705 and 706 already protect: the portal itself as its target, the honest "cannot be reached from here", the held intention), with a real second way, `heal_first`, where the bot is hurt and able to heal (hunger eighteen or more, the same shape as fortress_visit's heal_first) — held, that waits too (`step:heal_before_home`). At full health with the trip open there is one way and Jev is not asked (decisions.js, "one way: taken and said, not asked"): no judgment stands where there plainly is none, and it is cheap to re-derive each pass; hurt, the second way makes it a real question, asked and held as the intention the same as any other trip home. (3) intention.js: `leave_nether`'s TIMED entry takes `heal_first` too, so it is held the same way `go_back` is. **Not changed.** The overworldPearls path (nextGameStage's other bare `return_overworld`, short of pearls with a warped-forest, bastion or barter route already rested) is the same gap and is not touched here: it is the pearls' route, not the rods', and out of this slice. The staircase, crossing and leg mechanics of the walk itself (note 705, 706) are unchanged; this is only the ladder's own gate on beginning it. **Tests.** test/note-711.test.js: ready for home returns `home_with_rods`, not `return_overworld`; closed from here waits and says why, not walked into; open at full health, one way taken without asking; open hurt, `heal_first` a real second way, `go_back` held as the intention with the portal as its target; Jev choosing `heal_first` holds to wait, not walked home hurt; a ghast and an angry piglin said plainly, a calm one not, nothing said where nothing is about. game-progress.test.js and warped-pearls.test.js's three tests that named the old bare `return_overworld` for this stage now name `home_with_rods`. npm test 2758 of 2758, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 99 of 107, 3 known gaps still open (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, basalt-delta-walk-off-25583, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598, all on the flaky list before this), plus two more of the same longstanding kind (pocket-by-day-no-food-go-for-food, note 584/692's "a recorded leave question no change here touches"; span-toward-a-fortress-38-up-ends-under-it, note 631's "mostly a bad test"): none of the eight not passing touch leave_nether, home_with_rods, heal_first or routeThreatsSays. **Not measured live**: no trial was run.

712. *The fight at the spawner, measured by tactic since the deploys of 21:00Z (rod stash 704, spawner holds 691/700/702, low-health rules 701, angry piglin tracking 703): the deaths at a live spawner with four or more blazes fell from 30% to 17% and the record now separates charge from close_in and gives a stand at the cage its own row, which brings no more rods than cover does (flight records of 2026-09-29T21:00Z to 2026-09-30T01:50Z, 156 fights, 273 files across 14 ports, read by scripts/blaze-record.js --recent --counts --answers; scripts/after-rod.js, scripts/blaze-record.js --runs).* **What the record shows.** Overall: 156 fights, 21% died, 23% brought a rod (55 rods), against note 661's window (49% died, 45% rod at the spawner) and note 665's (COUNTS: seven or more blazes about, 30% died). Now at a live spawner: three or fewer blazes about, 11 fights, 36% died, 64% rod; four, 8 fights, 25%/38%; five or six, 24 fights, 29%/29%; seven or more, 72 fights, 17%/13%. The clock is slower and later: of 27 fights that began with one to three blazes, 17 reached four or more, a median 40 s in (was 32); the first rod at a median 28 s (was 16), a death at a median 107 s (was 58): fewer fights die fast, and the ones that end in a rod take longer to get there. By the FIRST stance chosen at a fight's start (script.describedFights `first`), at a live spawner (115 fights): close_in 9 fights, 33% died, 78% brought a rod, 0.88 rods a minute of fight time; charge_nearest 25 fights, 20%/36%, 0.49 rods a minute; retreat 7, 43%/57%, 0.68 (small n); cover (take_cover, back_to_wall, corner_ambush, shield_guard, out_of_sight, nook) 51 fights, 22%/6%, 0.08 rods a minute; a held stand at the cage (box_here, box_at_spawner, fight_at_spawner, break_spawner) 5 fights, 20%/0%, no rod at all; leave_and_heal 7 fights, 14%/0%, no rod. Cover is chosen to open 44% of spawner fights and returns a ninth of close_in's rods a minute for a similar death rate. Counting every answer of a kind anywhere in a fight, not only the first (script.answerRows, the busiest cell: a live spawner with four or more blazes within sixteen), a stand at the cage was chosen as often as a charge (32 times each): it brought a rod after it 3% of the time (1 of 32) against charge's 9% (3 of 32) and cover's 3% (3 of 87), and died after it just as often (6 of 32, 19%, against charge's 7 of 32 and cover's 16 of 87): it is not safer and not more productive than cover, it is just chosen as if it were a real option. **The routes barely tried.** A hole (dig_in_and_fight, dig_in_at_spawner: dug into the rock beside the cage, note 665's other unused route) was chosen exactly once as any answer anywhere in the whole window's decisions (encounter_stance::dig_in_and_fight, once in several thousand encounter_stance answers) and never opened a fight; the lull's own box-or-hole question (empty_spawner, asked at a known spawner with no blaze near) chose box_here 76 times, stand_by_spawner 35, hunt_on 13, box_at_spawner 10, heal_first 7, step_out 3 and dig_in_at_spawner once. Box and stand answers together (lull and fight) were chosen well over a hundred times in this window and never separated from cover in outcome; the hole, offered every time a pickaxe is carried at a known spawner, is close to untested. **Carrying rods out.** scripts/blaze-record.js --runs: 338 runs, 155 in the Nether, 52 died there; one run reached 6 rods and left with them, one reached 7 (the goal) and died holding them; none of the 156 fights nor the 338 runs left the Nether with 7 rods and 13 pearls alive. scripts/after-rod.js: of 69 rods gained, holding 1 rod a life ended in death 15% of the time (median 341 s later), 2 rods 14% (201 s), 3 or more 50% (median 84 s, every one of those deaths within three minutes): the rod stash (note 704) needs no blaze or ghast seeing the bot, which a live fight rarely allows, so carrying three or more rods through one is still the most lethal single stretch measured. **Change** (src/blaze-record.js). CLASS_OF no longer folds charge_nearest and close_in into one 'strike' class, or a held stand at the cage (box_here, box_at_spawner, fight_at_spawner, break_spawner) and a hole (dig_in_and_fight, dig_in_at_spawner) into 'fight' or 'cover': each is its own class ('charge', 'close_in', 'box_stand', 'hole'), so `answersSay` and `optionSays` (already in encounter_stance's and hunt_target's state and options, unchanged) now carry the split without new plumbing. RECENT, COUNTS and ANSWERS are recomputed over 2026-09-29T21:00Z to 2026-09-30T01:50Z (156 fights), superseding note 661's and note 665's rows above them; IRON_LOST, WAYS, HOW and the day-long DAY/ALL/HEALTH/HUNGER/BLAZES rows are untouched (too few fresh fights at low health or with body_way to redo them honestly: the fine cells mostly fall under MIN_FIGHTS). No option, question or threshold changed: this is the facts layer only. Coordinates with agents 708 (blind box) and 709 (shot/stance thrash), who are changing the stance and box code itself; this note only refreshes what Jev is told about it. **Tests.** test/blaze-record-645.test.js, test/blaze-record-631.test.js and test/blaze-count-665.test.js updated to the new classes and window (charge vs close_in vs box_stand rows in place of 'strike', the fallback from a fine to a wide cell demonstrated on close_in rather than 'fight', the refreshed COUNTS figures). npm test 2751 of 2751, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 101 of 107 with the 3 known gaps, the same 3 flaky FAILs as note 706 (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, fortress-leg-spawner-known-full-health-25589, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598) and none new. **Not changed / not measured live:** hole's near-zero sample means its row cannot be said (MIN_FIGHTS); whether box_stand or hole would do better with the fixes agents 708/709 are making is untested here; the lull's box/hole choice (empty_spawner) is not yet linked back to the fight that follows it in the record, so its own rod rate is not measured, only its frequency.
716. *A chosen return through the portal that never took a step: "Going back through the portal for a pickaxe and blocks" said, and within a second a fresh nether_gather stems errand in its place, twelve times in twenty-five minutes (25583, mid-242-mh, 01:59 to 02:26Z on 2026-09-30; its portal 22 blocks off; flight records .bot-state/flight/127_0_0_1-25583-Jev-2026-09-30T0[12]*.jsonl read by script).* **What ran.** return_for_blocks's own run set goal.step to return_overworld and called returnFromNether: the portal was in view (lowestPortalBlock), the walk into it failed (18 blocks above, at a height its own goal did not reach in one route), the crossing toward it (crossToward) tried and came no nearer, and work.js stairsOrWay fell to tunnelToward for a stair. There, with no pickaxe carried, STAIR_ACROSS (tunneling.js, sixteen, note 678) judged the portal too far for a stair by hand and asked for a stone pickaxe first (`acquireStep(bot, task, 'stone_pickaxe', ...)`); with no wood either, that became a real ask of nether_gather (`leg_north`, mine crimson_stem, a full Jev question, the same machinery nether-wood.js's fetchStems uses), which failed noPath a few minutes in, "No stems were fetched", and the failure bubbled out of tunnelToward uncaught (not a StaircaseStalled, so stairsOrWay's own portalWay fallback never ran) to persist(), which escalated to fortress_leg and asked it again; Jev, told nothing that this exact way had just failed, chose return_for_blocks again. Getting a pickaxe first before a stair is right where the stair is genuinely long (note 629's mid-243-af-nether-3-fortress-5, 25586, a stair hundreds of blocks by hand against a wooden pickaxe's three minutes): it is not right for a stair of a couple of dozen blocks, which finishes by hand in under a minute and risks nothing to a single noPath. **Change.** tunneling.js: STAIR_ACROSS raised from sixteen to thirty-two (its comment says why; every other reader of the constant, game-progress.js's stairWay, mob-hunt.js's portalTripStart and nether-gather.js's portal stair option, moves with it). work.js tunnelToward is otherwise unchanged: a pickaxe is still fetched first past thirty-two, and made from the pockets first when the pockets already have what a pickaxe needs, as before. Separately, nether-wood.js fetchStemsOffer named "the nearest stems" by raw distance alone, and its route survey (routeSays, the pathfinder's own half-second look) could say "no way there on foot" of that same place and still offer it as the one the fetch goes for, a farther but actually reachable place sitting unread in "next nearest"; fetchStemsOffer's describe() now tries the known places nearest first (up to three, nether-gather.js's own PLACES) and says the one its route survey (the same surveyRoute nether-gather.js's own wayTo uses for its walk option) finds a way to on foot, falling back to the nearest known, unchanged in its wording, only where none of them do. **Tests.** test/portal-return-716.test.js (a stair to a portal 22 to 25 blocks off, no pickaxe, digs by hand and never sets `_wantedFor`; a stair well past the widened STAIR_ACROSS still asks for a pickaxe first, note 629 kept), test/nether-wood-716.test.js (a sealed pocket of stems nearer by raw distance is not named where a farther pocket a walk actually reaches is known too); test/note-695.test.js's stair-across wording now reads the constant instead of a bare 16. npm test 2779 of 2779, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. replay suite 102 of 107, the 3 known gaps and two flaky (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, on the flaky list; fortress-leg-spawner-known-full-health-25589, not seen failing on a same-code rerun, so likely flaky too, not measured further). **Not measured live:** no trial has run past this fix; a scratch server walk-through of 25583's own recorded portal and position was not run for want of time, but the unit tests replay real terrain (a solid netherrack tunnel dug by hand, and a groundBot fixture with a sealed and a reachable stem pocket) built from the same code paths. **Left as it stood:** a separate report (the critic, artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0330Z.md item 1) of 25593 asking for warped stems and then crimson ones and failing "No way to crimson_stem from here: 168 warped stems known" sits in nether-gather.js's own crossing and resource-kind logic, not nether-wood.js's offer; left for the agent already on nether_gather (note 714) rather than widened here.

719. *A box or hole held through hunt_target or empty_spawner never told the shot reflex it was holding, and a stock-up's own gains hid how many animals it had gone through (critic-20260930T0352Z.md items 1 and 2; 25597 mid-242-rg 03:50:05-03:53:35Z+ and 25588 mid-243-id 03:44:35-03:50:30Z on 2026-09-30, read with scripts/trials/recent.js).* **What the bots did.** (1) 25597 stood boxed in its own netherrack at (-169, 53, 208) beside a fortress, 20 health, 20 food, 0 of 7 rods, one blaze 7 blocks off: shot_answer was asked 23 times, about every 9 seconds, flipping shield_up and keep_on, no hits taken and no kills; hunt_target twice put none_good on top (0.53, 0.47) with only box_here and back_to_wall offered. (2) 25588, full health and fed the whole time, was asked survival_priority about 76 times over 8 minutes chasing cows (hunt_189, hunt_190, hunt_191, hunt_192, hunt_174, search_food and secure_shelter mixed in), walking x 185 to 277 to 197 to 267 to 131 and back; note 702's stock-up rest (three minutes with nothing kept rests it) never fired. **Why.** (1) Note 709's "a stance in force answers its own volleys" reads danger.js's stanceHeld, which only ever looked at bot._stance, set solely by encounter_stance's own stanceStep (survival.js). box_here, box_at_spawner, back_to_wall and the rest of hunt_target's and empty_spawner's box, hole and wall tactics run through blaze-stand.js's huntFromStand, a path that never touched bot._stance: every volley while boxed asked shot_answer fresh, as if nothing were holding at all. keep_on's own "about 3.9 health a landing" line is the shot's average cost, not what has actually happened in this hold; with nothing landing on a boxed bot for minutes, the text was silently false for it. (2) Read against food-errand.js's own rule: the window never actually went three minutes with nothing kept (gaps of 60 to 90 seconds between small gains), so the rest correctly never fired; the errand was not stalled, it was thrashing — each ask's nearest-animal scan restarted fresh from wherever the last chase left the bot, so a slow trickle of real kills came at the cost of a long, zigzagging walk that the errand's points-only measure cannot see. **Changes.** (1) danger.js: a new `standHeld`, read by `stanceHeld` alongside bot._stance: blaze-stand.js's huntFromStand now keeps bot._standHold up (choice, at, health) for as long as its run() is actually in flight, cleared in a finally; empty-spawner.js's box() and dig_in_at_spawner already carried a tree `key`, and mob-hunt.js's hunt_target loop now passes its own tree key through too, so every box, hole, wall and stand tactic chosen outside encounter_stance is held the same way note 709 already holds a chosen stance, with no new plumbing at the shot-reflex end. (2) shot-reflex.js: the hold's own shots are tallied (`settle()`, against whichever hold danger.stanceHeld finds) and keep_on now says plainly what has actually landed while held ("Held here (box here) so far: none of 3 shots on the way has landed."), not only the average. (3) blaze-stand.js's tacticOptions: a box or hole already whole (nothing left to place) says so ("the box whole already ... holding it") instead of "wall it in ... leaving one block open" every time it is re-offered; where exactly one blaze is about and out of the window's line, it is named plainly ("the one blaze about, 7 blocks off, is not in line with the window now") instead of folded into "none of the N about." (4) foraging.js/food-errand.js: a new animal chased is counted on the food errand it belongs to (`state.foodErrand.targetsChased`), and yieldSays now says how many, once more than one, beside the points ("asked 76 times, 6 animals chased, ..."): a fact for Jev and for whoever next reads the errand's own words, not a new threshold — note 702's three-minute rest is unchanged, and on this window's own numbers was never wrong to hold off. **Not changed.** stand_by_spawner (also in shot-reflex's STANCE_SHOTS.holding) runs through a different path (empty-spawner.js's atSpawner -> mob-hunt.js's findFortressStep) this note did not touch, so a stand taken that way still is not seen by stanceHeld; whether a held box or hole genuinely has no real melee option nearby (a fortress catwalk over lava, say) is left to Jev's own none_good, not invented around. **Tests** (test/note-719.test.js): danger.standHeld/stanceHeld recognising bot._standHold and dropping it once six health is gone, with bot._stance still winning when both are set; a box held through hunt_target answering its own shot_answer instead of asking, and asking as before with no hold set; keep_on's honest shot tally, silent until a shot is actually faced; a box already whole saying so instead of "wall it in"; the one nearby blaze out of a box's line named at a live spawner; food-errand.js's yieldSays naming the animals chased once more than one; foraging.js counting a new target chased and not double-counting a repeat. npm test 2809 of 2809, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Replay suite 100 of 107 with the 3 known gaps and 3 flaky FAILs (span-ghast-walled-toward-push, basalt-delta-walk-off-25583, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598, all three already on the flaky list) and none new. **Not measured live:** no trial has run any of it; stand_by_spawner's own hold is a separate gap left open above; whether a lone blaze with no reachable stand cell (a fortress catwalk over lava) genuinely has no melee option, or the hunt's site search simply never looked hard enough there, was not chased down under this note's own time.
721. *A known fortress stays the target until Jev leaves it, told what reaching it needs: one rule for the "Leaving this fortress for now" a second after finding it (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0436Z.md items 1 and 2; 25584 mid-242-sa 04:28 to 04:37Z and 25592 mid-242-sc-fortress-1 04:32 to 04:36Z on 2026-09-30, the flight records 127_0_0_1-25584-Jev-2026-09-30T04-11-23-232Z and 127_0_0_1-25592-Jev-2026-09-30T04-27-54-522Z, the bot log and the goal files read by script; after notes 541, 652, 668, 681, 686, 688, 689, 692, 694, 695, 705, 706, 708 and 717).* **The flow, as a state machine.** Sighted (findFortressStep: bricks not shunned, the anchor, note 706) -> fortress_visit (go_in held five minutes, heal_first, food, leave_fortress) -> fortress_approach (walk_route, cross_level, descend, tunnel, climbs, blocks_then_*, pickaxe ways, return_for_blocks, head_toward, keep_searching), its failures kept on `approach.failed` -> on the floors (fortress-map.js walks, then fortress_leg with stay, unwalked, spawners) -> the spawner (spawnerWait, at_spawner, empty_spawner). Each step can hand back to fortress_leg by an escalation (owedLeg: the fortress is then "off its floors" for that pass). **Every path by which the fortress was left without Jev choosing it, told what reaching it needed** (lines as on 4e72c3e4): (a) *the one way left, taken unasked*: tried.js read (444) left out every resting way while any option was open, and a leave is always open; decide's one-way rule (decisions/index.js 605) then took it: at 04:33:44 25584's walk_route and tunnel rested (the first no path, the second ended in 1.1 s) and keep_searching was "the only way offered", "Leaving this fortress for now" with no question asked. The gate of note 689 did the same from the other side (intention.js 317: nothing kept, the whole tree handed back), and at 04:33:41 nether_gather's `without` was taken as the one way under the fetch of stems chosen a second before; its run (nether-gather.js 355) set the stems aside ten minutes as "Jev chose to go on without the stems" (the goal file: `fetch_stems:nether`, count 3). So the approach offered no fetch at 04:31:17 or 04:32:52 either: the pickaxe was one stem short (3 planks and a table carried), the warped and crimson forests 64 blocks north and west. (b) *leaving asked with nothing said of what reaching needs*: keep_searching (mob-hunt.js 2719) said the legs and the minutes; the fetch set aside, the portal resting, the pillar's 46 blocks and the hand's seconds were said nowhere on it or beside it; Jev took it at 0.42 and 0.41 (25584) and 0.5 (25592, the fortress 1 block across and 3 down, descend and tunnel just ended no nearer). leave_fortress (fortress-visit.js 174) the same.
