(c) *a leg chosen with the fortress in view, never recorded as leaving*: an escalation owed to fortress_leg made the pass "off its floors" (mob-hunt.js 3435), the leg question was asked with the fortress 1 block off and back_to_fortress not offered, a leg was taken (3577) and nothing set the fortress aside, so the next pass found the same bricks and asked the visit again: 25584 at 04:34:05 to 04:34:43, "Leaving the fortress for now, searching on (leg 4, heading west)" and (leg 5, heading south) five seconds apart. (d) *a sub-need cut*: the fetch chosen under the fortress work ended by (a), and the fortress's visit was asked in its place (go_in 0.99 at 04:33:42); where the fetch is cut by a preemption instead, the visit asked while it holds sets it down (intention.js 312). (e) *heal_first at full health* (fortress-visit.js 118: offered where hunger was under 18 with food carried): 25592 took it at 0.95 at health 20 and said "Healing before going into the fortress: health 20". (f) *a stall set aside sixteen blocks of it* where no approach was under way yet (work.js 190: a wait to heal, a walk to its blazes), with no why, not said to Jev. The plan chain's escalation (note 705) that ended go_in at 04:33:43 and the at-once rest of the tunnel (note 695) are not leaves: they end what holds and hand the choice back, which (a) then took unasked. **The rule** (src/fortress-hold.js, new, one place): (1) leaving is Jev's, asked: a leave (keep_searching, leave_fortress, without, other_way) is not a way on for the ledger, so beside a lone open leave the resting ways stay on offer with their rests said (tried.js read `leave`, `keptBesideLeave`); a lone leave, or a lone resting way kept only beside one, is never taken unasked: where the question is the way of an intention holding (nether_gather under the fetch) that intention fails with why ("No way on for fetch stems from here: ..."), else the question above is asked with it said (escalate; fortress_approach -> fortress_leg) (decide's takeOne, `loneWhy`); (2) leaving says what it leaves, in the question's facts as `leaving` (reachSays): the fortress's place and distance, what reaching it needs (the pickaxe and what it is short of, what one changes, the hand's seconds on the straight line, the climb's blocks, whether a route on foot was found), each way to that as it stands (the fetch offered, or set aside with how long and why; the trip home offered or why not; the ways in offered), and that searching on takes the same pockets to the next one; on the approach, the visit and the leg question asked with the fortress in view; (3) one set-aside (`leave`): by the fortress's anchor and reach, from where, over which ways, with a chat that says where ("Leaving the fortress at (-140, 43, 153) for now, 21 blocks off. Searching on for another."), taken by keep_searching, leave_fortress and a leg chosen with the fortress in view; (4) a way failing is a fact on the next asking (the approach's `failed`) and a stall is a failure on the fortress's approach (work.js looseEnds, begun where none was under way), never a set-aside; (5) a fetch of stems still holding when the search's step comes round is carried on (`errandHolding`, findFortressStep), not set down by the fortress's questions; one chosen under go_in runs as its way and the approach is asked again after (unchanged, now shown end to end); (6) heal_first only below full health. **Removed**: the two copies of the set-aside (keep_searching's run and the visit's leave callback), the unexplained sixteen-block shun of looseEnds, heal_first's "health is full, heals nothing now" branch (note 643's words, now never offered), mob-hunt.js's own LEFT_FROM_MS. **Probes** (live Jev, the recorded fortress_approach questions with the recorded state, 5 runs each, scratch script): with `leaving` in the facts, 25584 04:31:17 keep_searching 5 of 5 as the fetch then stood (set aside, said; recorded 0.42), and fetch_stems 5 of 5 with the fetch on offer as it would have been had `without` not been taken unasked; 04:32:52 return_for_blocks 5 of 5 as it stood (recorded keep_searching 0.41), fetch_stems 5 of 5 with the fetch on offer; 25592 04:32:33 keep_searching 5 of 5 (0.57; its ways in had just ended and nothing else of this fortress was offered: see Left). Said on keep_searching itself instead, the same text read as the option's case: keep_searching 24 of 25 over the same five questions (fetch_stems 1 of the 10 where it was on offer), so it is in the facts. **Tests** (test/note-721.test.js on the frames, test/fixtures/leaving-721.json: each question's options as asked, the body and the answer): 25584's gathering under the fetch with only `without` left fails the fetch and asks nothing, the stems not set aside, and asked again `without` is Jev's; its approach with walk and staircase resting is asked with both kept and their rests said, and a lone keep_searching is sent to fortress_leg, not taken; `leaving` at 04:31:17 names the fortress, the stem short, the fetch set aside and why, the climb's 46 blocks; 25592's visit at health 20 has no heal_first and its facts carry `leaving`; a synthetic walk-through of the whole flow on a corridor fortress across lava from a ledge with a spawner (sighted, visit go_in, walk_route failing and said on the next asking with keep_searching not on offer under go_in, fetch_stems chosen under it running to a wooden pickaxe with go_in still holding, cross_level with it, the floors walked, fortress_leg, wait_at_spawner at the cage) with nothing shunned and no "Leaving" said; the leg question with the fortress 1 block off carries `leaving` and a leg taken sets it aside once, said; looseEnds with no approach keeps the fortress. test/fortress-visit-638.test.js takes the full-health rule; test/mob-hunt.test.js's leave by the anchor's reach (62, all of the 61 in view). npm test 2820 of 2820. **Not measured live**: no trial has run any of it. **Left**: 25592's fortress 1 block across and 3 down had its busiest blaze place 27 blocks off and nine blazes heard; the approach offers no other place of the same fortress (its blazes, its spawner, its other floors are fortress_leg's), so leaving was the one alternative to the two ways that had just failed; the approach's target there (the nearest brick) is likely a wall or footing brick. `without` and leave_fortress taken as Jev's least bad (none good) still leave; a lone leave is never asked alone, so that only happens beside other ways Jev weighed.
720. *A hole no pickaxe closed off, a fortress's own extent never learned before the gate needed it, a food way that held nothing, and a charge priced the same at one blaze or fourteen (critic-20260930T0414Z.md, items 1 to 4; 25594 mid-242-sc 04:00-04:15Z and 25592 mid-243-ia-fortress-1 04:12-04:15Z on 2026-09-30, read with scripts/trials/recent.js and the flight records by script).* **(1)** 25594 sat eighteen minutes at a live cage, full health and fed, 0 blazes killed: stand_by_spawner said "no covered cell found near it" and the only box offered (box_in_line) was 13.2 blocks off, seeing about 7 in 100 of the spawner's blazes. dig_in_at_spawner, which could have made a covered cell of its own within four blocks, was withheld the whole time because no pickaxe was carried — a hidden threshold, not a game fact: netherrack, basalt, blackstone and nether bricks all break by hand (hand-dig.js, note 705), only slower and dropping nothing, and spawnerHoleSite's own digMs already prices whichever tool is at hand. **(2)** fortress_approach fired at the cage nine blocks off and again four minutes later from a box 13.2 blocks off, though note 717's gate holds fortress questions within the known fortress's own extent: the extent was never known. findFortressStep's own bricks search, which sets state.fortressAt, only runs past the atCage early return; a trial that reaches a live cage before that search ever ran once — every earlier tick already quieted by the flat eight-block rule note 717 meant to replace — never learns the fortress's extent at all, so the gate falls back to the flat rule for the whole run. **(3)** 25592, sealed at 1.2 health with no food and a blaze at the wall, chose go_for_food's own ways (return_for_food, then hoglin_food) five times in two seconds; none of them ran, then leave and stay. survival.js's "held" check for a chosen pocket_next answer read only `options[plan.choice]`, but a way chosen under go_for_food lives in `foodWays`, never `options`, so the check always came up empty for one and a fresh decide() was asked every tick instead of the ninety seconds any other answer holds for — never giving the chosen way's own leave and walk the time to run before the next tick asked afresh. **Checked, not changed:** note 706's last-hit fact (last-hit.js) is added by decide() itself to every gameplay-area question once the body qualifies; probed directly at 1.2 health, no food, ordinary armour, it fires (`lightest` 1.4 to 3, `health` under it), and both turn_priority and fortress_visit are gameplay-area questions that receive it. It gates nothing by design ("nothing here gates an answer," note 706): hunt and go_in staying choosable at 1.2 health is Jev's judgment call with the fact in hand, not a wiring gap. **(4)** At 18 health with no shield Jev charged 14 blazes at a live spawner (18 to 1.2 in 28 seconds): note 712's rows split charge from close_in but were not conditioned on the blazes in reach or the shield carried, so a charge into one blaze and a charge into fourteen, shielded or not, were the one row. **Changes.** (1) empty-spawner.js's lullOptions no longer gates dig_in_at_spawner on a pickaxe carried; the option prices the real dig time (hand or tool, from spawnerHoleSite's own digMs) and says the rock and what it is dug with. (2) mob-hunt.js: a new `seedFortressAt`, called from findFortressStep the moment a live spawner is known and no fortress anchor exists yet, scans for bricks near the cage itself and seeds state.fortressAt from them (the same bricks search the fortress-leg code runs, just run early and only once); the extent is then known from the cage's first tick, not only after a leg walks free of the flat eight-block gate. (3) survival.js: the pocket_next "held" check now reads `options[plan.choice] || foodWays[plan.choice]`, so a food way chosen under go_for_food holds for its ninety seconds like any other answer. (4) blaze-record.js's cellKeys takes a shield-carried cell (`|shield` or `|no shield`), finer than the plain spawner|blazes|health cell, wherever MIN_FIGHTS of one kind fall in it (rowOf tries it first, then the plain cell, then any health); scripts/blaze-record.js's answerRows carries the shield through from each stance's own recorded state, and a new `firstStanceCells` groups a fight's first stance by class, the blazes at that ask (BLAZES_ABOUT's 0-1/2-3/4+) and the shield, dropping (and saying) a cell under its own minimum rather than rounding a handful of fights into a rate (`node scripts/blaze-record.js --first-cells`). **Measured** (scripts/blaze-record.js --answers, --first-cells; the fights of 2026-09-29T21:00Z to 2026-09-30T04:30Z, 292 fights, up from note 712's 156, superseding its ANSWERS table): at a live spawner with four or more blazes about, over 16 health, charging with a shield (54 fights) brought a rod 11% of the time and died 24%; without one (11 fights) it brought none and died 27% — the exact situation 25592 was in, and the fact that was missing from the row it saw. By first stance and shield (firstStanceCells, informational only, not yet wired into any live text): charge into one blaze or none, shielded, 7 fights, 0% died, 71% rod; into two or three, shielded, 30 fights, 13% died, 60% rod; into four or more with no shield, 9 fights, 33% died, 0% rod; into four or more shielded, 24 fights, 17% died, 21% rod — four cells with too few fights to say (under 5) are named as such rather than rounded. **Tests** (test/note-720.test.js): dig_in_at_spawner offered with no pickaxe, priced by the stubbed site's real digMs, naming the rock and "by hand"; seedFortressAt filling state.fortressAt from a bricks scan at the cage and the extent gate then holding from the first ask, 13.2 blocks off; seedFortressAt doing nothing once an anchor is already known; a food way chosen under go_for_food (search_food) asked once and held on the next tick, not re-asked; blaze-record.js's cellKeys and rowOf taking the shield-carried cell first, and the critic's own no-shield row; scripts/blaze-record.js's firstStanceCells grouping by class, blazes and shield and marking an under-minimum cell `tooFew` rather than a rate. npm test 2808 of 2808, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 101 of 107, the 3 known gaps and the same 3 flaky FAILs already on the flaky list in notes 706, 708, 712, 715 and 717 (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-ghast-walled-toward-push, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598), none new. **Not changed / not measured live:** the shield-carried cell is added only where MIN_FIGHTS of one kind fall in it; most cells still fall back to the plain or wide row exactly as before, so most of the record's text is unchanged; firstStanceCells is a reporting function only (scripts/blaze-record.js), not wired into any option or question text, unlike cellKeys' shield cell which already is (optionSays, answersSay); this branch was cut from main before notes 718 and 719 landed there and does not carry them; no trial has run any of this live.

722. *A drop question that could trade a golden apple for a stick, and a stand taken as the least bad that a different question could undo unasked (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0436Z.md, items 3 and 5: 25581 mid-243-ic 04:36:32Z and 25590 mid-242-sd 04:34:57-04:35:38Z on 2026-09-30; flight records .bot-state/flight/127_0_0_1-25581-Jev-2026-09-30T04-09*.jsonl and 127_0_0_1-25590-Jev-2026-09-30T04-09*.jsonl read by hand).* **(1) 25581 dropped its only golden apple for a stick.** At 04:36:32, told only "Dropping 1 golden apple (4 food points) to make room for the stick," it dropped its one golden apple while cobblestone (131, three over its 128 cap) and dirt (34, two over its 32 cap) sat in the same pockets, offered no differently from any other food stack. **Why.** inventory-tidy.js's drop question sorted junk (no-use items, a stack over its keeping cap) to the front of the list but never stopped offering the rest alongside it, and a golden apple carried only the same "food" note cooked beef or mutton gets: nothing said it was harder to replace, or that dirt and cobblestone alone would have given the room. **Change** (src/inventory-tidy.js). Where any junk exists at all (dirt, surplus cobblestone, a flower, anything over its cap or with no use on the way to the dragon), only junk is offered: a valuable, a life-saver or a tool is asked about only once no junk is left to give the room instead. A golden apple (and the enchanted one) is no longer folded into "food": it is said as an emergency heal — a bite's regeneration and four absorption hearts, the enchanted one's five minutes of fire resistance besides (note 656) — the only one carried, and what remaking it costs (an apple and 8 gold nuggets, or 8 gold blocks for the enchanted one). **(2) 25590 abandoned a 6-of-ten cast frame for a fourth site with none cast.** At 04:34:57 portal_method judged none of its options good (none_good 0.48 on top) and took cast_at_lava as the least bad (0.22 of the real options); nine seconds later, at 04:35:06, surface_trip's climb sent it "back to daylight" instead of digging a site where it stood, and by 04:35:38 the frame was a new one, 0 of ten cast, thirty blocks from the lava — farther than the frame it gave up (20 blocks). **Why.** Note 714 already withholds surface_trip's climb and mine_first while a stand to build the portal holds (intention.js's WAYS), but note 693's "the least bad is not Jev's choice: it begins no intention" meant cast_at_lava, taken as the least bad, never became that stand: `decisions/index.js` passed `chosen: !decision.noneGood` to intention.after regardless of what was actually taken, so a none-good pick began nothing to hold, and surface_trip's climb was never withheld nine seconds later. **Change** (src/decisions/index.js, src/work.js). A none-good fallback still holds as an intention when the answer taken is a stand, not a walk: intention.js's own WALKS regex already marks which TIMED answers are walks (their own yield measure ends them once they gain nothing, note 699, so abandoning one costs only the time spent); a walk taken as the least bad (nether_gather's leg_east, fortress_leg's back_to_fortress, note 693's own measured cases) still begins no intention, unchanged. A stand (portal_method's cast_at_lava among them) has already put down real, harder-to-redo progress, and the very next, unrelated question undoing it costs the same whether Jev was confident or only taking the best of a bad set — so it now holds regardless. Separately, and whether or not the intention holds, surface_trip's climb and mine_first now say what a frame already begun would cost to leave: how many of ten stand, how far off, and that a new site up top leaves it as it stands — a half-built portal is progress by the rung's own measure, and abandoning it is now always a stated choice, never a silent one. **Tests.** test/inventory-tidy.test.js (25581's own pockets: the golden apple withheld while cobblestone and dirt sit over their caps; offered alone, said as an emergency heal and what remaking it costs, not "food"). test/note-722.test.js (25590's judgment replayed: cast_at_lava taken none good still holds, surface_trip asked with climb and mine_first withheld and dig_site the only way left; nether_gather's leg_east taken none good still begins no intention, note 693's own test unchanged; a frame 6 of ten standing said in climb's and mine_first's own text, with tripCost's real column search stood in with open sky above and the frame's own obsidian blocks below). test/none-good-693.test.js, test/intention-689.test.js, test/note-714.test.js and test/decisions.test.js re-run clean. npm test 2816 of 2816, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 102 of 107, the 3 known gaps unchanged (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-ghast-walled-toward-push, nether-pocket-no-food-never-stay-677) and none new. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past this fix; whether a none-good stand held this way ever collides with a *different* stand's own WAYS entry (two stands both wanting to hold at once) was not exercised, since none of the TIMED questions' WAYS entries currently name each other both ways.

723. *A leave that threw NoRoute stayed held for the rest of its ninety seconds while the claim above it kept promising pocket_next, secure_shelter kept asking after refugeStep's own rest had already said there was no way to shelter here, and a defer the hunt had just given was reversed a second later by a stance that never heard it, out_of_fire losing the same way to shot_answer's own walk (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0458Z.md, items 1, 3 and 4; 25590 mid-242-sd 04:45-04:53Z, 25594 mid-242-tb and 25585 mid-242-sg 04:50-04:51Z, 25597 mid-242-t 04:59:17-56Z, all 2026-09-30; read with scripts/trials/recent.js).* **(1) 25590.** Sealed against a piglin 15 blocks off, out of sight, from 04:46:57, pocket_next answered leave at 04:47:59 and again at 04:48:30; turn_priority went on choosing survival at 04:49:32, 04:50:32, 04:51:32 and 04:52:32, its own claim text reading "whether to stay, leave or do something else there is asked next" each time, and no pocket_next came again until 04:53:36, five minutes on. **Why.** survival.js's pocket_next code set `this.state.pocketPlan` to the chosen way before running it, meaning to clear it again once the run was done (`if (!(await options[choice].run())) { delete this.state.pocketPlan; ...; await options.stay.run(); }`); the leave's own walk threw NoRoute rather than returning false, which skipped both the delete and the fallback, leaving the plan "leave" held for the rest of its ninety seconds while every pass quietly rethrew the same NoRoute into stepOnce's own outer catch (a different one, resting a fact three minutes back on `survival:walk` and returning false) with no question asked at all. Separately, pocket-wait.js's own "wait for nothing" rule (notes 679, 698) read a mob as gone only once it passed sixteen blocks off or came into sight; a piglin held off out of sight the whole wait but never crossing sixteen read as still about, so once pocket_next did come again a stay would have been offered its own full ninety seconds too. **Change** (src/survival.js, src/pocket-wait.js). A pocket_next choice's run is now caught the way a stance's own run already is (survival.js stanceStep, note 585): NoRoute and SetAside are read and turned into the same "did nothing" result a plain `false` return gets, so the plan is always cleared and stay always runs meanwhile, and the very next pass asks pocket_next fresh rather than silently retrying a dead choice. pocket-wait.js's `waitsForNothing` also reads a sealed-against mob that has gone unseen for a whole HELD_MS (a minute) as nothing left to wait for, whether or not it ever crossed sixteen blocks, said as "has not been seen since the seal, N minutes ago" beside the existing "is gone" wording. **(2) 25594 and 25585.** Already sealed, survival_priority asked secure_shelter 38 and 45 times in seven and eight seconds. **Why.** refugeStep had already found no way to shelter here and rested it for 180 seconds (`refuge`, `anywhere`, the same mechanism note 476's "no wood yet" case uses), but nothing above it in survival_priority's own tree-building checked that rest before offering secure_shelter again, so it kept being chosen and declined at once, refugeStep itself doing nothing each time. **Change** (src/survival.js). survival_priority does not build tree.secure_shelter while refugeStep's own `refuge`/`anywhere` rest stands, or while the bot is already sealed in the shelter it would build (`shelter.inside` and `shelter.sealed` on the same refuge); the held-plan shortcut above it (the one that already runs a shelter plan without a fresh question each tick, as the walk home for the night does) lets the plan go once that rest is what stopped it, rather than calling refugeStep again next pass regardless. **(3) 25597.** hunt_target answered defer at 04:59:27; one second later encounter_stance answered charge_nearest against the same blazes, not told defer had just been chosen. Fireballs landed, it burned, and body_way's out_of_fire kept losing to shot_answer's own behind_cover walking it off its route, three times running, before it ate on fire at 11 health and died. **Change** (src/danger.js, src/mob-hunt.js, src/survival.js, src/vitals.js, src/shot-reflex.js). hunt_target keeps its last defer (`goal.lastHuntDefer`: when and where), and encounter_stance reads it (`danger.huntAnswerJustNow`, thirty seconds and twelve blocks) and says it in the state and on every closing option (shot-reflex.js STANCE_SHOTS.closing) that would reverse it: "This reverses defer (hunt target), chosen N seconds ago from about here: the hunt read the situation as unsuitable then." Not refused: as plan-chain.js's own reversal (note 705) is said to the plan's own questions, this says it to Jev, who still chooses. Separately, vitals.js's outOfFire now holds `bot._bodyWayRunning` while its own walk is in flight, cleared in a finally whether it finishes, stops at a fall, or throws; shot-reflex.js's stanceAnswer reads it the way a closing stance already is (note 709): a warning while it holds is answered by the shield in place, never behind_cover, which would walk the body off the route out of the fire. **Tests** (test/note-723.test.js): a pocket_next choice whose run throws NoRoute cleaned up the same as one that returns false, with pocket_next asked fresh the very next pass rather than the same failing leave retried in silence; a piglin fifteen blocks off, never seen, read as waiting for nothing once it has been held off a minute, even though it never crossed sixteen blocks; survival_priority not offering secure_shelter again while refugeStep's own rest stands; danger.huntAnswerJustNow read near and recent, not far off, long ago, or unrecorded; encounter_stance saying the reversal on a closing option against blazes a defer was just given for; shot-reflex.stanceAnswer answering the shield while a body_way run is held, not behind_cover, and falling silent once it has gone stale; vitals.outOfFire's own hold set for exactly the one step its walk is taking and cleared after. npm test 2820 of 2820, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 98 of 107 with 4 FAILs and known gaps, all on the flaky list from recent notes (span-ghast-walled-toward-push, basalt-delta-walk-off-25583, fortress-leg-spawner-known-full-health-25589, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598, nether-pocket-no-food-never-stay-677) and none new. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past these fixes; whether 25590's piglin would in fact have wandered off given the extra minute pocket_next now gets asked in, or whether a closing stance chosen over hunt_target's defer with the reversal said would in practice be chosen any less often, is left for the next live trials to show.
727. *The classic enderman roof, built as a real option, not just a fact (notes 713 and 718: the warped_forest drills survive 3-5 endermen but pearls per minute stay low, the cheap roof named the next thing to add and not built; a scratch server, port 25727, .test-combat-727 in the main checkout, built and dropped after).* **The gap, as 718 left it.** An enderman is 2.9 blocks tall and cannot path into a cell under three of headroom (combat-estimate.js MOBS.enderman's own `note`); a lone one is fought or, below eight health, sealed out of a full two-high pocket (survival.js's single-enderman fast path, gated to exactly one within eight blocks and nothing else). Once a second is drawn in, that fast path does not apply and the crowd falls to the general stance question (stanceOptions, `encounter_stance`): note 718 got the fact itself said there (`seal` and `fight` both now name the height), but named the tactic a lid alone makes possible — capping just the two blocks overhead, no walls, fighting on underneath it — as the next real option to add, not built. **What was built** (src/enderman-roof.js, new; src/survival.js stanceOptions; src/decisions/survival.js's catalogue). A `cap_fight` stance: offered only where every threat about is an enderman (a zombie or a spider fits under the same lid and would go on landing its own hits, so it is withheld the moment one is mixed in), it either takes a two-high gap already within three blocks (a walk, no blocks), stands pat where one is already overhead, or places one block above the bot's own head (one block, about two seconds) — priced the same way `seal` is (the setup's own cost against whatever is already at arm's length, stanceCost), then hands off to `fight`'s own run so the sword goes on swinging once the lid is up. Kept off `seal`'s own full shell (eight to thirty blocks and no fighting meanwhile): this is one block or none, and the bot never stops swinging. **Measured, the arena** (scripts/arena.js, ARENA_JEV=1 JEV_ENCOUNTERS=1, real Jev decisions). `enderman_single` (unchanged by this note, the fast path's own case): 3 runs, 0 deaths, 3/3 cleared, median 5.3 damage, matching its own bar. `enderman_forest_trio` (3 endermen, 90 s): 3 runs, 0 deaths, 2 drops, 3 kills, 4.1 damage on the one run that engaged; `cap_fight` was offered once (alongside `fight`, `shield_guard`, `pillar`, `bunker`, `seal` and `retreat`, all seven priced) and Jev took `shield_guard` over it at 0.93 confidence — a real choice made with the tactic in hand, not a forced one. `enderman_forest_five` (5 endermen, 120 s each): 3 runs, 0 deaths (matching 718's own "zero deaths in every completed run"), 2 kills, 0 drops (against 718's 1 pearl over its own 4 runs; two of these three runs answered `defer` the whole time and never engaged at all, the third fought from 20 down to 9.9 health with `shield_guard`, `cap_fight` offered there too and passed over, then ate back to full and closed out the drill with nothing more struck). Read plainly: the option is real, priced honestly, and offered exactly where 718 said it should be, but Jev did not choose it over `shield_guard` either time it came up in these runs — the crowd's own engagement rate is not moved by this note alone, matching 718's own reading that most of both drills' runs still choose not to fight at all. **Tests** (test/note-727.test.js, new): enderman-roof.js's `roofPlan` finding an existing gap over a lid it would otherwise place, standing pat where one is already overhead, and returning null with no material and no gap; the crowd's `cap_fight` offered, priced, and worded with the height fact and the count of endermen about, only where every threat present is one (a zombie in the mix withholds it); taking it hands off to the fight stance's own swinging once the lid is confirmed. test/enderman.test.js and test/survival.test.js's own enderman cases (the span rail-and-fight, the mob-note dedup) re-run unchanged. npm test 2850 of 2850, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. Replay suite 101 of 107, the 3 known gaps (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-toward-a-fortress-38-up-ends-under-it, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598) and none new. **Not done.** Whether Jev would take `cap_fight` over `shield_guard` or `fight` with a larger sample, or in the actual warped-pearls hunt rather than the arena's own drills, was not measured past these six runs; gaze.js's own eyes-off-endermen behavior and the hunt's one-target-at-a-time provoking (mob-hunt.js fightForTarget, already looking only at the mob it strikes) were read and are already what the task asked for, not touched here. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past this build.

724. *One rule in the ask layer for answers that changed nothing (Fable's check-in artifacts/fable/checkin-20260930T0458Z.md, problem 2 and "Stop"; flight records of 2026-09-30 from 00:00Z to 05:30Z, 309 records, 4,569 bot-minutes, read with scripts/unchanged-asks.js, new; the storm on 25585 at 04:52:21 to 04:52:37Z kept as test/fixtures/unchanged-25585-secure-shelter.json).* **What the bots did.** survival_priority answered secure_shelter 42 times in 16 seconds on 25585 (about five a second from 04:52:28, the bot on one block at (-24, 70, 115), dug in already, carrying the same) and 38 times on 25594 (04:50:41 to 04:54:50Z); each run of refugeStep, sealed already, did nothing, and the step asked again. The repeat rule's hold (repeats.js, notes 560 and 571: the same facts and the same answer back at once twice running) never fired there: the survival action just before was a hold or an emergency (dig in), so every such asking counted as a wait chosen (waitingByChoice), and only its words (sameAnswerAgain, "chosen 41 times") went with each ask. Notes 659 to 719 had patched the same thing question by question. **Measured.** 25,664 asks weighed by Jev, 5.62 a bot-minute. By question, asks (a bot-minute, the peak in one minute): turn_priority 5,322 (1.17, 90), encounter_stance 3,813 (0.84, 20), shot_answer 2,918 (0.64, 46), win_strategy 2,138 (0.47, 16), upkeep 1,744 (0.38, 10), survival_priority 1,159 (0.25, 49), fortress_leg 1,129 (0.25, 12), night_mine_target 930 (0.20, 24), fortress_approach 830 (0.18, 10), unstuck_move 661 (0.15, 37), body_way 450 (0.10, 27), crossing_kit 350 (0.08, 6). Asks whose previous answer to the same question changed nothing (the same block, the same things carried, the same health band; blocks dug or placed are not in the frames, so this is a little high): 5,012 (19.5%): turn_priority 1,359, shot_answer 1,256, encounter_stance 873, fortress_leg 207, unstuck_move 198, survival_priority 162, hunt_target 121, rung_progress 112, fortress_approach 102, night_mine_target 85, upkeep 62; crossing_kit only 3 (its 19 cross_now answers moved the bot). Of those, the question's own facts were the same too (the record of past answers set aside, below) for survival_priority 133 of 162, night_mine_target 57, fortress_approach 36, hunt_target 30, upkeep 28, fortress_leg 20, rung_progress 16, unstuck_move 8 (its moves change the ground it reads). Between two askings with nothing changed, the facts that differed were nine times in ten the record of the answers themselves: fortress_leg's lastLeg, legsSoFar, legsResting and lastIntention; unstuck_move's recentMoves and here.notOffered; rung_progress's stalled.strikes and stalled.tried; leastBadLast and planAnswersJustNow everywhere. **The rule** (src/decisions/unchanged.js, new, applied in decide(), src/decisions/index.js). Every answer Jev gives to a question about playing the game is kept with the block the bot stands in, every item's count carried, the blocks dug or placed (stillness.js markCell's count), the health band (fours, full on its own) and the question's own facts (the state less the record of past answers at any depth, clocks and counts aside, and the options offered by their keys). Asked again with none of the first four changed, that answer changed nothing, and the asking says so: in the facts, answerChangedNothing ("secure shelter was chosen 1 second ago and changed nothing (the bot on the same block, carrying the same, no block dug or placed, health as it was); this question was held 10 seconds for something to change, and nothing changed meanwhile."), glossed in the instructions, and on the option ("Chosen N seconds ago, and it changed nothing"), unless the ledger's own words on it already say it came to nothing. With the facts the same too, the question is not asked yet: the bot holds (the turn marked "held: <question>"), the task's check, the air and the caller's interrupt watching as they do while a question is out, until the block, the carried things, the blocks or the health band change (then the question comes back stale and its caller builds it afresh) or the stated wait passes: ten seconds after the answer, thirty after two such answers in a row, a minute after three. Said, never held: body_way and shot_answer (the body's physics), encounter_stance and ranged_response (the stance, whose scene has its own rules, notes 659, 700, 715), turn_priority and stillness_detour (the routing and the stall's own question). And an option whose builder marks it `satisfied` (its goal already so) is left out and said as a fact (alreadySo), as a wait that cannot come is (waits.js, note 698). **Replayed.** The 25585 storm through the rule: 44 asks become 6 (38 held); asked live with its recorded facts and a loop asking as fast as it returns, a 0.2/0.4/0.8-second test clock gives 4 asks in a second where the record has five a second. All the records through the rule: 338 asks held (1.3% of all; survival_priority 133, night_mine_target 57, fortress_approach 32, upkeep 28, hunt_target 27, fortress_leg 18, rung_progress 16, portal_method 8, unstuck_move 7), 5.54 asks a bot-minute after against 5.62; the other 4,674 asks that followed an answer that changed nothing are asked with it said. The rule's own lever is the saying; the hold ends storms, which are few but were the worst (Fable's 38 to 45 in 7 to 8 seconds). **What it subsumes.** Removed: the repeat rule's hold on the same facts and the same answer back at once twice running (repeats.js before(): its `hold`, HOLD_AFTER and the `waiting` exemption), which the new hold meets first for every question; its words (sameAnswerAgain) stay, and so does the hold on answers back at once whatever the facts (quickBefore, note 570), which the same facts never meet. Kept, with why: note 697's rest of an answer Jev chose twice running from here with nothing come of it (leastBad.chosenBefore) acts on repeats minutes apart, which a ten-to-sixty-second hold does not, and it rests the answer where this rule only says it; note 672's turn_priority scene answer, notes 659, 700 and 715 (the stance's scene and holds), 709 and 719 (the stance and stand holds the shot reflex reads) are the stance's and the routing's own, which this rule says and never holds, and they are safety reflexes; notes 693 (least bad), 695 (an answer ending at once, read at another question), 699 (flip pairs, the step's) and 705 (chains across questions) are across questions or below the ask layer. **Agent 723's overlap.** Its secure_shelter change in survival_priority (not offered while sealed or while refugeStep's rest stands, said in state.secureShelterNotOffered) is the per-question form of `satisfied`: once both are in, the node can carry `satisfied: 'already sealed in the shelter it would build'` and the gate says it in alreadySo. Its pocket_next NoRoute fix is a failure path, not a hold, and is not subsumed. **Tests.** test/note-724.test.js (the 25585 storm replayed and asked live; a hold ended by a move comes back stale and the next is asked at once; a reflex stops a hold and gives the turn back; the stance said, never held; new facts asked at once with the answer said; the digest leaving out the record; `satisfied` left out and said). test/tried.test.js's note 573 test now expects the hold and the saying where the repeat rule's rest was (Jev asked three times, told, not rested unasked). test/support/jev-stand-in.js sets the test clock (5, 10, 20 ms) as it does jev-down's backoff. npm test 2837 of 2837, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 100 of 107, the 3 known gaps and four FAILs all on the flaky list (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-ghast-walled-toward-push, basalt-delta-walk-off-25583, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598), none new; each case is a first asking, which this rule does not touch. **Not measured live:** no trial has run with it; whether Jev, told an answer changed nothing, chooses otherwise is read in the next records (scripts/unchanged-asks.js).
725. *The fight text and spawner offers at 25589's mid-242-nc-fortress-3 (the live critic's reports artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0543Z.md item 1 and artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0604Z.md item 1; 2026-09-30 05:32-06:06Z, read with scripts/trials/recent.js).* **(a) A typo'd double comma in the "hardest hitter" lead-in; which mob it names is a known, open gap.** At 06:05:39-43Z every encounter_stance option opened "The magma cube 8 to 9 blocks off, out of sight,, the hardest hitter of the 2 here that can get to the bot, hits for about 4.8 ... 5 blows end the bot" while a blaze 6.6 blocks off in sight had hit the bot two seconds before (06:05:37-39: two HURTs) and was never named, since blowsSay (survival.js, note 576) only considers biters, and a blaze is a shooter. **Why the comma.** Its "out of sight," clause and "the hardest hitter of N" clause each opened with a bare comma, so with both present ("out of sight" and more than one biter) they printed two commas running together. **Change** (src/survival.js). The two clauses now join through one list, comma-separated once, never twice. **Tried and backed out: a distance/sight cutoff on which mob leads.** A rule mirroring 1d055eda's per-mob notes ("only a mob in sight or within eight blocks bears on the stance") was written into blowsSay's `biters`/`creepers` filter and would have kept the magma cube from leading here; `npm test` immediately failed build-reach.test.js's own, deliberate case, a sword piglin 16 blocks off and out of sight that is meant to lead the pocket-building price because it can be at the bot in 2.7 seconds, well before a slow pocket seals (mid-242-ad-nether-3, note 581) — a fact that does not become less true for being far or unseen. Distance alone does not separate the two cases (the piglin arrives in 2.7s, 25589's magma cube in about 4.4s), so the filter was reverted rather than kept as a rule that happened to fit one trial and broke a tested one; which mob leads blowsSay's text is left as it was, a known gap, with what was tried and why recorded in the comment above the function. **(b) Two offers kept going after the game had already answered them.** `set_aside_rung` was taken on the rods at 05:40:26 while standing at a live spawner with blazes about: leaving the rods for thirty minutes made no sense when the spawner was handing them over right there, and the 06:04Z critic found the same offer again. Separately, `keep_working` said "(open a door)" at 05:56:56 while fighting at the spawner: `goal.step.action` still held `open_a_door`, set by mob-hunt.js's own stalking code (line 1115) the last time the hunt tried a door toward a mob, and never cleared once the stalk gave up, so the label read a stale, unrelated step rather than what carrying on at the cage meant. **Change** (src/work.js, src/survival.js). `set_aside_rung` is not offered for the rods while `cage-hold.js`'s `cageFight` finds the bot at a live spawner that still owes them (work.js, `atLiveSpawnerForRods`); away from a spawner it is offered as before. `keep_working`'s label reads the same `cageFight` and says "waiting at the spawner for blazes" there instead of whatever `goal.step.action` last held. **(c) fortress_approach's target could be a brick buried in the fortress's own wall.** With no floor yet seen (`fortressFloors` empty), `findFortressStep` picked the raw-nearest brick as the target regardless of whether anything stood open beside it; a brick with rock or more bricks on every side has no cell next to it to walk to, so every way in (`walk_route`, `cross_level`, `tunnel`) surveyed a short hop toward it and the actual navigate then came back `no_route` a block or two later (05:59:44 and 06:00:24Z, the bot 1 to 11 blocks from the bricks each time). **Change** (src/mob-hunt.js). `exposedBricks` filters the candidate bricks to those with open air on at least one side (or above) before the nearest is taken, falling back to every brick unfiltered only when none is exposed; wired into `findFortressStep`'s candidate list in place of the raw `bricks` fallback. **(d) A fortress already in use was announced as a new find.** At 06:05:00Z, mid-tunnel into the fortress's own wall, the bot said "Ooh, a nether fortress at 118, 364! I'll remember that" — its own position at that moment, tunnelling into a brick right beside it, while it had been working the fortress at (119, 71, 337) the whole trial. **Why.** `noticeLandmarks` (exploration.js) checks a sighting against `goal.landmarks` alone; the fortress the bot is actually approaching is tracked separately, in `goal.fortressSearch.fortressAt` (mob-hunt.js), which this detector never consulted, so the first brick it happened to notice near the bot read as a landmark never seen before. **Change** (src/exploration.js). The `nether_fortress` detector is skipped when the place found is within the fortress already anchored by the search (`fortressSearch.fortressAt`, its extent plus ninety-six blocks): the fortress in use is not re-found. **Tests** (test/note-725.test.js): the stance's lead-in joins "out of sight" and "the hardest hitter of N" with one comma, never two, with two biters and with one; exposedBricks prefers an open brick over a buried one at any distance and still returns every brick when none is open; a fortress already anchored by the search is not re-announced, while the same bricks with no anchor yet still are, once; set_aside_rung withheld at a live spawner with rods owed, offered as usual away from one. npm test 2850 of 2850; JEV_ARBITER=shadow 2851 of 2851, both clean; replay suite 101 of 107, 3 FAILs (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-ghast-walled-toward-push, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598) and 3 KNOWN gaps (blaze-at-1.4-cover-missing, fortress-approach-mine-then-cross-242ab, nether-pocket-no-food-never-stay-677), all on the flaky/known list from notes 723-724, none new. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past these fixes; whether Jev, no longer offered set_aside_rung at the cage or told a stale hunt step there, in fact fights or stands rather than sealing up is left for the next live trials to show.
726. *A food trip must hold against the rung, and staying does not walk it: 25598 sealed at 7 health with nothing to eat, chose return_for_food, and three rung_progress askings later was sealed in again with the trip never said given up; and the gather for planks took whichever kind was known, not one favoured over the other (the live critic's reports critic-20260930T0543Z.md item 3 and critic-20260930T0330Z.md item 1; 25598 mid-242-sf 05:39-05:44Z and 25593 mid-242-qg 03:27-03:32Z, both 2026-09-30, read with scripts/trials/recent.js).* **What the bots did.** (a) 25598 sealed at 7 health, hunger 6, nothing to eat, from 05:39:48Z: pocket_next answered stay twelve times at confidence 0.08 to 0.15, its own text already saying "not healing ... health comes back only at eighteen or more." At 05:43:00 it chose return_for_food (nether_food_kit, a 370-block trip to the portal). At 05:43:21 to 24, rung_progress was asked three times from the same spot: keep_at_it won each time, return_for_food the runner-up, and set_aside_rung stood beside them with no word that a trip for food had just begun. The bot sealed back into a pocket, and at 05:44:03 a blaze two blocks off took it from 6.5 to 1.7 health. (b) 25593 at 03:31:21Z said "I need 2 warped stems," and five seconds later "I need some crimson stems"; the fetch then threw "No way to crimson stem from here: 168 warped stems known at (-83, 36, 51)." Either kind makes planks. **Why.** (a) intention.js (note 689) keeps return_for_food as the bot's intention once chosen, but rung_progress and stillness_detour were asked with their full menu regardless: only GATED questions (fortress_leg, nether_food_kit and the rest) had DROP-type answers like set_aside_rung withheld while an intention held. rung_progress's own offer of set_aside_rung, in the same breath as keep_at_it and return_for_food, cost nothing to the ledger's bookkeeping when chosen (keep_at_it does not end an intention), but the option itself never said the trip was under way, and once the bot was hurt enough to reseal, nothing had made the choice to abandon it a real one Jev weighed. Separately, pocket_next's own `stay` never read a held return trip at all: `waitsForNothing` (note 698) only refuses a wait for nothing when the mob it hid from is gone, not when a trip already begun makes staying pointless on its own account, so `stay` kept looking as free as any other wait even with the trip's own clock running. (b) nether-wood.js picks the stem kind of the nearest *known* place correctly, but knownPlaces (nether-gather.js) let a merely noticed forest (a landmark guess, never an actual sighting, `n: 0`) compete for the same "nearest of each kind" slot as a confirmed cluster of blocks actually seen, and the final resort by raw distance put the guess first when it happened to sit a little nearer on the map than the real 168 warped stems: the fetch asked for a kind that was never really there, and "the reachable kind" went unsaid until the throw itself had to name it. **Changes.** (1) src/intention.js: rung_progress and stillness_detour are gated (ERRAND_GATED) whenever the held intention is an errand (fetch_stems, return_for_blocks, return_for_food, restock_food, restock_blocks, note 703's own list): their own way on (return_for_food, fetch_stems, ...) stays offered, keep_at_it (always KEEP) stays offered, and an answer that would drop the errand with nothing said (set_aside_rung, keep_searching, other_way) is withheld, the same protection GATED questions already had. A non-errand intention (a fortress leg, a walk) leaves rung_progress and stillness_detour open as before, since a real change is meant to be free to redirect those. (2) src/pocket-wait.js: starving in a pocket with a held food trip (goal.intention's return_for_food/restock_food, or goal.leaveNether's reason 'food' from before note 689 existed) says so on `stay` plainly: "A trip for food (return for food) was already chosen N minutes ago, toward (x, y, z): staying here does not walk it, and each minute sealed is a minute of it spent standing still." Sealing against a real mob is left Jev's to choose; this only stops it looking like a free wait. (3) src/nether-gather.js knownPlaces: a landmark or biome guess (no stem ever actually seen there) is now kept apart from confirmed sightings and never fills a slot ahead of one, nor ahead of a farther confirmed sighting merely for sitting nearer on the map; it only fills a slot a confirmed sighting of that kind does not. **Tests.** test/intention-726.test.js (rung_progress gated while a food errand holds: set_aside_rung withheld, keep_at_it and return_for_food kept, the intention not ended by keep_at_it; its own way on still carries the errand forward; a non-errand intention keeps rung_progress's full menu). test/pocket-wait.test.js (a food trip chosen before the seal, held either as goal.leaveNether or as an intention, said on `stay`). test/nether-gather-726.test.js (a confirmed cluster of one stem kind is not crowded out by a merely noticed forest of the other kind sitting nearer; with the slots already filled by confirmed places, an unconfirmed guess is left out entirely). npm test 2850 of 2850, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 103 of 107, the 3 known gaps and bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up (flaky list), none new. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past these fixes.

728. *The crossing's food search judged by food points, not by the ground it covers; a real target named or none said, and what carried food already covers priced against going on (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0627Z.md, item 1; 25597 mid-242-tf (Overworld) 06:12-06:28Z, node scripts/trials/recent.js 25597 --minutes 25 --options).* **What the bot did.** 25597 ran laps over a 40x70 patch for about fifteen minutes on the kit's food rung: win_strategy asked 22 times (20 rung_nether_food) roughly every ten seconds, food carried climbing slowly (0 to 30 of 80) while kit_food's own top_up_food_near walked the same two spots, (-44, 95, 134) and (-37, 103, 164), back and forth; the side_trip option alongside it listed "breed these chickens" (chickens are never hurt, so breeding them is never a food answer, and it read as one beside a food question); nether_first's "Stuck on" clause quoted a stillness_detour attempt count frozen at the moment the reach nether was set aside, unrefreshed for the whole rest that followed. **Root cause.** kit_food's own search (work.js gatherNetherFood, its explore('animals') walk) committed no intention at all: src/intention.js's TIMED map, which note 699's three-minute no-yield rule and note 702's errand rest both key off, had no entry for kit_food, so neither ever saw it. The unchanged-answer rule (note 724) does not catch it either, since it keys on the block stood on among other things, and that changes every lap. The rung's own measure, food points carried, was already tracked by kitFoodStep's own stall watch (ten working minutes without a point more), but ten minutes was never reached because points were, in fact, slowly climbing — the walking itself was never weighed as the thing to end, only the total absence of any gain over a much longer window. **Change.** (1) src/intention.js: kit_food's top_up_food and top_up_food_near are now TIMED (committing an intention) and counted among WALKS, so a search under them is judged the same way a fortress leg or a walk back through the portal is (note 699): three minutes without a gain on the rung's own measure — food points carried, which rung-measure.js already carries on every rung — ends the walk, marks the answer come to nothing, and throws the stall to kit_food, which is asked again with why. kit_food joins GATED so a plan question asked while it holds is filtered the same way. The ended reason now says food specifically ("no food gained"), not a phantom "no nether food" item (src/tried.js rungItems no longer names a kit rung, nether_food among them, as if it were a countable item of its own; it already has food's own measure). (2) src/work.js: foodTopUpSays names the nearest known real target (an animal in view or remembered, a village, a plot) when one exists, or says plainly "no food target is known right now" rather than promising a search "with no bound on how far"; kitFoodStep's go_without now says what cooking the raw meat carried, or baking the wheat carried into bread, would add, so going on with what is carried is a priced choice and not just a bare count against 80. breed_chickens is withheld from side trips while the Nether food kit is short or being worked (goal.stockFood), so it never again appears beside a food question. (3) src/game-progress.js: rungAsideSays' "Stuck on" clause now says "as it stood when set aside", since the tried counts inside it are that moment's and may no longer hold by the time the rest question is read again. **Tests.** test/note-728.test.js: kit_food's top_up_food_near begins an intention and holds while food gains keep coming; laps that gain no food for three minutes end by that measure regardless of the ground covered, throw the stall to kit_food with "no food gained" said, and mark the answer blocked in the ledger (replaying 25597's own two lap points); a real gain of two or more food points in a look keeps the hold. test/work.js's foodTopUpSays and go_without wording updated in test/crossing-food.test.js and test/ruined-portal.test.js; test/note-694.test.js's rungAsideSays wording updated. npm test 2846 of 2846, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 101 of 107, 3 known gaps and 3 FAILs (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, span-toward-a-fortress-38-up-ends-under-it, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598), all on the flaky list, none new. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past this fix; whether Jev, asked kit_food again with "no food gained" said, chooses go_without or a fresh way more often is left for the next live trials.
729. *Netherrack at the feet and the portal offered "for stone"; a span's tip with no pickaxe and no way back to ground; a preempt that could not see through its own box; and a spawner held past its cap with no word that it was capped (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0649Z.md items 1 to 3, and a follow-up on critic-20260930T0710Z.md item 1; 25591 mid-242-u 06:43-06:50Z, 25594 mid-242-tb 06:35-06:50Z, 25598 mid-242-uc 06:38-06:50Z and 07:07:55Z, all 2026-09-30).* **What the bots did.** (a) 25591 stood on netherrack with an iron pickaxe and was told, at every fortress_leg asking, "Go back through the portal ... for stone to lay spans with", 109 blocks off; separately, `stillness_detour`'s recovery layer (recovery-options.js) chased "dirt", "cobblestone" and "stone" in the Nether too, each ending "no stone seen within 128 blocks" or "no way to cobblestone/dirt", none of which exist there. (b) 25594 sat 14+ minutes on the tip of its own span with no pickaxe and 197 blocks carried: `cross_toward` priced digging 39 blocks of rock by hand (110 s), passed over each time, and `back_to_ground` (note 695's walk to the rock last stood on, which needs no digging at all) was never offered because it sat behind the same pickaxe gate as `restock_blocks`, which does dig. (c) 25598 at the spawner cycled `box_here`, `back_to_wall`, `charge_nearest`, `corner_ambush` and `fight` 118 times in 11 minutes (7.35/min), each restarted by arbiter.js's newcomer preempt firing on "a blaze came within 4 blocks" while the box's own wall kept every one of them out of sight, so the count of the box's own doing kept undoing the box's own point. The 07:07:55 follow-up: the same cage, 36+ minutes, 5 kills, 2 rods, 12 to 15 blazes within 16 blocks (11 out of sight, behind rock): the spawner's own cap (BaseSpawner, fewer than 6 of its kind near the cage or it tries none more) had plainly been met, and nothing said so; the rods still wanted were in the blazes already out, not in the ones the box waited on. **Root causes.** (a) mob-hunt.js's `returnForKitSays`, with a pickaxe carried, always said "for stone" regardless of dimension, and the option was built and offered with no look at what `restock_blocks` (computed two lines above it in the same function) had already found diggable close by. recovery-options.js's own `supplies` map (its stillness-layer recovery, separate from the fortress search) was hardcoded to `dirt` and `cobblestone`, the Overworld's footing blocks, with no Nether branch at all. (b) `back_to_ground` was built inside the same `if (... && !pickaxeFirst(bot).none)` guard as `restock_blocks`, though the walk back digs nothing new: it only uses the blocks already carried. (c) arbiter.js's newcomer rule counted a mob a newcomer when `t.visible || t.distance <= 4`, a fallback that ignores walls entirely; note 708 gave `visible` a real raycast (`lineClear`) that already respects them, but the raw-distance fallback undid that for anything within four blocks of a box's own wall. The cap fact existed nowhere on the hold's own options: `stay_and_fight` counted blazes within 16 of the bot (not within the spawner's own 4.6-block range of the cage), and no option ever said the cap was already met or offered the one real way on while it was: going to a blaze already out. **Changes.** (1) mob-hunt.js `returnForKitSays` now says "netherrack" (not "stone") in the Nether, and, given `restock_blocks`'s own plan, adds the fact honestly rather than hiding the option: "Of the 60 the longest leg short of blocks needs, 7 can be dug from ground walked to from here (restock_blocks); the rest is not to be had that way," or "Nothing ... can be dug from ground walked to from here" when there truly is none. The option itself is kept, not withheld: the note's own rule (693, "no bandaids") says the choice stays Jev's, adding a fact rather than a hidden threshold. `chooseLeg` keeps its `plan` past the block that computes it so both the portal option and (2) can see it. (2) recovery-options.js: the footing `supplies` and the terrain-scan block ids are netherrack (or blackstone/basalt, matching the ground underfoot) in the Nether, dirt/cobblestone in the Overworld as before. (3) mob-hunt.js: `back_to_ground` is offered whenever a leg is short of blocks, pickaxe or not (only `restock_blocks`, which digs, still needs one); note 695's walk needs nothing but the blocks already carried. (4) arbiter.js: the close-range fallback for a newcomer now excludes shooters (`mob-policy.js`'s `shooter`), which have no reach of their own, only sight — already carried faithfully by `visible`'s raycast. A melee mob at point-blank range (where a raycast can miss) still counts as before. (5) spawner-clock.js `nearCage`/`capSays`: how many of the spawner's own kind are within its own range of the cage now, against its cap of 6, said plainly ("6 ... already within its own range of the cage: at its cap of 6, it tries none more until fewer are there," or "N ... of the 6 it caps at"). cage-hold.js's `stallAnswers` puts it on `stay_and_fight`, and adds `go_to_blaze_about`: a walk on foot to the nearest blaze already known about (mob-hunt.js's own `blazesAbout`, exported), out of sight first, offered beside the stay rather than only inside the wider fortress search the cage's own stall never reaches. **Left, checked, not changed.** rung_progress choosing `work_free` at a productive box (note 700) already carries the warning that it leads away from the spawner where the rods are fought for (`workFreeSays`), and is not otherwise gated: removing it as an option would be the hidden-threshold bandaid the project's own fixes avoid, so it stands as Jev's informed choice, not a bug. **Tests.** test/note-729.test.js (recoveryOptions asks netherrack, not dirt or cobblestone, in the Nether; returnForKitSays' dimension and honest plan fact; back_to_ground offered with no pickaxe on the same ground the existing restock test uses, minus the pickaxe; the cage's cap fact and go_to_blaze_about on a cage with six blazes already at it). test/arbiter.test.js (an unseen blaze close by is not a newcomer; the same blaze seen is; an unseen melee mob that close still is, as before). npm test 2868 of 2868, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 102 of 107, the 3 known gaps and 2 on the flaky list (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598), none new. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past these fixes.
730. *Food dropped for a stick, and six minutes spent hunting it back (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0710Z.md, item 2: 25597 mid-242-tf 07:05:55Z, 2026-09-30; flight record .bot-state/flight/127_0_0_1-25597-Jev-2026-09-30T06-52-09-214Z.jsonl read by hand, and scripts/trials/recent.js).* **What it did.** Crafting a stick with no free slot, at 07:05:55Z it said "Dropping 7 mutton (14 food points) to make room for the stick," while carrying 15 oak fence, 16 raw copper, 9 lapis lazuli, a wooden hoe, 3 wool stacks, 2 blue eggs and a spider eye besides. Four seconds later rung_nether_food and top_up_food sent it hunting, and it spent the next six-plus minutes and about 25 obtain_food asks walking between two points 90 blocks apart, each hunt ending in under a second. **Why.** Note 722's rule (src/inventory-tidy.js, jevMakesRoom) offers only junk — a no-use item, or a stack over its keeping cap — to drop when any is carried; a valuable, a life-saver or ordinary food is asked about only once no junk is left. 25597 carried none: the oak fence and lapis lazuli have no cap at all, and the raw copper sat exactly at its cap of 16, not over it. With nothing junk, the rule fell back to offering every stack on equal footing, food included, named no differently than the fence or the copper ("food," the same word a golden apple used to get before note 722) — and Jev picked the mutton over stacks it was never told cost less to lose. **Change** (src/inventory-tidy.js). Ordinary food (isFood, short of a golden or enchanted golden apple, which keeps its own separate place in line from note 722) is no longer offered on equal footing with everything else carried: it is the last resort to drop, offered only once nothing else carried is left to drop, or when the thing being made room for itself outranks food (a valuable, another life-saver, or more food). And with no junk to offer, a stack that carries no note of its own (not the only tool, not a valuable, not needed by the step or the rung ahead) now says plainly what dropping it costs — "no flagged use for the run ahead, but not junk either: another would mean finding, mining, trading or crafting one again" — rather than being named and left blank. The "don't pick it up" option this called for is the drop question's own "none" (go without the thing the room was for), already there and untouched by this change. **Tests.** test/inventory-tidy.test.js (25597's own pockets replayed: the mutton excluded from the offer while the oak fence, raw copper and the rest remain, each carrying its own honest note; note 722's golden-apple case re-run unchanged, still offered once no junk is left, for a stick as before, since a golden apple is not ordinary food). test/food-and-crafts-690.test.js (unprotected food may still go for something that outranks it, a gold ingot, as before the item asked was changed from a stick to keep that case true; a stick added as a second case, where food is withheld even with nothing else flagged junk and nothing protecting it). npm test 2864 of 2864, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past this fix; the replay suite (scripts/replay-suite.js) was not run for this change.

733. *win_strategy held its answer no longer than the tree's own shape, which flips regime with a small craft (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0733Z.md item 4; 25585 mid-242-vc 07:25-07:34Z, read with `node scripts/trials/recent.js 25585 --minutes 60 --options` and the flight record .bot-state/flight/127_0_0_1-25585-Jev-2026-09-30T06-52-13-004Z.jsonl).* **What the bot did.** win_strategy swung between rung_nether_pickaxe, rung_nether_food, nether_first and stage_reach_nether six times in nine minutes, small crafts between (a table, a stone pickaxe, planks, a stone pickaxe again), the portal 52 to 51 blocks off the whole time: 07:25:43 (workingOn iron leggings) rung_nether_pickaxe, 07:25:51 (same stage, 8 s later) rung_nether_food, 07:28:06 (same stage) nether_first, 07:28:14 (workingOn nether pickaxe) rung_nether_pickaxe, 07:28:18 (workingOn reach nether, 4 s later) stage_reach_nether, 07:30:57 (workingOn nether pickaxe) rung_nether_pickaxe, 07:31:04 (workingOn reach nether, 7 s later) stage_reach_nether. Beside it, 24 `unstuck_move` asks in the same 24 seconds just before the first of these (07:25:19-07:25:43), 8 of them none_good: a separate loop (the bot working through unstuck.js's own ladder of ways off one stuck cell), not entangled with win_strategy's own thrash and not touched here — it ended on its own once a way worked, and none of its answers ever recorded a real change to hold on. **Root cause.** strategy.js's own hold (note 709) kept an answer only while the tree's own key set stood (`held.keys === keys`, or nothing new since) and `held.ladderNext === stage.phase`. A rung Jev puts ahead of the ladder's own default (here, the pickaxe over the leggings) runs its own crafts, which `nextGameStage` reads fresh on every tick with no memory of the override strategy.js gave it a moment before: whether that read lands back on the rung itself or moves on to the ladder's next default is independent of anything the chosen rung did, and each landing flips the tree's whole regime (`rung_*` keys while the default is a rung itself; `stage_*`, `nether_first` and the side trips once it is past the preparation ladder). Both halves of the old hold read that flip as "the question changed" and asked again, mid-craft, with nothing about the rung itself resolved either way. **Change** (src/strategy.js). A rung answer (`rung_${phase}`) now holds on the rung itself — `game-progress.js openRungs`, read fresh each call — not on the tree's shape or the ladder's own stage.phase: it holds while that phase is still open and no rung neither open nor known at the moment of the answer (`openPhases`, captured then) has opened since (note 709's own case kept: a wholly new requirement still asks fresh), up to the existing ten-minute cap regardless. It gives way the moment the held rung finishes, is set aside, or that cap is reached. `rungStatus` and `lastStrategyFact` read what a held answer has brought (openRungs and the aside ledger, nothing new kept); asked again, the facts say what was chosen, how long ago, and whether it finished, was set aside, or is still open with nothing decided about it since (`state.lastStrategy`), and every other option on offer says plainly it would reverse a rung still open that way. A non-rung answer (a side trip, the ladder's own plain default) is unaffected, held exactly as before. **Tests** (test/note-733.test.js, new): a rung put ahead of the ladder holds through the regime flip a craft causes and is not asked again on every small craft, replaying 25585's own pattern; a genuinely new rung opening mid-hold (note 709's own case) still asks again; past the ten-minute cap with the held rung still open, every other option is tagged as a reversal and Jev's own switch away from it is logged as one (`[strategy] reversal: ...`). test/strategy.test.js and test/flip-trip-709.test.js's existing hold cases pass unchanged. npm test 2873 of 2873, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 98 of 107 (none of its cases touch win_strategy), the same known/flaky names as recent notes, none new. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past this fix; whether win_strategy is in fact asked markedly less often on a rung Jev puts ahead of the ladder, or whether the reversal wording changes how often Jev switches away from one still open, is left for the next live trials to show.
735. *A water storm with no move that works in water; a craft's second try as blind as its first; and an ore that said "no route" kept coming back as ore_0 (the live critic's report artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0755Z.md, items 3 to 5; 25584 mid-242-ve 07:52-07:56Z, 25595 mid-242-vh 07:52-07:53Z, 25594 mid-242-vf 07:55Z, 25589 mid-242-wb 07:48-07:51Z, all 2026-09-30, read with node scripts/trials/recent.js and the flight records).* **What the bots did.** (a) 25584 sat at the flooded portal cast (40, 60-63, 64) over four minutes: 30 unstuck_move asks, 14 topped by none_good (0.4-0.81), step_north and step_south flipped at 07:53:48-50 while it swam for air three times ("Low air"), and cast_portal's own drain phase made no progress. 25595 and 25594 ran the same storm on dry ground (24 and 20 asks): dig_*_feet/head/over scored 0.06-0.2 against none_good at 0.5-0.74. (b) 25595, mid-storm, also timed out "stone pickaxe after crafting... 0 free slots" and was retried once more, unchanged, before the step failed. (c) 25589's night_mine_target asked ore_0 about twenty times from 07:48:49 to 07:51:43Z, roughly every two seconds, with "no route" told twice. **Root causes.** (a) unstuck.js's pillar move was withheld outright while `inWater`, though its own solid-floor check (the block under the feet) already tells a shallow flooded cell, where the bot stands on solid ground under the water, from a deep column with nothing to place against: the check needed no `!inWater` at all, and 25584 stood on solid ground the whole four minutes. swim_up and the place moves at the feet were already offered and already say what they do; the missing move was specifically the one that raises the floor under the feet out of the water. (b) work.js's craft() checks room for the output before the first try (`roomForOutput`), but the retry after a timeout skipped that check and clicked the same recipe again on the same guess (`freesSlot`, that consuming an ingredient stack would free a slot) with no fresh look at the pockets, which is exactly the guess note 690's own "0 free slots" showed wrong. (c) survival.js's nightMine only abandons a target (and rests it, `attemptsFor`, ten minutes) on NoSafeWay, three failures, or a "not gaining" message; a plain NoRoute — as definitive a "this one will not work" as NoSafeWay is — waited for the third failure before it rested, and each of the first two picked the same or a different ore fresh from `night_mine_target`, so the storm looked like the same question over and over though the ore under `ore_0` was not always the same one. Nothing in src/decisions/unchanged.js was at fault here: it holds an unchanged answer to the same question, but each of these askings followed a real abandon (a cleared `mine.target`), a genuinely new choice each time, not a repeat unchanged.js's rule was built to catch. **Changes.** (1) src/unstuck.js: the pillar move is offered whenever the block under the feet is solid, in water or not; in water the space it rises into only needs to be open (not dry), since a further swim up or pillar carries on from there, and the move says it is filling the water at the feet. (2) src/work.js: craft()'s retry, on a first timeout, now re-checks room for the output against the pockets as they are (not the guess made before the click); with room gone it makes room the same way the first try does (drop-for-room) before clicking again, and with nothing to drop it fails at once with the same "No free slot" reason rather than clicking a second doomed try. (3) src/survival.js: nightMine's catch abandons (and rests) the target on NoRoute at once, the same as NoSafeWay, instead of waiting for a third failure. **Tests.** test/note-735.test.js: a pillar is offered standing in shallow water over solid ground (not in a deep column with nothing under the feet); a craft that times out with no free slot drops junk and tries again once room exists, and fails at once with the reason when there is none to drop, in each case never clicking a second doomed try; a night-mine dig that throws NoRoute abandons and rests its target on the first failure, not the third. npm test 2875 of 2875, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow. replay suite 101 of 107, the 3 known gaps and 2 on the flaky list (bridge-sword-piglin-cannot-get-up, leg-mostly-seen-over-a-fresh-one-25598 on one run, span-ghast-walled-toward-push and fortress-leg-spawner-known-full-health-25589 on another, neither repeating on a third run), none new or persistent. **Not measured live:** no trial has run past these fixes.
734. *A food trip home is not held against a stall's own detour, and legs and the work's own turn are silent on the health and food that trip was for (the live critic's reports artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0755Z.md items 1 and 2, and artifacts/critic/critic-20260930T0817Z.md item 2; 25597 mid-242-tf 07:48-07:55Z, 25588 mid-242-rb-fortress-3 07:48-07:57Z and 25592 mid-242-wa 08:10-08:17Z, all 2026-09-30, read with node scripts/trials/recent.js and the flight records by hand).* **What the bots did.** (a) 25597 chose fortress_visit's go_back at 07:49:48Z, hp 14, nothing to eat ("Going back through the portal for food"). Thirty seconds later a find_fortress stall's stillness_detour chose differently, then cross_toward; nether_food_kit's restock_food followed, then hoglin_pillar; the work claimed the turn as fortress_leg's leg_north, and the bot was back on fortress legs, never returning to the portal. It died at hp 3 with no food, a hoglin's blow the last hit. The stall's own chat named a fortress "near -70, 140": that is 25588's fortress, on a different port. (b) 25588's hunt_target chose back_to_wall at 07:54:09Z and held two minutes to its own time limit with nothing changing (no blaze ever saw the spot: "the hold waits for one to wander into sight," but none of the 17 about did). nether_food_kit then chose restock_food -> hoglin_pillar at hunger 20, health 20 ("Stocking up on food here first"), and fireballs landed seconds later. (c) 25592, mid-approach to a fortress, chose nether_food_kit's restock_food -> hoglin_pillar at hunger 20 and health 20 too, then sealed itself three blocks from that fortress's own bricks; the pocket's own text said the wait waited for nothing (health full, nothing sealed against left), yet turn_priority kept giving survival the turn every 60 seconds while the work's claim still read "find fortress" with a fortress right there, and the chat logged "Leave shelter isn't getting me anywhere." **Root causes.** (a) src/intention.js's ERRAND_GATED protects a held errand (fetch_stems, return_for_food, restock_food, restock_blocks) from being dropped in silence by rung_progress or stillness_detour (note 726), but its `ERRANDS` regex never listed `go_back`, fortress_visit's and leave_nether's own name for the same portal trip: `errandGate` was false for it, so stillness_detour's full menu (differently, cross_toward, restock_food, mine_nearby, again, ...) was offered wide open the moment the trip began, with no filtering and no word that a food errand was already under way. The "-70, 140" fortress was checked against both trials' worlds: mid-242-rb-fortress-3 (25588) and mid-242-tf (25597) are sibling branches of the same "mid-242" source world (scripts/trials/start-stage.sh, checkpoint.sh: a stage snapshot's world file and bot-state are copied together to start a new trial, and the .trial-checkpoints/stage-starts.log shows mid-242-rb-031658 alone starting three fortress trials); goal.fortressSearch lives only in each trial's own per-port state file, with no shared or global store found anywhere in the source, so the shared coordinate is a true fact of the shared lineage, not a leak. (b) back_to_wall's hold already has a real end (bunker.js HOLD_MS 120000, QUIET_MS 20000, a rod, or under 8 health) and already says what it waits for; what neither hunt_target nor fortress_leg nor turn_priority's work option said anywhere was the bot's own health, whether food was carried, or what fights begun this hurt came to in the played record (blaze-record.js), so nothing on offer weighed the cost of going on this hurt against it. Separately, nether_food_kit's restock_food line (src/nether-food.js askStayKit, a different path from the honest restock_food already reached through fortress_visit/stillness_detour/rung_progress, which already says its own "why") only ever said the ways to more food and their prices, never that the food already carried, and the hunger and health, might already be enough; asked at hunger 20 and health 20 it read as if nothing were known of the bot's own state. (c) work.js's `stepSays` turned `goal.step.action` into words alone ("find fortress"), never reading `step.found` or `step.fortress` (the nearest brick or the map's own anchor), which find_fortress's own step already carries once a fortress is in view. **Changes.** (1) src/intention.js: `ERRANDS` now includes `go_back`, so stillness_detour and rung_progress are gated the same way while a fortress_visit or leave_nether food trip holds: their own way on (cross_toward, return_for_food, toward the same portal) stays offered, and an option that serves nothing of the trip (mine_nearby, differently, restock_food to a different end) is withheld. (2) src/nether-food.js askStayKit: the `restock_food` option now states the food points already carried, the minutes they last, and the current hunger and health, saying plainly when both are already full ("this is for the stay ahead, not this moment"). (3) src/mob-hunt.js chooseLeg: fortress_leg's state now carries a `fitness` fact whenever health or hunger is short of full — health, whether it comes back, and food carried in words (as hunt_target's own fitnessSays already does) — and under the fight floor (14 health) adds the played record's row for fights begun this hurt (blaze-record.js rowSays), since the search is toward those fights; said nothing extra at full health and hunger. (4) src/work.js: `stepSays` (and `workClaim`, now passed the bot) names the fortress in reach — its coordinates and distance — when find_fortress's own step carries one and the bot is not already walking its floors, instead of the bare "find fortress." **Left for a follow-up.** 25592's "Leave shelter isn't getting me anywhere" (the pocket stuck sealed near the fortress) needs its own investigation into src/survival.js's `leave()`: whether it opens a door onto real open ground or just digs one hole into more rock and calls it done. Flagged as a background task rather than fixed here, since it needs its own flight-record tracing and is a different bug from the food-trip gating above. **Tests.** test/intention-734.test.js (stillness_detour gated while fortress_visit's go_back holds: cross_toward withheld, keep_on kept, the trip not ended by keep_on; its own way on, offered under a different key to the same portal, carries the trip forward; a non-errand intention, going into the fortress, keeps stillness_detour's full menu). test/nether-food-kit-734.test.js (restock_food states the food points already carried and that hunger and health are already full). test/fortress-leg-fitness-734.test.js (a fitness fact with the played record's row under the fight floor; nothing extra at full health and hunger). test/work-claim-fortress-734.test.js (the work claim names the fortress in reach with its distance; stays plain "find fortress" with none in reach or once walking its floors). npm test 2879 of 2879, the same under JEV_ARBITER=shadow; replay suite 101 of 107 (3 known gaps, 2 FAILs on non-deterministic model-answer cases not seen on the unpatched code's own run of the same suite, itself showing a different single FAIL of the same kind: this suite calls the real model and its picks vary run to run). **Not measured live:** no trial has run past these fixes.
